cards.title: The ITE-Transformer: A pre-trained foundation model for predicting individualized treatment effects from electronic health records
cards.abstract: Transformer-based foundation models have shown strong potential for modeling longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), yet existing models focus primarily on risk prediction rather than treatment effect estimation, which limits evidence generation. Here, we introduce the ITE-Transformer, a transformer-based framework that combines self-supervised representation learning from longitudinal patient trajectories with doubly robust causal machine learning for predicting individualized treatment effects (ITEs). As a result, our ITE-Transformer allows to study counterfactual questions of how an individual patient's outcome may differ under alternative treatment strategies. The ITE-Transformer learns temporally contextualized representations of patients' diagnosis and medication histories and subsequently uses these representations to predict treatment assignment, treatment-specific outcome risks, and patient-specific ITEs. The ITE-Transformer is trained using structured EHR data from ~350,000 participants in the All of Us Research Program and evaluated in two clinically different comparative-effectiveness tasks: (i) GLP-1 receptor agonists versus DPP-4 inhibitors among patients with type 2 diabetes, with major adverse cardiovascular events as the outcome, and (ii) immunotherapy versus chemotherapy in a pan-cancer cohort, with all-cause mortality as the outcome. Across both applications, the ITE-Transformer improves the discrimination and calibration of treatment assignment and outcome models compared with existing tabular machine learning approaches and an otherwise identical transformer trained without self-supervised pre-training. The ITE-Transformer further identifies substantial heterogeneity in predicted ITEs and yields interpretable patterns of treatment response associated with patients' diagnoses, medication histories, and comorbidities. Together, our work demonstrates how clinical foundation models can be developed for analyzing heterogeneity in treatment effects and thus support real-world evidence generation.

cards.title: Comprehensive proteomics reveals stage-specific signatures in blood that precede diabetic kidney disease onset and progression
cards.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease is the leading cause of kidney failure worldwide, yet the molecular events underlying disease initiation and progression remain unclear. We measured 5,420 circulating proteins in 830 adults with type 1 diabetes and examined their longitudinal associations with onset and progression of kidney disease over 10 years of follow-up. We identified 130 proteins associated with at least one outcome independent of established clinical risk factors, of which 59 replicated in an independent cohort. HAVCR1/KIM-1, GFRA1, CD14 and GDF15 predicted albuminuria onset up to a decade before detectable disease. Albuminuria progression pointed to the kidney-liver axis (ASGR1, RBP4), whereas rapid kidney function decline and incident kidney failure pointed to immune and tumor necrosis factor receptor signaling. Mendelian randomization prioritized UMOD, SORT1, CLSPN, MAST4 and EGF as potential targets. These findings reveal molecular perturbations preceding clinical manifestations of diabetic kidney disease and identify distinct pathways associated with disease progression.

cards.title: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
cards.abstract: Clinical interventions for cancer treatment toxicities can reduce morbidity, mortality, and healthcare cost, if high risk patients can be identified. We developed SPARC, a transformer-based foundation model, using real-world, longitudinal, routinely collected health measurements, to predict adverse event risk. Pre-training and fine-tuning SPARC on 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients with cancer led to state-of-the-art performance at predicting cancer-related adverse events on (i) held-out data from the development cohort, (ii) a prospective validation cohort from the same center (Npatients=23,126), (iii) multiple publicly available external datasets (Npatients=26,012), and (iv) external, multi-hospital cohorts (Npatients=562,620, 206,840). SPARC generalized to multiple external centers and identified patients most likely to benefit from an intervention (G-CSF). Pooled multi-institution, more than single-institution, fine-tuning improved generalizability. We release SPARC as a community resource. Our results highlight the utility of AI time series models in oncologic management.

cards.title: A Proteome-Wide Gain-of-Function Atlas Mapping the Landscape of Chemotherapy Response
cards.abstract: Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling. Results: Stratified modeling of over 230,000 gene-drug interactions defined distinct functional categories that are strongly enriched for clinical cancer biomarkers and prognostic relevance. Global network analysis and organelle-specific lysosomal functional screening uncovered that chemotherapeutic agents, most prominently the nucleoside analog TAS-102 (Lonsurf), converge upon a shared survival hub centered on the BCL-2 family-associated autophagy-endolysosomal network. Mechanistically, TAS-102 triggered lysosomal activation as an adaptive survival response. Co-treatment with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-263 (Navitoclax) attenuated this TAS-102-induced lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance across colorectal and pancreatic cancer models in vitro and in colorectal cell line- and patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX) models in vivo. Conclusions: Our study establishes an open-access, proteome-wide GOF reference atlas that systematically maps chemotherapeutic responses, recapitulates canonical resistance biology, and nominates rational drug combinations. This systems-genomics resource bridges massive-scale perturbation mapping with actionable target discovery, providing a translational framework to overcome therapeutic resistance and reprogram cancer drug responses.

cards.title: Functional Heritability Partitioning, Multi-Tissue Transcriptomic Colocalization, and Pharmacogenomic Target Deconvolution Across 127 Alzheimer's Disease Susceptibility Loci
cards.abstract: Background: The landmark genome-wide association meta-analysis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-by-proxy across N = 2,815,127 individuals (Uffelmann et al., Nature, 2026) expanded the known susceptibility landscape to 127 independent genomic risk loci (160 association signals) and established an autosomal common-variant SNP heritability of h2_SNP = 16.0% on the liability scale. Translating these 127 static statistical signals into pathway-stratified clinical trials requires resolving three quantitative gaps: how the non-APOE polygenic architecture partitions across distinct cellular programs, which effector genes operate via cortical parenchymal versus peripheral myeloid gene expression, and which targets possess nanomolar human bioactivity suitable for genetically stratified trials. Methods: Operating entirely on individual-genotype-free summary statistics structured along a previously established tridimensional diagnostic framework (Axis 1: Etiology and Genetic Architecture; Axis 2: Molecular Pathophysiology and Biomarker Programs; Axis 3: Neuroanatomical-Cognitive Topography; Menendez-Gonzalez, Alzheimers Dement, 2025), we ingested the complete NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog build GCST90695466 (8,159,496 autosomal and 160,704 X-chromosome variants). First, we performed functional heritability partitioning via stratified excess chi-square inflation and additive genetic variance (sum 2pq*beta^2) across +/-50 kb cis-regulatory windows of 50 fine-mapped effector genes organized into five mechanistic Axis 2 programs (MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE, PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY, ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR, SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM, and MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE). Second, we conducted Summary-data-based Mendelian Randomization (SMR) and Approximate Bayes Factor colocalization (PP.H4) across 54 human tissues in GTEx v10 (4,415 matched cis-eQTLs) alongside Open Targets v4 SuSiE fine-mapped credible sets spanning ROS/MAP dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), BrainSeq, primary human monocytes, and UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP) plasma pQTLs. Third, we queried EMBL-EBI ChEMBL v34 across 2,785 human bioactivity assays (IC50, Ki, Kd, EC50) and Open Targets tractability matrices to construct an empirical pharmacogenomic target atlas. Results: Across 8,159,496 autosomal variants, the genome-wide mean test statistic was chi2_GW = 1.5099. Outside the APOE/TOMM40 super-locus (max chi2 = 3,267.15; 2pq*beta^2 = 0.0882, accounting for 74.82% of top-locus additive variance), 89,589 cis-regulatory SNPs across 48 non-APOE effector genes exhibited a 12.88-fold heritability enrichment over the autosomal background. Normalized across the 16.0% polygenic liability scale, non-APOE functional heritability concentrated in MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE (39.22% share; h2_SNP = 6.28%; 13.02x enrichment; mean chi2 = 7.64) and PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY (36.34% share; h2_SNP = 5.81%; 14.98x enrichment; mean chi2 = 8.64), followed by ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR (16.71% share; h2_SNP = 2.67%; 12.69x enrichment; mean chi2 = 7.47), SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM (5.40% share; h2_SNP = 0.86%; 10.05x enrichment; mean chi2 = 6.13), and MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE (2.33% share; h2_SNP = 0.37%; 5.24x enrichment; mean chi2 = 3.67). Multi-tissue SMR and colocalization resolved a striking divergence between Axis 3 cortical parenchyma and myeloid compartments: QPCT (rs2300880; Z_SMR = -4.62, p_SMR = 3.93e-6, PP.H4_cis = 0.919, PP.H4_local = 0.994 in Brain_Cortex; PP.H4_local = 0.979 in Brain_Frontal_Cortex_BA9) and AXL (rs12979764; p_SMR = 2.13e-4, PP.H4_cis = 0.902, PP.H4_local = 0.924 in Brain_Cortex) colocalized directly within human cerebral cortex and ROS/MAP DLPFC. Conversely, canonical myeloid and endocytic drivers (BIN1, CD33, TREM2, INPP5D, SYK) exhibited near-zero bulk cortical eQTL colocalization (PP.H4_cis <= 0.025 in Brain_Cortex) despite high SuSiE Locus-to-Gene scores (L2G = 0.875-0.968) and robust colocalization in primary monocytes and spleen (INPP5D PP.H4_local = 0.992; BIN1 PP.H4_local = 0.999). ChEMBL v34 bioactivity profiling confirmed low-nanomolar human target potency for clinical-stage compounds across all five programs, including isradipine (2.0 nM) and nilvadipine (19.0 nM) for CACNA1S, omaveloxolone (2.2 nM) for KEAP1, fostamatinib/R406 (41.0 nM) for SYK, and varoglutamstat/PQ912 (61.0 nM) for QPCT. Conclusion: Over three-quarters (75.56%) of the non-APOE common-variant heritability of Alzheimer's disease resides within microglial immune surveillance and proteopathic clearance networks. If prospectively validated in genotype-stratified clinical cohorts, these empirical summary-statistics findings suggest that therapeutic efficacy in sporadic AD may depend on matching pathway-selective drugs to a patient's individual Functional Pathway Burden Score rather than administering uniform monotherapies to genetically unstratified populations.

cards.title: Integrative multi-omics decoding of the host response to Klebsiella pneumoniae infection reveals an itaconate-centred metabolic-immune axis and a spatially organised inflammatory programme
cards.abstract: Background: Klebsiella pneumoniae (Kp) is a leading cause of hospital and community acquired pneumonia and bacteraemia, and hypervirulent and carbapenem resistant lineages continue to expand worldwide. Although individual omics layers of Kp infection have been profiled, the host-level molecular logic that connects transcriptional, cellular, metabolic and spatial programmes has not been systematically integrated. Methods: We curated 16 public datasets spanning four modalities-bulk and dual host pathogen RNA-seq (six datasets; 118 libraries), single-cell RNA-seq (four datasets; {approx}164,000 cells), untargeted/targeted metabolomics (four datasets; 1,842 molecular features) and Visium spatial transcriptomics (two datasets; {approx}11,400 spots) covering murine lung infection models, hypervirulent and classical Kp strains, carbapenem-resistant isolates and human clinical specimens. Datasets were harmonised through a standardised pipeline (Salmon/DESeq2; Scanpy/Harmony; MetaboAnalyst; RCTD/spacexr), and integrated by WGCNA, GSVA, CellChat, Monocle3, SCENIC, joint-pathway analysis, RCTD deconvolution, and machine-learning feature selection (LASSO, random forest, SVM-RFE, XGBoost) with 1,000x bootstrap internal validation and independent external validation. Results: Kp infection evoked a coherent 920 gene neutrophil inflammatory response ({approx}520 up-/{approx}400 down-regulated genes) dominated by IL-17/TNF/NF-{kappa}B signalling, neutrophil degranulation, HIF-1-linked glycolysis and itaconate biosynthesis. A turquoise co-expression module (r = 0.86 with infection status) yielded a ten-gene hub signature (IRG1, S100A9, IL1B, CXCL2, SLC7A11, HMOX1, PTGS2, NFKBIA, LST1, FCGR3B). Single-cell profiling resolved twelve major lung lineages and eleven myeloid substates, tracing a Monocle3 trajectory from Cxcr2hi inflammatory neutrophils through an Irg1/Slc7a11hi oxidative phase into Cxcr4hi/Trem2hi suppressive states; CellChat identified S100A8/A9-TLR4 and CXCL2-CXCR2 as the most amplified axes (8.5x and 4.2x). Metabolomics revealed 30-fold pulmonary itaconate accumulation together with succinate and lactate elevation, glucose/glutamine depletion and glutathione collapse, and joint-pathway analysis positioned the TCA-cycle itaconate and ferroptosis modules as the strongest convergent perturbations. Spatial transcriptomics mapped these programmes onto five anatomical niches, with IRG1 expression peaking in the infection core (58% neutrophil content) and declining radially. A ten-gene host-response classification model reached AUC=0.958 in discovery, 0.937 in internal validation and 0.884-0.912 in two independent external cohorts (Brier score 0.071). Conclusions: By vertically integrating public multi-omics data, we define an itaconate-centred metabolic-immune axis that couples inflammatory myeloid expansion to spatially segregated metabolic niches, and we deliver a validated host-side molecular signature that discriminates Kp infection from non-infected states.

cards.title: Dense Longitudinal Multi Omics Reveals Microbial Metabolic Immune Succession During Immune Checkpoint Therapy
cards.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can induce durable clinical responses, yet relationships among the gut microbiome, microbial function, intestinal metabolism, and host immunity remain incompletely resolved. We performed dense longitudinal multi-omics profiling of a single patient with colorectal cancer metastatic to the liver during ICI therapy and sustained tumor regression. Eleven serial stool samples spanning approximately 7.3 months were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, microbial metatranscriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and stool host RNA immune profiling and aligned with serial clinical imaging. A major intestinal ecosystem transition accompanied the emergence of clinical response. Microbial abundance and transcriptional activity were frequently discordant, demonstrating that compositional profiling alone incompletely captured microbial dynamics. Taxon-resolved functional analysis revealed sequential microbial states rather than a single responder associated configuration. Loss of early Bacteroides/Fusobacterium associated functions accompanied purine/sphingolipid remodeling and changes in myeloid-associated immune signatures. At T5, a transient Bifidobacterium carbohydrate/fermentation program coincided with lactate/indole-3-lactate remodeling and broad adaptive T cell, memory/regulatory, mucosal, and B-cell immune changes. At T6, marked Clostridium transcriptional emergence and lipid/coenzyme A pathway activation coincided with fatty acid/lysophospholipid remodeling and a distinct immune configuration. Historical HUMAnN reconstruction using original UniRef90 and MetaCyc resources confirmed taxon-specific, reaction-associated gene-family support for prioritized functional programs. These findings define a temporally ordered microbial metabolic immune succession during ICI response. Although this N of 1 design cannot establish population generalizability, dense within-person multi omics resolves transient functional states obscured by cross-sectional analyses and generates testable hypotheses for larger prospective cohorts and personalized studies of ICI response.

cards.title: Real-world longitudinal multi-omics separates weight-loss-associated responses to incretin agonists from a broader response not dependent on weight loss
cards.abstract: The benefits of incretin agonists, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists, are largely attributed to glycemic control and weight loss, as these therapies enhance insulin secretion, suppress glucagon release and delay gastric emptying to produce satiety. Yet treatment is also associated with lower risk of cardiometabolic, renal and other chronic diseases. Whether these broader benefits depend on weight loss itself or reflect direct effects of treatment on physiology remains unclear, as does the basis of the marked variation in how patients respond. Resolving these questions has been difficult because weight loss and drug effects occur together, and because molecular studies of treated patients have been limited in scope. Here we profiled paired plasma samples collected before and after treatment from 165 individuals drawn from DynamiQ, a biorepository that links plasma samples to longitudinal clinical records, combining mass spectrometry-based proteomics, a targeted inflammation proteomics panel (NULISAseq) and non-targeted metabolomics to capture metabolic function, inflammation and markers of chronic disease. Treatment was associated with broad remodeling of the plasma proteome and metabolome, but the extent to which this remodeling depended on weight loss differed across the molecular layers. The metabolome carried a lipid signature that scaled with the weight lost, whereas proteomic and inflammation-panel changes largely did not depend on weight loss. Among these changes, treatment was associated with lower circulating mitochondrial oxidative proteins and cardiolipins, consistent with relief of lipid-driven metabolic stress, and with a shift of the inflammation panel toward a less inflamed state. A metabolic aging clock showed that age acceleration decreased by a mean of 2.96 years after treatment (95% confidence interval -4.95 to -0.98; P = 3.7 x 10-3), a change that did not depend on weight loss or on the interval between samples, with the largest reductions in participants starting from the highest age acceleration, most of whom had diabetes. Treatment-associated features overlapped with features associated with cardiometabolic, renal and hepatic disease. Before treatment, higher systemic inflammation, reflecting chronic tissue stress and repair, was associated with less subsequent weight loss. Together, these findings indicate that incretin agonist treatment is associated with lower markers of metabolic and inflammatory stress and with a younger metabolic age, changes that do not depend on weight loss, identify baseline inflammation as an axis of heterogeneity in treatment response, and suggest that biorepositories linking longitudinal multi-omic profiling to clinical records can relate drug pharmacodynamics to disease risk and to variation in patient response.

cards.title: Disease-anchored organ aging clocks enable multi-organ risk profiling from routine labs
cards.abstract: Organ clocks estimate the biological age of organs from blood, but current clocks assign tissue-enriched proteins to organs and train on chronological age, which requires proteomics and does not yield organ-specific disease risk. In the UK Biobank, we trained organ clocks on first onset of disease of each organ using routine laboratory tests and froze the coefficients. Under an age label, organ-clock readouts arose equally in size-matched random protein panels; with a disease label, clocks selected their own organs proteins and predicted their own organs diseases. Defining extreme aging by multiples of disease risk concentrated flags on own-organ disease. Frozen clocks kept organ correspondence in the US NHANES cohort, predicted first onset of own-organ disease in the Japanese JMDC cohort and added more information to clinical risk scores than current organ clocks. Trained once where disease follow-up exists, organ clocks can be used wherever routine laboratory tests are measured.

cards.title: Multi-omics reveals selective metabolic remodelling with trace element supplementation in chronic kidney disease
cards.abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) imposes persistent metabolic stress, yet whether metabolic organization can be preserved under sustained renal stress remains unclear. Essential trace elements support redox defense, mitochondrial function, and intermediary metabolism, and their homeostasis is disturbed in CKD; however, single-element supplementation has yielded heterogeneous results. We examined whether a defined multi-element formulation preserves metabolic resilience in CKD. Methods: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 80 maintenance dialysis patients received standard care alone (n = 40) or plus a trace element cocktail (TEX, 20 mL/day; n = 40). Longitudinal trajectories were analyzed with linear mixed-effects models; endpoint plasma metabolomics and fecal metagenomics were profiled in subsets. A 5/6 nephrectomy mouse model was used to quantify plasma tryptophan-pathway branches and renal spatial metabolism by MALDI imaging mass spectrometry. Results: TEX was well tolerated, with no treatment-related safety signal, and was associated with modestly more favorable creatinine and eGFR trajectories. Supplementation constrained, rather than erased, CKD-associated metabolic displacement (median |Cohen's d|, 0.25 versus 2.09 for disease effects), selectively realigning circulating metabolism toward the healthy state. The host kynurenine branch responded most strongly, whereas microbial indole metabolism and gut community structure changed little. Renal metabolic remodeling was region-specific, with preservation of selected tubular and antioxidant features. Conclusions: Trace element supplementation preserved metabolic resilience in CKD, limiting metabolic displacement without complete restoration. Preservation of metabolic organization may represent a complementary dimension of therapeutic response in CKD. Trial registration: International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry, ITMCTR2026000263 (registered 3 February 2026).

cards.title: TWEAK signaling drives the transition from psoriasis to atopic dermatitis-like inflammation in paradoxical eczema.
cards.abstract: Targeted biologics have transformed the treatment of inflammatory skin diseases such as plaque psoriasis. However, some patients with psoriasis paradoxically develop eczematous skin reactions after therapy targeting tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interleukin-17 (IL-17), or IL-23. Although paradoxical eczema (PE) resembles atopic dermatitis (AD) clinically and histologically, the molecular mechanisms that drive its development remain poorly understood. Here, we generated high-resolution cellular and spatial maps of human skin using single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, and in vitro assays, profiling lesional biopsies from patients with PE (n = 8 donors), alongside healthy control, psoriasis, and AD skin (n = 4 donors per group). In PE, we identified distinct transcriptional changes characterized by myeloid and T cell expansion and an altered keratinocyte phenotype shaped by TNF-like weak inducer of apoptosis (TWEAK; encoded by TNFSF12) signaling through its receptor TNFRSF12A, confirmed at the protein level by immunohistochemistry. To define the underlying mechanism, we stimulated immortalized (N-TERT) and primary human keratinocytes and found that TWEAK acted together with IL-13 to drive a T helper 2- and type I interferon-polarized epithelial program that partially recapitulated the keratinocyte signature of PE lesions. We validated key target genes by quantitative polymerase chain reaction in primary keratinocytes. In THP-1 cells and primary human CD14+ monocytes, anti-TNF treatment induced TWEAK expression, suggesting a compensatory inflammatory circuit. Together, these findings identify the TWEAK-IL-13 axis as a key driver of PE and suggest how cytokine blockade may reshape cutaneous immune responses.

cards.title: Deciphering Molecular Language for Spectral Interpretation with a Foundation Model Pretrained on Repository-Wide Metabolomics Data
cards.abstract: In-depth, scalable structural interpretation of tandem mass spectra from diverse biological tissues and environmental samples is essential for understanding the molecular diversity of cellular environments and the metabolic architecture of living systems. Although community-driven resources such as GNPS and MassIVE have aggregated massive volumes of tandem mass spectra spanning a wide range of organisms, clinical cohorts and environmental surveys, modeling and interpreting this exponentially expanding spectral corpus to distill molecular information and derive meaningful biological insights poses a fundamental challenge for established computational methods. Here we present UltraMS, a dual-polarity foundation model tailored to decipher the molecular language latent in tandem mass spectra through large-scale pretraining on more than 160 million spectra encompassing both positive and negative ion modes. Our findings illustrate that UltraMS is capable of effectively decoding the chemical semantics of molecules underlying mass spectra via self-supervised learning, achieving superior performance across a variety of downstream tasks, including elemental detection, molecular identification, molecular property profiling, and metabolic landscape characterization. Remarkably, UltraMS enables conducting molecular identification with fine-grained spectral interpretability, simultaneously elucidating molecular structures from untargeted MS/MS spectra and providing peak-by-peak substructural attributions via annotation transfer. Deployed on a clinical cohort of human plaque samples, UltraMS demonstrates significant potential in discovering previously unrecognized phenotype-linked metabolites supported by structurally grounded fragment-ion formation pathways, while effectively correcting likely misannotated clinical markers. Furthermore, building on the structure-aware spectral representations learned by UltraMS, we construct UltraAtlas, a chemical-property-resolved map that organizes millions of experimental spectra into a unified coordinate system, enabling millisecond-scale molecular profiling and offering practical guidance for exploratory navigation across vast chemical space. Applied to human scalp metabolomics, UltraAtlas effectively captures distinct metabolic variations across individuals, highlighting phenotype-specific chemical signatures while shedding light on the chemical niches of the resident microbiome. Together, UltraMS and UltraAtlas constitute a generalizable framework for structural elucidation and biological discovery from tandem mass spectra, empowering the comprehensive exploration of the largely undeciphered metabolomes across different domains of life.

cards.title: Metabolome-wide analysis suggests antidepressant exposure counteracts risk of depression in fatty-acid pathways
cards.abstract: Antidepressants are widely prescribed, yet their biological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Large-scale metabolomics and linked electronic health records provide a unique opportunity to characterise metabolic profiles associated with medication exposure. We investigated metabolic signatures of antidepressant exposure using 251 nuclear magnetic resonance biomarkers in UK Biobank (N = 222,911), with external validation in NESDA and ALSPAC (N = 6,082) and longitudinal analyses (n = 5,820, mean follow-up = 4.2 years). We identified 152 metabolites associated with current antidepressant use (PFDR < 0.05), characterised by elevated triglycerides and very-low-density lipoproteins. Current users also showed higher omega-3 fatty acid levels and lower omega-6-to-omega-3 ratios, both associated with lower depression risk. Metabolic profile scores significantly distinguished antidepressant users in both external cohorts (OR = 1.07- 1.39, ROC AUC = 0.58-0.73). Longitudinal analyses identified nominal associations between antidepressant initiation and increases in nine lipid biomarkers ({beta} = 0.144- 0.229). These findings suggest metabolic signatures associated with antidepressant use may not be solely explained by underlying depression and are characterised by both potentially beneficial fatty acid alterations and adverse lipid profiles. Validation across independent cohorts and consistency with longitudinal findings strengthen our evidence, supporting insights into antidepressant mechanism and its relevance to cardiometabolic health.

cards.title: Plasma Proteomic Identifies GDF15 as a Candidate Lithium Treatment Response Biomarker in Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Secondary Analysis of the LATTICE Randomized Clinical Trial
cards.abstract: Lithium (Li) demonstrates neuroprotective effects relevant to Alzheimer disease (AD). However, its molecular mechanisms remain insufficiently characterized. This study analyzed plasma proteomic profiles from the Li as a Treatment to Prevent Impairment of Cognition in Elders (LATTICE) randomized clinical trial to identify markers associated with amyloid beta pathology, disease progression, and response to Li treatment. In the LATTICE trial, 80 older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) were randomly assigned to receive either low-dose Li carbonate or placebo for two years. Longitudinal plasma samples were analyzed using the NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel 120 proteomic panel. Baseline protein levels were compared according to randomized treatment assignment, amyloid beta PET status, and MCI subtype. Analyses included longitudinal changes in protein levels associated with treatment and time, associations between baseline protein levels and subsequent cognitive, functional, and neuroimaging trajectories, and the influence of baseline protein levels on Li treatment effects. Among the 80 participants, 62 had amnestic MCI and 21 were positive on amyloid beta PET. Baseline proteomic differences were more strongly associated with amyloid beta PET status than with randomized treatment assignment. Plasma p-tau217 concentrations were elevated in individuals who were positive on amyloid beta PET and remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Over time, CALB2 and TREM2 exhibited nominal treatment-by-time interactions in the full cohort, while in the amnestic MCI subgroup, CALB2, TREM2, and amyloid beta 40 demonstrated nominal effects. None persisted after multiple-testing correction. GDF15 showed the most consistent associations with CDR Sum of Boxes trajectories and treatment-effect modification that remained significant after false discovery rate correction in the amnestic MCI subgroup, whereas p-tau217 was most consistently associated with hippocampal volume trajectories. Other protein-outcome associations were exploratory. Plasma proteomics identified distinct molecular patterns associated with amyloid beta pathology and the MCI phenotype, along with exploratory evidence of Li-associated protein changes. Plasma GDF15 and p-tau217 emerged as potential markers of clinical progression and treatment-response heterogeneity, warranting validation in larger, adequately powered trials.

cards.title: Myeloid subpopulations correlate with responsiveness to therapy in a prospective, longitudinal study on RA patients
cards.abstract: Background: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is an autoimmune disease associated with the destruction of cartilage and bone, increased risk of cardiovascular disease and a higher mortality rate. Despite the many therapies that exist for RA, there is little information to guide selection of the most effective treatment for an individual patient. Ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies have created an opportunity to investigate the target tissue. While a number of studies have characterized the stromal and immune cell populations using single-cell technology on synovial biopsy samples, here we performed a longitudinal study, where we collected comprehensive clinical data over a one-year period on each patient in the process of changing their therapy. Methods: Samples from minimally invasive, ultrasound-guided synovial biopsies were collected from RA patients at baseline prior to start of a new therapy and 4-6-week follow-up under IRB-approved protocols with informed consent. Comprehensive clinical data from each appointment were recorded into a shared REDCap database. Failure to respond to therapy was based on clinical disease activity index (CDAI) for RA after 12-18 weeks post therapy. Biopsied samples were dissociated, enriched for CD45 or CD45CD11b cells, and processed on the 10X Genomics Chromium platform to generate libraries for single-cell RNA sequencing with cell-surface protein detection (CITE-seq). Spatial transcriptomics were performed on formalin-fixed paraffin embedded sections analyzed with 10X Xenium and NanoString CosMx. Results: We performed CITE-seq analysis on ~38,000 CD45+ synovial cells isolated from 17 patients who failed a conventional or biologic DMARD and planned to change therapy. We then subclustered on the myeloid population to reveal 12 myeloid subpopulations that consist of macrophages (n = 8), Osteoclast-like cells, DCs (n = 2) and proliferating cells. The proportion of cDCs was significantly higher in responders, while the proportion of macrophages was significantly lower in responders. The proportion of ISG15+ and THBS1+macrophages were enriched in the non-responder patients. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that ISG15+ macrophages were preferentially localized to the synovial lining, while the THBS1+ macrophages are likely interacting with lymphoid cells within the sublining tissue. Conclusions: These data are among the first to prospectively profile macrophage populations as predictors of response to therapy. Future studies are required to verify whether myeloid subpopulation associations hold across specific therapies.

cards.title: Transportability of mouse gene knockout models to human complex phenotypes
cards.abstract: Mouse gene knockout studies are a valuable resource for understanding human gene function and the mechanisms underlying disease. However, translating insights to humans requires causal similarities between mouse and human phenotypes. A mouse model is transportable if gene perturbations that impact the mouse phenotype also affect (in orthologous genes) the corresponding human phenotype of interest, with consistent directionality. To assess the transportability of mouse models to human complex traits we combined laboratory mouse gene perturbation data from the high-throughput International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium with predicted loss-of-function data from the UK Biobank within the Gene Perturbation Analysis for Transportability (GPAT) framework. Applying GPAT to 30 matched mouse-human phenotype pairs, we found evidence of transportability for 12 mouse phenotypes including biochemical (e.g. total cholesterol), cellular (e.g. lymphocyte counts) and anthropometric (e.g. length/height) phenotypes. In contrast, there was limited evidence for others such as fat mass and body mass index in the context of the murine experimental conditions. We also found some evidence of transportability of mouse glucose measurements to diabetes mellitus in humans. Genome-wide perturbation effects on matched phenotypes were on average positively correlated between mice and humans (meta-analysis GPAT P = 2.3x10-27). However, the degree of correlation was generally modest and heterogeneous across phenotypes with some gene perturbations strongly associated in both species in opposite directions. Our framework illustrates how perturbation data can be used to quantitatively validate experimental models for understanding human disease aetiology and highlights the need for a range of orthogonal model systems, which may include challenges and perturbations to the mouse knockouts, to interrogate the mechanistic basis of human genetic associations.

cards.title: Biological augmentation of electronic health records through estimation of patient proteomes.
cards.abstract: High-dimensional proteomic profiling can improve clinical risk prediction and provide insight into disease biology, but routine acquisition of omic data at population scale remains impractical. We developed Real-world AI-based Biomarker Inference Technology (RABIT), a machine learning framework that biologically augments electronic health records (EHRs) by projecting longitudinal clinical histories into a high-dimensional proteomic representation space learned from paired EHR and plasma proteomics. RABIT was trained using patients with paired EHRs and measured plasma proteomics and externally validated in an independent cohort with paired data. RABIT profiles showed broad concordance with measured protein expression and more closely resembled measured proteomics than their input EHR. Incorporating these biologically augmented representations improved 5-year disease onset prediction across 14 conditions (n = 449,223; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 33.7%) and generalized to an external cohort (n = 1,038,419; mean adjusted AUPRC increase of 70.3%). RABIT profiles reproduced clinically meaningful organ-specific biological changes in response to aging and further outperformed models built from comprehensive established clinical predictors in prediction of chronic kidney disease progression, major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and response to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. Last, RABIT enabled biological signatures derived from small discovery cohorts to be extended to population-scale clinical datasets, generating clinically relevant hypotheses linking cytomegalovirus-associated immune states to variation in brain tumor outcomes. Together, these results demonstrate that biological augmentation of EHRs can enable molecularly informed clinical prediction and hypothesis generation at population scale.

cards.title: Untargeted Screening of Environmental and Endogenous Metabolites and Risk of Incident COPD: A Prospective Study in Three European Populations
cards.abstract: Objective: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of death in the industrialized world. Although smoking, air pollution, and occupational exposures are well established risk factors, the molecular pathways linking environmental exposures and biological susceptibility to COPD remain incompletely understood. Untargeted metabolomics offers a unique opportunity to simultaneously capture internalized environmental chemicals and endogenous metabolic perturbations. However, large prospective studies integrating broad exposomic and metabolic screening prior to COPD onset are lacking. Methods: We conducted a nested case-control study within three European population-based cohorts (Doetinchem Cohort Study, KORA, SAPALDIA) and analyzed 1473 prospectively collected plasma samples. COPD was defined by a pre-bronchodilation FEV1/FVC ratio below 0.7 at follow-up (4-16 years after blood sample collection). We applied complementary untargeted liquid- and gas chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC- and GC-HRMS), enabling extensive coverage of endogenous metabolism and exogenous environmental contaminants, including pesticides, plastic-related chemicals, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Controls maintained normal lung function and were matched to cases on age, sex, follow-up time, and sample collection round. We performed separate conditional logistic regression models for each metabolomic feature, and used Mummichog for prediction of biological pathways involved. The false discovery rate (FDR) was controlled using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Long-term measurement reliability was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) from repeat samples in the Doetinchem Cohort Study. Results: In total, thousands of metabolomic features were screened, including 724 annotated exogenous compounds, 13 endogenous metabolites, and 197 features that could be derived as both. Nicotine and cotinine intensity levels were statistically significantly associated with COPD incidence at an FDR of 10%, validating the analytical and epidemiologic framework. Beyond smoking-related markers, lower levels of butyrylcarnitine were associated with increased COPD risk among never-smokers, implicating altered mitochondrial fatty-acid metabolism as a potential early pathway independent of tobacco exposure. Although most screened environmental contaminants, including PAHs and pesticides, were not associated with COPD at stringent significance thresholds, restricting analyses to temporally stable metabolites identified the insecticide metabolite phenyl N-methylcarbamate as a predictor. Conclusion: This large-scale, prospective untargeted metabolomics study represents one of the most comprehensive assessments to date of both environmental and endogenous metabolic predictors of COPD. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of exposome-wide molecular screening years before disease onset, identify butyrylcarnitine as a novel metabolic predictor in never-smokers, and highlight the importance of accounting for temporal variability in metabolomic epidemiology.

cards.title: A Reproducible Pre-Transplant γδ T-cell Effector Signature Reveals Immune-Metabolic Programs Associated with Kidney Allograft Rejection
cards.abstract: Despite optimized immunosuppression, acute kidney transplant rejection affects 10-20% of recipients within the first year, and no reliable pre-transplant molecular test exists to identify patients at high risk, independent of the donor HLA matching. Across three independent cohorts of kidney transplant recipients, profiled by bulk RNA-sequencing with T-cell receptor repertoire analysis, flow cytometry, CyTOF with paired metabolomics, we identified a reproducible depletion of {gamma}{delta} T cells associated with rejection: an elevated {beta}/{gamma}{delta} T cell ratio in two post-transplant, biopsy-matched cohorts, and depletion of specific {gamma}{delta} T effector clusters in a third, longitudinally sampled cohort. In this third cohort, {gamma}{delta} T cell depletion was already present at the pre-transplant baseline in patients who subsequently developed rejection and remained detectable across the transplant course, indicating that it reflects recipient baseline immune biology rather than a consequence of graft injury. Longitudinal metabolomic profiling in this cohort identified time-dependent metabolic changes, including in amino acid metabolism that co-occur with the {gamma}{delta} signature and converge with it upon multi-omics integration. At the pre-transplant baseline, {gamma}{delta} T-cell marker expression alone showed exploratory discriminatory value for rejection risk (AUC = 0.69), improving marginally when integrated with metabolomic features (AUC = 0.71); larger prospective studies will be needed before clinical translation.

cards.title: Marking Time: Multilayered and Multimodal Frameworks for Measuring Human Biological Aging
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Human aging is a complex and multifactorial process characterized by progressive physiological decline, increased susceptibility to chronic diseases, and reduced stress resistance. Chronological age (CA) alone is insufficient to reflect significant interindividual differences in biological aging (BA) or the asynchronous decline of organs. This limitation has driven the development of biomarkers of BA, or “biological clocks” (BC), which have evolved from chronological predictors based on a single omics analysis to sophisticated multidimensional approaches. These modern systems integrate multiomic data derived from epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, clinical, and physiological analyses of distinct organs and species. This perspective traces the evolution of the aging clock (AC) framework from first‐generation predictors of CA to phenotypic/mortality, aging rate, causality‐based, cross‐species, and multimodal models. Consequently, a primary multidimensional framework for AC can be proposed based on their training objectives, biological scope, and validation properties, highlighting their potential applications in risk stratification, personalized medicine, monitoring of interventions, clinical trial design, guidelines for healthy aging, and public health planning. Two recent studies illustrated the emergence of highly integrated BC of aging. Special attention is given to the technical and practical trade‐offs of multiomic integration, which encompasses dimensionality, reproducibility, computational complexity, cost, interpretability, and clinical scalability. Despite substantial progress, significant obstacles remain, including overfitting, unfavorable trade‐offs between dimensionality and cost, population‐specific calibration, limited generalizability across species and various demographic groups, and uncertainty regarding whether biomarker associations reflect true causal mechanisms. Overcoming current limitations is essential for developing reliable and widely applicable AC for routine integration in personalized geromedicine.

cards.title: Ciliated keratinocytes define a spatially restricted pro-inflammatory state in psoriasis and atopic dermatitis
cards.abstract: Abstract Background: Psoriasis vulgaris (Pso) and atopic dermatitis (AD) are characterized by recurrent flares and incomplete disease resolution. Primary cilia are antenna-like sensory organelles that project from the cell surface and coordinate extracellular signaling. Although epidermal ciliated cells are rarely detected in healthy skin and are selectively increased in AD and Pso, their molecular identity, functional properties, and clinical relevance remain unclear. Objective: To characterize epidermal ciliated cells in Pso and AD and determine their molecular identity, functional properties, and clinical relevance. Methods: We integrated single-cell-resolved spatial transcriptomics with primary cilia immunostaining in healthy skin (n=6), AD lesions (n=10), and paired psoriatic skin before and after phototherapy (n=7 each). Functional analyses using HaCaT cells with increased primary cilia formation included MAPK/NFkB signaling assays, ATAC-seq, and pathway inhibition assays. Results: Ciliated cells were largely restricted to AD and both pre and post treatment psoriatic skin, with KCs accounting for more than 70% of all ciliated cells. Ciliated KCs were predominantly localized to the basal and spinous layers. These cells exhibited disease and stage specific inflammatory programs and formed spatially organized communication networks with surrounding cells, including non ciliated KCs, fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and myeloid cells, suggesting a ciliated KC centered inflammation niche. Mechanistically, increased primary cilia formation enhanced MAPK and NFkB signaling and increased chromatin accessibility at inflammatory gene loci enriched for AP1 motifs, even in the absence of stimulation, consistent with a chromatin primed state. Higher residual ciliated KC abundance after phototherapy was associated with subsequent treatment escalation. ERK1/2 inhibition reduced cytokine induced primary cilia formation. Conclusions: Ciliated KCs represent an inflammatory epithelial cell state associated with residual disease activity in AD and Pso. The suppression of cytokine-induced primary cilia formation by ERK1/2 inhibition suggests that inflammation associated primary cilia formation may be modifiable process in persistent skin inflammation.

cards.title: Tumor Associated Neutrophils Extend NETs To Spatially Drive Necroptosis In Glioblastoma
cards.abstract: Background: Glioblastoma is pathologically characterized by extensive pseudopalisading necrosis, a hallmark linked to therapeutic resistance and dismal prognosis. While traditionally viewed as a passive ischemic event, the precise radiogenomic drivers and spatial immune architectures orchestrating active tumor necrosis remain poorly understood. Methods: We integrated macroscopic clinical MRI radiomics with public genomic datasets (n=3,639), single-cell spatial transcriptomics, and high-resolution protein immunofluorescence (IF) assays in a novel co-mutant murine model to map the necrotic microenvironment. Results: Radiomic analysis of patient MRIs demonstrated that high tumoral necrotic volume serves as a powerful independent biomarker for poor long-term survival. This macro-structural necrosis phenotype is radiogenomically driven by cell-intrinsic TP53, PTEN, and NF1 (PPN) co-mutations. Spatial transcriptomic profiling of PPN-deficient tumors revealed distinct cellular topography, separating a proliferative, invasive niche (EGFR+ SOX+, TypeInv) from a hyper-aggressive necrotic niche (ERBB3+, TypeNec). Mechanistically, TypeNec cells deploy a prominent CCL5/CXCL2 chemokine milieu that actively recruits and prompts tumor-associated neutrophils to undergo neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. This overactive neutrophil infiltrate drives a feed-forward loop of intrinsic tumor necroptosis mediated by the release of the damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) protein HMGB2. This cascade could be therapeutically dismantled using targeted anti-inflammatory compounds. Finally, multi-cohort clinical validation confirmed that an HMGB2high signature dictates a high-risk, myeloid-rich immunosuppressive microenvironment in glioblastoma patients. Conclusions: Our findings redefine glioblastoma necrosis as an active, mutation-driven immunopathological process. The HMGB2-mediated DAMP necroptosis cascade and associated myeloid chemokines provide robust prognostic biomarkers and immediate therapeutic vulnerabilities to disrupt the immunosuppressive necrotic niche.

cards.title: Multiplex proteomics of cerebrospinal fluid reveals markers of clinical and neuropathological heterogeneity in Lewy body dementia.
cards.abstract: Lewy body dementia (LBD), which encompasses Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD) and dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), lacks established biofluid markers of its complex clinical and neuropathological heterogeneity. Multiplex proteomic tools, such as the recently developed nucleic acid-linked immunosandwich assay (NULISA), can assess a diverse array of neurodegenerative targets and address these biomarker gaps. We used this platform to analyze 852 baseline and longitudinal cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from control participants and participants with PD and DLB in the Parkinson's Disease Biomarker Program. In three separate analyses, we examined LBD protein signatures of clinical diagnosis, cognitive progression, and underlying neuropathology. Clinically diagnosed LBD demonstrated alterations in numerous proteins across a wide range of pathophysiologies, including synaptic, inflammatory, and vascular dysfunction. Stratifying cases by cognitive progression revealed a smaller subset of proteins with baseline or longitudinal abundance changes linked to clinical declines. To identify neuropathological protein signatures, we stratified 209 cases by the presence of underlying synuclein and amyloid-beta (Aβ) pathology using CSF alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay results and NULISA phosphorylated tau 217 levels, respectively. These neuropathological subgroups revealed synaptic markers with decreased abundance relative to synucleinopathy but increased abundance relative to Aβ accumulation, complicating the interpretation of these markers in cases with copathology. Many of these neuropathological signatures were replicated in an independent cohort of 917 cases from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative. Overall, these results highlight the utility of multiplex proteomic analysis in identifying candidate CSF markers of disease heterogeneity in LBD that could enhance precision in its diagnosis and management.

cards.title: Context-dependent associations between recent antibiotic treatment, gut microbiome composition, blood metabolites, and metabolic health.
cards.abstract: Antibiotics are among the most widely prescribed drugs, and they reliably disrupt the commensal gut microbiota. Large epidemiological studies link antibiotic exposure to type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk, yet smaller randomized intervention trials have failed to find this connection. Whether this discordance reflects a true lack of signal or subpopulation-dependent responses to antibiotics remains unclear. Here, across three independent cohorts (N=4,122), we show that recent antibiotic use may reshape host physiology in specific dietary, microbial, and metabolic contexts. Recent antibiotic use was associated with reduced gut microbiome richness, greater Bacteroides and pathobiont dominance, lower predicted butyrate production, and altered levels of 34 blood metabolites, including several microbe-host co-metabolites, such as hippurate and isoursodeoxycholic acid, while the blood proteome was unchanged. Diet and microbiome composition influenced the magnitude of these effects: preference for liquor was associated with steeper diversity loss, and the presence of specific bacterial genera either dampened or amplified antibiotic-associated blood metabolite differences. Clinical chemistries did not differ, on average, across antibiotic treament groups, affirming the intervention trials. However, recent antibiotic users with T2D showed elevated methylmalonic acid, homocysteine, and alkaline phosphatase, suggesting B-vitamin deficiency. Furthermore, antibiotic users with poorer metabolic health (e.g., blood metabolomics-inferredBMI > measured BMI) showed lower circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D. Overall, metabolic disruption associated with recent antibiotic use appears to be related to vitamin deficiencies and is concentrated in metabolically vulnerable subgroups, arguing for further research into context-aware prescribing and targeted co-therapies, like higher fiber diets, probiotics, or supplements.

cards.title: High-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Millimeter-Scale Malignant Territories and Immune Exclusion patterns in Human Salivary Gland Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma
cards.abstract: Background/Objectives: Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the salivary gland (SGACC) is a rare malignancy with frequent late recurrence and limited response to systemic and immune therapies. Bulk and single-cell sequencing do not preserve tissue architecture, so the spatial organization of its MYB-driven myoepithelial and luminal tumor cells, stroma, and immune cells remains poorly defined. This study aimed to map the SGACC tumor microenvironment at near-cellular resolution. Methods: Visium HD based spatial transcriptomics was performed on four SGACC tissue sections from three patients with tubulo-cribriform tumor form in stage III - IV. Bins of 10 x 10 {micro}m were annotated and deconvolved with cell2location using an integrated single-cell reference of 119,189 cells from 20 donors. Pseudobulk differential expression, spatial autocorrelation, potency and spatial trajectory inference, permutation-based territory analysis, Hotspot module detection, and marker-based immune profiling were applied. Results: MYB-expressing luminal (LECs-MYB) and myoepithelial (MECs-MYB) epithelial cells occupied 55.7% of bins on average. The MECs-MYB to LECs-MYB ratio increased from the nest interior toward the tumor edge, where cancer-associated fibroblasts rose sharply. Potency and trajectory analyses placed MECs-MYB upstream of LECs-MYB. Malignant states formed territories of up to 38.0 mm2 that persisted over 1.5 mm in three sections and contained spatially restricted programs. Hypoxic stressed territories also showed mTORC1, unfolded protein response, and cell-cycle programs. T/NK, myeloid, MHC class I and II, and plasma cell signatures were 1.4- to 5.7-fold higher in stroma than in tumor nests, whereas VTCN1 (B7-H4) was the only B7 family ligand enriched within nests. Conclusions: SGACC shows an ordered arrangement of malignant lineages, millimeter-scale malignant territories, MHC class - I and II enriched stroma, and immune-excluded nests enriched for B7-H4. These features provide evidence to be validated in larger cohorts with protein-level and clinical data.

cards.title: Media matters: A resource for understanding the determinants of migratory potential of malignant and non-malignant cells
cards.abstract: Cell mobility is critical for homeostatic processes such as wound repair and diseases like cancer metastasis. While the advent of migrastatic and antimetastatic therapies has promise, the identification and translation of pathways important for migratory plasticity into druggable targets approved in clinical trials are considerably lacking. To better understand why, we developed an unbiased high-throughput wound-healing/invasion assay to screen for the migratory potential of >60 non-malignant and malignant cell lines derived from the pancreas, colon, skin, breast, prostate, and lung. The goal of this phenotypic screen was to provide a resource of migration/invasion potential and insight into the differential properties not only between malignant and non-malignant cells but also the various carcinomas. Surprisingly, we found non-malignant epithelial cells of the lung, skin, and pancreas migrated/invaded faster than their malignant counterparts. We observed perturbation of glucose metabolism, via inhibition of glycolysis, restricted the migration of non-malignant but not cancer cells, whereas inhibition of oxidative phosphorylation limited the mobility of malignant more than normal cells of the lung, skin, and pancreas. Short-term acclimation of cancer cells in low-nutrient media, containing low/no serum, low calcium, and physiological concentrations of glucose, increased in vitro migration/invasion and in vivo metastatic potential of lung but not pancreatic carcinomas. Phenotypic and metabolic screens presented here could identify prospective therapeutics not only for cancer metastasis, but also diseases driven by the dysregulation of wound-healing/regeneration.

cards.title: Spatial organization of a SPINK1-associated tumor-stromal ecosystem links metabolic remodeling to immune restriction in bladder cancer
cards.abstract: Spatially organized tumor-stromal interactions contribute to metabolic remodeling and immune suppression in bladder cancer (BLCA). Using spatial transcriptional programs to define single-cell states, we identified a niche comprising SPINK1-high epithelial cells (E2) and TPM2-high cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) (C1). SPINK1 promoted tumor growth and myofibroblastic CAF programs, with EGFR and TGF-{beta} signaling implicated in tumor-CAF communication. Inferred metabolic reactions and spatial metabolite distributions supported a candidate circuit linking tumor-derived lactate to CAF oxidative metabolism and glutamine provision, followed by tumor glutamine utilization for reductive carboxylation and fatty acid synthesis. SPINK1 perturbation altered extracellular glutamine and lactate concentrations. Predicted chemokine interactions implicated C2/C3 CAFs in T cell recruitment, whereas the E2-C1 niche exhibited checkpoint and exhaustion-associated features. RHCG-positive tumor regions contained higher proportions of TOXCXCR4 cells among CD3 T cells, suggesting a possible association between ammonia handling and T cell dysfunction. In vivo, Spink1 loss attenuated tumor progression, increased cytotoxic CD8 T-cell infiltration, and enhanced tumor control during PD-1 blockade. These findings identify a spatially organized tumor-stromal niche associated with metabolic cooperation and immune restriction, supporting SPINK1 as a candidate therapeutic target in combination with immunotherapy.

cards.title: Plasma Proteogenomic Uncovers Novel Molecular Mechanisms of Soluble Endoglin and Identifies AZI2 as a new Player in Arteriovenous Malformations in Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia
cards.abstract: Endoglin is a transmembrane glycoprotein that plays a key role in vascular development, angiogenesis and endothelial homeostasis. Its soluble form (Sol-ENG), generated through proteolytic shedding of the membrane-bound protein, has been implicated in the pathophysiology of numerous cardiovascular diseases, ranging from common conditions such as preeclampsia and thrombosis to rare diseases such as hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT). Leveraging large-scale genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics data from public and original resources, we identify a molecular signature of 24 markers associated with plasma levels of Sol-ENG. This signature was enriched in genes coding for GPI-enchored proteins and included metabolites participating to glycosylation and redox homeostasis. Furthermore, we observed that ABO blood groups and genetically predicted plasma levels of 5-Azacytidine Induced 2 (AZI2) associate with the risk of arteriovenous malformations in HHT patients. This study provides new insights into the physiological mechanisms underlying Endoglin regulation and opens clinical perspectives for the management of HHT patients.

cards.title: A multimodal arrayed Perturb-seq platform for dissecting microglial state dynamics and target identification
cards.abstract: Microglia are highly dynamic immune cells of the central nervous system that can adopt diverse functional states in health and disease, making them both emerging therapeutic targets and challenging systems for target identification. Here, we developed TF-iMG, a human pluripotent stem cell-derived transcription factor-induced microglia model generated by inducible expression of SPI1 and CEBPA in Cas9-expressing stem cells. TF-iMG rapidly acquired microglia-like transcriptomic, morphological, inflammatory, and phagocytic features while remaining compatible with efficient lentiviral CRISPR knockout workflows that can be completed within one week. We next established an arrayed multimodal Perturb-seq platform that integrates lentiviral CRISPR knockout, multiplexed single-cell RNA sequencing, cytokine profiling, and live-cell imaging. Single-cell analysis showed that TF-iMG recapitulates intrinsic microglial heterogeneity and captures homeostatic, activated, inflammatory, and proliferative signatures. Stimulation with IL1B and IL4 reproducibly induced distinct pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory states, respectively, providing a framework for perturbation-based interrogation of microglial state regulation. Targeting IL1B and IL4 pathway components validated the platform by attenuating expected stimulus-driven state shifts. Profiling of putative microglial regulators and Alzheimer's disease-associated genes further revealed perturbation-specific transcriptional signatures, altered state occupancy, and multimodal phenotypes spanning cytokine release, morphology, and trajectory. Together, this platform enables scalable target identification in microglia.

cards.title: Integrative analysis identifies LATS1 as a context-specific regulator of melanoma progression and immune response
cards.abstract: Malignant melanoma incidence is increasing, and survival remains poor following metastasis. The main driver oncogenes are BRAF and NRAS. Advancements in targeted agents and immunotherapies have improved survival rates, especially for patients with BRAF mutant melanoma. However, no targeted therapy options are available for patients with NRAS-mutant melanoma. Unfortunately, the development of resistance to all existing therapies remains a challenge. Recent evidence has shown that the MST2/Hippo pathway is deregulated in melanoma. The MST2 pathway core kinase LATS1 is a signalling hub that mediates the crosstalk between cell death and proliferation networks, and its inactivation has been related to melanoma progression and resistance to targeted therapy. However, the mechanisms by which LATS1 influences melanoma biology remain unclear. Here, to investigate this role of LATS1, we developed a lats1 knockout zebrafish melanoma model driven by either BRAF or NRAS mutations. Loss of Lats1 associates with reduced tumour-free survival in BRAF-mutant melanoma and a more invasive phenotype in NRAS-mutant melanoma, confirming a tumour-suppressive function. Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics datasets, we mapped molecular mechanisms mediated by Lats1 in tumours driven by these oncogenes, including pathways associated with the immune response regulated by Lats1. Subsequent validation in patient data confirmed an immune-evasive phenotype, associated with decreased LATS1 expression in BRAF-mutant melanoma. Additionally, the loss of LATS1 in NRAS mutant melanoma patients altered the expression of key DNA damage repair genes. Thus, this study identifies novel pathways controlled by LATS1 in melanoma, which aid in our understanding of the disease and offers new insights to be explored for the development of novel treatment strategies.

cards.title: Cortical surface area is an independent predictor of incident dementia
cards.abstract: Cortical surface area (cSA) is associated with intelligence and cognition, yet structural MRI studies of neurodegeneration in Alzheimers disease and related dementias (ADRD) have emphasized quantification of cortical thickness (cTH) and volume, with very limited evaluation of cSA. We examined whether cSA of AD-relevant brain regions provide diagnostic, prognostic, and biological information beyond cTH and volume across 5,430 participants (3,124 cognitively unimpaired; 1,634 mild cognitive impairment [MCI]; 672 ADRD) from three aging and dementia cohorts: the National Alzheimers Coordinating Center, Alzheimers Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, and Carotids and Minds study. In cross-sectional analyses, cSA and cTH showed weak correlation, and lower cSA was independently associated with greater odds of MCI and ADRD after adjustment for cTH and covariates. Participants with both low cSA and low cTH had greater risk of MCI and ADRD compared to low cSA, cTH, or volume alone. In longitudinal models, baseline cSA predicted incident ADRD independent from cTH, and combined cSA/cTH models outperformed cSA, cTH, or volume alone for predicting incident ADRD over a mean follow-up of 4.3 years. Complementing these findings, proteomics analyses revealed distinct signatures associated with cSA compared to cTH. Overall, these findings support cSA as a clinically informative and biologically distinct dimension of AD-related cortical vulnerability.

cards.title: Epigenomic circuits shaping cellular heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma
cards.abstract: Pleural mesothelioma (PM) is an aggressive and lethal malignancy with current treatments offering limited clinical benefit. In this study, we utilized single-cell chromatin accessibility and transcriptomic profiling of patient-matched samples to infer the epigenomic regulation underlying cellular heterogeneity in PM. High-resolution epigenomic profiling suggested transcriptional regulators with putative pro-tumoral roles in mesothelioma, whose function was experimentally tested using genetic perturbations across four PM cell lines. Furthermore, we observed several putative associations between epigenomic circuits and macrophage ontogeny, a sarcomatoid-like neoplastic state, and a fetal-like endothelial cell state. Our analysis also showed similarities between the chromatin accessibility landscapes of exhausted CD8 T and KLRC1 natural killer cells and identified NR4A2 as a potential shared regulator of dysfunction in both lymphocyte subsets. We further identified a state-specific distal enhancer near NR4A2 and experimentally validated its regulation of NR4A2 expression in Jurkat cells. Together, we provide an epigenomic map of PM and nominate candidate transcription factors and regulatory elements for future functional investigation, including their potential relevance to epigenetic editing strategies to limit tumor growth and enhance anti-tumor immunity.

cards.title: Human Plasma Proteomics Links Modifiable Lifestyle Exposome to Disease Risk
cards.abstract: Lifestyle exposures influence disease risk, yet the molecular signatures linking modifiable behaviors to human biology remain incompletely characterized. Here we show that the plasma proteome carries a measurable record of modifiable lifestyle exposures. We developed the Human Exposomic Architecture of the Proteome (HEAP), a framework linking lifestyle exposures, plasma proteins, and disease risk at population scale. Applying HEAP to more than 50,000 UK Biobank participants, 2,686 plasma proteins, and 169 lifestyle exposures, we identified exposure-associated protein signatures that organized along shared health-behavior patterns and connected lifestyle variation to disease-relevant biology. Integrating disease associations, mediation analyses, Mendelian randomization, and colocalization showed that only a minority of exposure-responsive proteins were consistent with causal intermediates, whereas many appeared to function as biological reporters of exposure burden, disease liability, and early disease processes. Comparisons with exercise-training and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist studies linked observational lifestyle signatures to intervention-induced proteomic changes, suggesting that part of the exposomic signal reflects biology modifiable by intervention. Furthermore, proteome-based exposure scores captured exposure-associated biology, tracked behavioral change over time, and predicted disease risk. Overall, HEAP provides a resource for advancing disease prevention and precision medicine by linking modifiable lifestyle exposures to disease-relevant protein signatures.

cards.title: SPOUT: An open-source hardware and software platform to study decision making while manipulating and recording from neural activity
cards.abstract: Recording and manipulating brain activity during behavior is critical to understanding the underlying mechanisms of decision-making. Linking neural activity to behavior requires behavioral hardware and software tightly integrated with recording and perturbation systems on a shared clock. We built SPOUT (State-machine Platform for Operant Uni/dual-spout Tasks), an open-source, Teensy-driven state-machine platform with a MATLAB interface that runs 10 unique decision-making tasks (with dozens of variations available through user-friendly settings) to study behavior in head-restrained mice. The platform is built on several custom hardware devices: a dual-lick detector, headplate designs for optogenetics and two-photon calcium imaging, a three-axis motorized spout manipulator, and an optogenetics power modulator. The firmware differentiates between one and two lick spout tasks and can be controlled by a user-friendly interface. Task settings can be selected through the interface or by loading predefined settings files. We validated the clock speed and lick detection against an independent, external acquisition system and identified highly precise, sub-millisecond detection of single licks. Using a pseudo-random synchronization pulse generated by SPOUT, we corrected for missing data due to glitches in the acquisition system and clock drift. We showcase the versatility of SPOUT by training mice on an uninstructed lick-left/lick-right task in which the rewarded side switches unexpectedly and found that mice use history-dependent action-outcome associations to guide future behavior. Transiently inhibiting the anterior lateral motor cortex (ALM) during cue presentation induced contralateral deficits, without affecting ipsilateral trials. Finally, two-photon imaging of ALM neurons revealed stronger population responses during contralateral choice licks compared to ipsilateral ones. Together, SPOUT offers an open-source, affordable platform to study decision-making in head-restrained mice while combining neural recordings and manipulations.

cards.title: Insulin resistance reverses despite weight gain with pan-PPAR agonism, revealing its plasma molecular correlates in type 2 diabetes
cards.abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) and body weight are closely linked in type 2 diabetes (T2D), so their molecular correlates are hard to separate in observational data. Pan-PPAR agonism offers a test, because it improves insulin sensitivity while body weight increases. In the ChiHOPE cohort of 835 T2D patients from two randomized phase 3 trials of chiglitazar, 53% of chiglitazar-treated patients with HOMA-IR-defined IR at baseline no longer met the IR threshold after treatment, compared with 29% with placebo and 32% with sitagliptin, while BMI rose. We integrated plasma metabolomics and proteomics into a molecular estimate of HOMA-IR. It outperformed routine clinical measures, disagreed with HOMA-IR classification in 27% of patients, and identified adverse lipid, liver and inflammatory profiles within each HOMA-IR class. With chiglitazar, the molecular estimate fell despite weight gain, with lower proteoglycan 4 and higher glutamine and glycine. Circulating markers of IR can therefore improve without weight loss.

cards.title: scDisentangle: sequential disentanglement for single-cell perturbation response prediction
cards.abstract: Predicting the transcriptional response of single cells to perturbation is a central goal of single-cell modeling, with broad application to analysis and experimental design. Existing methods often fail to beat simple baselines and offer little insight into how biological variation is organized. We present scDisentangle, a model that decomposes single-cell expression into observed attributes and a sequence of residual components, generating counterfactuals that preserve source cell identity. scDisentangle outperformed current models and naive baselines on cytokine stimulation, liver infection, and unseen combinatorial genetic perturbations, on which accuracy was largely independent of how closely a response resembled the average perturbation effect. In an immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis cohort, cell-resolved counterfactuals predicted donor-specific intracardiac CD8+ T cell states from peripheral blood. In a castration-regeneration prostate atlas, predictions recapitulated luminal dynamics and progenitor-marker kinetics upon androgen add-back. scDisentangle's coarse-to-fine latent structure aligned with hematopoietic lineage organization, with early levels capturing a less differentiated core progressively refined into cell-type-specific programs.

cards.title: Plate design confounds donor variation and model evaluation in single-cell perturbation screens
cards.abstract: Single-cell screens of immune cells from many donors are used to study why individuals respond differently and to benchmark response models. Each donor-perturbation combination typically occupies one well, controls are grouped, and donors share one layout, so technical effects can look biological. Using a 90-cytokine screen, two compound screens, four cohorts and simulations, we show that well effects explain most replicate-control variation in abundant cell types, controls carry a shared offset, and identical control wells differ by hundreds of differentially expressed genes at a standard threshold, about as many as two receptor-negative proteins do. Negative controls, design-aware estimators and perturbation-specific evaluation change the interpretation of four recent analyses. A deep-learning model that scores below a perturbation-agnostic predictor under standard evaluation outperforms a simple baseline on perturbation-specific differences in two of three cell types (significantly in one with stricter controls), but predicts less well the component shared with inert wells.
