cards.title: Perturbation-induced gene programs map the hidden regulatory architecture of complex diseases
cards.abstract: Steady-state molecular profiles incompletely capture the regulatory programs through which genetic variation influences complex disease, particularly programs that emerge only when cells are perturbed. Here, we introduce Perturbscape, a computational framework that learns multiscale gene programs for individual perturbations in a CRISPR Perturb-seq screen using linear and nonlinear contrastive approaches alongside complementary program-learning methods, and integrates them with human genetics to prioritize disease-relevant genes, perturbations and downstream regulatory pathways. Across 15,859 perturbation-by-context profiles from 7 Perturb-seq systems and 53 complex diseases and traits (mean GWAS N=291K), perturbation-induced programs showed up to 4.3-fold higher heritability informativeness than analogous steady-state multi-tissue gene prioritization, and retained significant conditional heritability informativeness across all 34 matched cell system-trait comparisons after accounting for steady-state prioritization. Preserving perturbation-specific programs further yielded 2.5-5.3-fold higher trait relevance scores than programs derived from control cells, pooled perturbations or differential-expression summaries. In K562, Perturbscape-prioritized genes showed stronger enrichment for rare-variant burden genes than steady-state prioritization and were supported by orthogonal enhancer CRISPRi screens. In HepG2, LDL cholesterol-associated perturbation-induced programs specifically revealed statin-responsive pathways not significantly enriched by steady-state PoPS prioritization, supported by pharmacological transcriptional responses and population plasma proteomics. Perturbscape also recovered blood-related trait-conditioned trans-regulatory relationships that were specifically supported by population trans-eQTLs in IFN-gamma-stimulated monocytes (OR = 1.30, P=1.6e-05). Perturbscape further revealed developmental-stage-specific convergence between monogenic diabetes regulators and polygenic T2D risk during pancreatic islet differentiation, and neuronal-subclass-specific autism-associated regulatory programs in vivo. Together, these findings establish perturbation-induced gene programs as a complementary layer of disease-relevant regulatory information, revealing genetically informative pathways and context-specific regulatory relationships incompletely represented by steady-state molecular atlases.

cards.title: Unravelling the mechanisms of clozapine-induced neutropenia in treatment-resistant schizophrenia using cellular genomics
cards.abstract: Background: About one-third of individuals with schizophrenia do not respond to first-line antipsychotics. Clozapine has superior efficacy for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), yet remains underutilised partly due to a 1% risk of potentially fatal clozapine-induced neutropenia (CIN). However, the biological mechanisms underlying CIN remain poorly understood. Methods: We recruited six individuals with TRS who had previously received clozapine: three who ceased clozapine following CIN and three who stopped for reasons unrelated to CIN. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were collected and cultured in vitro under three conditions: untreated, clozapine alone, or clozapine with its two major metabolites. Single nucleus RNA sequencing was performed to profile the cellular transcriptomic landscape following exposure to clozapine and its metabolites. Results: After quality control, 59,313 cells spanning 26 distinct clusters were retained. Multiple cell type-specific genes were differentially expressed in TRS with CIN, or in response to clozapine exposure in TRS donors with CIN (but not in those without CIN), after adjusting for age, sex and smoking status. We also identified a CIN-associated co-expression module in naive CD4 T cells that was driven by the transcription factor SREBF1, and robust evidence for differential cell-cell communication involving seven intercellular ligand-receptor pairs. There was limited evidence that clozapine-related metabolites contributed to these transcriptional changes. Conclusions: Our findings provide novel insights into cell type-specific transcriptional changes associated with CIN status and/or clozapine exposure in TRS with CIN. With replication in larger, independent cohorts, this work may contribute to the future development of predictive biomarkers for CIN and safer therapeutic strategies for TRS.

cards.title: Performance of a foundation model to generate thousands of predicted outcomes across multiple use cases
cards.abstract: Background. Predictive artificial intelligence (AI) models hold great promise for medical care. While many types of models have proliferated across healthcare and the life sciences, systematic, rapid generation of multi-condition predictions of diagnoses, future medical events and future clinical outcomes from a single foundation-model architecture remains rare. PhenOM(R) is a generative AI foundation model trained and validated on longitudinal medical-event data from more than 400 million patient records in the OM1 Real World Data Cloud (RWDC) and designed to complete predictive tasks for a broad array of medical diagnoses, events and clinical outcomes (collectively outcomes) at varying time intervals, currently up to five (5) years. This paper describes the implementation of PhenOM to complete a vast number of predictive tasks across clinical domains and outcomes. Methods. PhenOM was evaluated across four outcome categories (Future Risk, Screening, Care Opportunity, and Treatment Effect) in multiple domains spanning chronic disease, acute medical events, healthcare utilization, and rare and frequently undiagnosed conditions. Performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Outcomes were defined within an eligible-population framework using standardized medical code sets (ICD-10, SNOMED, CPT, NDC, LOINC) unless outcomes could not be specified with an existing code. All benchmarks reported were derived from data excluded from training. Results. As of this publication, the single PhenOM model has been used to complete and validate thousands of predictive tasks covering more than 1,770 outcomes spanning most organ systems and clinical specialties, with new predictive tasks being validated each day. Overall, 80 percent of predictive tasks achieved AUROC of at least 0.70 and 30 percent achieved AUROC of at least 0.80. We present a sample of 177 of these tasks as examples that show the breadth of tasks the model can complete. Performance varied systematically by outcome and clinical domain. Conclusions. PhenOM demonstrates the ability to complete thousands of predictive tasks across clinical domains and outcomes at the individual patient level, without additional training. Outcomes include screening for undiagnosed conditions, predicting future conditions, medical events, effects of treatments, and assessing care opportunities. These can be ascertained at the individual patient and population levels. These findings support applications in individual and population health management, risk management, drug development, and real-world evidence generation, and establish a transparent, reproducible performance reference for a large-scale real-world predictive AI platform.

cards.title: Plasma proteomic markers of cognitive and brain aging in a multi-ethnic cohort
cards.abstract: Advances in ultrasensitive proteomics offer opportunities to characterize molecular pathways underlying brain aging. We measured 220 plasma proteins using NULISAseq Neuro220 in 250 Chinese, South Asian, and non-Hispanic White older adults (mean age=68.2 years; 70.4% female). Proteins implicated in neurodegenerative diseases (including brain-derived phosphorylated Tau; BDpTau), synaptic function, oxidative stress, and inflammation were associated with poorer cognition. Phosphorylated Tau205 was associated with reduced entorhinal thickness, whereas inflammatory proteins were associated with imaging markers of cerebral small vessel disease. Several findings were replicated in 1,381 participants in the Alzheimers Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, including associations of BDpTau species, NPTX2, BACE1, TREM1, CCL17, PRDX6, and IGF1R with cognitive decline and clinical progression. Cardiometabolic risk factors were associated with widespread proteomic alterations, many of which were also linked to poorer brain health. These results identify promising molecular markers of brain aging and extend proteomic research to ethnically diverse populations historically underrepresented in Alzheimers disease research.

cards.title: Primary sclerosing cholangitis: epidemiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnosis, and management.
cards.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare cholangiopathy characterized by multifocal inflammation and fibrostenotic remodeling of the bile ducts, cholestasis, and increased risks of cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal cancer. No pharmacological therapy has yet improved transplant-free survival. Clinical care therefore depends on accurate phenotyping, surveillance, treatment of biliary and intestinal complications, and timely liver transplantation. Population-based and clinical studies define the epidemiology, risk factors, presentation, diagnosis, and management of PSC. Studies of human biospecimens, including microbiome and metabolomic analyses, describe biological changes associated with the disease, whereas organoid and animal models are used to investigate potential mechanisms. The available evidence links genetic susceptibility and PSC-associated inflammatory bowel disease to cholangiocyte injury, immune activation, disturbed bile acid homeostasis, and microbial alterations. At the bile duct interface, cholangiocyte senescence and barrier dysfunction may interact with microbial exposure and immune-cell recruitment to promote periductal fibrosis. PSC is therefore more plausibly viewed as a multicellular process than as the consequence of a single microbial, immune, or bile acid pathway. Whether dysbiosis and altered bile acid profiles contribute to disease development or instead reflect established PSC remains unresolved. Concomitant inflammatory bowel disease, medication use, biliary obstruction, and previous biliary interventions further complicate causal inference. Longitudinal human studies may distinguish early drivers from secondary changes. Mechanistic findings should ultimately improve patient phenotyping, surveillance, endoscopic management, and selection for targeted trials. Such trials will require biologically informed designs and endpoints that capture durable clinical benefit.

cards.title: Evaluation of Semaphorin 3G (SEMA3G) as a biofluid biomarker of cerebral amyloid angiopathy: evidence from neurodegenerative disease and memory clinic cohorts
cards.abstract: Introduction: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) is characterised by amyloid-beta (A{beta}) deposition in cerebral vessels, and frequently co-occurs with Alzheimer's disease (AD). Diagnosis based on MRI-based Boston criteria is not definitive, and CAA biofluid biomarkers are needed. Semaphorin 3G (SEMA3G) was recently shown to be selectively enriched in CAA-affected vessels, and correlated with CAA severity. We therefore evaluated SEMA3G as a biofluid biomarker of CAA. Methods: SEMA3G profiles were examined across diagnoses in the Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium dataset (GNPC) in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) (N=1982) and plasma (N=6917). SEMA3G was then evaluated in the Healthy Brain Ageing (HBA) memory clinic cohort (N=161) with 3T MRI, where lobar cerebral microbleed burden was used as a proxy for CAA likelihood, with participants grouped by microbleed count (0, 1-2, or [≥]3). Results: CSF and plasma SEMA3G were significantly lower in AD and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) compared to cognitively unimpaired controls in GNPC, and were associated with hypertension. Longitudinally, plasma SEMA3G declined significantly over time in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD. In the HBA cohort, plasma SEMA3G did not differ by cerebral microbleed burden on MRI, nor correlate with plasma A{beta} isoforms and white matter hyperintensities. Discussion: Although CSF and plasma SEMA3G levels were significantly lower in AD and FTD, plasma SEMA3G was not associated with CAA-associated MRI features in individuals at risk of AD. While these findings do not support plasma SEMA3G for identifying individuals with higher CAA-associated burden, its potential utility warrants further evaluation in genetically susceptible or neuropathologically confirmed CAA cohorts.

cards.title: Virtual spatial transcriptomics links kidney histopathology to disease-associated molecular programs
cards.abstract: Introduction: Spatial transcriptomics can resolve compartment-specific molecular programs in kidney disease, but its cost and technical requirements limit its use in clinical diagnostics and in large biopsy archives. Predicting spatial gene expression from routine histology with artificial intelligence could extend molecular characterization to existing clinically annotated kidney tissue collections. Methods: We adapted DeepSpot-M, a pretrained multimodal foundation model that predicts spatial gene expression from histology, using paired hematoxylin and eosin images and Visium spatial transcriptomics from 209 Kidney Precision Medicine Project (KPMP) participants. We evaluated virtual profiles in held-out human biopsies, associated them with histopathologic and biochemical injury markers in 567 rats with defined nephrotoxin exposures from a public toxicogenomics database, and generated a virtual atlas from 1,534 histology slides of 476 additional KPMP participants. Results: Kidney-specific adaptation of DeepSpot-M doubled the mean Pearson correlation of each model's 1,000 best-predicted genes (0.43 versus 0.22) and exceeded recent foundation models. Virtual profiles preserved the direction of all 13 disease-marker differences in measured expression, including tubular injury, maladaptive repair, gluconeogenesis, and fibrosis-associated programs. All 11 measured associations between molecular programs and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were also preserved. Without rat-specific training, a virtual injury score distinguished moderate or severe histopathologic lesions (area under the curve, 0.85) and at least twofold blood urea nitrogen elevation (0.82). In our atlas of 5.46 million virtual spots, higher proximal tubule program scores were associated with higher eGFR (partial r, 0.32) and less interstitial fibrosis (-0.57), and program-pathology associations agreed with those of measured Visium profiles in independent participants (Spearman rho, 0.64). Conclusions: Kidney-adapted virtual spatial transcriptomics links histology-derived molecular programs to experimental renal injury and human clinical and histologic phenotypes. Our approach enables spatial molecular analyses in routine biopsy histology, which could help decipher disease-associated pathways in existing biopsy archives.

cards.title: Time-Resolved Proteomics of a Polyglutamine-Expanded Huntingtin in vitro Cell Model Reveals Early RNA-Regulatory Compensation and Late Respiratory-Chain Remodeling
cards.abstract: Huntington disease (HD) is caused by a polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin protein that exerts progressive cellular toxicity. However, the temporal order of pathogenic events, and in particular which changes arise early and which emerge late, remains incompletely defined, despite their distinct therapeutic implications. To examine this trajectory, we profiled the proteome of a huntingtin-expressing cell model at early (72 h) and late (144 h) stages. Rather than a linear progression, the proteome changed in two distinct stages. At the early stage, cells showed increased abundance of RNA-processing, splicing, and protein-synthesis proteins, which may reflect an adaptive response to preserve gene-expression fidelity under stress. By the late stage, many of these proteins were depleted and mitochondrial energy-metabolism proteins dominated the response. Notably, 85% of proteins altered at both time points reversed direction between stages (95% at a false-discovery rate below 5%), and all reversals were supported by a significant genotype-by-time interaction, indicating that mutant huntingtin reorganizes the proteome rather than amplifying a fixed set of perturbations. Subunit-level analysis of the respiratory chain showed that Complex IV and ATP synthase subunits were reduced at 72 h, whereas at 144 h subunits of all five complexes were broadly increased, most strongly in Complex I and III, with a few distal subunits (COX5B, ATP5F1A, ATP5F1B) remaining reduced. Leveraging this proteomic map, we applied an AI-assisted, direction-aware drug repurposing strategy. Of 1,712 differentially abundant proteins, 498 were druggable, 109 had at least one agent whose mechanism was concordant with the required correction, and 89 of these 109 proteins mapped to at least one agent listed as approved in the source databases (56 to an agent with current regulatory approval). These included the approved Complex I inhibitor metformin, the investigational Complex I inhibitor ME-344, and pathway-level mitochondria-directed agents (elamipretide/SS-31, approved only for Barth syndrome; MitoQ, a dietary supplement), several of which have previously been evaluated in HD models. Collectively, these findings describe a two-stage proteomic response to mutant huntingtin in this cell model and suggest a putative early window for preclinical intervention testing, before late respiratory-chain remodeling is established.

cards.title: Benchmarking foundation models for resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging time series in cognitive aging research
cards.abstract: Foundation models trained on large neuroimaging datasets could help smaller studies investigate cognition from brain recordings. However, whether the foundation model-derived representations improve assessment of current cognition, prediction of follow-up cognition, or characterization of cognitive change remains unclear. We evaluated nine configurations from five model families that process regional resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging time series, using 3,103 scans from 1,653 participants across two observational and five intervention aging cohorts. Primary frozen representations showed no consistent superiority over conventional functional connectivity for concurrent cognitive associations or diagnostic classification. Changing the readout improved selected concurrent cognitive associations without updating model weights, indicating that performance depended partly on how representations were extracted. Additional post-training and embedding alignment yielded gains in selected settings but did not consistently improve performance across outcomes. In the primary longitudinal analyses, imaging representations did not establish added value beyond baseline clinical measures. These findings show that readout choice influences concurrent cognitive associations, while the added value of these representations for longitudinal outcomes remains unestablished.

cards.title: Micro-fragmented adipose tissue reprogrammes the systemic molecular landscape of inflammatory knee osteoarthritis
cards.abstract: Knee osteoarthritis affects an estimated 374 million people and has no approved disease-modifying treatment. In our double-blind randomised trial (ISRCTN88966184), intra-articular micro-fragmented adipose tissue (MFAT) outperformed hyaluronic acid (HA) on pain, function and cartilage composition, but clinical endpoints alone cannot say whether the disease changed or only the symptoms. Here we answer that question from the blood. Using an interpretable AI data-fusion framework based on non-negative matrix tri-factorisation, we integrated longitudinal plasma proteomics, N-glycomics and miRNA transcriptomics with patient genetics and prior molecular networks at baseline, one and six months, resolving 93 gene and 30 miRNA pathways, almost all significantly enriched in Gene Ontology Biological Process and Reactome annotations. By six months the two injections had left sharply distinct molecular fingerprints. HA remained dominated by canonical OA pathogenesis, including the cartilage-degrading effectors MMP13 and LIMK2 and persistent markers of synovial inflammation. MFAT instead shifted the systemic landscape towards chondroprotection, anti-inflammatory signalling and bone-cartilage homeostasis, prioritising effectors including SIRT7 and NDUFC1. These are, to our knowledge, the first in vivo human data to explain why a regenerative therapy outperforms viscosupplementation in knee osteoarthritis, and they place MFAT on the disease-modifying rather than the symptomatic side of that divide.

cards.title: JUMP Cell Painting chemical dataset: Morphological map of 115,796 compounds in human cells
cards.abstract: Image-based profiling decodes complex cellular states for high-impact biological and therapeutic applications, yet a large, public reference dataset of chemical perturbations has been lacking. We present Cell Painting images and 1.53 billion single-cell profiles for 115,796 compounds in human osteosarcoma cells, generated by the Joint Undertaking for Morphological Profiling (JUMP)-Cell Painting Consortium of 18 industry and non-profit partners. Despite technical variability across 12 data-generating laboratories, more than 15% of compounds show statistically significant phenotypic activity, reproducibility drops only 34% versus single-laboratory data, and compounds sharing biological targets often show similar image-based profiles. JUMP establishes a validated public reference resource that brings image-based profiling on par with genomics and transcriptomics. The dataset, shared alongside previously released genetic perturbation data in the Cell Painting Gallery, is a powerful predictive engine for the impact, mechanism, targets and activities of compounds, fundamentally accelerating chemical and cell biology and early-stage drug development.

cards.title: Informed, scalable and unified transport couplings for single-cell alignment and downstream inference with scBIOT
cards.abstract: Single-cell genomics requires methods that account for technical variation while preserving biological signals, remain tractable at atlas scale and support analyses beyond visualization, but existing approaches discard the fitted correspondence that could connect these tasks. Here we introduce scBIOT, a biologically informed optimal-transport framework that formulates single-cell alignment as an explicit and inspectable coupling between cells. scBIOT incorporates prior biological knowledge to preserve known cell identities, compresses transport through prototypes for large datasets and quantifies gene-level changes induced by alignment using coupling-derived transport scores. Across transcriptomic and spatial mapping benchmarks, scBIOT balanced biological conservation, batch correction and label-transfer accuracy while distinguishing batch-associated stress responses from biological immune and drug-response programs. Prototype transport scaled coupling-based analysis to approximately 100 million perturbed cells. Because the coupling encodes probabilistic correspondences rather than only corrected coordinates, the same fitted coupling supports state mapping, trajectory inference, perturbation analysis, multimodal comparison and spatiotemporal localization. Applications to cancer, hematopoiesis and embryonic development identified condition-specific cell states, modality-dependent regulatory programs and spatially resolved developmental transitions. Informed, scalable and unified transport couplings therefore link atlas alignment to downstream biological inference within a single framework.

cards.title: Multi-omics causal deep learning reveals regulatory structure while interventions refine perturbation predictions
cards.abstract: Inferring gene regulation from single-cell data is difficult because observational measurements cannot distinguish correlation from causation and access to perturbational data, especially with multiple modalities, remains limited. Here we present the Cross-Modal Causal Variational Autoencoder (CMC-VAE), which learns a network linking genes and proteins (gene-gene, protein-protein and gene-protein) in the latent space and maps each connection back onto measured features. Trained on 809,130 observational CITE-seq profiles, CMC-VAE recovers co-expression, transcription factor regulons and immune signalling programs, and learns a sparse cross-modal map enriched for transcript-protein cognate pairs. On three CRISPR screens used during development, it ranks knockout-responsive genes better than correlation and latent-VAE baselines. Fitted to a screen's unperturbed control cells, without perturbation labels, the model translates measured knockout RNA responses into protein responses better than a correlation map and cognate transcripts. The direction of gene-to-gene regulation, however, is not recovered from observational data. On the CITE-seq screens, fine-tuning only the latent network improves held-out response correlation, mainly by learning a response shared across knockouts. On larger Perturb-seq screens, with about 1,000 training perturbations, fine-tuning the latent network learns gene-specific effects that transfer to held-out genes, more so than a gene-level causal model fine-tuned on the same cells, and in simulation, such interventions also restore edge orientations that observational training leaves unresolved.

cards.title: Metabolic priming recruits tumour cells across a mitochondrial vulnerability threshold and sensitizes them to chemotherapy
cards.abstract: Intratumour heterogeneity allows a fraction of cancer cells to escape otherwise effective treatment. Here we ask whether metabolic priming can recruit heterogeneous tumour cells into a transient mitochondrial state that is selectively vulnerable to photodynamic damage. Tetramethylrhodamine methyl ester (TMRM) has previously been shown to act as a mitochondria targeted photosensitizer; we exploit its voltage-dependent accumulation and dynamic fluorescence during pulsed illumination to quantify vulnerability in single cells. The response is a reproducible fluorescence excursion, a rise to a maximum followed by a decay, accompanied by reactive oxygen species production. Comparing seventeen descriptors of this excursion against subsequent fate in 195 cells across four arms shows that quantities referenced to each cell's own resting value outperform static intensity. The simple difference Fmax F0 predicts death with held-out areas under the curve of approximately 0.75 to 0.79, whereas resting intensity alone carries little transferable information and time to peak does not discriminate fate in the datasets tested. Metabolic priming with the PKM2 activator TEPP46 or with ethyl pyruvate increases the fraction of responding cells; under TEPP46 almost the whole population enters the responding state. PKM2 abundance is associated with faster entry into that state, and PKM2 is heterogeneous in human skin tumour sections. Four hours of camptothecin shifts the response distribution, increasing the fraction of cells above the untreated median from 50% to 76%, identifying a candidate intervention window. In combination experiments, TMRM photodynamic treatment produced survival below the Bliss-independence expectation with camptothecin or TRAIL, in both treatment orders and across three cell lines; these combination measurements are descriptive and require independent replication. The study therefore identifies a perturbation-revealed mitochondrial vulnerability that can be pharmacologically recruited and followed dynamically at single-cell resolution. It is a proof of concept in cultured cells and human tumour sections and has not been tested in vivo.

cards.title: MASH-in-a-dish reveals fatty acid-driven itaconate crosstalk between Kupffer cells and hepatocytes
cards.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is driven by interactions between metabolically stressed hepatocytes and non-parenchymal liver cells, leading to hepatocyte injury, inflammation, and fibrosis. Metabolites can mediate intercellular communication, yet their contribution to MASH pathogenesis remains poorly understood, partly because tissue dissociation disrupts the local metabolic environment. To address this challenge, we developed a novel in vitro MASH model, "MASH-in-a-dish", a Transwell co-culture system of mouse hepatocyte-derived organoids (HepOrgs), Kupffer cells (KCs), and hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) in a serum-free, chemically defined liver co-culture medium. MASH-in-a-dish modelled key features of clinical MASH, including steatosis, hepatocyte ballooning, inflammation and fibrosis, and allowed for rapid cell separation and cell type-specific metabolomics and stable-isotope fluxomics analysis. Using MASH-in-a-dish, we identified 21 MASH-associated interactive metabolites originating from 6 metabolic pathways, including the tricarboxylic acid cycle and the urea cycle. As a proof of concept, we further characterized itaconate-mediated intercellular crosstalk. Under MASH conditions, fatty acids replaced glucose to drive carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CTP1A)-dependent itaconate production in KCs. Itaconate exacerbated oxidative stress, steatosis, and hepatocyte injury in lipid-stressed HepOrgs. Inhibiting itaconate production by KC-specific Acod1 knockout in the MASH-in-a-dish system mitigated hepatocyte damage. These findings identify fatty acid-driven itaconate production as a mechanism for lipid stress-induced immunometabolic crosstalk, linking adipose tissue insulin resistance to hepatocyte injury in MASH. In conclusion, our results establish MASH-in-a-dish as a powerful and versatile in vitro platform to investigating cell-cell interactions and metabolite crosstalk in MASH pathogenesis, and identify fatty acid-driven itaconate crosstalk between Kupffer cells and hepatocytes as a novel pathogenic mechanism and a potential therapeutic target in MASH.

cards.title: Spatial single cell multi-omics identifies divergent melanoma-cell states associated with metastatic outcomes in thin primary melanomas
cards.abstract: Thin melanomas (Breslow thickness [≤]1 mm) generally have favorable outcomes, yet some metastasise, highlighting the need for biomarkers of progression. Here, we combined same-section single-cell spatial transcriptomics and proteomics to identify seven melanoma-cell states organized along two inferred trajectories sharing a common trunk, extending from an in situ epithelial-adjacent state through developmental stress to melanocytic differentiation before diverging into two lineages. Lineage 1 progressed through an IFN-associated stress intermediate state towards mesenchymal-invasive cells enriched in metastasizing tumors and associated with immune-hot neighborhoods, extracellular-matrix remodeling and angiogenesis, potentially supporting vascular mimicry and metastatic dissemination. Lineage 2 terminated in cohesive nevus-like cells retaining melanocytic features within relatively immune-cold neighborhoods and enriched in non-metastasizing tumors. We confirmed these associations using H&E-inferred spatial transcriptomics in an international multicentric cohort and independent bulk transcriptomic datasets in primary melanomas, linking spatially organized melanoma-cell programs to metastatic outcome and identifying potential biomarkers of progression in thin melanoma.

cards.title: Adversarial Robustness of Capsule Networks for Medical Image Classification
cards.abstract: PurposeDeep learning models are increasingly being used in medical diagnostics, but their vulnerability to adversarial perturbations raises concerns about their reliability in clinical applications. Capsule networks (CapsNets) are a promising architecture for medical imaging tasks, given their ability to model spatial relationships and train with smaller amounts of data. Although previous studies have focused on adversarial training approaches to improve robustness, exploring alternative architectures is an underexplored direction for combating poor adversarial stability. Prior work has suggested that CapsNets may exhibit improved robustness to adversarial perturbations compared to convolutional neural networks (CNNs), but performance on adversarial images has not been studied systematically in clinical environments. We evaluated the robustness of CapsNets compared to CNNs and vision transformers (ViTs) across multiple medical image classification tasks. MethodsWe trained two CNNs (ResNet-18 and ResNet-50), one ViT (MedViT), and two CapsNets (DR-CapsNet and BP-CapsNet) on four distinct medical imaging datasets (PneumoniaMNIST, BreastMNIST, NoduleMNIST3D, and BloodMNIST) and one natural image dataset (MNIST). Models were evaluated on adversarial examples generated by projected gradient descent, fast gradient sign method, AutoAttack, Carlini & Wagner, and black-box transfer attacks. Models also underwent PGD adversarial fine-tuning to assess whether architectural differences persisted after adversarial training. Interpretability experiments, including latent space and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analyses, were conducted to better understand model stability on adversarial inputs. ResultsUnder conventional training, CapsNets demonstrated superior robustness under adversarial perturbations compared to CNNs and ViTs across all medical imaging datasets and the natural image dataset. Latent space and Grad-CAM visualizations revealed that CapsNets maintained more consistent feature representations and attention maps after adversarial perturbations compared to CNNs and ViTs, suggesting that advantages in CapsNet robustness are supported, at least in part, by more stable feature encodings. PGD adversarial fine-tuning improved robustness across models, with MedViT exhibiting the largest gains and thereby narrowing the performance gap. ConclusionCapsNets exhibit advantages in adversarial robustness over CNN- and ViT-based models on medical imaging tasks. These findings suggest that capsule-based architectures may be a promising direction for robust medical image classification. Future work should validate CapsNet robustness across more complex medical imaging tasks, independent external datasets, and broader sources of real-world imaging variability.

cards.title: A comprehensive temporal proteome and phosphoproteome dataset of Y1 adrenocortical cells under FGF2 stimulation and SOS inhibition
cards.abstract: The Y1 mouse adrenocortical tumor cell line is a classic model for cancer studies and ACTH mediated steroidogenesis. The KRAS gene amplification and SOS mediated activation sustain elevated ERK levels, which drive the tumor phenotype of this cell line. In addition, the mitogen FGF2 induces atypical cytotoxic stress and consequent cell death rather than proliferation in this system, imposing a strong perturbation on KRAS ERK signaling dynamics. Recent research from our group revealed that SOS is not solely responsible for KRAS activation in the Y1 cells, indicating a more complex regulatory landscape of GEFs and GAPs. This motivated the generation of a comprehensive time resolved proteome (DIA) and TMT phosphoproteome (DDA) in a 0 to 30 minute time course under FGF2 stimulation or combined with SOS inhibitor, with the presence or absence of FBS stimulation, in technical triplicate using Q Exactive and Thermo Lumos mass spectrometers, respectively. This dataset can enable latent mechanisms between the life and death switch caused by FGF2 signaling and the alternate stress response caused by impaired SOS dependent activation. This analysis yielded 14,512 phosphosites and 8,919 protein groups, where 10,471 phosphosites and 111 protein groups showed differential abundance with statistical significance (limma, FDR < 0.05). This dataset provides a versatile resource for downstream applications, which includes dynamic modeling such as ordinary differential equation based frameworks, for which temporal datasets remain scarce. The data contained in this preprint will be available on jPOST Repository after the publication.

cards.title: CellVocal Attributes Transcriptional Dynamics to Spatial Signalling
cards.abstract: Understanding how local signalling shapes cell-state transitions requires linking spatial context to transcriptional dynamics. Here we present CellVocal, a framework that integrates spatial RNA velocity with cell-cell communication to decompose cell-state transitions into intrinsic and communication-associated components and further attribute their contributions to signalling modules and neighbouring sender cells. CellVocal recovered complex trajectories and communication perturbations in simulations and reconstructed coherent dynamics and spatially restricted ligand-receptor programmes across the mouse brain, gut and lung. Further analyses linked inferred NCAM1-NCAM1 signalling to lower cell-cycle-associated RNA velocity during embryonic neurogenesis. In melanoma, inferred local MIF-CD74+CD44 signalling corresponded to a predicted decline in the melanocytic programme. Analysis of acute liver failure identified hepatocyte-derived ANGPTL4-SDC1 signalling in association with acetaminophen-related communication enrichment and predicted matrix-remodelling RNA dynamics. By converting static ligand-receptor maps into velocity-constrained networks of signalling influence, CellVocal provides a general strategy for generating spatially resolved hypotheses about how intercellular communication contributes to predicted transcriptional changes.

cards.title: Cognitive Performance in Prodromal Neuronal α Synuclein Disease
cards.abstract: Importance: Cognitive abnormalities may emerge during prodromal neuronal a-synuclein disease (NSD), but their domain specificity and longitudinal course are uncertain. Objective: To characterize baseline cognition and longitudinal change in prodromal NSD compared with healthy controls, NSD-negative genetic carriers, and sporadic Parkinson disease (PD). Design: Longitudinal cohort study using Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI) data, with first visits from July 2010 through April 2026 and up to 4 years of follow-up. Setting: Multicenter cohort. Participants: Healthy controls (HC; n=244), GBA1 or LRRK2 nonmanifesting carriers without NSD (n=323), prodromal NSD participants recruited through hyposmia or isolated rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder cohorts (n=1640), and sporadic PD (n=824). Exposures: NSD status and clinical cohort. Main Outcomes and Measures: Cognitive summary scores for verbal memory, executive function, processing speed, language, and visuospatial function, and PPMI-defined mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Models adjusted for age, sex, education, and APOE {varepsilon}4 status. Results: Among 3031 participants (mean [SD] age, 66.6 [7.0] years; 1322 female [43.6%]), prodromal NSD participants had lower baseline verbal-memory performance than HC (adjusted difference, -0.20 SD; 95% CI, -0.34 to -0.07; adjusted P = .007); NSD-negative genetic carriers did not differ from HC. No other cognitive domain was lower than HC at baseline or longitudinally. In the primary age-adjusted analysis, verbal-memory trajectory differed from HC over 4 years (P = .009), whereas in a smaller age-matched sensitivity subset through year 3, it did not (P = .62); the baseline difference persisted (adjusted difference, -0.28 SD; 95% CI, -0.46 to -0.10; P = .003). Adjusted MCI probability increased from 10.2% to 15.1% in prodromal NSD, compared with 8.4% to 5.0% in HC and 13.4% to 17.7% in PD. The increase was greater than in HC (ratio of annual odds ratios, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.58; adjusted P = .04) but not PD (P = .62). Conclusions and Relevance: Prodromal NSD was associated with modestly lower verbal memory and increasing MCI probability relative to HC, without lower performance in other cognitive domains. The baseline verbal-memory difference was robust, whereas the longitudinal trajectory finding was not reproduced in the smaller age-matched sensitivity subset.

cards.title: Cross-ancestry proteome-wide Mendelian randomization of plasma proteins and breast cancer susceptibility
cards.abstract: BackgroundThe plasma proteome may help connect inherited breast cancer susceptibility to biologically interpretable and potentially actionable pathways, but proteome-wide evidence across ancestries remains limited. MethodsWe conducted proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses of breast cancer risk using cis-protein quantitative trait loci for 1,962 distinct plasma proteins from 34,557 European-ancestry participants in the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project. Breast cancer genome-wide association studies included 156,901 cases and 204,634 controls of European, East Asian, and African ancestries. Ancestry-specific MR estimates were combined by fixed-effects meta-analysis. Candidate proteins were further evaluated through subtype-specific and reverse-direction MR analyses, statistical colocalization, replication in independent European and East Asian proteomic datasets, and analyses of associations between protein polygenic scores and breast cancer status in All of Us. ResultsTwelve proteins achieved Bonferroni significance in the cross-ancestry meta-analysis (P < 0.05/1,971 tests), including eight previously reported proteins and four newly prioritized by MR. DNPH1 showed cross-ancestry heterogeneity, while CASP8, RALB, and USP28 showed cross-subtype heterogeneity after accounting for shared controls (all P < 0.05/12). Complementary support varied: six candidates showed strong colocalization (PPH4 [≥] 0.80); four replicated with a consistent direction and nominal significance in deCODE, two in the Japan COVID-19 Task Force, and four in All of Us (all P < 0.05). The strongest cumulative support was observed for LRRC25, PARK7, and LRRC37A2. ConclusionsThese findings prioritize circulating protein candidates for mechanistic, prevention-oriented, and translational follow-up in breast cancer, while underscoring the need for larger ancestrally diverse proteomic resources to support equitable target and biomarker discovery.

cards.title: Stage-Specific Roles of Plasma GFAP in Linking Amyloid Cascade in Alzheimer Disease
cards.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Astrocytic reactivity, measured by plasma glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), is robustly elevated across the Alzheimer disease (AD) continuum, yet its relationship with the amyloid cascade remains poorly understood. METHODS: We integrated plasma GFAP with multimodal AD biomarkers, including cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) or plasma amyloid-beta (Abeta42/40), amyloid and tau positron emission tomography (PET), structural MRI, and clinical severity, across a discovery cohort (Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center, n=278) and an independent replication cohort (Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, n=236). RESULTS: In the overall samples of both cohorts, plasma GFAP statistically mediated the associations between soluble Abeta42/40 and amyloid PET and between amyloid PET and tau PET; both remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. In tau-negative individuals, the indirect association between soluble Abeta42/40 and amyloid PET remained significant after correction only in Knight ADRC. In amyloid-positive individuals, the indirect association between amyloid PET and tau PET remained significant after correction only in ADNI. Interaction findings were not consistently replicated across cohorts, either before or after correction. Plasma proteomics identified a GFAP-associated protein network enriched for extracellular matrix and immune-related pathways. DISCUSSION: These findings support associations of plasma GFAP with amyloid and tau biomarkers within A/T-defined groups and identify GFAP-associated extracellular matrix and inflammatory protein signatures that warrant further investigation.

cards.title: Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis of Molecular Associations and Biological Pathways Underlying Neurodevelopmental Conditions in a Twin Cohort
cards.abstract: Neurodevelopmental conditions (NDCs) arise from complex genetic-environmental interactions, yet their molecular underpinnings remain incompletely defined. We applied an integrative multi-omics approach within a deeply phenotyped twin cohort to identify systemic molecular signatures and pathways associated with NDCs. Our study included 237 twins aged 8-28 years from the Roots of Autism and ADHD Twin Study in Sweden (RATSS), with one or more omics layers available per individual, including serum and cerebrospinal fluid proteomics, urine and fecal metabolomics, blood metallomics, and whole-genome sequencing in a subset of 14 monozygotic twin pairs. Using the DIABLO framework, we identified cross-omics features that distinguish individuals with and without NDCs. The identified features converged on enriched metabolic and immune-related pathways, including purine metabolism, lysine degradation, PI3K-Akt, and MAPK signaling. Several key molecules also showed differential abundance at the single-molecule level in generalized estimating equation (GEE) models. ADA protein, pyrimidine-related metabolites (thymidine, glutamine, and 2'-deoxyuridine), and copper showed suggestive associations within NDC-discordant MZ twin pairs, pointing to potential non-shared condition-related effects, while flavin mononucleotide and manganese associations with NDCs were influenced by shared genetic or familial environmental factors. Our findings indicate that NDC-related molecular alterations manifest across multiple biological layers and tissues, and are detectable through integrative systems-level analysis. Our scalable framework provides critical insights into altered metabolic and immune processes in NDCs and highlights candidate features that may inform future biomarker development and mechanistic research in precision psychiatry.

cards.title: Glutamine antagonism suppresses tumor growth in adrenocortical carcinoma through inhibition of de novo nucleotide biosynthesis
cards.abstract: Dysregulation of cellular metabolism is a hallmark of cancer, which remains poorly understood in adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC). Here, we dissected ACC metabolism by integrating transcriptional profiling from human and mouse ACC, targeted tissue metabolomics from a mouse ACC model, and untargeted serum metabolomics from a large patient cohort, providing cross-species validation of metabolic rewiring in ACC. This study revealed global metabolic dysregulation, involving glutamine-dependent pathways such as amino-acid and hexosamine biosynthesis, nucleotide metabolism, and glutathione biosynthesis, suggesting glutamine catabolism is a critical metabolic vulnerability in ACC. Treatment with glutamine antagonists 6-Diazo-5-Oxo-L-Norleucine (DON) and JHU-083 elicited robust anti-tumor responses. Mechanistic studies revealed DON's anti-tumor effect was primarily driven by selective inhibition of glutamine-fueled de novo nucleotide biosynthesis. Additionally, DON led to DNA damage, which yielded potent synergism with inhibition of the DNA damage response pathway. Collectively, this work highlights glutamine metabolism as a central metabolic dependency and therapeutic target in ACC.

cards.title: Proneural lineage identity is the primary determinant of embryonic synchrony patterns in the developing hindbrain
cards.abstract: Does the stem cell origin impact on how daughter neurons acquire functional characteristics? Here, we uncovered that progenitor identity, defined by proneural gene expression, hardwires the functional mode (synchrony vs. asynchrony) of a neuron. Multimodal cell lineage reconstruction combining intersectional lineage tracing, newly developed computational tools, and genetic knockouts revealed that different progenitors produced functionally distinct neuronal subtypes in the zebrafish hindbrain. Dynamics of neuronal production suggest that progenitor competence changes over time. Whereas neurog1-expressing progenitors contributed to both glutamatergic and GABAergic lineages at early embryonic stages, later, other progenitor pools also assumed this role. Whole-hindbrain 3D atlases, in which we combined calcium imaging to monitor spontaneous neuronal activity with genetic perturbations and progenitor origin, unveiled that the emergence of neuronal activity patterns was presaged by their progenitor identity. This suggests a link between cell ontogeny and neuronal activity in the zebrafish hindbrain, and more fundamentally how the embryonic progenitor identity controls the emergence of neuronal diversity in glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal populations.

cards.title: Spatial transcriptomics of juxtaglomerular renin cells under angiotensin re-ceptor blockade in human IgA nephropathy
cards.abstract: Background: Renin-angiotensin system (RAS) blockade is the foundation of treatment in IgA nephropathy, yet the response of the renin cells, the macula densa and the arterioles of the human kidney to this treatment has hardly been described. Methods: Single-cell-level spatial transcriptomics was obtained from archival biopsies of 154 participants, including 60 patients with IgA nephropathy, 26 of whom took an angiotensin receptor blocker. Renin cells and the macula densa were assessed at each vascular pole and along the arterioles and compared with plasma renin and the Kidney Precision Medicine Project atlas. Results: Treated patients had 2.66 renin cells per glomerulus and untreated patients 0.99 (adjusted difference 1.30; 95% CI 0.42 to 2.18), with or without hypertension. The increase came from pole juxtaglomerular cells, more of which transcribed REN (19 percentage points; 7 to 31), with as many pole smooth muscle cells as in untreated patients. Renin cells of treated and untreated patients had a similar distribution along the arteriole and the same renin-cell program, in contrast to the changes reported in mouse renin cells. At each vascular pole, macula densa marker genes of the adjacent tubule increased with the number of renin cells, and treated patients had more renin cells without more macula densa cells. Plasma renin rose with tissue renin cells in treated and untreated patients alike, and neither was related to the composite kidney outcome. Conclusions: In human IgA nephropathy, RAS blockade is accompanied by a larger population of juxtaglomerular renin cells, in which more juxtaglomerular cells transcribe renin, with the same renin-cell identity and distribution as in untreated patients, in contrast to the findings in mice. At each vascular pole, renin cells increase with macula densa marker genes of the adjacent tubule, and plasma renin rises with tissue renin cells.

cards.title: Transcriptional aging across CNS tissues in the ALS-FTD spectrum reflects clock architecture and disease-associated cellular signatures
cards.abstract: Background. We examined transcriptomic (gene expression-based) aging in postmortem central nervous system (CNS) tissues from donors across the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-frontotemporal dementia (FTD) spectrum and investigated the molecular and cellular features underlying disease-associated differences in transcriptional aging clocks. Methods. Six transcriptomic clocks (RNAAgeCalc DESeq2, GTExAge, Pearson and GenAge; Pasta REG and age-shift) were applied to 2,235 RNA-sequencing samples from 609 donors across 11 CNS regions, with adjustment for age and tissue-specific technical variables. We compared transcriptional age across ALS, ALS-FTD, FTD, and controls, examining regional variation, gene-level contributions, cell composition, disease duration, and C9orf72 status, with independent validation of gene contributions in a cervical spinal cord cohort. Results. Disease-associated differences in transcriptional age varied by diagnosis, tissue, and clock. ALS and ALS-FTD showed the strongest differences in spinal cord, while FTD differences localized primarily to the frontal and temporal cortex. In ALS spinal cord, RNAAgeCalc DESeq2 estimates were lower than controls, whereas other clocks estimated higher transcriptional age when significant. CHIT1 was identified as the primary contributor to the DESeq2 transcriptional age decrease in ALS. Cell composition adjustment attenuated ALS spinal cord differences, reflecting microglial, lymphocyte, oligodendrocyte, and astrocyte signatures, though the lumbar GenAge increase in transcriptional age and DESeq2 decrease remained significant. The higher transcriptional age in ALS motor cortex also remained significantafter adjustment. Clinical associations were likewise clock dependent. Higher spinal DESeq2 age acceleration (AA) was associated with longer ALS duration, though this association was strongly influenced by the CHIT1 term. Higher GTExAge AA in cervical spinal cord, thoracic spinal cord, and occipital cortex was associated with shorter disease duration; no significant associations were observed for the other clock-tissue combinations or for ALS-FTD. No clock differed by C9orf72 repeat expansion status. Conclusions. In this study we found disease-associated differences in transcriptional age that localize to clinically relevant tissues. Differences in transcriptional aging across the ALS-FTD spectrum reflect interactions among clock architecture, disease-associated gene expression, tissue region, and cellular composition. Resolving these components reveals the biological context underlying divergent clock estimates and provides a framework for interpreting changes in transcriptional aging.

cards.title: Population-level learning of non-additive effects enables accurate and efficient prediction of combinatorial perturbation responses
cards.abstract: Combinatorial perturbations are widely used to study genetic interactions and to develop drug combinations, but the number of possible combinations grows quadratically with the number of perturbations, and only a small fraction can be measured in a screen experiment. Despite their growing sophistication, deep-learning and foundation models often fail to outperform a simple additive baseline based on measured single-perturbation responses. This suggests a simpler approach that builds on these measurements and directly learns deviations from additivity at the population level. We therefore developed GAIN, a lightweight model that implements these principles by predicting the pseudobulk response to a combination as the sum of its two single-perturbation responses and a learned interaction term. Across three single-cell datasets of genetic and drug combinations, GAIN corrected deviations from additivity and outperformed the additive model and cell-level methods across generalization settings and metrics, while training 3- to 64-fold faster. Applied to a combinatorial CRISPR screen of leukemia differentiation regulators, GAIN revealed synergy between key regulators of the differentiation block and genes that restrain differentiation but have little effect alone. It also revealed dampening by the histone chaperone FACT, which supports the induction of differentiation genes. These results establish population-level modeling of the deviation from additivity as a simple, accurate and scalable approach to predicting combination responses.

cards.title: A latent tau amplifier in the neuronal proteome lowers the seeding threshold for Alzheimers disease pathology
cards.abstract: The stereotyped spread of tau pathology through connected brain regions is accompanied by striking differences in the vulnerability of individual neuronal populations, pointing to cell-intrinsic determinants of susceptibility. Using a combination of computational APR analysis, in vitro and cellular aggregation assays, and quantitative proteomics of human postmortem brain, we identify the splicing factor TRA2B as an endogenous modifier of this susceptibility. TRA2B enhances the activity of patient-derived tau seeds, promotes tau pathology in vivo, and progressively redistributes from the nucleus into insoluble tau-associated material in Alzheimers disease brain. Mechanistically, TRA2B contains two aggregation-prone regions (APRs) homologous to tau nucleation sites that are required for tau interaction and seeding enhancement. Yet this activity is not constitutive: isolated TRA2B APRs promote aggregation, whereas the full-length protein can inhibit, amplify or have little effect on tau aggregation depending on protein state and seeding context. Perturbation of the regulatory RS2 region switches TRA2B away from its amplifying state, revealing that its sequence-encoded aggregation potential is regulatable. Thus, TRA2B acts as a latent tau amplifier, providing a mechanism by which the neuronal proteome can tune cellular susceptibility to the propagation of pathological tau.

cards.title: Methamphetamine use reshapes cellular and plasma immune signatures in a lineage-specific manner in people with HIV
cards.abstract: Methamphetamine use is common among people with HIV (PWH) and is associated with worse neurocognitive and clinical outcomes, but how it reshapes HIV-associated immune dysregulation across cell types and compartments is unknown. In this cross-sectional and observational study, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from controls without HIV, PWH without methamphetamine use and PWH who use methamphetamine, then scored pathway enrichment, cytokine response and transcription factor activity in each cell population. We then profiled plasma from the same three groups in a larger set of participants by targeted proteomics, with PWH who use cocaine added as a stimulant comparison. In the single-cell data, methamphetamine use acted in opposite directions across lineages. HIV-associated changes were reversed most often in monocytes and CD8+ T cells, with interferon, antigen presentation and JAK-STAT programs shifting in monocytes and IFN-{gamma}, IL-2 and MYC programs shifting in CD8+ T cells, whereas HIV-associated proliferative and TNF signaling programs persisted in CD4+ and {gamma}{delta} T cells of Meth+HIV participants. Central memory CD8+ T cells of Meth+HIV participants showed reduced type 1 effector programs. In plasma, HIV was associated with a cytotoxic lymphocyte activation signature (KLRK1, IFN-{gamma}, TNF, granzyme B and CXCL9) that was further elevated with methamphetamine use, together with higher IL-6, CXCL13 and neurofilament heavy chain. IFN-{gamma} was the most connected protein in the plasma interaction network, linking a cytotoxic module to a lymphoid chemokine module. These data define lineage- and compartment-specific immune consequences of methamphetamine use in PWH and nominate IFN-{gamma} signaling, acting through monocyte antigen presentation and CD8+ T cell effector programs, together with TNF, IL-6 and CXCL13, as candidate mediators of neuroimmune dysfunction in PWH who use methamphetamine.

cards.title: Combinatorial regulation of cellular rotation during dorsal-ventral axis establishment in Caenorhabditis elegans
cards.abstract: Cellular rotation is an understudied mechanism that regulates animal morphogenesis. In C. elegans, the dorsal-ventral axis is established when the two-cell-stage AB cell rotates within the eggshell as it divides, generating the diamond-shaped blastomere arrangement at the four-cell stage. Multiple mechanisms, including actomyosin-dependent oriented division, chiral cortical flow, and eggshell shape, have been proposed to regulate this arrangement, but whether these represent conflicting hypotheses or co-acting mechanisms remains unclear. Here, we show that CUL-3-actomyosin-dependent oriented division, eggshell geometry, and the Ras-MAPK signaling pathway regulate distinct steps of cellular rotation. AB cell rotation occurs in two distinct phases: Phase I during AB cytokinesis and Phase II during neighboring P1 cytokinesis. We found that CUL-3-actomyosin-dependent oriented division, eggshell geometry, and Ras-MAPK signaling are required for Phase I rotation. Errors in Phase I can be fully corrected by subsequent Phase II rotation. However, perturbation of CUL-3-actomyosin-dependent oriented division compromises this robust fail-safe mechanism, leading to dorsal-ventral axis defects. These results show the combinatorial and robust regulation of cellular rotation and its critical role in C. elegans embryogenesis.

cards.title: Machine learning cross-platform proteomic imputation enables protein quality scoring and replication of epidemiological associations
cards.abstract: High-throughput affinity-based proteomics has advanced biomedical research, yet fundamental, persistent discordance between mainstream platforms (SomaScan and Olink) routinely undermines the replication of findings. This platform-driven non-replication complicates downstream biological validation and biomarker prioritization. Here, we develop a machine learning-based framework for cross-platform protein value imputation to navigate this translational bottleneck. Using paired proteomic data measured by both SomaScan and Olink from 5,325 participants of the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, we developed models to impute cross-platform measurements and applied them to two independent and demographically distinct cohorts (Cardiovascular Health Study [N=3,171] and UK Biobank [UKB; N=41,405]) to evaluate downstream replication. Our bidirectional model 1) established an imputation performance-based protein fidelity index, validated against gold-standard / orthogonal measurements (ELISA and Simoa/Quanterix in Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities study [ARIC, N=101] and Nurses' Health Study [NHS, N=54], and published mass spectrometry data), 2) enabled imputation of platform-exclusive protein measurements, and 3) facilitated calibration of overlapping proteins. We demonstrate the utility of this framework through three applications: 1) fidelity-informed analyses enhanced the replication of biomarker discovery, 2) recovery of SomaScan signals that were previously inaccessible in UKB's original Olink measurements, and 3) improved replication performance for overlapping proteins. Our study offers a translational roadmap that helps researchers identify more confident cross-platform measurements to support replication efforts, identify potential assays warranting future optimization, and distinguish proteins where biological signal likely dominates platform-specific measurement.

cards.title: PedDx: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumor Diagnosis with Agentic AI-Enabled Independent External Evaluation
cards.abstract: Reliable clinical translation of diagnostic artificial intelligence (AI) requires evaluation beyond classification accuracy. We developed PedDx, a segmentation-free framework for pediatric posterior fossa tumor diagnosis using T2-weighted MRI, pretrained 3DINO representations, calibrated predictions, and confidence-based abstention. Evaluation included 492 discovery, 114 replication, 129 external validation, and 40 independently tested cases, alongside 236 out-of-distribution (OOD) cases and controlled imaging perturbations. Classification accuracy was 79.8% in replication and 81.4% in external validation, increasing to 90.5% and 88.7%, respectively, among non-abstained cases. OOD analyses revealed performance degradation and confidently incorrect predictions, while perturbation analyses identified acquisition and alignment vulnerabilities. An external institution independently executed the complete agentic workflow, successfully generating predictions and structured quality-control reports for all 40 cases, with classification accuracy of 92.5%, increasing to 97.3% among non-abstained cases. PedDx demonstrates how uncertainty assessment, failure-mode characterization, external validation, and independently reproducible, traceable reporting can collectively inform the reliability and limitations of diagnostic AI systems.

cards.title: Manifestation-Guided Adaptation of CT Foundation Model for Early Neurological Prognosis after ECPR
cards.abstract: Purpose. To develop a data-efficient, clinically guided transfer-learning framework for hyperacute neurological outcome prediction from head CT in patients undergoing extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) after cardiac arrest by leveraging free-text radiology report. Methods. This retrospective study included 683 patients with available CT examination and radiology reports from December 2015 to November 2025. The primary outcome distinguished favorable neurological outcomes (Cerebral Performance Category [CPC] 1-2) from neurological death due to brain death or cerebral herniation (CPC 5). A cross-attention adaptor jointly learned to predict neurological outcome and five report-derived manifestations of brain injury from a frozen pretrained head CT encoder. Outcome prediction used CT images alone at inference. The manifestation-guided adaptor, trained with and without additional patients who contributed only manifestation labels, was compared with outcome-only adaptor and two pooled-feature baselines. Performance was summarized as mean {+/-} SD across five held-out folds. Results. Of 683 patients, 197 were eligible for outcome evaluation (63 with favorable outcomes and 134 with neurological death), and 486 formed the manifestation-only cohort. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.918 {+/-} 0.044 for the outcome-only adaptor. The manifestation-guided adaptor achieved an AUROC of 0.927 {+/-} 0.042. With additional manifestation-only training data, the adaptor achieved the mean AUROC (0.929 {+/-} 0.037), specificity (93.7% {+/-} 6.5%), with a sensitivity of 79.9% {+/-} 9.2%. Conclusion. Manifestation-guided adaptation outperforms outcome-only adaptation for neurological outcome prediction from hyperacute head CT after ECPR. Report-derived manifestation labels enabled training with additional examinations without eligible outcome labels while preserving CT-only prediction.

cards.title: Acute hypertension causes focal coronary artery perivascular cGAS-, IRF3, and IFNAR-dependent type I interferon responses
cards.abstract: Hypertension exposes coronary arteries to dynamic mechanical forces that alter the structural integrity and lead to pathologic changes such as aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis. Although the effects of chronic hypertension have been extensively studied, the early molecular responses to increased luminal pressure remain poorly understood. Here, we find that acute hypertension in murine coronary arteries induced by transverse aortic constriction (TAC) causes focal perivascular type I interferon (IFN) responses in the vessel wall in contrast to comparatively homogeneous perivascular fibrosis. Spatial transcriptomics and RNAscope independently demonstrate spatially clustered expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in the walls of pressurized left and right coronary arteries in the first week after TAC. Genetic disruption of cGAS or IRF3 each markedly attenuated the perivascular ISG response, indicating the response is a consequence of DNA sensing. Pharmacologic disruption of type I IFN signaling using an anti-IFNAR antibody abolished pressure-induced induction of focal ISG expression suggesting the pathway can be inhibited therapeutically. Since focal type I IFN signaling in the infarct borderzone of the left ventricle increased risk of dilation and rupture, we propose that focal perivascular type I IFN signaling in the vessel wall may serve as a nidus for analogous pathologies like aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis and represent a potential target for therapy.

cards.title: Granger-causal inference to study crosstalk between two actin regulators in live cell imaging
cards.abstract: Dynamic actin filament assembly at the cell membrane drives cell migration. Its regulation is governed by functionally overlapping actin regulators and complex feedback loops that hinder conventional perturbation-approaches from dissecting actin regulatory pathways. Here we present an extended, perturbation-free statistical framework based on Granger causality (GC). The framework rests on statistical models that capture the interdependence among subcellular fluctuations of molecular and cell morphodynamic activities extracted from three-channel live-cell imaging. Applied to the inference of cause-effect relationships among actin, its regulators and cell-edge movement, the GC analysis identifies distinct regulatory hierarchies of the actin regulators Arp2/3, VASP and mDia1 on actin dynamics and cell edge movement. Notably, we find that mDia1 plays a critical role in translating actin filament assembly into cell-edge movement, whereas Arp2/3 and VASP function primarily as regulators of polymer extension. By imaging three actin reporters simultaneously, we also demonstrate that the GC framework can distinguish the distinct causal roles of filamentous vs monomeric actin in driving cell edge movements.

cards.title: LabARIA: A Multi-Agent System for Integrative Analytics in Clinical Laboratories
cards.abstract: Background Laboratory medicine underpins clinical decision-making across nearly every care setting. Clinical laboratory errors and delays can compromise diagnostic reliability and patient care. However, laboratory quality and operational data are commonly reviewed through separate manual workflows, limiting timely recognition of emerging problems across complementary data sources. Methods We developed and evaluated LabARIA (Laboratory Agentic Reasoning and Integrative Analytics), a multi-agent AI system for coordinated surveillance of specimen workflows, analytical quality control, and laboratory operations. We conducted a single-center retrospective system development and evaluation at NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medical Center using laboratory data collected from May 1 through June 18, 2026, including 177,480 specimen-panel records, 75,103 internal quality-control (IQC) measurements, 633 proficiency-testing challenges, and 422 recalibration or maintenance actions. Forecasting agents were evaluated using patient-result streams with controlled perturbations, and synthetic staffing and inventory data. We assessed specimen rejection, cancellation, and turnaround-time patterns; warning recall and lead time before documented laboratory actions; assay-specific patient-based real-time quality control (PBRTQC) performance; and exploratory operational forecasting discrimination. Findings LabARIA characterized specimen and workflow patterns across clinical units and time periods, including hemolysis-related potassium rejections in the intensive care unit during early morning hours (49 of 367 tests [13.3%]). For analytical quality monitoring, the IQC agent generated warnings before 407 of 422 recorded QC actions (recall, 0.964 [95% CI, 0.942-0.978]), with a median lead time of 5.40 days (95% CI, 3.75-6.07). PBRTQC agent selected different monitoring strategies across 35 analytes. In a separate analysis, adding PBRTQC increased action recall from 0.964 to 0.993 (95% CI, 0.979-0.998). A dashboard presented tiered alerts for human review, and an accompanying chatbot supported interactive exploration of the summaries. For the operational forecasting module, areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve for 7-day inventory and staffing risk forecasting were 0.800 (95% CI, 0.696-0.881) and 0.877 (95% CI, 0.778-0.950), respectively. Interpretation LabARIA demonstrated the feasibility of coordinating laboratory quality surveillance across heterogeneous data sources, providing a foundation for intelligent clinical laboratories. Prospective studies are warranted to determine whether this approach improves monitoring beyond conventional methods, supports laboratory decisions, and benefits patient care without excessive alert burden.

cards.title: Regulation of the Epstein-Barr Epigenome by Histone Variant MacroH2A
cards.abstract: Histone variants play an important role in regulating chromatin dynamics of Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV). Here, we investigate the role of histone variant macroH2A in EBV chromatin structure, gene expression and copy number control during latent infection. ChIP-seq analysis in EBV+ SNU719 gastric carcinoma and Mutu I Burkitt lymphoma cells revealed that macroH2A was most enriched at repetitive DNA elements, including oriLyt, BHLF1, LF3 and terminal repeat (TR) regions of the EBV genome. MacroH2A depletion in EBV-associated gastric cancer cell line SNU719 led to a small increase in some viral lytic genes and increase in viral DNA copy number. RNAseq transcriptomics after macroH2A depletion identified major perturbations in cellular gene pathways, including beta-catenin/TCF signaling and chromatin remodeling. Depletion of macroH2A during EBV lytic reactivation reduced EBV lytic gene activation, but increased EBV DNA copy number. Previous study demonstrated a colocalization and cooperative binding between histone variant H2A.Z and EBNA1. We now show that depletion of macroH2A causes an increase in both H2A.Z and EBNA1 at oriP and cellular binding sites for EBNA1. We also found that gammaH2AX localizes to oriP and that this depends on macroH2A. Finally, we show that CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of macroH2A increases the replication and episome maintenance of oriP-containing plasmids. Taken together, these findings indicate that macroH2A localizes to the repetitive elements of EBV, including oriLyt, and can function to limit H2A.Z and EBNA1 binding at oriP, which alters DNA damage signaling at oriP and limits episomal replication. These findings provide a novel role for macroH2A in maintaining EBV copy number and genome integrity.

cards.title: A population-scale isoform atlas enables isoform-based trait association and regulatory analysis in lettuce
cards.abstract: Genomic variation shapes phenotypic diversity, yet how genetic variation contributes to transcript isoform diversity remains poorly understood at the population scale. Here, we integrated transcriptomic data from 240 lettuce accessions with a lettuce pangenome to construct a comprehensive pan isoform atlas comprising 531,657 isoforms from 49,729 transcribed loci. Isoform presence absence variation (iPAV) captured extensive transcript diversification during domestication and horticultural differentiation, providing additional resolution beyond locus-level analyses, particularly within loci shared across the population. To facilitate the systematic analysis of isoform trait associations, we developed ISONET-GWAS, a computational framework that integrates isoform-based association mapping, functional annotation, and network-based candidate prioritization. ISONET-GWAS recovered the known chlorophyll regulator LsGLK, identified 455 metabolite isoform associations across 77 metabolites, and prioritized candidate regulators of chlorophyll metabolism supported by functional validation. Genome-wide splicing quantitative trait locus (sQTL) mapping identified 10,498 sQTL associations, revealing widespread distal genetic associations with alternative splicing and candidate trans-sQTL hotspots. Notably, we identified a trans-sQTL hotspot overlapping LsPPR, which encodes a pentatricopeptide repeat RNA-binding protein. Perturbation of LsPPR resulted in widespread changes in alternative splicing of floweing-related genes, accompanied by delayed bolting and flowering and altered splicing of flowering-related genes. Together, our study establishes a population-scale pan-isoform resource and a broadly applicable analytical strategy for isoform-level trait association, candidate prioritization, and complementary analysis of the genetic regulation of alternative splicing in crops.

cards.title: Digital Twin-Based Risk Stratification Integrating Aortic Shape and Wall Mechanics in Acute Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection
cards.abstract: Objective This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events. Methods We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk. Results At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher- versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher- versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792). Conclusions Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.
