cards.title: Bone Health in Female Athletes Using Hormonal Contraceptives.
cards.abstract: The objectives of this study were to (1) report the prevalence and type of hormonal contraception (HC) use among Canadian elite and world-class athletes and (2) investigate associations between current HC use and bone density, microarchitecture and strength, accounting for sport type (endurance vs. non-endurance). Participants included 61 high performance athletes, mean age 24 years. Endurance-based sport affiliations include long-track speed skating (n=16), cross-country skiing (n=13) and biathlon (n=9). Non-endurance sports were ski cross (n=7), figure skating (n=6), luge (n=4), ski jumping (n=4), and combat sports (n=2). High-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography scans of the radius and tibia were acquired and outcome measures included bone mineral density, microarchitecture, geometry and bone strength. Questionnaires captured sport affiliation and reproductive health information. Two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed to examine the effects of current HC use (yes/no) and sport type (endurance/non-endurance) on bone variables. HC prevalence was 69% (n=42) and the majority of athletes used progestin only intrauterine devices (IUDs, n=29). No evidence of detrimental effects resulting from HC use was found in this cohort. Although some differences were observed between groups, no interaction effects remained significant after multiple-comparison correction and these findings should be interpreted with caution. Overall, the results do not support clinically meaningful differences in bone health between HC groups. These findings highlight the need for longitudinal research examining the effects of currently prevalent HC methods, particularly IUDs, on overall bone health and strength along with lifetime fracture risk in athletes.

cards.title: Body mass index and the risk of first hip fracture in older Chinese adults: a longitudinal analysis of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study with death as a competing event.
cards.abstract: Low body mass has been linked to fracture risk, but most cohorts measure it once and few account for competing death. Composite nutritional phenotypes embed body mass index (BMI), and their muscle-mass components derive from it, so their added value is unclear. We examined repeatedly measured BMI and first hip fracture in older Chinese adults. Using five waves (2011-2020) of the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, we followed community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older without prior hip fracture. Wave-specific BMI was the exposure; the primary analysis used intervals with contemporaneously measured anthropometry (2013-2018), and death was handled as a competing event. 4,515 participants contributed 7,366 person-periods (18,391 person-years), with 129 hip fractures and 423 deaths. Each 1 kg/m2 higher BMI was associated with a lower hazard of hip fracture (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99, p=0.019), similarly in the wider window and with a single 2013 measurement. Standardized hip-fracture risk through 2020 was 4.6% (95% CI 3.4-6.4) for BMI <18.5 and 3.1% (2.4-4.2) for BMI 23.0-27.4 kg/m2. Persistently low BMI across 2013-2015 carried a higher exploratory hazard (2.01, 0.99-4.05). A nutritional phenotype added no information to a model containing continuous BMI (p=0.87). Lower BMI was consistently associated with a higher hazard of first hip fracture, independently of the analytical window and of repeated measurement. A composite nutritional phenotype added no information beyond BMI; the outcome was self-reported, so causal conclusions are not warranted.

cards.title: Preparatory beta activity reflects the precision demands of an upcoming movement
cards.abstract: Noise and external disturbances continuously push the limb away from its intended path, but not every deviation compromises the goal of an action. The accuracy constraints of a task define the range of acceptable endpoints and thereby set its precision demands, that is, how much noise must be attenuated for the task to succeed. Whether neural activity during movement preparation reflects these precision demands remains largely unexplored. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) while healthy human participants (n = 27) prepared reaching movements toward narrow or wide targets at the same location and with the same timing constraints. An instructed delay before the go cue allowed preparatory activity to be isolated, and mechanical perturbations were applied during movement to probe feedback responses. Narrow targets led to more precise movements, with greater endpoint accuracy, lower variability and smaller perturbation-induced deviations. This was achieved without a reduction in movement speed, and involved greater muscle co-activation and larger long-latency responses to perturbations. Before movement onset, beta power (13-30 Hz) was lower for narrow than for wide targets, an effect that emerged late in the delay period and was concentrated over bilateral parieto-occipital electrodes. In contrast, alpha (8-12 Hz) and theta (4-7 Hz) activity did not differ between conditions. These findings demonstrate that preparatory beta activity is sensitive not only to kinematic requirements of the movement but also the precision with which it must be produced.

cards.title: Beyond Biochemical Detection: Longitudinal Target-Organ Outcomes and Parathyroidectomy in Laboratory-Detected Primary Hyperparathyroidism.
cards.abstract: Laboratory-based case finding can identify primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) before clinical suspicion arises, but the subsequent occurrence and documentation of target organ involvement remain poorly characterized. To characterize the longitudinal occurrence of newly documented target-organ involvement after laboratory-based case finding of PHPT and to examine its temporal association with parathyroidectomy. Retrospective cohort study in a health area serving >230,000 inhabitants. We studied a retrospective cohort of 229 patients with PHPT identified through laboratory-based hypercalcemia detection; 228 contributed to time-to-event analyses. The primary endpoint was time to first occurrence of newly documented target-organ involvement, defined as the detection of nephrolithiasis, fracture, osteoporosis, or renal deterioration. Parathyroidectomy was modelled as a time-dependent exposure in a multivariable Cox regression model, adjusted for age, sex, the Charlson Comorbidity Index, and baseline surgical criteria. Landmark analyses were performed at 12 and 24 months, along with an exploratory analysis of the restricted mean survival at 5 years. During follow-up, 55 patients experienced a first newly documented target-organ involvement event. Parathyroidectomy was associated with a lower estimated hazard of the composite endpoint (adjusted HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.25-1.30; p = 0.182). The association was directionally similar in landmark analyses, although estimates remained imprecise (24 month HR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.08-1.01; p = 0.052). Newly documented skeletal and renal target-organ involvement occurred during follow-up after laboratory-based detection of PHPT. Parathyroidectomy was consistently associated with a lower estimated hazard; however, the primary analysis was imprecise and did not provide statistically conclusive evidence. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support prospective evaluation of longitudinal outcomes after laboratory-based PHPT detection.

cards.title: Estrogen replacement therapy for postmenopausal osteoporosis: a systematic review and meta‑analysis.
cards.abstract: To clarify the efficacy and safety of estrogen replacement therapy (ERT) in patients with postmenopausal osteoporosis(PMO). We searched PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov (2000-2026) for randomized controlled trials comparing ERT with placebo. Primary outcomes were fracture incidence and bone mineral density (BMD) changes; secondary outcomes included neoplasm, cardiovascular events, and adverse events leading to discontinuation (treatment duration ≤2 years). Risk of bias was assessed with RoB2, meta-analysis used Stata 17.0, and evidence quality was graded with GRADE. Eleven studies (37859 participants) were included. ERT significantly reduced clinical fractures (OR 0.73; 95% CI 0.68-0.78; high-quality evidence) and improved BMD at lumbar spine (SMD 0.42; 95% CI 0.25-0.59;moderate-quality), femur (SMD 0.27; 95%CI 0.04-0.52; moderate-quality), and hip (SMD 0.18; 95%CI 0.00-0.35; moderate-quality). No dose-response relationship was found. For treatment duration ≤2 years, ERT showed no statistically significant association with neoplasm (OR 1.32; 95% CI 0.20-8.84; low-quality), cardiovascular events (OR 0.85; 95% CI 0.26-2.85; low-quality), or discontinuation due to adverse events (OR 1.22; 95%CI 0.68-2.21; low-quality evidence). ERT reduces fracture risk and improves BMD in postmenopausal women, but short-term safety evidence is of low quality, requiring careful patient selection.

cards.title: Integrative serum metabolomics reveals osteopenia-specific lipid and amino acid networks for early osteoporosis risk stratification.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP), characterized by compromised bone strength, remains profoundly underdiagnosed owing to its asymptomatic progression until fracture. Osteopenia constitutes a crucial window for intervention, yet existing diagnostic modalities predicated on bone mineral density (BMD) are deficient in sensitivity for detecting early metabolic perturbations. Metabolomics provides a systems-level approach to pinpoint novel biomarkers that mirror dynamic skeletal metabolism. Metabolomic profiling was performed in 220 adults recruited in Wuhan and classified by BMD into healthy control (HC), osteopenia (ON), and osteoporosis (OP) groups, integrating untargeted metabolomics with targeted amino acid analysis using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Pairwise comparisons discerned 30, 55, and 49 differentially expressed metabolites for ON vs. HC, OP vs. HC, and OP vs. ON, respectively, with the majority predominantly up-regulated under low bone mass conditions. Lipid species represented the predominantly altered class, alongside organic acids and nucleosides. Targeted analysis identified six amino acids correlated with BMD. Pathway enrichment revealed perturbations in Steroid degradation, Flavonoid metabolism, phenylalanine and tyrosine metabolism, and vitamin B6 pathways. Sex-stratified network analysis suggested osteopenia-specific metabolic reconfiguration involving phosphatidylcholine and amino acid metabolites. The top-ranking metabolites exhibited discriminative ability for ON vs. HC (AUC > 0.8), with acceptable performance for OP vs. HC (AUC ≈ 0.8) and OP vs. ON (AUC > 0.7). The favorable ability at osteopenic stage supports these metabolite panels as exploratory tools for early risk stratification, laying the foundation for potential metabolomic biomarkers to improve the early detection and prevention of fragility fractures.

cards.title: Anti-osteoporosis therapy after hip fracture and the risk of mortality and subsequent fracture: a target trial emulation.
cards.abstract: Older adults sustaining a hip fracture are at high risk of death and subsequent fragility fractures. Among patients managed within a Fracture Liaison Service who were alive and fracture-free at the 60-day landmark, early anti-osteoporosis treatment initiation was associated with a lower hazard of all-cause mortality. Hip fractures are associated with high mortality and risk of subsequent fragility fractures. Estimating the association between anti-osteoporosis treatment and clinical outcomes in observational settings is challenging because of treatment selection, confounding, and time-related biases. We evaluated the association between early anti-osteoporosis treatment initiation and all-cause mortality and subsequent fragility fractures among patients managed within a Fracture Liaison Service (FLS), using a target trial emulation framework. We included consecutive patients aged ≥50 years admitted with an index fragility hip fracture and assessed within an FLS between March 2023 and March 2024. Baseline clinical data were prospectively collected during the index hospitalization, with clinical outcomes recorded throughout follow-up. A 60-day landmark was applied, including patients alive and fracture-free at day 60 and classifying treatment according to initiation within this period. Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was used to address measured baseline confounding. Associations with all-cause mortality and subsequent fracture were estimated using doubly robust Cox and Fine-Gray competing-risk regression models and reported as hazard ratios (HRs) and subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs), respectively, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 529 patients (mean age, 83 ± 9 years; 71.6% women), 420 (79.4%) initiated anti-osteoporotis treatment within 60 days. During a median follow-up of 19.7 months, 147 deaths and 51 subsequent fractures occurred. Treatment initiation was associated with a lower hazard of all-cause mortality (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.57-0.89; p = 0.006). IPTW-weighted cumulative mortality risks by 24 months after index admission were 26.5% among treated patients and 35.0% among untreated patients. No statistically significant association was observed between treatment initiation and subsequent fragility fracture risk (sHR 0.66, 95% CI 0.30-1.45; p = 0.301). Among older adults with hip fracture managed within an FLS, initiation of anti-osteoporosis treatment within 60 days was associated with a lower hazard of all-cause mortality. No statistically significant association with subsequent fragility fracture risk was observed, although statistical precision for this secondary outcome was limited.

cards.title: Multi-Layer Functional Metabolomics Reveals Chemical Interactions Between the Plant-Associated Bacterium Serratia marcescens and Phytophthora
cards.abstract: Oomycete pathogens of the genus Phytophthora cause devastating crop losses worldwide, highlighting the need for novel biocontrol agents. Here, we developed a multi-layer functional metabolomics workflow that incorporates an LC-MS/MS-based metal infusion assay in combination with microfractionation-based bioassays against Phytophthora infestans and metal-binding assays to map bioactivity from Serratia marcescens extracts. MS/MS analysis and feature-based molecular networking supported the annotation of activity-associated metabolites, including prodigiosin, serratiochelins, and an uncharacterized putative serratiochelin analog designated serratiochelin G. Complementary chrome azurol S assays and post-column iron infusion provided evidence of iron-binding properties. Comparative genomic analysis and L-lysine supplementation supported a proposed biosynthetic origin of serratiochelin G involving cadaverine incorporation. This workflow enables metabolite prioritization by integrating non-targeted LC-MS/MS with chromatographically resolved bioactivity and complementary functional assays.

cards.title: Dissociable patterns of neurophysiological alterations during guided search in schizophrenia and autism: Evidence from fixation-related potentials, alpha modulation, and functional MRI.
cards.abstract: Schizophrenia (SZ) and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are associated with convergent differences in social perception relative to non-autistic, non-schizophrenia controls (NC), but divergent patterns of alterations in early visual activity. Here, we used multimodal imaging during the Guided Visual Search task to investigate the differential patterns of early visual alteration across SZ and ASD including superior colliculus (SC) and pulvinar nucleus. In Experiment 1, simultaneous eye tracking and EEG were obtained from 91 individuals (35 NC, 20 ASD, 36 SZ). Fixation-related potential (FRP) was time-locked to fixation onset. In Experiment 2, fMRI during Guided Search was obtained from a partly overlapping sample of 71 individuals (27 NC, 25 ASD, 19 SZ). In behavioral analyses, SZ was associated with significantly prolonged search time (d=.74, p=.003), which was attributable primarily to reduced mean saccade amplitude, whereas ASD was associated with a small advantage (d=.35), which was not statistically significant. In EEG analyses, SZ was associated with reduced amplitude of the FRP P1 (lambda) response (d=1.15, p<.0001) relative to NC that remained significant following control for saccade size (p<.0001), but with normal task-related modulation of background alpha activity. In contrast, ASD was associated with normal FRP amplitude and larger alpha suppression (d=.83, p=.007) that was attributable to increased alpha levels during pre-task fixation (at matched pre-onset alpha levels, d=.14, p=.66). Within SZ, P1 correlated with the MCCB composite (r=.56, p=.001). Within ASD, ADOS-2 Communication correlated with P1 (r=.51, p=.024) and with the broadband change from pre-onset to search (r=-.51, p=.030). In fMRI, SZ was associated with correlated activation reductions in the Visual1 (Sidak p<.001) and Visual2 (Sidak p=.022) networks and SC (Sidak p=.019), whereas activation was unaffected in the Dorsal Attention and Frontoparietal networks, Frontal Eye Fields and pulvinar. In ASD, activation was increased in pulvinar (Sidak p[≤].038), but unaffected elsewhere. Cortical activation patterns associated with SC activation resembled those associated with P1 generation across groups. Overall, the findings support bottom-up disturbances of visual processing in schizophrenia. In autism, pre-onset alpha was higher and task-related suppression was larger.

cards.title: Visually guided analysis of single cell proteomics data with SCP-Viz
cards.abstract: Single cell proteomics (SCP) is a specialized, but expanding, field of research today. One of many challenges slowing SCP adoption is the inherent instability of the proteome and the changes that can occur before getting cells to a lab for preparation and analysis. Additionally, all current interpretation tools require experienced bioinformaticians to make the step from data to interpretation. Here, we present a visual toolkit that can accept SCP data from any instrument or common data processing algorithm. To demonstrate the capabilities of this tool we apply it to the analysis of dried digests of single human cancer cells following long room temperature storage. Remarkably, proteomic depth of the dried and stored samples analyzed is higher than the original analysis of these same digests on a similar system directly following isolation. Critically, when comparing control and drug treated cells, both the protein abundance and post-translationally modified peptides appear similar in both fresh and stored digests of these single cells. These findings are highly encouraging and, taken together, may help decrease the barriers for entry and collaboration for the field of SCP globally.

cards.title: MetaboRx: R Shiny application for quality assessment and preprocessing of mass spectrometry-based metabolomics data
cards.abstract: Introduction Metabolomics datasets offer deep insights into biological systems, yet the multi-step analytical workflow, from sample preparation through instrumental analysis, introduces unwanted variation. This variation, including signal drift and batch effects can confound true biological signals. Although rigorous quality control (QC) and data preprocessing are prerequisites for downstream analysis, existing workflows are often fragmented, time-consuming, and inaccessible to non-experts. Objectives To develop a user-friendly software tool for rapid quality assessment and rigorous preprocessing of metabolomics feature tables. Methods MetaboRx is an R Shiny application that integrates orthogonal quality metrics into a single workflow, enabling systematic and transparent evaluation of metabolomics data before and after preprocessing. The application identifies formatting errors and analytically unreliable features and provides flexible preprocessing and visualization options. Results MetaboRx is freely available at https://github.com/ETaylorLab/MetaboRx. Using a semi-targeted LC-MS metabolomics dataset from mouse plasma, perturbed with simulated low-quality data, we demonstrate how MetaboRx facilitates detection of data quality problems, reduces unwanted variation, and prepares data for downstream analysis. Conclusion MetaboRx streamlines metabolomics data quality assessment and preprocessing through an interactive and integrated workflow. The application may improve consistency and reproducibility in metabolomics studies by supporting informed preprocessing decisions and transparent reporting of QC outcomes prior to downstream analysis.

cards.title: Sample preparation for mass spectrometry-based tissue (phospho)proteomics
cards.abstract: This protocol describes the workflow for the preparation of tissue samples for proteome and phosphoproteome analyses using mass spectrometry. The tissue samples are cryogenically pulverized and homogenized in a sucrose-based buffer to ensure proper tissue disruption. For depletion of lipid contaminants, proteins are purified using chloroform-methanol precipitation, followed by a resuspension in a urea-based buffer for enzymatic digestion. Peptides are desalted and enriched for phosphopeptides prior LC-MS/MS analysis. The workflow was developed for skin biopsies but is compatible with a broad range of tissue types.

cards.title: Validation of Primary and Hospital Care Resource Use and Cost Estimates in OMOP-mapped vs Source Healthcare Administrative Datasets.
cards.abstract: To assess whether estimates of primary and hospital care resource use and costs from Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model (CDM) mapped data are consistent with source healthcare administrative datasets and to discuss implications for OMOP-based health economic analyses. We conducted a retrospective cohort study (2010-2018) of women aged >50 years with a fragility fracture. Analyses were performed in parallel using source Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum linked to Hospital Episode Statistics data and two OMOP-based strategies: OMOP-standard (standardised concepts only) and OMOP-source (also including source variables). Primary and hospital care utilisation and costs were estimated over two years. Mean differences were summarised with bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals. Cohorts were comparable (23,106 source; 22,900 OMOP), with similar characteristics and follow-up. Resource utilisation was consistent across databases (<1% difference). Total cost differences were 2.2% (OMOP-standard) and 1.7% (OMOP-source, not statistically significant). Primary care, inpatient and outpatient cost differences were ≤3% among costed records. Emergency care costs were ∼21% lower in both OMOP strategies, reflecting a different costing method rather than mapping fidelity (0.1% when the same method was applied to source data). Discrepancies were mainly due to costing assumptions, and less so to incomplete vocabularies and structural constraints. OMOP-mapped data produced resource use estimates highly consistent and aggregate cost estimates concordant with source data. Remaining cost discrepancies were concentrated in specific settings and reduced when source variables were used. Refining mapping and costing approaches will improve accuracy and support federated economic research using OMOP-CDM.

cards.title: Intrinsic capacity and hip fracture: A multinational analysis across 15 countries.
cards.abstract: Managing hip fracture (HF) risk in older adults remains a major clinical challenge, with current prevention strategies heavily reliant on pharmacological agents that carry serious adverse events. The World Health Organization's intrinsic capacity (IC) framework offers a function-centred alternative, but robust cross-population evidence is limited. We harmonized data from four longitudinal ageing cohorts across 15 countries (n = 33,452). IC was assessed across five domains, with higher scores indicating greater capacity. The primary outcome was incident HF. We employed Cox proportional hazards models, random-effects meta-analyses, bidirectional cross-lagged panel networks, and sensitivity analyses to examine baseline IC, its domains, and changes in IC over time. Higher baseline IC was associated with lower incident HF risk in the fully adjusted pooled individual-level analysis (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.975, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.966-0.985; p < 0.001). Associations were significant in CHARLS, ELSA, and SHARE, but not in HRS (HR = 0.986, 95% CI: 0.972-1.000; p = 0.0555). The random-effects summary HR was 0.951 (95% CI: 0.916-0.987), with substantial between-cohort heterogeneity (I2 = 89.43%), indicating that the association was not uniform across settings. Higher cognitive, locomotor, and psychological capacities were associated with lower HF risk, whereas sensory capacity showed a small positive association and vitality was not significantly associated with HF. Evidence for IC changes was mixed: trajectory associations varied with score weighting, and continuous IC change was not significantly associated with HF in the pooled analysis. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the baseline IC association. Higher baseline IC was associated with lower incident HF risk overall, but the HRS finding and substantial heterogeneity do not support a uniform association across national or cultural settings. Its value for HF risk prediction requires further evaluation.

cards.title: Polarized Canine Liver Organoid Monolayers Capture Features of Western Diet-Induced Hepatic Metabolic Reprogramming Across Transcriptomic, Lipidomic, and Biogenic Amine Signatures
cards.abstract: Liver responses to Western-diet (WD) exposure remain incompletely defined, partly because conventional rodent models and immortalized hepatic cell lines incompletely recapitulate species-specific features of liver biology. Here, we established polarized epithelial monolayers from canine liver organoids derived from healthy beagles and beagles exposed to a WD for 8 weeks. We then used this platform to characterize diet-induced hepatic reprogramming and to explore differential responses to two SGLT2 inhibitors, dapagliflozin and bexagliflozin. The monolayers developed reproducible apical-basal polarity, with transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) values of 123-335 {Omega} cm2, enabling compartment-resolved sampling. Bulk transcriptomics, lipidomics, and biogenic amine profiling each independently separated WD-derived from healthy monolayers. Periodic acid-Schiff staining provided qualitative support for this diet-associated molecular signature, showing increased carbohydrate-rich material consistent with glycogen accumulation in WD-derived monolayers. By contrast, 24-hour apical exposure to dapagliflozin or bexagliflozin at 20 M produced no detectable transcriptomic differences and only weak, context-dependent metabolomic separation, which was restricted to the apical compartment in the untargeted metabolomics dataset. These findings establish canine liver organoid-derived polarized monolayers as a tractable in vitro platform that captures WD-induced hepatic reprogramming across transcriptomic, lipidomic, and biogenic amine readouts, while providing a foundation for future targeted studies of candidate interventions for diet-associated hepatic dysfunction.

cards.title: In Vitro Budding and Floatation based enrichment of Mitochondria-derived Vesicles for Proteomics Mammalian Hearts
cards.abstract: Mitochondria-derived vesicles (MDVs) are carriers involved in mitochondrial quality control, yet their biogenesis and trafficking remain poorly understood. We describe an in vitro protocol to generate MDVs from animal heart mitochondria. The workflow allows for isolation of distinct MDV subsets and their proteomic analyses. The protocol improves vesicle yield and purity for NTA, TEM, or western blotting-based readouts. This facilitates the identification of novel MDV cargo and regulators of MDV biogenesis in different model organisms. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Rajeev T et al., [1].

cards.title: Large language models complement established workflows for mechanistic model construction and refinement in systems biology
cards.abstract: Mechanistic models provide a framework for describing, understanding, and predicting biological processes, but their development requires an interdisciplinary team with expertise in biology, mathematics, and computation. Here we present Octomod, a multi-agent workflow based on large language models (LLMs) that integrates biological knowledge retrieval, model construction, parameter estimation, and hypothesis testing. Built on established software tools, including AMICI and pyPESTO, and community standards, including SBML and PEtab, Octomod supports model development and refinement through natural-language interaction with a user. The agents' proposals must pass defined checks and the user's decision before they are used. Every input, model, check, and decision is recorded, so that model building remains transparent and reproducible. We applied Octomod to four problems. Three used published data and differ in model size and in how much the user guided the run: Octomod constructed a model that matched a published model without user guidance, supported the interactive refinement of a gene-regulatory model, and built models of cell-cell communication that explained the responses of five immune cell types to different stimuli. In the fourth application, on newly generated and unpublished lipidomics data, Octomod helped to determine which processes the measurements could inform, identify unresolved label fluxes, and reduce a supplied model to those processes. Together, these results show how LLMs can strengthen and complement established workflows for constructing and refining biologically informed models.

cards.title: Multimodal imaging links molecular identity with nanoscale-resolved 3D cell morphology in opossum cortical cultures
cards.abstract: In the mammalian central nervous system (CNS), the ability to regenerate after injury drops sharply in the first weeks after birth, but how this change is reflected in cell morphology and organization is still not fully understood. Here we cultivated cortical cell cultures from the gray short-tailed opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and compared cells derived from early postnatal pups (postnatal day 3-6, "Pyoung") with those from older pups (postnatal day 16-18, "Pold"), which differ in their capacity to regenerate after injury. For each culture, we assessed marker-defined cellular composition using fluorescently labeled markers for neurons, glia, and immature/progenitor cells, and characterized their nanoscale-resolved three-dimensional morphology using label-free scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM). Pyoung cultures exhibited active change in shape over time, contained a higher proportion of immature SOX2 cells, and grew more neurites (TUJ1) into the lesion site after injury. Moreover, Pold cultures showed more stable soma size (e.g., thickness, area, volume), a larger astroglial (SOX9) population early in culture, and a glia-dominated lesion response. These early astroglia included more immature or reactive (vimentin) astrocytes. SICM further revealed cellular bridges across the lesion, ridges left in the substrate by the injury, and aligned neurite outgrowth. Across all measurements, changes in molecular markers were associated with corresponding changes in cell morphology. This multimodal combination of fluorescence labeling and SICM therefore relates marker-defined cellular composition to physical organization across micro- and nanoscale features during and after postnatal in vitro development.

cards.title: Impacts of Environmental Nickel and Chromium Exposure on the Blood Proteome of House Sparrows (Passer domesticus) in New Caledonia
cards.abstract: New Caledonia holds some of the world's largest ultramafic mineral deposits, and nickel (Ni) smelting operations have created a gradient of Ni and chromium (Cr) contamination across the archipelago. Molecular impacts of Ni and Cr toxicity on wildlife remain largely unexplored. Here, we used the house sparrow (Passer domesticus) as a sentinel species to characterise the blood proteomic response to Ni and Cr exposure near the Doniambo smelter in Noumea. Blood was collected from 52 free-living sparrows across 18 sites classified by soil metal concentration. Plasma and blood cell pellet fractions were analysed by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Plasma proteomics identified histidine-rich glycoprotein (HRG) as the most prominent responder, with approximately 2.1-fold elevation in exposed relative to low-exposure birds. HRG contains a conserved histidine-rich region that binds cations including divalent nickel, and paired plasma-liver analysis confirmed hepatic-driven synthesis. Blood cell pellet proteomics revealed that Ni-Cr co-exposure predominantly disrupts the nuclear compartment: histone depletion indicated chromatin collapse, NUP153 dysregulation impaired nuclear pore function, and VRK1/TRIP13 upregulation suggested DNA damage response activation coupled with mitotic checkpoint override. Concurrent RNA processing collapse (DDX17, DHX15, RBMX, ALYREF) and changes in telomere-associated proteins (TERF2IP, hnRNPA1 and VRK1) implicated disrupted genome maintenance. These findings identify HRG as a candidate plasma biomarker of Ni-Cr exposure and reveal a coordinated nuclear toxicity signature linking heavy metal contamination to DNA damage and epigenetic disruption in a free-living vertebrate.

cards.title: Basic-peptide depletion and precursor masking in bottom-up proteomics
cards.abstract: Biomarker proteomics studies report protein identities at the canonical precursor level, yet the underlying mass-spectrometry evidence consists of peptides whose physicochemical properties may diverge from the annotated protein. We reanalyzed peptide-level evidence from public datasets with a proteoform-aware pipeline that maps detected peptides to canonical sequences under a five-level confidence taxonomy, computes sequence-derived physicochemical features for precursors, peptides, and detected regions, and tests class-composition bias against digestion-matched backgrounds. Across ten public studies spanning five result-file formats and 70,020 peptide-evidence rows, detected peptides are depleted in the basic isoelectric-point class relative to their own proteins' theoretical tryptic peptides (fixed-effect odds ratio 0.45, 95% CI 0.44-0.46; leave-one-study-out envelope 0.44-0.49). The depletion is absent among fully tryptic peptides (OR 1.06) and concentrates in missed-cleavage peptides (OR 0.62-0.57), is invariant to detected-abundance stratification, and retains its direction under three independent pI-calculator models. Case studies reveal both directions of precursor-centric masking. Two orthogonal validations ground the framework: a digestion-free synthetic-peptide analysis (basic-class odds ratio 0.73, 95% CI 0.71-0.76 under standard DDA) and a paired top-down benchmark, in which detected regions recover top-down sequence space (90% of spans overlapped) but do not delimit proteoform boundaries (8% containment). Pipeline, data, and code are public.

cards.title: National Trends, Predictors, Healthcare Utilization, and Disparities of Post-Traumatic Endophthalmitis Following Open Globe Injury: A Nationwide Analysis of the National Inpatient Sample, 2016-2022.
cards.abstract: Post‑traumatic endophthalmitis (PTE) is a rare but vision‑threatening complication of open globe injury (OGI). Data on incidence, risk factors, and healthcare utilization at the population level are still scarce. This study evaluates national trends, predictors, and outcomes of PTE after OGI in the United States from 2016 to 2022. We analyzed the National Inpatient Sample (NIS), including all acute OGI admissions with a primary diagnosis or globe-repair procedure. PTE was defined with ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes. We used survey-weighted logistic and log-linear regression to assess healthcare utilization outcomes. We used joinpoint regression to assess temporal trends. Stratified models assessed pediatric vs adult risk profiles. Among 4,691 OGI admissions (weighted estimate, 23,455), 93 patients (1.98%) developed PTE. The strongest positive predictors were corneal ulcer (OR 17.81, 95% CI 8.96-33.81) and retinal detachment (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.38-5.65), while rupture (OR 0.31), avulsion (OR 0.05), and orbital floor fracture (OR 0.03) were associated with lower odds of PTE. PTE was not associated with increased in-hospital mortality (0% vs 0.85%) but was associated with increased length of hospital stay (adjusted geometric mean ratio 1.42, 95% CI 1.18-1.71). Incidence was stable from 2016 to 2022 (APC +5.86%, p = 0.372). PTE after OGI is rare but results in a prolonged hospital stay. Corneal ulceration and retinal detachment are key risk factors, and age modifies the impact of IOFB. These findings inform risk stratification, resource allocation, and targeted interventions for the prevention of visual morbidity in ocular trauma patients.

cards.title: Computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation of tibial fractures.
cards.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of computer-assisted Taylor spatial frame (TSF) for correcting malalignment after unilateral external fixation (UEF) of tibial fractures. This retrospective cohort study included 18 patients with tibial misalignment after UEF between February 2019 and February 2024. Using the TSF technique, X-ray parameters (deformity, frame, and mounting) were entered into software to generate a six-axis correction prescription. Reduction time, number of X-ray exposures, total external fixation duration, clinical fracture healing time, complications, and functional recovery were recorded. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used to compare preoperative and final visual analogue scale (VAS) scores because the paired differences were not normally distributed; data are presented as mean (range) or median (interquartile range [IQR]). All 18 patients were followed up for a mean of 14.9 months (range: 12-18 months). Satisfactory reduction was achieved in all cases after TSF adjustment. Mean reduction time was 19.0 minutes (range, 15-24 minutes), and patients received a mean of 1.4 X-ray exposures (range, 1-3). Clinical fracture healing occurred after a mean of 24.0 weeks (range, 21-29 weeks), and total external fixation lasted a mean of 25.2 weeks (range, 22-30 weeks). Johner-Wruhs ratings at final follow-up were excellent in 15 patients and good in 3 (100% excellent/good). Median VAS scores improved from 7 (IQR, 6-8) before surgery to 1 (IQR, 0-2) at final follow-up (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Z = -3.77, P < .001). Superficial pin tract infections developed in 3 patients (16.7%; 3/18) and were controlled with oral antibiotics and dressing changes. No patient had deep infection, pin loosening, nonunion, or bone exposure. In this small, single-arm retrospective cohort, all 18 patients achieved satisfactory reduction with computer-assisted TSF, and adjustment times were short. No patient underwent secondary open reduction or fixation. These preliminary findings suggest that TSF may serve as a feasible minimally invasive option for correcting early malalignment following UEF of tibial fractures; however, multicenter controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these results.

cards.title: Zebrafish models for investigating skeletal muscle aging and sarcopenia.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is characterized by progressive loss of skeletal muscle strength, mass, and function during aging, driven by impaired proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered metabolism, regenerative failure, and neuromuscular decline. Experimental models are needed to determine how these processes drive muscle degeneration and identify testable therapeutic mechanisms. Zebrafish combine whole-animal physiology with genetic manipulation, live imaging, and scalable phenotypic analysis, making them well suited to this purpose. Natural-aging, telomerase-deficient, dexamethasone-induced, high-fat-diet, and genetically defined zebrafish models each reproduce distinct structural, functional, metabolic, regenerative, or neuromuscular changes relevant to sarcopenia. In this Review, we compare study designs, measured endpoints, and mechanistic evidence to distinguish age-associated phenotypes from responses to induced stresses or defined molecular perturbations. Natural-aging models capture spontaneous age-associated changes in muscle structure, performance, and mitochondrial integrity; telomerase-deficient models reveal defects in tissue maintenance and regeneration; and dexamethasone- and high-fat-diet-induced models enable controlled analysis of proteostatic and metabolic stress. Genetic models directly test relationships between molecular perturbations and muscle phenotypes. Current studies, however, have notable limitations: swimming performance reflects whole-animal physiology rather than muscle strength, many markers do not directly measure pathway activity, and some models represent specific stress rather than primary sarcopenia. Across these models, shared phenotypes do not establish a common causal mechanism; model-specific findings require validation during natural aging and in mammalian and human studies.

cards.title: Physiological mapping and prediction reveal stress-responsive translation initiation landscapes
cards.abstract: Translation initiation defines the protein output of the transcriptome, but its physiological dynamics in cells and tissues remain incompletely characterized. Here we develop TISCA2, an inhibitor-free method that captures eIF5B-associated initiating ribosomes to map translation initiation sites genome-wide. By directly identifying start sites rather than inferring translation from elongating-ribosome periodicity, TISCA2 improves the detection of short and overlapping translons. Translation of a subset of TISCA2-identified translons is supported by N-terminal proteomics and HLA-I immunopeptidomics. The arsenite-induced integrated stress response broadly redistributes start-site usage, reducing upstream initiation in favor of downstream initiation. TISCA2 further reveals tissue-specific initiation landscapes in vivo, with increased detection of downstream candidate start sites in the testis. Finally, we develop IncepTIS, a sequence-based deep learning model that predicts position-resolved and condition-dependent initiation landscapes. IncepTIS-guided optimization generates de novo mRNA 5' leaders with stress-responsive initiation patterns. Together, TISCA2 and IncepTIS provide an experimental and computational framework for mapping, predicting and engineering translation initiation in mammalian cells and tissues.

cards.title: Compartment-Resolved Matrisome Shifts During Postnatal Tendon Maturation in Mice
cards.abstract: Tendons acquire their load-bearing capacity during the first month of postnatal growth, driven by the extensive remodeling of the extracellular matrix (ECM). While the role of specific individual components to this process have been well characterized, a comprehensive assessment of how the tendon matrisome changes during this critical window is lacking. This, in part, is due to the challenges associated with solubilization of mature ECM, which is underrepresented by conventical proteomic approaches. To address this, we performed compartment-resolved proteomics on murine Achilles and plantaris tendons at postnatal days 0 (P0), P14, and P28. Sequential extraction methods leveraged a CHAPS-soluble fraction, capturing cellular and soluble matrisome proteins, from the insoluble mature ECM fraction, solubilized by guanidine hydrochloride and hydroxylamine hydrochloride and separately analyzed by label-free quantitative LC-MS/MS. Analysis shows that the two compartments followed distinct trajectories during maturation. The insoluble matrix was dominated by collagenous proteins, which increased from 95% to over 99% of the identified signal intensity, and its composition was largely established by P14. Within the soluble matrisome compartment, collagens increased from 50% to over 60% by P14, accompanied by dynamic regulation of proteins implicated in collagen processing (P4HA1, PCOLCE), crosslinking (LOX, LOXL2), and regulators of collagen fibril assembly and growth (DCN, BGN, FMOD, THBS3, THBS4). Beyond these established regulators, we observed dynamic regulation of less-characterized fibril-associated proteoglycans (KERA, OGN, CHAD), matricellular (COMP, POSTN, MATN2), and angiogenic regulatorily proteins (SERPINF1, ECM1). Together, this work establishes a comprehensive protein-level reference for postnatal tendon maturating, provides new insights into the molecular regulation of functional tendon development.

cards.title: A digital twin roadmap for adult spinal deformity.
cards.abstract: Adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery is a high-risk, high-cost domain in which preoperative planning plays a critical role in determining alignment goals, surgical strategy, and the balance between deformity correction and treatment-related complications, yet decisions still rely heavily on static radiographs, classification systems, and surgeon experience. In parallel, medical digital twins, continuously updated, patient-specific computational models that simulate alternative treatment paths, are emerging in other medical disciplines but have not been formally articulated for ASD. In this narrative review, we adapt the recently proposed five-component medical digital twin framework (patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and synchronization policy) to adult spinal deformity by mapping each component to ASD-specific data sources, computational models, clinical workflows, and validation pathways. We outline how existing tools in ASD, including classification systems, frailty and bone-health metrics, biomechanical modeling, motion analysis, mobile health data, and machine learning risk calculators, can serve as inputs to an ASD digital twin. We highlight priority use cases, such as choosing the magnitude of surgery, bone-health-aware planning, pelvic fixation and rod strategy, and selection among open, hybrid, and minimally invasive approaches, all reframed as comparative simulations with explicit uncertainty bands. Finally, we propose a staged roadmap, from minimal viable twins evaluated via retrospective replay, to shadow-mode deployment, to oversighted clinical pilots, while detailing challenges in data harmonization, model validity, governance, and equity. Rather than claiming that a mature ASD digital twin exists today, this work offers a practical blueprint for how digital twins could evolve into auditable, patient-specific decision-support tools that augment, rather than replace, surgeon judgment in spinal deformity surgery.

cards.title: [Healthcare structures and diagnostic strategies for spinal trauma in childhood and adolescence : Results of a survey in German-speaking countries].
cards.abstract: Spinal injuries in childhood and adolescence are rare, accounting for 1-4% of all fractures. This study aimed to record the structures of healthcare and diagnostic strategies in German-speaking countries, evaluate the structural resources and assess the awareness and implementation of the CHILDSPINE treatment recommendations. An anonymized online cross-sectional survey was conducted between July and September 2023 among members of orthopedic, trauma and pediatric surgical societies. The questionnaire consisted of 31 items covering demographics, clinical protocols (standard operating procedures, SOP), infrastructure, case volumes and clinical case studies regarding diagnostics. The questionnaire was developed by consensus within the working group; no formal pilot testing or validation was performed. As the access link could be forwarded freely within the societies, a response rate cannot be calculated; the proportion of fully completed questionnaires (159/169; 94.1%) and the item-level completeness (98.8%) are reported instead. Of the 169 participants (79.9% orthopedics/trauma surgery), 50.3% worked at supraregional trauma centers. Hospitals with higher case volumes (> 8 cases/year) had significantly more frequently diagnostic SOP (37% vs. 10%), pediatric-specific computed tomography/magnetic resonance imaging (CT/MRI) protocols (84% vs. 53%) and specialized orthotic inventories (65% vs. 34%). Only 25.5% of respondents had read the thematic issue containing the CHILDSPINE treatment recommendations. In the case vignettes the decision for primary MRI was significantly influenced by patient age (more frequent in younger children), medical specialty (neurosurgery with a higher tendency for MRI) and seniority (chief physicians more likely to order MRI than attending physicians), whereas no statistically significant effect was demonstrable for awareness of the CHILDSPINE treatment recommendations or for institutional case volume. The care of the very rare pediatric spinal trauma in German-speaking countries remains highly heterogeneous. As the publication of treatment recommendations alone has been insufficient to unify clinical practice, the findings suggest that national guidelines combined with structured implementation strategies, e.g., defined minimum standards, imaging algorithms developed jointly with (pediatric) radiology and structured training formats, could contribute to more uniform care.

cards.title: Joint association of frailty and depressive symptoms with new-onset chronic kidney disease in middle-aged and older adults: a longitudinal analysis from the CHARLS cohort.
cards.abstract: Although frailty and depressive symptoms have both been associated with the risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD), their joint association with incident CKD and potential mediation pathways remains unclear. This analysis used data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Frailty was quantified using a 35-item deficit-accumulation frailty index and depressive symptoms were defined using the CES-D-10. New-onset CKD was ascertained by self-reported physician diagnosis or an eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Cox regression models were used to estimate associations, and mediation analyses were conducted to explore potential explanatory pathways. During a mean follow-up of 6.87 years, 327 of 6,854 participants (4.8%) developed CKD. Depressive symptoms and frailty were each independently linked to incident CKD, with HRs of 1.50 (95% CI: 1.19-1.88) and 1.95 (95% CI: 1.52-2.49), respectively. Participants with coexisting depressive symptoms and frailty showed the greatest risk compared with those with neither condition (HR = 2.10, 95% CI: 1.59-2.77). In mediation analysis, frailty accounted for an estimated 66% of the observed association between depressive symptoms and CKD. Coexisting frailty and depressive symptoms were associated with the highest risk of incident CKD. Mediation analysis suggested that frailty may partly explain the observed link between depressive symptoms and CKD. Concurrent screening for depressive symptoms and frailty may help improve CKD risk stratification in aging adults.

cards.title: timePlex: Increasing mass spectrometry throughput using time-encoded sample multiplexing
cards.abstract: Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) can enable precise and accurate quantification of analytes at high-sensitivity, but the rate at which samples can be analyzed remains limited. Throughput can be increased by data-independent-acquisition (DIA) using short separation times and by multiplexing samples in the mass domain with plexDIA; yet multiplexing along one dimension scales throughput only linearly with plex. To enable combinatorial scaling of proteomics throughput, we developed a complementary DIA strategy that multiplexes samples in the time domain, termed `timePlex'. timePlex staggers and overlaps the separation periods of individual samples. This strategy is orthogonal to isotopic multiplexing, which enables combinatorial multiplexing in mass and time domains, and thus multiplicatively increased throughput. We demonstrate this with a 27-plex (3-timePlex and 9-plexDIA) exceeding 1,200 samples (4M protein datapoints) per day. These results establish timePlex as a framework for multiplexing both label-free and labeled samples that supports sensitive and accurate protein quantification and combinatorial scaling.

cards.title: An Integrated Experimental and Informatics Strategy Enables Large Proteoform Identification in Top-Down Proteomics
cards.abstract: Top-down proteomics enables identification and characterization of intact proteoforms, preserving information on co-occurring sequence variations and post-translational modifications. However, identifying large proteoforms remains challenging due to an exponential decrease in signal-to-noise ratio with increasing molecular weight, interference from coeluting smaller species, unresolved precursor isotopic envelopes, difficulty obtaining informative MS/MS spectra, and limitations of current informatics tools. To address these challenges, here we present an integrated experimental and informatics strategy combining protein separation, data acquisition, precursor mass assignment, and MS/MS interpretation. First, we demonstrate that online two-dimensional liquid chromatography coupling size-exclusion and reversed-phase separations enables facile detection of large proteoforms. We then utilize a precursor mass correction strategy to enable conventional database searching of data-dependent acquisition (DDA) data containing isotopically unresolved precursors. Finally, we use data-independent acquisition (DIA) optimized for large proteins to enhance fragment signal and enable identification through intact-mass-guided candidate discovery and MS/MS validation. Applied to human heart tissue, the integrated strategy identified 703 nonredundant proteoforms from 236 unique proteins, including 65 proteins >30 kDa and 22 proteins >50 kDa, with identifications extending to 223 kDa. This integrated strategy bridges the detection-to-identification gap for large proteins and expands the accessible mass range of discovery top-down proteomics.

cards.title: The Findings Workflow: An agentic, collaborative, provenance-tracked framework for scientific data analysis with Claude Code
cards.abstract: Scientists presented with quantitative data often face two related problems: confidence that an analysis is statistically and computationally correct, and provenance sufficient to reproduce the resulting figures and conclusions. Large language models (LLMs) can make sophisticated analyses accessible through a collaborative, conversational interface, but unstructured use can worsen both problems by producing plausible but incorrect results and obscuring the steps that produced them. Here we present the Findings Workflow, a free, open-source Claude Code plugin designed to retain the flexibility of conversational LLM-assisted analysis while placing it within a structured, verifiable, and reproducible environment. The workflow uses staged, gated progression to ensure the science, metadata, and data are understood and tested data loaders are built before downstream analysis begins. Specialized subagents perform statistical analysis, programming, visualization, research, reporting, and validation, with independent review incorporated throughout. The plugin also provides vetted analysis templates, conventions, and methodological guidance that serve as trusted sources of opinion when deciding how analyses should be performed. Scientists remain actively involved throughout, exploring their data and directing the analysis through natural-language conversation, while the workflow supplies structure, verification, and persistent state around that collaboration. Findings are recorded automatically together with the data, code, methods, figures, and provenance needed to reproduce them. We demonstrate the workflow with a worked example that reproduces central findings from a published plasma extracellular vesicle proteomics dataset examining Alzheimer's disease (Mag-Net). Together, these features are designed to make LLM-assisted scientific analysis easier to trust, inspect, and reproduce without sacrificing its conversational and exploratory nature.

cards.title: Bazi Bushen Attenuates Skeletal Muscle Decline Associated With Oestrogen Deficiency and Modulates FGFR1/ERK Signalling.
cards.abstract: Postmenopausal oestrogen deficiency is associated with skeletal muscle loss and functional decline, thereby increasing the risk of sarcopenia in women. Considering the safety risks linked to hormone replacement therapy (HRT), alternative strategies are needed to attenuate skeletal muscle decline after menopause. A total of 24 female C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 6 per group): Sham-operated (SHAM), ovariectomized (OVX), OVX treated with estradiol valerate (OVX + E2) and OVX treated with Bazi Bushen (OVX + BZBS). Skeletal muscle mass and function were evaluated in four groups. RNA sequencing was applied to explore the molecular mechanisms and key signalling pathways underlying BZBS-induced muscle protection. We further examined the role of the FGFR1/ERK signalling pathway in mediating the effects of BZBS on myogenic differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts. The results showed that OVX mice had reduced grip strength and skeletal muscle mass, increased fat accumulation, reduced lean mass and impaired metabolic activity. These phenotypic alterations were accompanied by myofiber atrophy, increased collagen staining, endocrine perturbations and elevated expression of p16, p21, Atrogin-1 and MuRF1. BZBS ameliorated these abnormalities. RNA-seq suggested that FGF/MAPK signalling may be involved. In D-gal-treated C2C12 myoblasts, BZBS reduced Atrogin-1 and MuRF1 expression while restoring MYHC and MYOG expression. Mechanistically, BZBS suppressed FGFR1/ERK signalling activation and bFGF partially reversed the protective effects of BZBS. Taken together, these findings suggest that FGFR1/ERK signalling may contribute to the protective effects of BZBS. Our findings provide evidence for the beneficial effects of BZBS on skeletal muscle deterioration associated with oestrogen deficiency.

cards.title: Dietary fibre responses emerge through host-dietary regime interplay: Apple pectin modulates immune reactivity in adult zebrafish
cards.abstract: Dietary fibres are rarely consumed independently. Instead, they form part of an overall diet that includes dietary fibres from different sources, in varying amounts and consumed under different feeding patterns. Here, we tested how dietary regimes containing apple pectin, oat {beta}-glucan, or cellulose shaped the host. We analysed gut microbiome composition by 16S rRNA sequencing, measured brain and intestinal SCFA profiles by targeted metabolomics, and assessed immunomodulation by measuring gene expression systemically in the blood and locally in the spleen, as well as intestinal enzyme activity. The dietary intervention was conducted for 12 weeks on adult female and male zebrafish (Danio rerio). Our results show that the gut microbial composition can be relatively stable across different dietary fibre exposure patterns yet still vary significantly between the sexes. Additionally, the effect of sex on the gut microbiome may become more evident when dietary fibres are administered at high dosages, but intermittently. Dietary fibre regimes can alter intestinal short-chain fatty acid profiles more readily than brain profiles, which show a stronger sexually dimorphic response. Interestingly, apple pectin modulated the zebrafish immune response through interactions dependent on the overall regime, tissue, sex, and host immune status. Notably, tissue il1b gene expression differed depending on how apple pectin was administered and the host's physiological state. Collectively, our study emphasises the highly context-specific effects of dietary fibres, shaped by the dynamic interplay between the overall dietary regime and intertwined host factors.

cards.title: PepPr: De Novo peptide sequencing with peptide priors
cards.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based peptide sequencing underpins proteomics. Database search confines to predefined candidates, whereas de novo peptide sequencing (DNPS) struggles with incomplete spectra. Existing hybrid methods use databases only for post hoc correction or retrieve previously identified spectra to guide decoding. We instead combine DNPS with a peptide prior: a language model fitted to a reference proteome, tolerating variants yet uncertain on strongly divergent sequences. Relative to prior-free DNPS, our implementation, PepPr, improved reference peptide identification and improved rather than suppressed variant identification. Using a related proteome as prior, it matched or outperformed homology-driven database search, and its gain over prior-free DNPS grew with relatedness. In antibody sequencing, it improved recovery of peptides spanning the variable-constant boundary, deamidation calls, and assembly, while preserving recall of hypervariable regions inaccessible to database search. Peptide priors thus bring reference knowledge into DNPS without limiting discovery.

cards.title: Pediatric emergency medicine in Lebanon: Physician-perceived comfort levels, challenges, and educational needs.
cards.abstract: Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) is a rapidly evolving subspecialty that improves the quality and safety of care for children. Despite global advancements, PEM remains underdeveloped in many low- and middle-income countries, including Lebanon. Despite a large pediatric population there is no formal paediatric emergency medicine system in place, and care largely delivered by physicians practicing without standardized or specialized training. This lack of dedicated PEM training and organized emergency care pathways may compromise the timely recognition and management of pediatric emergencies, potentially affecting patient outcomes. The present study aimed to assess physicians perceived comfort in managing pediatric emergencies, identify training gaps, and explore systemic and institutional challenges affecting pediatric emergency care in Lebanon. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted among physicians involved in pediatric emergency care across Lebanon. The questionnaire assessed self-reported comfort in managing pediatric emergencies, perceived challenges, and priorities for training and PEM workforce development. Responses from 59 physicians were analysed. Most were male 38 (64.4%), with a median clinical experience of 7 years. General pediatricians represented 28 (47.5%), emergency physicians 17 (28.8%), PEM specialists 8 (13.6%), and pediatric intensivists 6 (10.2%). Physicians reported high perceived comfort in pediatric fluid management 52(88.1%), chest X-ray interpretation 46 (77.9%), and general pediatric emergencies 42 (71.2%), but lower comfort in procedural sedation, suturing 35 (59.6%), fracture stabilization 35 (59.4%), and Extended Focused Assessment Sonography in Trauma (EFAST) 22 (41.8%). General pediatricians reported greater comfort with general pediatric emergencies, while emergency-focused physicians had higher comfort with trauma-related skills and procedural interventions. Major challenges included gaps in practical and theoretical training, limited hospital infrastructure, shortages of devices and human resources, and the need for continuing medical education. Nearly all participants 57 (96.6%) supported the establishing a dedicated PEM fellowship, highlighting training priorities in trauma, medical emergencies, life support, procedural skills, and pediatric imaging. Pediatric emergency care in Lebanon is constrained by gaps in skills, training, and systemic resources. There is an urgent need to establish standardized PEM training pathways, enhance curricula, and strengthen system-level preparedness. Implementing these measures will support a competent PEM workforce and improve the quality and safety of emergency care for children nationwide.

cards.title: Examining the patient- and system-related forces influencing the responsiveness of hip fracture care in Zimbabwe: Findings from an ethnographic study.
cards.abstract: Rapidly rising longevity and the projected increase in fractures among older adults in Southern Africa underscores the necessity to strengthen healthcare systems in the region. Delivering orthopaedic care to older people within a multi-disciplinary framework is widely recommended. This ethnographic study sought to examine the responsiveness of hip fracture care in Zimbabwe and the influence of patient- and system-related forces We used ethnographic methods to examine the experiences of patients and caregivers and characterise hip fracture care provision. Case studies were undertaken with 40 patients (22 male, 18 female) and 33 caregivers (6 male, 27 female), including family members and friends. These data were complemented by interviews and observations of clinical practice with 42 healthcare professionals (23 female, 19 male) involved in the delivery of hip fracture services, including orthopaedic surgeons, physicians and physiotherapists. Participants were purposively sampled from six hospitals providing hip fracture care across Northern Zimbabwe. Snowball sampling was also used to recruit additional study participants. Data were analysed using an abductive analytical approach. Patients' and caregivers' experiences revealed lengthy hospital stays, poor communication concerning diagnosis and treatment, undignified continence management, and limited access to social support. Patients' experiences highlighted the importance of access to pain relief medication, and the impact of unaffordable care - elements distinct from those within current responsiveness frameworks. Health professionals explained how resource constraints, understaffing, and changes in pain management processes impacted their ability to meet patients' needs. Yet, their narratives told of the various actions they employed to circumvent health system constraints and respond to patient priorities. Considering these findings, we highlight key considerations for health systems responsiveness, including considering the role of socioeconomic factors. We also propose practical recommendations for improving responsive hip fracture care in Zimbabwe, such as developing guidelines for patient optimisation and standardisation of hip implant costs.

cards.title: Targeting the gut-bone axis in osteoporosis: probiotic interventions and other microbiota-based therapeutic strategies.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a systemic bone metabolic disorder characterized by impaired bone homeostasis and increased fracture susceptibility. With the rapid aging of the global population, the number of fractures related to osteoporosis continues to increase, along with persistently high rates of disability and mortality, thereby imposing a huge and constantly growing burden on the healthcare system. Emerging evidence indicates that probiotics, as key regulators of host metabolic and immune networks, play critical roles in the pathogenesis, progression, and therapeutic modulation of OP. Through a bidirectional regulatory network known as the gut-bone axis, probiotics influence the dynamic balance between bone formation and bone resorption via multiple interconnected mechanisms, including immune modulation, microbial metabolite production, intestinal barrier integrity, and endocrine signaling. Recent animal and clinical studies further demonstrate that targeted modulation of the gut microbiota to restore gut-bone axis homeostasis can significantly improve bone mineral density and related skeletal parameters, highlighting the translational potential of probiotic-based interventions. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms by which probiotics regulate bone metabolism and places particular emphasis on emerging microbiota-based mechanisms and therapeutic strategies, with a specific focus on probiotics, aiming to provide a theoretical framework and future translational directions for the development of innovative microbiota-based treatments for OP.

cards.title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
cards.abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

cards.title: Targeting Accelerated Aging in COPD: The AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COpd) Trial Design.
cards.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognized as a disease of accelerated biological aging characterized by progressive lung function decline, emphysema progression and multiple age-related comorbidities. Current therapies improve symptoms and reduce exacerbations but have limited effects on disease progression. Metformin has demonstrated anti-aging properties through modulation of pathways involved in oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cellular senescence, making it a potential disease-modifying treatment in COPD. AMICO (A Trial of Metformin In COPD) is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III trial conducted in anonymous. A total of 212 patients with clinically stable COPD, centrilobular emphysema on computed tomography, post-bronchodilator FEV1 40%-70% predicted and accelerated FEV1 decline (>40 mL·year-1) will be randomized (1:1) to receive metformin (850 mg twice daily) or matching placebo for 36 months in addition to standard COPD treatment. Assessments include pulmonary function, chest computed tomography, exercise capacity, health status, muscle strength, body composition, age associated comorbidities development and aging-related biomarkers.The primary endpoint is the annual rate of FEV1 decline over 36 months. Secondary endpoints include emphysema progression, changes in diffusing capacity, COPD Assessment Test score, 6-minute walk distance, BODE index, handgrip strength, exacerbations, major cardiovascular events, cancer incidence and renal dysfunction. AMICO is the first randomized trial specifically designed to evaluate metformin as a gerotherapeutic and disease-modifying intervention in COPD. The study may provide novel evidence supporting geroscience-based approaches to slow disease progression and improve long-term outcomes in patients with COPD.

cards.title: Harnessing the power of Scutellaria baicalensis: Advances in active compounds and their impact on skeletal system diseases (Review).
cards.abstract: Skeletal system diseases (SSDs) encompass a variety of conditions affecting bones, cartilage and joints, including osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis and osteosarcoma. These diseases significantly impair physical function, rank among the leading causes of disability worldwide, and can even lead to mortality, affecting the lives of hundreds of millions of individuals. Scutellaria baicalensis, a widely used traditional Chinese medicinal herb, is rich in flavonoids, including baicalein, baicalin, wogonin, oroxylin A and wogonoside. Given the increasing prevalence of SSDs and their profound impact on quality of life, existing research highlights the promising therapeutic effects of Scutellaria baicalensis. The present review explores the therapeutic potential of Scutellaria baicalensis and its active compounds in combating SSDs. By investigating their mechanisms of action, the current study highlights how these compounds influence key biological functions, including proliferation, apoptosis, senescence, inflammation, oxidative stress, ferroptosis and autophagy in stem cells, osteoblasts, chondrocytes, osteoclasts and immune cells. Furthermore, it explores critical signaling pathways such as MAPK, NF‑κB, AKT, mTOR, TGF‑β/Smad3, c‑Fos/AP‑1 and Wnt/β‑catenin. The present review also discusses various nanoparticle and microparticle drug delivery systems, including functionalized metal‑organic frameworks, injectable hydrogels and calcium polyphosphate microparticles, which are designed to improve the bioavailability and targeted delivery of active compounds from Scutellaria baicalensis, thereby enhancing their therapeutic efficacy. The current findings underscore the promising role of Scutellaria baicalensis in the management of SSDs, offering valuable insights into innovative treatment strategies and the intricate biological processes involved.

cards.title: Integrating Multidimensional Clinical Data to Develop a Visual Nomogram for Individualized Prediction of Postinfectious Bone Loss in Patients With Spinal Infection: Retrospective Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Postinfectious bone loss can lead to spinal instability and severe neurological complications, with potentially devastating outcomes. However, prognostic models to support individualized risk assessment remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a visual nomogram integrating multimodal clinical data to estimate postinfectious bone loss risk in patients with spinal infection and inform individualized monitoring strategies. This retrospective cohort study used consecutive sampling at Shandong Public Health Clinical Center. Baseline clinical and laboratory data were extracted from medical records. Eligible patients had confirmed spinal infection, a baseline vertebral bone destruction height ratio less than one-third, and complete baseline and follow-up data. Postinfectious bone loss was defined as a height ratio greater than or equal to one-third on computed tomography 12 months after baseline. Predictors were selected from 31 baseline variables using univariable logistic regression followed by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Multivariable logistic regression was used to construct the nomogram. Internal validation used 500 bootstrap resamples, repeating all predictor selection and model-fitting steps. Performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, decision curve analysis, and clinical impact curve analysis. Postinfectious bone loss occurred in 48.9% (109/223, 95% CI 42.4%-55.4%) of patients. The nomogram combined infection characteristics (multidrug-resistant bacterial infection and infected spinal segment), skeletal status (osteoporosis), and laboratory markers (interleukin-6, albumin, and plasma fibrinogen) to estimate individual risk. In the multivariable model, the odds ratios (ORs) were 2.718 (95% CI 0.993-7.444; P=.05) for multidrug-resistant bacterial infection and 7.345 (95% CI 2.757-19.570; P<.001) for osteoporosis. Relative to cervical infection, ORs were 14.041 (95% CI 1.079-182.662; P=.04) for thoracic, 28.876 (95% CI 2.648-314.895; P=.006) for lumbar, and 12.604 (95% CI 0.436-364.075; P=.14) for thoracolumbar infection. Per unit increase, ORs were 1.004 (95% CI 0.996-1.012; P=.30) for interleukin-6 (pg/mL), 3.673 (95% CI 2.410-5.598; P<.001) for plasma fibrinogen (g/L), and 0.834 (95% CI 0.749-0.929; P=.001) for albumin (g/L). Discrimination remained high after optimism correction, with an AUC of 0.946 (95% CI 0.919-0.972), compared with an apparent AUC of 0.954 (95% CI 0.931-0.978). Calibration assessment yielded an intercept of 0.00 (95% CI -0.43 to 0.43) and a slope of 1.00 (95% CI 0.75-1.25), while the Brier score was 0.096 (95% CI 0.064-0.118), indicating close agreement between predicted and observed risks and low overall prediction error. This study developed a visual nomogram integrating baseline clinical characteristics, imaging features, and laboratory parameters to predict postinfectious bone loss in patients with spinal infection. Extending previous association studies to individualized risk prediction, the model showed good discrimination and calibration in internal validation. This approach may help identify high-risk patients and inform closer monitoring and timely reassessment before further structural deterioration and neurological complications.
