cards.title: Aged Macrophage‐Derived Signaling Impairs Regulatory T Cell Induction and Is Associated With Persistent Intraocular Inflammation
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Immune‐mediated intraocular inflammation, called uveitis, is a leading cause of global blindness, with the highest burden of visual impairment falling on older individuals. Immunosenescence, the functional changes in immune cells with aging, impacts the age‐associated immune response, but how immunosenescence and the molecular regulators of the age‐associated immune response affect the clinical course of uveitis remains unclear. In the murine model of experimental autoimmune uveitis (EAU), aged mice demonstrated a delayed onset and peak of intraocular inflammation compared to young mice. In contrast to the canonical monophasic inflammation that rapidly resolves in young mice, aged mice developed persistent, chronic inflammation. Transcriptomic and flow‐cytometric analyses of immune cells and the receptor‐ligand interactome revealed a dominant macrophage‐CD4 + T cell signature. This signaling pathway was functionally altered on both ends: macrophages from aged mice had an impaired capacity to generate peripherally induced regulatory T cells (pTreg) through an IL‐6 regulated pathway, while CD4 + T cells co‐cultured with aged macrophages demonstrated increased proliferation. Our study establishes aging as a key regulator of the effector immune response in uveitis. Regulatory T cells, specifically pTreg, are essential for resolving inflammation in uveitis and an impaired ability to induce pTreg led to a sustained, chronic inflammatory uveitis phenotype in old mice, thereby linking immunosenescence to persistent neuroinflammation. These findings highlight potential therapeutic avenues for vision‐threatening uveitis, especially in older patients.

cards.title: Implant Survivorship, Revision Burden, and Failure Mechanisms Following Simultaneous Bilateral Versus Unilateral Cementless Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Minimum 17-Year Comparative Study.
cards.abstract: We compared perioperative outcomes, revision burden, cause-specific failure mechanisms, and long-term implant survivorship between simultaneous bilateral and unilateral cementless total hip arthroplasty (THA). This retrospective comparative cohort included 327 patients (654 hips) who underwent simultaneous bilateral THA and 352 patients (352 hips) who underwent unilateral THA. Mean follow-up was 23.4 years (range, 17 to 28) and 23.5 years (range, 17 to 28), respectively. Patient-level outcomes included transfusion, 90-day mortality, and perioperative complications; hip-level outcomes included revision burden, cause-specific failure, radiographic findings, and implant survivorship. Analysis of hip-level time-to-event outcomes accounted for within-patient correlation in the bilateral cohort. The observed transfusion rate was 10% after simultaneous bilateral THA and 3% after unilateral THA. Ninety-day mortality was 0.3% in both groups. Major complications occurred in 1.8 and 1.4% of patients, and minor complications in 20 and 27%, respectively. Acetabular revision was performed in 42 of 654 hips (6.4%) and 23 of 352 hips (6.5%); femoral revision was performed in 22 of 654 hips (3.4%) and 12 of 352 hips (3.4%). Among femoral revisions, periprosthetic fracture accounted for nine of 22 revisions (41%) after simultaneous bilateral THA and one of 12 revisions after unilateral THA. At approximately 23.5 years, acetabular survivorship was 93.6% (95% CI [confidence interval], 90 to 100) versus 93.5% (95% CI, 90 to 100), and femoral survivorship was 96.6% (95% CI, 92 to 100) versus 96.7% (95% CI, 92 to 100), respectively. In this selected retrospective cohort, simultaneous bilateral cementless THA had a higher observed transfusion rate, whereas observed mortality, revision proportions, and long-term component survivorship were numerically close to those after unilateral THA. Periprosthetic fracture accounted for a greater proportion of femoral revisions after bilateral THA, but this finding was based on only nine versus one fracture-related revisions and should be considered hypothesis-generating.

cards.title: Comparing oral bisphosphonates, denosumab, hip protector, and bioactive hydrogel augmentation strategies for hip fracture prevention using subject-specific finite element models.
cards.abstract: Hip fractures lead to considerable morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. Pharmacological therapy (Pharma: oral bisphosphonates, denosumab) takes months to reduce fracture risk and hip protectors (HP) depend on consistent compliance; injectable bioactive hydrogels, acting within weeks, are emerging as a rapid-onset alternative. This study used subject-specific biofidelic finite element (FE) models to compare hip fracture prevention strategies. CT-based FE models were generated from two cohorts: the contralateral femur of a post-fracture cohort (Emilia-Romagna) and the baseline femur of a prospectively followed, pre-fracture cohort (KURE), and simulated under probabilistic fall conditions. The effect of Ageing and Pharma was modelled over 36 months, whereas HP and three hydrogel augmentations of increasing apparent density (HYD0.2: +0.2 g/cm3; HYD0.2-ext: HYD0.2 extended by an element layer; HYD0.4: +0.4 g/cm3) provided rapid-onset protection. Relative risk (RR) was calculated relative to the simulated Ageing trajectory for Pharma and relative to the unaugmented baseline for HP and hydrogels. Thirty-nine subjects (21 Emilia-Romagna, 18 KURE; mean age 78.8 ± 5.3 years) were simulated. Ageing significantly increased RR to 1.12 [95% CI: 1.11-1.13]. All interventions reduced RR; applying real-world adherence rates (oral bisphosphonates: 49.4%; denosumab: 53.8%; HP: 50%), RR was 0.93, 0.91, and 0.82, respectively. Hydrogel augmentation required no compliance adjustment: HYD0.2 0.81 [0.81-0.82], HYD0.2-ext 0.76 [0.75-0.77], and HYD0.4 0.73 [0.72-0.74]. All strategies demonstrated fracture-risk reduction; at real-world adherence rates, hydrogel augmentation achieved the greatest within-subject benefit among the rapid-onset comparators and remained sensitive to the magnitude of augmentation volume.

cards.title: Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw at the Site of a Presumed Pre-Existing Mandibular Dense Bone Island: A Longitudinal Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Case Report.
cards.abstract: BACKGROUND Dense bone island (DBI), also known as idiopathic osteosclerosis, is a localized intraosseous radiopacity of unknown etiology that is typically asymptomatic and incidentally detected. It most commonly occurs in the posterior mandible as a well-defined, homogeneous radiopaque lesion without cortical disruption or effects on adjacent structures. Its behavior in patients receiving antiresorptive therapy remains largely unexplored. Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a recognized complication associated with antiresorptive agents, including denosumab and bisphosphonates. This case report describes a 70-year-old woman receiving long-term denosumab therapy for osteoporosis who developed MRONJ at the site of a pre-existing mandibular lesion provisionally diagnosed as a DBI and was evaluated using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). CASE REPORT A 70-year-old woman receiving long-term denosumab therapy for osteoporosis developed Stage 2 MRONJ at the site of a presumed pre-existing mandibular DBI. CBCT initially demonstrated a hyperdense lesion in the left posterior mandible. Four years later (at age 74), the patient presented with an intraoral fistula. Follow-up CBCT revealed a mixed osteolytic-osteosclerotic process at the same site, with mandibular canal involvement, and sequestrum formation. Surgical excision and histopathologic examination confirmed MRONJ. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the value of longitudinal CBCT in documenting the radiographic evolution of MRONJ at the site of a previously identified lesion provisionally diagnosed as a DBI. However, the observed temporal and spatial association does not establish a causal relationship between the baseline lesion and subsequent development of MRONJ.

cards.title: Cellular Senescence as a Multiorgan Driver of Diabetes-Associated Cardiovascular and Kidney Disease.
cards.abstract: Cellular senescence may contribute to persistent cardiovascular and kidney dysfunction in diabetes, but its effects depend on cell identity, tissue compartment and disease stage. This targeted narrative review integrates mechanistic, preclinical and early human evidence into a proposed multiorgan framework. Experimental studies support functional effects of senescent beta-cell, adipose, vascular and tubular populations, while predominantly post-mitotic cardiomyocytes and mature podocytes exhibit senescence-like states. Local paracrine mechanisms, including tubular-to-fibroblast signalling, are better established than source-specific transmission between distant organs. Adipose-derived extracellular vesicles provide an experimental adipose-to-heart example in diabetic mice, whereas the broader contributions of circulating SASP factors, metabolites and immune-cell trafficking remain incompletely resolved. We therefore present the diabetes-heart-kidney senescence loop as a conceptual interpretation of the available evidence, rather than a validated causal network. Senolytic and senomorphic interventions improve selected phenotypes in preclinical models. Major unresolved questions concern the pathogenic cell populations in patients, the direction and specificity of interorgan signalling, and the timing and safety of intervention. Clinical translation requires cell-resolved biomarkers and evidence that senescence-directed treatment adds functional benefit to established cardiometabolic care while preserving beneficial repair and immune functions.

cards.title: Real-World Outcomes of Long-Acting Beta-Agonist Add-On Therapy to Inhaled Corticosteroids in Preschool Children with Asthma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
cards.abstract: The role of long-acting beta-agonist (LABA) add-on therapy to inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) in preschool children with asthma remains uncertain. Although ICS+LABA is an established step-up strategy, data in children younger than 6 years are limited. In children ≤6 years with asthma, how were morbidity outcomes associated with ICS+LABA therapy compared with ICS alone, before and after LABA initiation? and Methods: This retrospective comparative effectiveness study used the TriNetX research network, a multicenter electronic health record database. Children aged ≤6 years with asthma treated with ICS+LABA were compared with propensity-matched children treated with ICS alone (n≈12,100 per cohort). To account for treatment timing and the age-related effects on asthma severity and incidence, analyses were conducted using two index definitions: asthma diagnosis with LABA initiation within 12 months, and the time of LABA initiation itself. Outcomes included systemic corticosteroid exposure, bronchodilator use, ED visits/hospitalizations, pneumonia, fractures, and gastroenteritis. When indexed at asthma diagnosis, ICS+LABA was associated with higher hazards of systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.32-1.43), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.36-1.46), and pneumonia (HR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.28-1.52) compared to ICS alone. When reindexed to LABA initiation, these associations were attenuated, but not eliminated: systemic corticosteroid exposure (HR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.09-1.18), bronchodilator use (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.13-1.21), and pneumonia (HR, 1.11; 95% CI, 1.02-1.22). Direct comparison of the ICS+LABA cohort across index definitions showed lower rates of asthma-related outcomes after LABA initiation. Findings were similar in unmatched analyses, and in sensitivity analyses by younger age, later follow-up, Bayesian analysis and LABA type. In young children selected for ICS+LABA escalation, excess morbidity was greatest compared to ICS alone before LABA initiation and attenuated after LABA initiation. These findings may provide real-world evidence for ICS+LABA effectiveness in a selected group of preschool children with uncontrolled asthma and the basis for future prospective studies.

cards.title: Surgical versus conservative management of acute subdural hematoma in elderly patients: a systematic review of functional outcomes and prognostic factors.
cards.abstract: Management of acute subdural hematoma in the elderly requires nuanced clinical decision-making. While the Brain Trauma Foundation incorporates clot thickness and midline shift in their ASDH management guidelines, they do not quote an age bracket cut-off. Evidence to date suggests the elderly see disproportionately high morbidity and mortality regardless of surgical or conservative management. To systematically review the evidence comparing surgical evacuation versus conservative management of ASDH in elderly patients and assess the impact of patient factors on outcomes, a systematic review was conducted examining six observational studies (n = 812) comparing surgical and conservative management of traumatic ASDH in patients aged 60 or older. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, 6-month mortality, and functional outcomes. MEDLINE, Embase and CINAHL were searched up to December 2025. Risk of bias assessment was performed using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale. Results were presented descriptively and synthesized narratively by outcome timepoint as clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Surgery was not consistently associated with improved mortality nor improved functional outcomes. Surgical patients presented with worse clinical and radiological severity. In-hospital mortality analysis of three cohorts demonstrated substantial heterogeneity, with relative risks ranging from 1.37 to 13.63, favoring conservative management. Six-month mortality showed even greater heterogeneity with directionally inconsistent findings. Functional outcomes, when reported, either favored conservative management or were neutral. Current evidence does not establish a consistent mortality or functional advantage for surgical evacuation of ASDH in elderly patients. Patients with poor neurological status demonstrate high mortality regardless of intervention, while those with mild neurological impairment may not derive meaningful benefit from surgery. Future prospective studies should standardize frailty assessment alongside clinical and radiographic parameters to identify where true clinical equipoise exists and establish guidelines in this distinct patient population. No funding was received for this review.

cards.title: Digital-health fracture liaison service continuation in a citywide multihospital registry: subsequent fracture, mortality, and injectable treatment initiation after osteoporotic fracture surgery.
cards.abstract: Among 9211 adults undergoing osteoporotic fracture surgery, care at an FLS-designated hospital was associated with fewer subsequent fractures after a prespecified 90-day landmark. We found no evidence of reduced all-cause mortality, while recorded target-dose injectable treatment initiation was higher in the FLS-designated setting. To compare surgery-treated subsequent fractures, all-cause mortality, and recorded target-dose injectable treatment initiation between a fracture liaison service (FLS)-designated index hospital and pooled non-FLS hospitals in a citywide registry. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults aged ≥50 years with a first recorded eligible major fracture and repair procedure in a citywide registry (1 January 2022-10 May 2026). Exposure was fixed by the hospital performing the index operation. The prespecified primary endpoint was a surgery-treated fracture at a different skeletal site after a 90-day landmark. Multivariable Cox models evaluated this endpoint and all-cause mortality; recorded target-dose zoledronic acid 5 mg or denosumab 60 mg initiation was exploratory. Among 9211 patients (2149 FLS-designated; 7062 non-FLS), 363 deaths were recorded. The 90-day landmark analysis included 8691 patients and 135 endpoint events. The FLS-designated hospital was associated with a lower subsequent-fracture hazard (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.44-0.84; P = 0.002). We found no evidence of reduced all-cause mortality within the available follow-up (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.76-1.16; P = 0.587). Among patients without recorded pre-index target-dose use, either-agent initiation by 365 days was 464/2112 (22.0%) versus 795/6945 (11.4%; adjusted RR 1.52, 95% CI 1.39-1.67). Index surgery at the FLS-designated hospital was associated with fewer surgery-treated, different-site subsequent fractures and higher recorded target-dose injectable initiation, but not with demonstrably lower mortality. Hospital-level exposure and the surgery-only endpoint preclude patient-level FLS inference.

cards.title: Clinical and radiographic outcomes of SpineJack mechanical kyphoplasty versus conservative management in traumatic thoraco-lumbar compression fractures.
cards.abstract: Prospective, comparative, observational cohort study. To compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes of SpineJack mechanical kyphoplasty versus conservative management in neurologically intact patients with traumatic thoraco-lumbar compression fractures (AO type A). Thoraco-lumbar compression fractures can be managed conservatively, with prolonged bed rest and rigid orthoses; with minimally invasive techniques originally developed for osteoporotic fractures, such as vertebroplasty and kyphoplasty; or with open or percutaneous pedicle screw fixation. A total of 246 consecutive patients with a Magerl type A thoraco-lumbar fracture were included in this non-randomized prospective study between January 2018 and December 2023. After counseling, 124 patients elected Group A (conservative management: bed rest and a three-point brace) and 122 elected Group B (percutaneous kyphoplasty with SpineJack). At the final 12-month follow-up, 104 patients in Group A and 100 patients in Group B were evaluated, with a total of 42 patients lost to follow-up. The Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) were used to assess clinical outcome. Radiographic outcome was assessed by measuring the vertebral height loss rate (HLR) and regional kyphosis angle (RKA). Patients were followed up at 1, 6, and 12 months. Pain relief and recovery of functional ability were significantly better in Group B. Radiographic metrics showed a better outcome in the surgical group. Mechanical kyphoplasty with the SpineJack system is a safe and effective treatment for post-traumatic compression fractures, providing a significant improvement in pain, disability, and radiographic morphometric parameters that is maintained at long-term follow-up.

cards.title: Medial Malleolar Cortical Thickening with Non metallic implants for Prophylactic fixation in Total Ankle Arthroplasty.
cards.abstract: Metal and non-metal fixation has long been utilized in orthopedic procedures but carries drawbacks including migration, breakage, osteolysis, imaging interference, and potential need for removal. Although absorbable hardware has historically shown mixed results, advancements in bio-integrative technology promise non-metal alternatives that reduce stress shielding and support healing. Periprosthetic fracturing in the setting of total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) is an area of high concern which can lead to severe clinical ramifications. The purpose of this study was to assess changes in medial malleolar thickness in TAA specifically comparing use of integrative technology to a control. The authors reviewed a single surgeon operative database of patients who underwent primary total ankle replacement (TAR) between December 2018 and February 2024 with a minimum of 1 year follow up. Ninety-one subjects that underwent TAA were included in this study. We found a statistically significant increase in cortical thickness post-operatively in the group who had prophylactic fixation of the medial malleolus with the bio-integrative implant compared to preoperative cortical thickness, with an average increase of 0.63 cm (p-value < 0.0001). However, this finding did not demonstrate an association with the incidence of medial malleolar stress fractures. Although biointegrative prophylactic fixation was associated with increased medial malleolar cortical thickness following TAA, the clinical significance of this finding remains uncertain. Further studies are warranted to determine whether biointegrative fixation provides meaningful protection against medial malleolar stress fractures. Level 3, retrospective cohort study.

cards.title: Development and external validation of a nomogram for predicting re-fracture after percutaneous kyphoplasty: A two-center study
cards.abstract: Background: To identify independent risk factors for subsequent vertebral re-fracture after percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP) in patients with osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture (OVCF) and to develop and externally validate a predictive nomogram for individualized risk assessment. Methods: This two-center retrospective study enrolled 1,720 OVCF patients who underwent PKP between January 2023 and April 2025. The training cohort (n=963) and internal validation cohort (n=413) were derived from Beijing LUHE Hospital, while the external validation cohort (n=344) was from the other participating center. The primary outcome was postoperative re-fracture confirmed by imaging within a minimum 12-month follow-up. To find independent risk variables in the training cohort, multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed after potential predictors were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Based on these variables, a nomogram was created. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to evaluate model performance for each of the three cohorts. Results: Five independent factors of re-fracture were found using multivariate logistic regression: advanced age ([≥]65 years) (OR=2.58, 95% CI: 1.81-3.67), body mass index (BMI) [≥]18.5 (protective, OR=0.32, 95% CI: 0.21-0.49), bone mineral density (BMD) (OR=0.13, 95% CI: 0.08-0.20), osteocalcin (BGP) (OR=1.16, 95% CI: 1.09-1.22), and Cobb angle correction (OR=1.36, 95% CI: 1.21-1.53). The nomogram demonstrated good discrimination in the training cohort (AUC=0.810, 95% CI: 0.779-0.841), internal validation cohort (AUC=0.801, 95% CI: 0.732-0.870), and external validation cohort (AUC=0.809, 95% CI: 0.750-0.867). DCA verified net benefit over a threshold probability range of 0-0.6, and calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between projected and observed probabilities. Conclusion: The externally validated nomogram, incorporating age, BMI, BMD, BGP, and Cobb angle correction, provides a robust and practical tool for individualized prediction of re-fracture risk after PKP in OVCF patients, which could facilitate risk-stratified postoperative management and potentially improve patient outcomes. Keywords: Osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture; Percutaneous kyphoplasty; Re-fracture; Risk factors; Nomogram.

cards.title: Immunosenescence in Metabolic Disorders: From Cellular Mechanisms to Therapeutic Strategies.
cards.abstract: This review comprehensively examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the crosstalk between metabolic disorders and immunosenescence and elucidates the fundamental roles of clonal hematopoiesis (CH) and immune surveillance while critically evaluating both classical and emerging therapeutic strategies that target these pathways. Recent evidence indicates that immune cells displaying senescence-associated phenotypes accumulate in adipose tissue, liver, and vasculature, where they exhibit mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic remodeling, and a maladaptive senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) driven by NF-κB and C/EBPβ. Key SASP components, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and CCL2, together with p53/p21- and p16/RB-mediated cell-cycle arrest and cGAS-STING pathway activation, contribute to adipocyte hypertrophy, insulin resistance, hepatic steatosis, and dyslipidemia. These changes are associated with the accelerated progression of obesity, type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), and atherosclerosis. Additionally, CH and impaired immune surveillance exacerbate chronic metabolic inflammation. This review discusses classical interventions, including metabolic modulators, senolytics, and senomorphics, alongside emerging strategies such as Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTAC)-based senolytics, CH-targeted approaches, and mitochondrial-targeted therapies, emphasizing mechanistic differences and supporting clinical evidence. Nevertheless, challenges related to achieving tissue-specific delivery while minimizing systemic toxicity remain unresolved. Immunosenescence plays a dual role; transient and context-dependent SASP signaling can contribute to tissue repair, whereas persistent or dysregulated SASP activity can promote pathology. Currently, validated clinical tools for assessing immune-driven metabolic dysfunction are lacking. This absence of standardized evaluation frameworks hinders the translation of these therapies into clinical practice, highlighting the necessity for a theoretical foundation to guide precision treatment of obesity-related metabolic diseases and to promote healthy aging.

cards.title: Spatiotemporal profiling reveals emergence of cell type-specific molecular aging and senescence programs in the spinal cord
cards.abstract: The spinal cord is the primary relay center between the periphery and the brain, playing a critical role in sensory, motor and autonomic function. Despite its functional importance, the cellular and molecular changes underlying spinal cord aging and their relationship to cellular senescence - a hallmark associated with aging - remain incompletely understood. Here, we generated a cross-species, multi-omic atlas of spinal cord aging in mice and humans by integrating a combination of liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, Visium spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing, and multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging. We identified converging age-associated increases in fibrinogen, laminin, and immune activation-associated proteins across the mouse and human spinal cord. Over the mouse lifespan, we further identified distinct spatiotemporal patterns of aging. Downregulated transcriptional programs, including synaptic signaling, mitochondrion organization, and autophagy, were most highly expressed in grey matter regions and in neurons. Upregulated transcriptional programs, including vascular and immune processes, were enriched in white matter regions and in endothelial cells and microglia, respectively. Notably, these increasing spatial modules were also enriched for senescence-associated genes. In the human spinal cord, endothelial cells and microglia were also most enriched for canonical senescence markers CDKN1A and CDKN2A, respectively. Overall, this study defines the shared, spatially-resolved, cell type-specific features associated with aging and senescence in the mouse and human spinal cord.

cards.title: Transcriptomic and Lipidomic Profiling of Human iPSC-Derived Microglia Reveals TREM2-Dependent and -Independent Processes
cards.abstract: TREM2 has been implicated in AD as a critical regulator of microglial functions and loss of function mutations in TREM2 increases one's risk of developing AD. Given the diverse functional roles of TREM2, we sought to unravel how it affects downstream pathways using human iPSC-derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) derived from TREM2 knockout (KO) and isogenic control lines and assessing the response to oligomeric amyloid-{beta} 42 (oA{beta}42). While previous studies have primarily used fibrillar A{beta}, we focused on microglial responses to oA{beta}42 given their disease relevance and potent cytotoxic effects. At baseline, we identified a set of TREM2-dependent genes, which corresponded to the DAM signature in mice and disease-associated signatures in humans. Additionally, loss of TREM2 resulted in increased expression of cholesterol biosynthesis genes. In response to oA{beta}42, we found that the transcriptional response was largely TREM2-independent and corresponded to a strong induction of inflammatory pathways, with TREM2 also being downregulated in control iMGLs. We identified subsets of genes and pathways that were unique to either control, such as mitochondrial DNA and RNA degradation, or TREM2 KO iMGLs, such as the senescence-associated secretory pathway and adipogenesis, suggesting some differences in gene expression driven by TREM2 in response to oA{beta}42. Given that the inflammatory response was TREM2-independent, we sought to identify signaling pathways that contributed to inflammation. Inhibition of toll-like receptor signaling significantly reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory genes and modestly increased expression of TREM2 and TREM2-dependent genes. Consistent with our transcriptional data, cytokine production and secretion in response to oA{beta}42 was significantly increased to similar levels in both controls and TREM2 KO iMGLs. Lipidomic profiling of microglia revealed that triglycerides and lactosylceramides were significantly increased in both control and TREM2 KO iMGLs in response to oA{beta}42. TREM2 KO iMGLs had decreased levels of BMPs and increased levels of cholesterol esters across all conditions, further highlighting a role for TREM2 in maintaining lipid homeostasis in microglia. Taken together, we describe genes, pathways, and lipids that are associated with TREM2 expression that likely influence microglial responses to oA{beta}42.

cards.title: Sex-Based Comparison of Remission in Patients with Severe Type 2 Asthma Treated with Biologics: A Real-World Analysis from the "Southern Italy Network on Severe Asthma Therapy".
cards.abstract: Sex influences asthma phenotypes and treatment outcomes. However, real-world data on sex-related differences in severe asthma patients treated with biologics are limited. The objective of this study was to assess sex differences in baseline characteristics and treatment outcomes in a cohort of severe eosinophilic asthma (SEA) patients treated with biologics. We retrospectively analyzed 370 SEA patients (235 females, 135 males) treated with mepolizumab, benralizumab, or dupilumab. Clinical remission was defined as no OCS use plus at least two of: no exacerbations, ACT ≥20, or FEV1 >80%. Logistic regression was used to identify sex-specific predictors of remission at 24 months. Severe type 2 asthma showed a prevalence in females (female-to-male ratio of 1.7:1). Baseline characteristics revealed higher prevalence of obesity (p = 0.015) and osteoporosis (p = 0.006) in females, and greater tobacco exposure (p = 0.05), FeNO (p = 0.03), and nasal polyposis (p = 0.0002) in males. Males had greater reduction in FeNO (p ≤ 0.05) and more male patients stopped exacerbations at 24 months (p < 0.0001), while females showed greater FEF25-75% (p ≤ 0.05) improvement and larger IgE drops (p < 0.0001). Remission rates were similar across sexes at both 12 months (64.3% versus 74.1%; p = 0.06) and 24 months (71.5% versus 77.0%; p = 0.27). In females, remission was associated with eosinophils >300/μL (OR: 2.68; 95% CI: 1.41-5.07; p = 0.003), FeNO >50 ppb (OR: 21.05; 95% CI: 10.24-43.34; p < 0.0001), and nasal polyposis (OR: 2.74; 95% CI: 1.46-5.13; p = 0.001); obesity (OR: 0.20; 95% CI: 0.11-0.37; p < 0.0001), smoking (OR: 0.38; 95% CI: 0.21-0.70; p = 0.002), anxiety (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.23-0.94; p = 0.04), and reflux (OR: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.27-0.84; p = 0.01) were negative predictors. In males, OCS dependency (OR: 0.35; 95% CI: 0.13-0.94; p = 0.03) and FEV1 <80% (OR: 0.18; 95% CI: 0.05-0.63; p = 0.004) were negative predictors. Biologics were equally effective in inducing clinical remission across sexes, but different predictors influenced outcomes. Sex-aware strategies may support personalized asthma care.

cards.title: Epilepsy and sarcopenia: shared neurometabolic mechanisms and emerging brain–muscle interactions
cards.abstract: Background Emerging evidence suggests that people with epilepsy (PWE) may be at increased risk of impaired muscle health and sarcopenia. However, the mechanisms underlying this association remain uncertain and have not been comprehensively synthesized. Methods A narrative review of clinical and preclinical literature was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science through March 2026. Studies addressing sarcopenia, muscle strength, physical performance, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, neurotrophic signaling, nutrition, physical activity, and anti-seizure medication effects in epilepsy were evaluated. Discussion Clinical studies indicate that PWE frequently exhibit reduced handgrip strength, impaired mobility and balance performance, greater frailty, and a higher prevalence of sarcopenia than controls. Reduced physical activity and mobility limitations are among the better-supported proposed contributors, although their causal contribution to sarcopenia in PWE remains unproven. Preclinical studies and evidence derived from parallel epilepsy and sarcopenia literature further suggest potential roles for chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, altered brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) signaling, insulin resistance, nutritional deficiencies, and anti-seizure medication-related metabolic effects. However, direct evidence linking these mechanisms to muscle loss in PWE remains limited. Conclusion Current evidence supports an association between epilepsy and impaired muscle health, with physical inactivity, mobility limitations, and antiseizure medication-related effects representing the most consistently supported contributors. Several biological pathways, including inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and altered neurotrophic signaling, remain plausible but incompletely validated mechanisms that require further investigation.

cards.title: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor cytoplasmic retention by p27^Kip1 in senescent astrocytes.
cards.abstract: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) regulates neurodevelopment, immune responses, and cellular homeostasis. Despite increased availability of endogenous ligands during aging and neurodegeneration, AhR transcriptional activity may decline through mechanisms that remain unclear. We investigated AhR dysfunction and its association with the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p27 in senescent human astrocytes. SVG p12 human astrocytes were exposed to hydrogen peroxide (50 or 100 µM, 30 min) to induce senescence-associated features and evaluated over 72 h. The AhR ligand indole-3-propionic acid (IPA; 200 µM) was administered after oxidative stress. Cellular assays included at least three independent experiments. AhR localization and signaling, p27 association, and senescence-associated phenotypes were evaluated using microscopy, gene expression analysis, protein assays, and molecular docking. Senescence was associated with cytoplasmic redistribution of AhR and reduced expression of its target gene, cytochrome P450 1A1 (CYP1A1). Increased cytoplasmic p27 accumulation coincided with greater AhR colocalization, and co-immunoprecipitation supported their association. Molecular docking suggested that acidic conditions could stabilize the AhR-p27 complex. IPA increased nuclear AhR localization, CYP1A1 expression, and proliferation while reducing senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity. These findings suggest that p27-associated cytoplasmic retention may impair AhR signaling during astrocyte senescence despite ligand availability. IPA treatment after oxidative stress attenuated the development of senescence-associated features. Modulating AhR localization and its association with p27 may offer a therapeutic avenue for age-related neurological disorders, although causality and therapeutic relevance require further investigation.

cards.title: Indications for Dose Adjustment of Thyroid Hormones in Older Patients.
cards.abstract: Thyroid dysfunction is common in older people (persons aged 65 and above). A meta-analysis of data from European countries revealed a 4.1% prevalence of undiagnosed subclinical hypothyroidism. It was found in a primary care study from the United Kingdom that approximately 10 percent of people over age 70 were under treatment for hypothyroidism. This narrative review is based on findings in relevant publications retrieved by a PubMed search and on the guidelines of the European Thyroid Association and the American Thyroid Association. Overtreatment with levothyroxine increases the risk of cardiovascular, cognitive, and skeletal complications (hazard ratio 1.37-2.02). Randomized controlled trials have not shown that treatment with levothyroxine (T4) improves presumed symptoms of hypothyroidism, body weight, or fatigue. In patients who are now taking levothyroxine, lowering the dose or stopping the drug should be considered; in older patients, the target range for thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) should be 4-10 mU/L. After levothyroxine is stopped, some patients remain euthyroid; in the absence of an indication, gradual tapering may be considered. Levothyroxine should not be given over the long term to patients with thyroid nodules. Subclinical hyperthyroidism in older people is associated with clinically relevant risks, particularly atrial fibrillation and bone fractures, and should therefore be treated. Its most common cause, however, is levothyroxine treatment that is either not indicated or improperly dosed. While overt hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism must be treated at any age, the need to treat subclinical hypothyroidism should be individually assessed; subclinical hyperthyroidism, by contrast, generally warrants treatment given its associated risks. In view of the risks of inadequately treated hyperthyroidism and excessively dosed levothyroxine, physicians should regularly review the indication for treatment, the dosage, and the possibility of lowering the dose or discontinuing the drug.

cards.title: Knowledge structure and emerging trends in research on osteoporotic fractures and cardiovascular diseases: A bibliometric analysis from 2005 to 2025.
cards.abstract: Osteoporotic fractures (OPFs) and cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are major age-related conditions that frequently coexist and may be linked through shared biological mechanisms, including chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, mineral metabolism disorders, vascular calcification, and frailty. Although research on OPFs and CVDs has expanded rapidly, the intellectual structure, collaborative patterns, and thematic evolution of this interdisciplinary field remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to map the global research landscape and identify emerging hotspots in OPF-CVD research from 2005 to 2025. English-language articles and reviews published during 2005 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on April 2, 2026. Analyses used VOSviewer 1.6.20 (Centre for Science and Technology Studies [CWTS], Leiden University), CiteSpace 6.4.R1 (Chaomei Chen, Drexel University), bibliometrix 5.3.0 in R 4.5.3 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing), and Microsoft Excel. We examined publication trends, collaboration networks, journals, co-cited references, keyword patterns, and citation bursts. A total of 1236 publications were included. Annual output increased from 24 publications in 2005 to 103 in 2025, corresponding to a compound annual growth rate of 7.56%. The United States had the highest publication count, raw citation count, and TLS. Harvard University was the most productive institution, and Katie L Stone was the most productive author. Reference co-citation analysis identified 8 major thematic clusters: calcium, bisphosphonates, heart failure, frailty, renal osteodystrophy, antihypertensive drugs, osteopenia, and phosphorus. Keyword analyses suggested a descriptive shift from epidemiological associations toward bone-vascular mechanisms, risk stratification, fragility-fracture management, diagnosis, and prevention. OPF-CVD research has developed into a multidisciplinary field with increasing clinical relevance. The bibliometric patterns are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causal relationships. Future research should evaluate integrated bone-cardiovascular risk assessment, pharmacological safety, and multidisciplinary care using prospective and clinically validated designs.

cards.title: Radiomics-based risk prediction: survival in sarcopenic gastrointestinal and genitourinary cancer cohorts using a population-specific sarcopenia definition.
cards.abstract: This study demonstrated that the recently proposed Asian (Japanese)-cohort-based skeletal muscle index (SMI) definition (< 36.2 cm 2 / m 2 for males and < 29.6 cm 2 / m 2 for females), along with other factors such as radiomic and clinical variables, could improve risk categorization for survival in sarcopenic, gastrointestinal (GI), and genitourinary (GU) cancer patients. This retrospective study involved 2,015 patients who underwent major surgery at our institution between 2006 and 2018. From the axial CT image of the L3 vertebral region, the skeletal muscle was segmented to calculate the SMI values. 646 radiomic features were extracted from the image, and the Boruta algorithm was used to identify the most pertinent features. The final set of features consisted of these features and clinical variables. The dataset was split into training and testing sets comprising 1,512 patients (75%) and 503 patients (25%), respectively. Four models were evaluated in this study: (1) random survival forest (RSF)-based radiomic model, (2) Cox proportional hazard-based model, (3) Asian (Japanese)-specific SMI definition-based model, and (4) integrated model, which combines experiments (2) and (3). The Kaplan-Meier (KM) curves, log-rank tests, and Harrell's concordance index (C-index) were computed to assess the predictive performance of the models. The integrated model achieved the highest performance in terms of C-index (0.760, 95% CI: 0.686-0.835) among all other models. Survival stratification was statistically significant across all the experiments (p < 0.0001). This work demonstrates the efficacy of utilizing recently proposed Japanese population-based SMI definition values to optimize risk stratification for sarcopenic patients. Question Can population-specific sarcopenia definitions, clinical variables, and CT muscle radiomics together improve overall survival risk stratification in patients with gastrointestinal and genitourinary cancers? Findings In this cohort of 2,015 patients, combining sarcopenia, clinical variables, and CT muscle radiomics yielded an overall survival C-index of 0.760. Relevance statement The incorporation of the Asian (Japanese)-specific skeletal muscle index definition improves risk stratification for the survival of sarcopenic cancer patients when combined with an imaging-based approach, such as radiomics and other clinical parameters, highlighting the value of multimodal integration.

cards.title: Clinical and radiological outcomes of open reduction and internal fixation for Kilfoyle type III pediatric medial humeral condyle fractures: a retrospective single-center study.
cards.abstract: Medial humeral condyle fractures are uncommon intra-articular injuries in children and are often overlooked because of delayed trochlear ossification. Delayed diagnosis or inadequate treatment may cause nonunion, malunion, growth disturbance, elbow deformity, and functional limitation. This retrospective single-center study evaluated clinical and radiological outcomes of pediatric medial humeral condyle fractures treated with open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) at a tertiary referral center. Children aged 18 months to 12 years who underwent surgery between March 2016 and February 2022 with at least 2 years of follow-up were included. Fractures were classified using the Kilfoyle classification on radiographs, with computed tomography when the configuration was uncertain. Demographics, injury patterns, surgical details, complications, radiographic union, and elbow range of motion were reviewed from medical records. Seventeen children met the criteria. Mean age was 6.2 years (range: 1.5-12), and all fractures were displaced (Kilfoyle type III). The mean interval from injury to surgery was 1.9 days. Union was achieved in 16 of 17 patients (94.1%). Six patients (35.3%) developed complications: one nonunion requiring revision fixation, one malunion requiring corrective osteotomy, two cases of cubitus varus, and two cases of persistent extension deficit despite physiotherapy. No infection, neurovascular injury, or ulnar nerve palsy occurred. Fifteen patients achieved full flexion, and 13 regained full extension. ORIF provides satisfactory clinical and radiological outcomes for displaced pediatric medial humeral condyle fractures, with a high union rate and acceptable functional recovery. However, complications may occur, particularly in older children. Early diagnosis, accurate anatomical reduction, and long-term follow-up remain essential.

cards.title: A randomized controlled trial of zoledronate and oral magnesium in post-menopausal women with osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Bisphosphonates are recommended to enhance bone mineral density (BMD) and reduce the risk of fracture in women with post-menopausal osteoporosis. Magnesium (Mg) has a beneficial effect on BMD, but no trial has so far addressed its additive effect with bisphosphonate treatment. Our objective was to explore whether Mg supplementation could have an additive beneficial effect with bisphosphonate on the concentration of serum carboxy-terminal collagen crosslinks (CTX), as a surrogate of bone status. A pilot randomized controlled trial (NCT05328154) included 44 women with post-menopausal osteoporosis at the University Hospital, Clermont-Ferrand, France. Patients were randomized after zoledronate infusion into 200 mg/day oral Mg carbonate (n=22, "BMg") for three months or standard care (n=22, "BMg0"). The primary endpoint was comparison of variation in CTX at one year in both groups. Other bone markers and quality of life were also assessed. Responder analysis was post-hoc. All statistical tests were two-tailed with type-I error set at α=0.05. CTX substantially decreased in both groups, but without significant difference between groups. A subgroup analysis in 30%, with both high CTX and low serum Mg levels at baseline, showed that these patients had the largest decrease in CTX levels (≥89%). DKK1 demonstrated the greatest difference between the BMg0 and BMg group, suggesting an osteogenic effect of Mg. No other significant differences were observed. This innovative pilot randomized trial suggests that in clinical practice, the subgroup of post-osteoporotic women with high CTX values and low serum Mg concentrations might benefit from Mg supplementation in addition to zoledronate. A larger randomized trial targeting this subgroup is warranted. Trial registration: NCT05328154; first registration date: 29/03/2022; first inclusion: 28/06/ 2022.

cards.title: Assessing Hand Surgery Resident Knowledge: A Comparative Analysis of Orthopaedic Surgery and Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery In-Service Training Examinations.
cards.abstract: The purpose of our study was to evaluate the depth and breadth of hand surgery knowledge assessed on recent orthopedic and plastic surgery residency in-training examinations. Identifying differences in hand surgery content and examination structure between these two assessments may inform efforts to improve resident knowledge and comfort with hand surgery in general practice, as well as readiness for advanced fellowship training or a career in hand surgery. This was a retrospective cohort study that used hand surgery questions from the 2020-2024 Orthopaedic Surgery In-Training Exam (OITE) and 2019-2023 Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery In-Training Exam (PSITE). Descriptive and statistical analyses were performed on the data. Statistical significance was set at P < .05. A total of 366 questions were analyzed (150 OITE, 216 PSITE). The OITE emphasized treatment management (43% vs 29%; P = .015), operative focus (59% vs 48%; P = .015), and trauma (46% vs 41%; P < .001), particularly fractures/dislocations (33% vs 10%; P < .001) and elbow pathology (33% vs 5%; P = .003). PSITE questions concentrated on elective conditions (52% vs 37%; P < .001), distal-to-carpus topics (71% vs 30%; P < .001), and nerve (12.5% vs 10.0%; P < .001), soft tissue reconstruction (22% vs 7%; P < .001), tumor (11% vs 1%; P < .001), and congenital anomalies (9% vs 6%; P < .001). Radiological imaging appeared more frequently in OITE items (39% vs 8%; P < .001). PSITE questions included more references per question (P < .001) and more textbook citations (24% vs 6%; P < .001) but referenced older studies (median 8.25 vs 6.5 years; P < .001). The OITE emphasizes trauma and operative management, whereas the PSITE focuses on reconstructive, elective, and congenital pathology. Reference patterns reflect differing academic traditions-PSITE drawing on textbooks and OITE on recent clinical studies. These findings underscore how training background shapes examination content and may inform curricular alignment for future residency education and hand surgery fellowship preparation. cards.title: Accelerating discovery and integration from RNA to Protein with R2T2P
cards.abstract: Integrating transcriptomics and proteomics data remains an unmet challenge in the post-genomics era, discouraging researchers from pursuing integrative approaches to molecular biology research. Leveraging the power of translation profiling, we present RNA to Translation to Protein (R2T2P), a computational platform integrating genome-guided transcriptome assembly with identification of translation and proteins, including a tailored differential analysis framework and support for multiple reference transcriptomes. We applied R2T2P to investigate a cellular model of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), where ectopic expression of the DUX4 retrogene in skeletal muscle triggers significant alterations in transcription and RNA metabolism. We uncovered hundreds of uncharacterized, highly overexpressed RNAs, including antisense and alternative transcripts, and quantified their contribution to translatome and proteome. Re-analysis of expression datasets from patient-derived myotubes and muscle biopsies validated this alternative transcriptome in FSHD patients, adding a reservoir of bona-fide novel molecular actors in a rare disease. Available at https://github.com/nfdata-omics/R2T2P/, R2T2P is a flexible and powerful workflow in modern integrative biology.

cards.title: Frailty Burden in Patients with HFrEF Undergoing Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation: Clinical Outcomes and Readmissions.
cards.abstract: Frailty is common and has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes across cardiovascular populations. However, its prognostic significance, particularly the impact of graded frailty burden, among patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) undergoing catheter ablation for ventricular tachycardia (VT) remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated the association between frailty burden and in-hospital outcomes among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation using the Nationwide Readmissions Database. Frailty was defined using the validated Johns Hopkins Adjusted Clinical Groups (ACG) frailty indicator. Cumulative frailty burden was quantified as the number of domains (range: 0-10). Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations with outcomes, and in-hospital mortality probabilities were estimated across increasing frailty burden. Among 17,367 hospitalizations for VT ablation in patients with HFrEF, 7.4% were classified as frail. Frailty was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.59; 95% CI, 1.19-2.13; p<0.001), and increased complication rates. Frail patients had higher 30-day (13.6% vs. 9.1%) and 90-day (33.7% vs. 28.1%) readmission rates compared with non-frail patients. Frailty burden demonstrated a graded association with in-hospital mortality, with estimated mortality increasing progressively with each additional frailty domain. Frailty is independently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes and higher readmission rates among patients with HFrEF undergoing VT ablation, with a graded increase in risk across increasing frailty domains. These findings suggest that frailty burden may serve as a clinically relevant risk stratification marker in this vulnerable cohort.

cards.title: Back extensor strength and incident GERD in women receiving osteoporosis treatment: a retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: We investigated factors associated with incident gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) in women receiving osteoporosis treatment. This retrospective cohort study included 82 women with osteoporosis, baseline Frequency Scale for the Symptoms of GERD (FSSG) scores < 8, and an available follow-up assessment at least 4 years later. Incident questionnaire-defined GERD was defined as a final follow-up FSSG score ≥ 8 among participants with baseline scores < 8. Clinical characteristics, radiographic parameters, bone mineral density (BMD), body composition, and muscle strength were compared between groups. Separate age-adjusted logistic regression models assessed follow-up back extensor strength and percentage changes in back extensor strength and lumbar spine BMD expressed as a percentage of the young adult mean (%YAM). At the final follow-up assessment, 19 participants (23.2%) were classified as GERD-positive. Follow-up back extensor strength was lower in the GERD group (10.6 ± 4.5 vs 14.3 ± 5.7 kg; p = 0.011). Higher follow-up back extensor strength was associated with lower odds of incident GERD (age-adjusted odds ratio, 0.86 per 1-kg increase; 95% confidence interval, 0.76-0.98; p = 0.019). Neither percentage change was significantly associated with incident GERD. BMD increased during follow-up, and radiographic parameters did not differ significantly between groups. Lower back extensor strength at follow-up was associated with questionnaire-defined GERD in women receiving osteoporosis treatment. Although temporal and causal relationships remain uncertain, prospective studies with strength assessments before symptom onset could clarify this association and inform future trials of back extensor strengthening.

cards.title: Risk factors and morbidity characteristics of surgical site infection following ankle fracture ORIF: A comprehensive analysis.
cards.abstract: This study aimed to describe the incidence and microbiological characteristics of surgical site infection (SSI) after open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of ankle fractures and identify clinical factors associated with SSI. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 248 patients who underwent ankle fracture ORIF between January and December 2023. SSI occurring within 30 postoperative days was identified from available inpatient and postoperative medical records. Demographic, injury-related, laboratory, and perioperative variables were compared between patients with and without SSI. Multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted associations with SSI. SSI occurred in 32 of 248 patients (12.9%), including 25 superficial and 7 deep infections. Cultured organisms included Escherichia coli (n = 10), Staphylococcus aureus (n = 7), Klebsiella pneumoniae (n = 6), Enterobacter cloacae (n = 5), and Staphylococcus epidermidis (n = 4). In multivariable analysis, open fracture, wound class II-III, and neutrophil percentage > 75% were associated with SSI. Age and body mass index (BMI) also showed positive associations, although the precise unit-specific effect sizes could not be reliably reconstructed from the archived statistical analysis; these comparatively large per-unit estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of SSI events and potential residual confounding. SSI occurred in 12.9% of this single-center ankle fracture cohort. Older age and higher BMI showed associations with SSI, together with open fracture, less-clean operative wounds, and neutrophilia. The magnitude of the age- and BMI-related effects should be interpreted cautiously because their original regression scaling could not be independently reconstructed.

cards.title: Resistant hypertension and accelerated vascular aging: evidence for PTEN-AKT-associated cellular senescence.
cards.abstract: Resistant hypertension (RH) is increasingly linked to accelerated vascular aging and is particularly prevalent among older and obese individuals. Cellular senescence has emerged as a potential driver of vascular aging, but its contribution to RH remains unclear. We examined age and body mass index (BMI) in the WalkByLab cohort and assessed whether RH was associated with vascular features consistent with accelerated aging. Obesity-related transcriptomic datasets were integrated with a curated senescence-associated gene set to identify candidate regulators, followed by validation in an independent RH dataset, PBMCs, and human endothelial cells. An exploratory clinical-molecular nomogram was also developed. BMI and age increased progressively from normotension to RH. RH was characterized by reduced flow-mediated dilation, increased pulse wave index, and unchanged ankle-brachial index, consistent with endothelial dysfunction and arterial stiffness. Transcriptomic analyses identified enrichment of inflammatory, PI3K-AKT, and senescence-associated pathways. In PBMCs from RH patients, PTEN expression was reduced, AKT phosphorylation was increased, and p16/p21 levels were elevated, indicating a systemic senescence-associated molecular profile. In human endothelial cells, exposure to obese serum or pharmacological PTEN inhibition induced AKT activation and cellular senescence, whereas AKT inhibition attenuated these effects. Together, transcriptomic, clinical, and experimental findings indicate that RH is associated with vascular and molecular features consistent with accelerated vascular aging. Human data indicate a systemic senescence-associated molecular profile, whereas endothelial cell experiments support endothelial senescence as a mechanistically relevant cellular component. PTEN-AKT-associated cellular senescence may represent one mechanistically relevant component linking obesity to vascular dysfunction in RH.

cards.title: Non-linear associations between parity and long-term risk of osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Our findings suggest that although pregnancy and lactation are periods of physiological calcium loss, higher parity is not associated with an increased risk of postmenopausal osteoporosis; rather, it appears to confer a long-term protective effect. Osteoporosis is a significant public health burden. While parity induces transient bone loss, their long-term skeletal impact remains poorly understood. This study aimed to clarify the associations between parity, defined as the number of live births, and the risk of osteoporosis, osteoporotic fractures, and bone mineral density (BMD). We analyzed data from 119,969 women in the UK Biobank. Associations between parity and incident osteoporosis or fractures were evaluated using unweighted and inverse probability of treatment weighting Cox proportional hazards models. Generalized linear models assessed associations with femoral neck and lumbar spine BMD. Models were adjusted for sociodemographic, genetic, lifestyle, and clinical factors. Compared with nulliparous women, those with a parity of 2 or 3 exhibited a significantly reduced risk of osteoporosis in the weighted fully adjusted model. In addition, parity of 3 exhibited a significantly reduced risk of osteoporotic fracture compared with the nulliparous group. This protection was evident in women ≥ 60 years and those with normal body mass index. Parity was not significantly associated with areal BMD changes after full covariate adjustment. In women aged 40-69 years at baseline, a parity of 2 or 3 confers long-term protection against osteoporosis and osteoporotic fracture (a arity of 3), occurring independently of BMD changes. These findings support the integration of parity into clinical risk assessment tools, ultimately contributing to more effective osteoporosis prevention and a reduced fracture burden across women's lifespan.

cards.title: Outcome Disparities in Geriatric Hip Fracture: Orthogeriatric Co-Management Versus Internal Medicine Admission.
cards.abstract: Hip fracture carries substantial morbidity and mortality in older adults. Orthogeriatric co-management has emerged as the evidence-based standard of care, yet the influence of admitting service on outcomes at institutions where such programs exist remains poorly characterized. Patients aged 65 or older who underwent operative management of hip fractures at an urban academic safety-net institution between January 2019 and December 2022. After excluding patients admitted to other services or requiring intensive care, the final cohort comprised 443 patients (349 orthogeriatric co-management, 94 internal medicine). This retrospective cohort study compared outcomes between patients admitted to an orthogeriatric co-management service versus internal medicine. Internal medicine patients received no formal geriatric involvement. Univariate logistic regression assessed associations between admitting service and binary outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression for 1-year mortality adjusted for age, sex, and ASA score. A matched analysis paired patients 1:1 on ASA score, sex, and age within 3 years using McNemar and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups, including ASA score, age, comorbidity burden, and fracture type. Internal medicine admission was associated with higher 1-year mortality (OR: 3.01, 95% CI: 1.53-5.83, p = 0.001), greater surgical delay beyond 24 h (OR: 3.16, 95% CI: 1.98-5.12, p < 0.001), longer length of stay (p < 0.001), and reduced follow-up within 3 weeks (OR: 0.32, p < 0.001). In 91 matched pairs, these associations persisted for 1-year mortality (p = 0.035), surgical delay (p < 0.001), follow-up (p = 0.003), and length of stay (p < 0.001). Multivariable analysis of 1-year mortality was consistent with the univariate and matched analyses (OR: 2.66, 95% CI: 1.32-5.25, p = 0.005). Admitting service is associated with hip fracture outcomes, and this association was not explained by measured patient complexity. These findings support implementation of service-agnostic hip fracture protocols ensuring consistent surgical timing and perioperative management regardless of admitting service, particularly when serving high-risk populations.

cards.title: Evaluating clinical outcomes associated with regional versus general anesthesia approach in blunt geriatric trauma patients undergoing major operative procedures for hip fractures.
cards.abstract: The optimal anesthetic approach for operative management of geriatric hip fractures remains debated, particularly among geriatric trauma patients with limited physiologic reserve and high comorbidity burden. This study evaluated perioperative outcomes associated with anesthesia type in geriatric patients undergoing surgery for isolated hip fractures. This retrospective cohort study was conducted to evaluate geriatric trauma patients (≥ 65 years) with isolated, blunt, moderate to severe (ISS ≥ 9) hip fractures utilizing the ACS-TQIP database from 2017 to 2023. Patients were grouped by anesthetic technique: regional or general anesthesia. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included regional anesthesia failure rate, complication rates, hospital length of stay (LOS), and ventilator-free days (VFDs). Among geriatric trauma patients with moderate to severe hip fractures undergoing hip fixation, no statistically significant association was detected between regional and general anesthesia regarding in-hospital mortality (aOR: 0.316, 95% CI: 0.076-1.311, p = 0.112) or VFDs (β = 4.548, 95% CI - 2.478-11.573, p = 0.202). Also, no statistically significant association was detected between patients receiving regional compared to those receiving general anesthesia for major complications, including DVT, PE, and stroke. The conversion-to-general-anesthesia rate was 0.96%. No statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were detected between regional and general anesthesia among patients with moderate-to-severe hip fractures undergoing major operative fixation. Anesthetic selection should remain individualized. Level III, Therapeutic/Care Management.

cards.title: Disability in chronic kidney disease.
cards.abstract: Frailty, sarcopenia, depression, and cognitive impairment are each well documented in chronic kidney disease (CKD) and have each been the subject of detailed, single-domain reviews, but are rarely considered together as a single construct that determines whether a patient can work, self-manage, and participate in decisions about their own care. This narrative review positions these overlapping yet distinct conditions within the World Health Organization International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework, arguing for a dedicated, cross-domain assessment pathway in nephrology. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched for literature (2006-2026) combining "chronic kidney disease" with "disability", "frailty", "sarcopenia", "depression", "cognitive impairment", "employment", and "rehabilitation". Reference lists were hand-searched. This synthesis focuses on epidemiology, mechanisms, assessment, and management, emphasizing data from 2022 to 2026. As a narrative review without formal risk-of-bias assessment, selection bias is an acknowledged limitation. Disability in CKD arises from five overlapping categories-the risk factors for CKD, CKD-related complications, co-existing conditions, treatment-related factors, and multifactorial contributors, such as sarcopenia and frailty. Once established, disability is perpetuated by two structurally parallel, self-reinforcing processes: a physical spiral of fatigue, symptom burden, and deconditioning, and an economic spiral of employment loss and financial hardship. Validated tools assess individual domains, but no integrated, CKD-specific disability instrument exists. Kidney replacement therapy can trigger abrupt functional decline, while kidney transplantation may improve long-term function but can temporarily worsen early post-operative frailty. The ICF-derived WHODAS 2.0 remains underutilized in nephrology. Disability in CKD is common but historically studied piecemeal through isolated literatures. Shifting the paradigm to recognize disability as a unifying, assessable construct, rather than a by-product of individual complications, may enable earlier identification. This framework supports the implementation of structured, cross-domain assessments and coordinated rehabilitation and prevention strategies in routine nephrology care.

cards.title: From T-cell renewal to immune longevity: a multilevel capacity framework for immune aging
cards.abstract: Consider what the T-cell compartment accomplishes. For decades it sustains immune competence while the thymus shrinks, antigens accumulate, and tissues change around it. We propose that this longevity rests on four coupled capacities: input renewal, repertoire maintenance and clonal dynamics, lineage-constrained plasticity, and tissue-contextual fitness. Input renewal is treated as a proxy domain inferred from calibrated peripheral correlates, not as a direct measure of thymic flux. Our claim is simple: these capacities need not age in concert, whether one compares individuals, tissues, or challenges. The biology behind them is well known. Thymic involution restricts the entry of naive T cells, antigen history reshapes the T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, metabolic and epigenetic changes erode proliferative reserve, and aged tissue niches alter survival, trafficking, and local function. Nevertheless, some individuals retain protective responses in particular subsets and tissues, a pattern consistent with compensation during aging and exceptional longevity. We introduce renewable potential as a broader concept than T-cell stemness and distinguish terminal differentiation from exhaustion and senescence-like phenotypes. We then consider how longitudinal turnover measurements, clone-aware analyses, and perturbation studies can move the field beyond cross-sectional, age-associated signatures. Its predictions are concrete: capacities may disagree within a person, compartments may age at different rates, the limiting capacity may depend on context, compensation may give way to maladaptive fixation, and intervention responses may vary with the baseline capacity profile. Vaccination and infection, cancer, transplantation, autoimmunity, and tissue inflammation illustrate these constraints. On this view, the T-cell immune-longevity capacity profile describes a context-dependent pattern of deficits and compensations, not a universal immune-age score or a proxy for chronological age.

cards.title: Intraoperative hypotension in older adults with hip fracture: a comparative analysis of different definitions.
cards.abstract: Intraoperative hypotension (IOH) is associated with adverse outcomes, but its definition varies widely and most definitions are derived from younger or mixed-age populations. Older adults undergoing hip fracture surgery are particularly susceptible due to reduced physiological reserve. This study compared absolute, relative, and duration-based definitions of IOH and evaluated their associations with postoperative adverse outcomes. This retrospective single-center cohort study included all patients aged ≥ 65 years who underwent hip fracture surgery at Maastricht University Medical Centre+ between January 2021 and December 2022. IOH was defined using absolute thresholds (MAP < 65 mmHg, SBP < 100 mmHg), relative reductions (≥ 20%), post-induction decreases, and duration below thresholds. Outcomes were acute kidney injury (AKI, KDIGO criteria), and 30 day mortality. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index, ASA classification, medication use, and nursing home residency. A total of 473 patients were included (mean age 80.9 years, 69.8% female). Postoperative AKI occurred in 9.9% and 30 day mortality in 5.5%. Absolute and relative IOH thresholds were not significantly associated with outcomes. In contrast, longer IOH duration (SBP < 100 mmHg) was associated with 30 day mortality (OR 1.09 per minute, 95%CI 1.02-1.16). After adjustment, higher ASA classification remained associated with AKI, while IOH duration remained significantly associated with mortality. In older patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, the duration of IOH, rather than static thresholds, appeared more strongly associated with adverse outcomes, particularly 30 day mortality. These findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of hypotension duration and support further prospective research to establish geriatric-specific IOH definitions and optimal perioperative blood pressure management strategies.

cards.title: Short-Term Risk of Pneumonia After Fracture by Anatomical Site in Adults Aged 65 Years or Older: A Propensity Score-Matched TriNetX Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: To compare short-term recorded pneumonia risk across fracture sites in adults aged 65 years or older, focusing on thoracic-region versus lumbar-region vertebral compression fracture (VCF). This retrospective TriNetX cohort study included adults with a first qualifying recorded diagnosis of one of six fractures. Pair-specific cohorts underwent 1:1 propensity score matching. The primary outcome was at least one recorded pneumonia diagnosis during Days 3-90; Days 3-30 were secondary. After matching, the maximum standardized mean difference was 0.031 or less in every comparison. In the primary analysis, 42 959 patients were included in each cohort. During Days 3-90, pneumonia occurred in 1469 patients (3.42%) after thoracic-region VCF and 1171 (2.73%) after lumbar-region VCF (risk ratio [RR], 1.25; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.16-1.35); the 3-30-day RR was 1.31 (95% CI, 1.17-1.46). Versus pair-specifically matched distal-radius cohorts, 3-90-day RRs were 2.29 for thoracic-region VCF, 1.91 for lumbar-region VCF, 2.33 for proximal femur fracture, 1.97 for single-rib fracture, and 2.39 for multiple-rib fractures. Multiple-rib fractures had greater risk than single-rib fracture (RR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.18-1.31). Relative associations with recorded pneumonia were generally stronger during Days 3-30 than during Days 3-90. Risk was higher in the thoracic-region VCF cohort than in the lumbar-region VCF cohort and in the multiple-rib fracture cohort than in the single-rib fracture cohort. These findings may inform respiratory surveillance based on fracture site and rib-fracture burden, subject to residual confounding and diagnostic-code limitations.

cards.title: Associations Between the Nutritional Risk Index for Japanese Hemodialysis Patients and the Risk of Bone Fractures in Patients Receiving Hemodialysis: The Q-Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis have elevated fracture risk, partly owing to undernutrition and protein-energy wasting. The Nutritional Risk Index for Japanese Hemodialysis Patients (NRI-JH) has been proposed as a surrogate marker of protein-energy wasting; however, its association with fracture risk has not been evaluated. Multicenter, prospective cohort study. This study analyzed 3,038 adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis, enrolled in the Q-Cohort Study. The baseline NRI-JH was calculated based on age, sex, body mass index, and serum levels of albumin, creatinine, and total cholesterol, and patients were categorized into 3 groups based on baseline NRI-JH values: group 1, 0-2; group 2, 3-6; and group 3, 7-13. First occurrence of clinically diagnosed bone fractures. Incidence rates were evaluated using the Kaplan-Meier analysis. Cox proportional hazards models and Fine-Gray competing risk models (with death as a competing event) were used to estimate HRs and 95% CIs. During a median follow-up period of 4 years, 140 fractures occurred. Groups 2 and 3 had a significantly higher incidence of fractures than group 1 (log-rank test; P < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, fracture risk remained higher in group 2 (HR, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.24-3.06) and group 3 (HR, 2.05; 95% CI, 1.25-3.38) than in group 1. Competing risk analyses yielded similar results. Subgroup analyses showed consistent associations across age, sex, diabetic nephropathy, inflammation, and chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder parameters without significant interactions. Single baseline measurement of exposure; lack of differentiation between fracture types; potential residual confounding. Higher NRI-JH values were independently associated with an increased fracture risk in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. The NRI-JH may serve as a comprehensive nutritional marker for identifying individuals at an elevated risk of fractures.

cards.title: Pharmacological Interventions for Osteoporosis in Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is a common complication after kidney transplantation and contributes to fracture risk and morbidity among kidney transplant recipients (KTRs). However, the efficacy of pharmacological interventions for osteoporosis in this population remains uncertain. Systematic review and meta-analysis. KTRs. PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched through December 2024 for randomized controlled trials evaluating pharmacological treatments' effects on bone turnover markers, bone mineral density (BMD), and fracture incidence in KTRs. Three independent reviewers extracted study characteristics, type of pharmacological interventions and comparators, and outcomes, including bone turnover markers, BMD, and fracture rates. A random-effects model was used to calculate weighted mean differences (WMD) for continuous outcomes and relative risks for categorical outcomes. A total of 33 randomized controlled trials (2,623 KTRs) were included in this meta-analysis. Pharmacological treatment was not associated with significant changes in parathyroid hormone, bone alkaline phosphatase, and osteocalcin levels. In subgroup analysis, only active vitamin D showed a significant reduction in parathyroid hormone levels (WMD -25.18 pg/mL [-32.59 to -17.77]). Interestingly, pharmacological therapy significantly improved BMD at lumbar spine (WMD 0.04 g/cm2 [0.00 to 0.08]; P = 0.04), radius (WMD 0.14 g/cm2 [0.08-0.19]; P < 0.001), and femoral neck (WMD 0.05 g/cm2 [0.03-0.07]; P < 0.001). However, no significant improvement in BMD was observed at the hip (WMD 0.03 g/cm2 [-0.01 to 0.07]; P = 0.12). Furthermore, there was no statistically significant reduction in fracture risk (RR 0.38 [0.14-1.01]; P = 0.05). Significant clinical and statistical heterogeneity (I2) because of varied pharmacological agents, initiation timing, and recipient characteristics. Pharmacological interventions for osteoporosis in KTRs significantly improved BMD at several skeletal sites, particularly radius site. However, a nonsignificant trend toward reduced fracture incidence was observed.
