cards.title: Macrophage reprogramming in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases: From tissue-niche biology to therapeutic translation.
cards.abstract: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMSDs), including osteoarthritis (OA), osteoporosis (OP), intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), and sarcopenia (SP), impose a major burden through pain, structural deterioration, mobility loss, fracture risk, and functional decline. Although these disorders are often grouped as age-related musculoskeletal conditions, they arise from distinct tissue niches and cannot be explained by a single pathogenic mechanism. Macrophages occupy a central position at the interface between degenerative stress and tissue outcome, but their functions extend far beyond a binary M1/M2 polarization model. This Review proposes a disease-niche-adapted framework for macrophage reprogramming in DMSDs. In this framework, macrophages are interpreted according to the pathological tasks they perform within each tissue environment: inflammatory amplification and pain-related synovial crosstalk in OA, osteoimmune remodeling in OP, immune-barrier disruption and macrophage-nucleus pulposus (NP) cell feedback in IVDD, and impaired regenerative support in aging muscle in SP. We discuss how macrophage functional states are shaped by transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, immunometabolic rewiring, inflammatory signaling, autophagy and organelle quality control, and local niche-derived cues. Therapeutic strategies are then evaluated according to whether they interrupt upstream niche stress, redirect inflammatory and metabolic decoding, restore quality-control capacity, or reshape macrophage-mediated tissue communication. Finally, we propose that macrophage-targeted therapy should be assessed through a hierarchy of evidence, progressing from marker changes to functional reprogramming, macrophage-causal validation, and disease-specific structural or functional improvement. This framework may help convert macrophage plasticity from a broad immunological concept into a more precise, testable, and disease-adapted therapeutic strategy for musculoskeletal degeneration. This Review provides a disease-niche-adapted framework for evaluating macrophage reprogramming in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases. By linking disease-specific macrophage tasks with regulatory mechanisms, therapeutic entry points, causal validation, delivery feasibility, and tissue-relevant endpoints, this framework may help guide both the design and translational assessment of macrophage-targeted interventions for musculoskeletal degeneration.

cards.title: Endothelial Matrin-3 Limits Cellular Senescence and Lipid Dysregulation to Protect Against Murine Atherosclerosis.
cards.abstract: Matrin-3 is a DNA- and RNA-binding protein implicated in cardiovascular development. However, the role of endothelial Matrin-3 in atherosclerosis has not been previously studied. Here, we found that Matrin-3 silencing induces endothelial senescence, characterized by reduced cell proliferation, increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, and impaired mitochondrial function in vitro. Quantitative proteomics and bulk RNA-sequencing identified hundreds of differentially expressed genes and proteins in human endothelial cells. Bioinformatic analyses revealed enrichment of pathways related to DNA replication, p53 signaling, cell-cycle regulation, and cellular senescence. To examine the role of endothelial Matrin-3 in atherosclerosis, we generated Matrin-3 floxed mice on a low-density lipoprotein receptor-knockout background and crossed them with mice carrying an endothelial cell-specific, tamoxifen-inducible Cre driver. In a mouse model of atherosclerosis, endothelial cell-specific Matrin-3 deficiency increased atherosclerotic lesion area by 1.41-fold and was associated with increased plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides, increased hepatic cholesterol and triglycerides, and substantial transcriptional alterations in the aortic intima. Endothelial Matrin-3 deficiency also induced hepatic steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation, and endothelial senescence. Single-nucleus RNA-sequencing of the liver further revealed transcriptional reprogramming of hepatocytes, including alterations in pathways related to lipid metabolism, inflammation, and constitutive androstane receptor signaling, consistent with a functional link between endothelial Matrin-3 deficiency and hepatocyte transcriptional responses. Finally, Matrin-3 expression was reduced in mouse and human atherosclerotic plaques. Together, these findings identify endothelial Matrin-3 as an important regulator of endothelial senescence and lipid homeostasis and demonstrate that endothelial Matrin-3 deficiency is associated with both local vascular alterations and systemic metabolic dysfunction in atherosclerosis.

cards.title: Discharge Mobility After Osteoporotic Thoracolumbar Fractures Using a 2-Stage Machine Learning Prediction Model: Prospective Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: Discharge mobility after osteoporotic vertebral fractures is heterogeneous and difficult to predict at admission. Machine learning offers structured approaches for multiclass functional outcome prediction, but existing models predominantly address binary end points and report global performance metrics without explicit analysis of the error structure. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a 2-stage machine learning framework with a predefined decision policy designed to reduce extreme (LOW-HIGH) misclassification for graded discharge mobility prediction in hospitalized patients with osteoporotic thoracolumbar fractures. This prospective, single-center cohort study enrolled consecutive patients aged 65 years or older admitted for acute osteoporotic thoracic or lumbar fractures (N=158). Discharge mobility was categorized as LOW (<50 m or nonambulatory), MID (50-500 m), or HIGH (>500 m or stair climbing). Clinical associations were analyzed using proportional odds ordinal regression. A predefined 2-stage architecture combined gradient-boosted trees (stage A: HIGH vs non-HIGH) and a random forest classifier (stage L: LOW vs non-LOW). The final 3-class prediction was assigned by a predefined decision policy designed to reduce clinically relevant extreme (LOW-HIGH) misclassification. All preprocessing steps, including fold-wise multiple imputation, were performed within training partitions only. The decision policy was additionally reevaluated in a nested cross-validation with fold-internal threshold selection across 10 repeated partitions. Prefracture HIGH mobility was the only significant independent predictor of discharge mobility (odds ratio [OR] 3.38, 95% CI 1.68-6.80; P<.001); age, comorbidity burden, fracture grade, and treatment were not. In the prespecified analysis with fixed thresholds, performance was moderate (accuracy 0.494; balanced accuracy 0.450; macro-F1 0.444). Binary discrimination yielded an area under the curve of 0.693 (HIGH vs non-HIGH) and 0.625 (LOW vs non-LOW). Using the predefined decision policy, major LOW-HIGH errors were less frequent than with the prefracture mobility-only baseline (5 vs 22), and no HIGH-to-LOW misclassification occurred in the prespecified analysis. In the leakage-free nested cross-validation, macro-F1 was 0.388 (SD 0.031) and major errors had a mean of 8.3 (SD 3.4) vs 22.5 (SD 1.1) for the baseline, with fewer major errors in all 10 partitions. HIGH-to-LOW errors had a mean of 2.6 (SD 2.2) in this analysis. Discharge mobility after osteoporotic thoracolumbar fractures is primarily determined by prefracture functional reserve rather than fracture severity or comorbidity. A 2-stage machine learning framework achieved moderate multiclass discrimination and reduced extreme LOW-HIGH misclassification relative to a mobility-only baseline; this reduction persisted under nested cross-validation, whereas the absence of HIGH-to-LOW errors was specific to the prespecified partition. External validation is required before clinical deployment.

cards.title: Effect of home blood pressure monitoring on major adverse cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality: results from the VA HOMESTEAD study
cards.abstract: Importance: Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) has been shown to lower blood pressure (BP) in randomized trials, however its real-world effect on clinical outcomes is not known. Objective: To determine the association between HBPM and clinical outcomes including cardiovascular events and mortality. Design: Target trial emulation employing matched cohorts with index-date follow-up. Setting: Veterans Health Administration (VHA) telehealth program. Participants: Eligible Veterans had uncontrolled BP (defined as a systolic BP >140 mmHg) at a primary care visit within VHA, with a systolic BP >140 mmHg at the prior primary care visit or average systolic BP >140 mmHg over the year prior. The HBPM (intervention) group included eligible Veterans who were enrolled in a HBPM program for hypertension between January 1, 2013 and December 31, 2019. Individuals in the control group (usual care) were selected from eligible Veterans who were not enrolled in HBPM. Controls were matched with those in the intervention, in part, on demographics, baseline blood pressure and antihypertensive medication use, baseline frailty, mortality risk, and selected comorbidities. Exposure: HBPM in the VHA telehealth program Main Outcomes: All-cause mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the first occurrence during follow-up of acute myocardial infarction, stroke, acute heart failure, or unstable angina. Results: Among 30,203 Veterans enrolled in HBPM and 30,096 non-enrolled controls, with a median duration of 202 days of HBPM and 6.4 years of follow-up, HBPM was associated with 8.3% lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio 0.92; 95% confidence interval 0.89, 0.95) and a 4.1% higher risk of MACE (HR 1.04; 95% CI 1.01, 1.08). In analyses calibrated for negative control outcomes, there was no longer a statistically significant association between HBPM and MACE. Conclusions and Relevance: HBPM as utilized in routine clinical care among a large national cohort of adults with uncontrolled hypertension was associated with reduced risk of mortality. The association between HBPM with increased risk of MACE may have been due to ascertainment differences between those enrolled and not enrolled in HBPM.

cards.title: Preoperative Frailty as a Predictor of Quality of Life Outcomes Following Cytoreductive Surgery.
cards.abstract: Frailty has emerged as a critical determinant of postoperative risk in patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (CRS + HIPEC). However, its impact on postoperative quality of life (QoL) remains underexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative frailty and postoperative QoL in patients undergoing CRS + HIPEC. This retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent CRS + HIPEC at the Royal Prince Alfred Hospital between May 2017 and June 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), with patients classified as frail (CFS ≥ 4) or non-frail (CFS < 4). QoL outcomes were evaluated using the EuroQol 5-Dimension 5-Level (EQ-5D-5 L) and Short Form-36 (SF-36) Health Survey at five time points. Subgroup analyses were conducted based on age (< 65 vs. ≥ 65 years). Of the 364 included patients, 49 (13.5%) were classified as frail. Frailty was significantly associated with poorer QoL outcomes, particularly in mobility, self-care, usual activities, and physical component summary (PCS) scores (all p ≤ 0.003) at baseline. These impairments persisted at three and 6 months postoperatively. Pain and discomfort also emerged as significant issues for frail patients at both three- and 6-months following surgery (p = 0.018 and p = 0.005, respectively). Older frail patients (≥ 65 years) experienced significantly greater impairments in self-care and usual activities at 6 months postoperatively, along with lower mental health summary (MCS) scores at 12 months compared to the non-frail group. Preoperative frailty was significantly associated with poorer QoL outcomes following CRS + HIPEC, highlighting the importance of routine frailty screening and prehabilitation strategies to optimize outcomes in vulnerable patients.

cards.title: Comparative effects of Etanercept and Tocilizumab on skeletal muscle fibers in aged zebrafish.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia, the age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to disability and mortality. Chronic low-grade inflammation, including signaling involving tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6), has been linked to age-related muscle loss. We evaluated whether Etanercept, a TNF-α inhibitor, and Tocilizumab, an IL-6 receptor antagonist, affected skeletal muscle fiber number and the qualitative infiltration of inflammatory cells in aged zebrafish. One hundred wild-type AB zebrafish aged 35-40 months were allocated to five groups (n = 20/group): untreated control, Etanercept 0.8 mg/kg/week, Etanercept 1.6 mg/kg/week, Tocilizumab 4 mg/kg/2 weeks, and Tocilizumab 8 mg/kg/2 weeks. Treatment continued for 3 months. Dorsal skeletal muscle was assessed histologically for cross-sectional area (CSA), number of fibers, and qualitative inflammatory-cell infiltration. Eighty-two of 100 fish survived to study completion. Mean measured dorsal muscle CSA was higher in the Etanercept 0.8 mg/kg group (6.56 ± 0.28 mm²) and the Tocilizumab 8 mg/kg group (5.82 ± 0.40 mm²) than in controls (5.10 ± 0.19 mm², P < 0.001). Etanercept 0.8 mg/kg-treated fish had fewer fibers in the 10,000 μm² sampling area than controls (approximately 26 vs. 57, P < 0.001). Qualitative histology showed minimal or absent inflammatory-cell infiltration in the Etanercept 0.8 mg/kg group. Etanercept 1.6 mg/kg-treated fish had greater endpoint body weight than controls. In aged zebrafish, selected Etanercept and Tocilizumab regimens were associated with differences in measured skeletal muscle fiber characteristics and body weight. Low-dose Etanercept was associated with a higher CSA of the dorsal muscle and a lower number of fibers within the standardized sampling area. These findings represent exploratory histological associations and do not establish preservation of total muscle mass, muscle function, or a specific molecular mechanism. The absence of young controls, functional testing, quantitative inflammatory assessment, and molecular validation limits mechanistic and translational interpretation.

cards.title: Associations of cumulative pulse pressure and pulse pressure trajectories with sarcopenia in two ageing cohorts.
cards.abstract: The relationship between long-term pulse pressure (PP) and sarcopenia remains poorly understood. We analyzed 7,159 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) and 728 from the U.S. Health and Retirement Study (HRS) to examine the association between cumulative PP and trajectories with incident sarcopenia in middle-aged and older adults, using area under the curve (AUC) and latent class trajectory modeling (LCTM). Multivariable logistic regression models were applied to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Potential interactions between PP and chronic conditions, particularly heart disease, were assessed using multiplicative and additive models. Higher cumulative PP was associated with increased sarcopenia risk (per 10 mmHg: CHARLS OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 1.05-1.15; HRS OR = 1.30, 95% CI: 1.13-1.50). Participants in high-stable PP trajectories had the highest risk (CHARLS OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.44-2.93; HRS OR = 1.93, 95% CI: 1.34-2.77). In HRS, the association was significant only among those with heart disease, with multiplicative and additive interactions indicating synergistic effects. Sensitivity and Mendelian randomization analyses supported robustness and potential causality. Cumulative PP and specific PP trajectories were associated with sarcopenia, especially with pre-existing heart disease, supporting PP monitoring for targeted prevention in older adults.

cards.title: Parity, skeletal health and osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Parity and lactation have long been investigated for their potential influence on bone health because of the substantial calcium demands and skeletal remodeling associated with reproduction. Whether these physiological adaptations have adverse long-term effects on maternal bone health remains uncertain. This review consolidates the existing evidence on the impact of pregnancy, lactation, and reproductive factors on bone mineral density (BMD), bone microarchitecture, and fracture risk. Pregnancy is associated with modest, site-specific changes in BMD, while lactation induces transient bone loss. Accelerated skeletal recovery after weaning restores bone mass in most women. Large prospective cohort studies consistently show that parity and lactation are not associated with an increased long-term risk of osteoporosis. However, adverse skeletal outcomes have been reported, potentially related to nutritional deficiencies, prolonged lactation, high reproductive burden, and metabolic comorbidities. Emerging evidence suggests that pregnancy-related skeletal adaptations extend beyond changes in areal BMD and include dynamic alterations in bone quality and microarchitecture. Current evidence suggests that pregnancy and lactation result in physiological, largely reversible skeletal adaptations without compromising long-term bone health in most women. Current evidence supports the largely reversible nature of pregnancy-related and lactation-related skeletal changes, but further longitudinal studies are needed to refine risk assessment and guide evidence-based management.

cards.title: TMAO regulates renal tubular epithelial cell senescence through circVmn2r1.
cards.abstract: The gut microbiota-derived metabolite trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) is an established risk factor for cardiovascular and renal diseases, yet its role in driving kidney aging remains poorly defined. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as critical regulators of cellular senescence, but their integration with systemic metabolic cues in aging processes is largely unknown. Here, we identify a novel signaling axis through which TMAO accelerates renal senescence by dysregulating a specific circRNA pathway. We demonstrate that TMAO treatment induces a senescent phenotype in renal tubular epithelial cells and promotes kidney aging in mice, as evidenced by increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity and elevated expression of p53, p21, and p16. Mechanistically, TMAO significantly upregulates the expression of circVmn2r1, a circRNA we previously identified as a key promoter of kidney aging. This upregulation triggers the activation of the the nucleotide-binding domain, leucine-rich repeat-containing family, pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome, leading to increased caspase-1 cleavage and elevated levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines pro-IL-1β and pro-IL-18. Crucially, genetic knockdown of circVmn2r1 in vitro and in vivo significantly attenuates TMAO-induced NLRP3 upregulation, inflammasome activation, and cellular senescence. Our findings reveal that TMAO functions as an upstream metabolic trigger that promotes renal aging via the circVmn2r1/NLRP3 inflammasome axis. This study elucidates a direct link between a diet-derived metabolite and a specific circRNA-mediated pro-aging pathway, identifying circVmn2r1 as a potential therapeutic target for mitigating metabolic stress-induced kidney aging.

cards.title: Changes in dystrophic calcification of the breast associated with abaloparatide therapy.
cards.abstract: High-risk osteoporosis treatment strategy aims at improving bone mineral density and fracture prevention. Clinicians' awareness of the indications and potential complications associated with osteoporosis treatments is important because it involves caring for patients with comorbidities who experience polypharmacy. We present a case of breast calcification changes after initiation of abaloparatide. A 65-year-old female started abaloparatide therapy and after 8 months of abaloparatide treatment, a significant progression of bilateral breast calcification was noted in screening mammogram prompting a biopsy that showed coarse calcifications without any features of dysplasia or malignancy. After 2 years of abaloparatide therapy, follow-up mammogram revealed stable breast calcifications but that were still significantly increased from baseline prior to abaloparatide. In the absence of possible etiologies such as trauma, end-stage renal disease, or secondary hyperparathyroidism, the strong temporal association suggested abaloparatide treatment as the possible etiology for changes of benign breast calcification.

cards.title: Epidemiology, Fracture Patterns, and Risk Factors Among Motorcycle Crash Victims Treated at Orthopedic Institute, Tanzania.
cards.abstract: Motorcycle crashes are a leading cause of injury and death in low- and middle-income countries, yet detailed data on fracture patterns and severity determinants remain limited in East Africa. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiology, fracture patterns, and associated risk factors among motorcycle crash victims treated at Muhimbili Orthopaedic Institute (MOI). A hospital-based cross-sectional study included 273 motorcyclists with confirmed fractures treated at MOI between January and December 2024. Data on demographics, crash characteristics, injury patterns, and treatment were extracted from medical records using a structured form. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were used to identify predictors of open fractures. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Participants were predominantly male (94.5%) and aged 18-40 years (78.0%). Most were self-employed commercial riders (64.8%) paying out-of-pocket for care (86.8%). High-risk behaviors were common: 45.1% were not wearing helmets, 36.6% had consumed alcohol before riding, and 45.4% of crashes occurred at speeds >80 km/h. Lower limb fractures predominated (62.9%), with tibia/fibula fractures accounting for 39.6% and femur fractures 23.4%. Open fractures represented 43.2% of cases. Crashes clustered during night/early morning and morning peak hours (44.1% each), whereas motorcycle-motorcycle collisions were the commonest crash mechanism (50.9%). On chi-square analysis, speed at impact (p = 0.034) and injury type (p < 0.001) were significantly associated with fracture severity, whereas helmet nonuse showed a nonsignificant trend (p = 0.090). In multivariable logistic regression, lower limb injury was the only independent predictor of open fractures (AOR = 3.42, 95% CI: 1.92-6.09, p < 0.001). Higher riding speeds showed a trend toward increased odds of open fractures but did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (p = 0.059 for the overall speed category variable). Motorcycle crashes in this setting predominantly affect young male riders and frequently result in severe lower limb injuries, with a substantial burden of open fractures requiring resource-intensive surgical care. Lower limb injury was the only independent predictor of open fractures. Speeding, helmet nonuse, and alcohol consumption were highly prevalent modifiable exposures but were not independently associated with open fracture status after adjustment. Drawing on external evidence, strengthening enforcement of speed limits and helmet legislation, implementing workplace-based safety programs for commercial riders, enhancing trauma and orthopedic surgical capacity, and expanding financial protection mechanisms for injured riders are recommended.

cards.title: Melatonin ameliorates calcification in senescent vascular smooth muscle cells under phosphate conditions via the PI3K/AKT pathway.
cards.abstract: In patients with chronic kidney disease, vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) senescence and osteogenic transdifferentiation induced by factors such as hyperphosphatemia are key pathological mechanisms underlying vascular calcification. Recent studies have shown that melatonin exerts protective effects by modulating this process. This study investigated whether melatonin improves calcification in hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-induced senescent VSMCs under phosphate (Pi) conditions through activation of the phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT) pathway, a critical regulator of cell survival and metabolism. A mouse VSMC line was used to establish an H2O2- induced senescence model. Cell viability was assessed using the Cell Counting Kit-8 assay. Senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-Gal) staining was used to evaluate cellular senescence. Western blot analysis was performed to determine the protein expression levels of PI3K, AKT, phosphorylated AKT (p-AKT), Runx-2, and p21. Alizarin Red S staining and intracellular calcium content measurements were conducted to assess VSMC calcification. Melatonin significantly reduced SA-β-Gal activity, enhanced VSMC viability, decreased the Alizarin Red S-positivearea, and lowered intracellular calcium levels. Melatonin downregulated Runx-2 and p21 expression while upregulating PI3K, AKT, and p-AKT expression. In contrast, the PI3K/AKT inhibitor LY294002 exacerbated calcification and inhibited activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway.These results suggest that melatonin may mitigate VSMCs calcification associated with aging in a phosphate-rich environment by activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway at the cellular level. LY294002(PI3K inhibitor)blocks this protective effect and aggravates cellular damage and calcification, further suggesting that the PI3K/AKT pathway plays a critical regulatory role incalcification process in cultured VSMCs.

cards.title: Fibrosis: Past Insights, Current Challenges, and Therapeutic Frontiers.
cards.abstract: Fibrosis is a maladaptive repair process marked by fibroblast activation, myofibroblast accumulation, and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, which can compromise tissue architecture and organ function. Its causes, cellular niches, reversibility, and therapeutic windows vary across the lung, liver, kidney, and heart. This review outlines the canonical pathological processes of tissue injury, inflammation, fibroblast activation, and matrix deposition, then discusses emerging evidence on metabolic reprogramming, hypoxia, epigenetic regulation, and mechanotransduction, while also considering cellular senescence and immune-stromal communication. We focus on the lactate-lactylation axis, which links altered metabolism to transcriptional and protein regulation through lactate production, transport, signaling, and histone or nonhistone lactylation. Evidence from numerous studies suggests that this axis may shape fibrosis-associated cell states, but its effects vary by organ, cell type, and disease stage. We therefore distinguish among associative observations, functional validation, and site-specific validation and assess whether lactylation acts as a driver, amplifier, or marker of fibrotic remodeling. We also evaluate current antifibrotic therapies and discuss metabolic and epigenetic interventions, modulation of immune-stromal interactions, and matrix-directed and precision-delivery strategies. Clinical translation requires context-specific causal evidence, standardized detection methods, biomarker-guided patient selection, and endpoints that distinguish slowed progression from fibrosis reversal.

cards.title: Utility of creatine kinase and myoglobin as adjuncts in the diagnosis of acute compartment syndrome: a retrospective case-control study.
cards.abstract: Acute compartment syndrome (ACS) can be difficult to diagnose clinically, and compartment pressure measurement is invasive and prone to technical inaccuracy. Creatine kinase (CK), released during muscle injury, has been proposed as a diagnostic adjunct, but optimal thresholds remain poorly defined. Retrospective Case-Control study. Adult patients with an isolated limb injury and an initial CK and/or myoglobin measurement, treated between January 2017 and June 2025, were reviewed. Patients who developed ACS and underwent fasciotomy were compared with patients with an isolated fracture who did not. Initial CK, myoglobin, creatinine, urea, and lactic acid were compared between groups. ROC curve analysis assessed the discriminatory ability of CK and myoglobin, and Firth penalised logistic regression evaluated CK as an independent predictor after adjustment for age, sex, open vs. closed injury, mechanism of injury, anatomical region, and time to first sample. Of 109 patients, 32 had ACS and 77 were controls; initial CK was available in 88 (24 ACS, 64 controls). Initial CK was significantly higher in patients with ACS (median 887 vs. 227 U/L, p < 0.001), as was myoglobin (523 vs. 321, p = 0.023). CK showed good discrimination for ACS (AUC 0.84, 95% CI 0.71-0.96), significantly outperforming myoglobin (AUC 0.67; p = 0.012 for comparison). A Youden-derived threshold of 405 U/L yielded 75.0% sensitivity, 90.6% specificity, and a positive likelihood ratio of 8.0; however, 25% of ACS cases fell below this threshold. CK remained independently associated with ACS after adjustment (OR 1.31 per 100 U/L, 95% CI 1.05-1.62, p = 0.015). Initial CK was independently associated with ACS and outperformed myoglobin as a discriminatory biomarker. However, no CK threshold was sufficient to exclude or confirm ACS, and CK should be used only as an adjunct to clinical assessment pending prospective external validation.

cards.title: 3D-CT-guided patient-specific instrumentation versus conventional implants for traumatic malunited distal radius corrective osteotomies: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: Corrective osteotomy for traumatic malunited distal radius fractures has traditionally relied on conventional pre-contoured plates. Patient-specific instrumentation (PSI) with three-dimensional (3D) CT-guided planning offers theoretical advantages through individualised design and improved anatomical fit, but comparative clinical evidence remains limited. We aimed to evaluate functional outcomes and complications following patient-specific versus conventional implants for distal radius corrective osteotomy. A comprehensive literature search was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines, including MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus and CINAHL databases for studies published up to September 2025. Clinical studies directly comparing PSI with conventional implants, and single-arm PSI studies, were included. Meta-analyses were performed when two or more studies reported identical outcome measures, using random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool (RoB-1). Eighteen studies (15 single-arm PSI, three comparative) with 321 patients (282 PSI, 39 conventional) were included; mean follow-up was 14.4 ± 5.5 months and mean age 46.8 ± 7.3 years. For radiological parameters, volar tilt showed a pooled mean difference (MD) of - 8.87° (95% CI - 11.42 to - 6.32; I2 = 0.0%) favouring less volar tilt with PSI; radial inclination showed a pooled MD of - 0.89° (95% CI - 4.19 to 2.41; I² = 0.0%); and ulnar variance a pooled MD of 1.19 mm (95% CI - 0.40 to 2.78; I² =265.9%). Flexion-extension improved by 26.63°, with a final pooled arc of 134.69° (95% CI 117.73 to 154.08). Pronation-supination improved by 23.33°, with a final arc of 159.71° (95% CI 153.83 to 165.81). The pooled complication rate was 4% (95% CI 1% to 7%) and the revision risk ratio was 0.60 (95% CI 0.27 to 1.35; I2 = 0.0%) for PSI. There was a promising trend towards fewer complications and revision surgery with PSI. Both techniques achieved acceptable radiological restoration, with PSI conferring a modest advantage in ulnar variance but resulting in slight under-correction of volar tilt. Functional outcomes and range of motion improved to a clinically meaningful degree with both approaches, though this was accompanied by substantial heterogeneity between studies. High-quality randomised controlled trials are required to confirm these findings and to justify the additional costs associated with PSI technology.

cards.title: Beyond oncologic cure: optimizing surgical outcomes in older adults with early colorectal cancer.
cards.abstract: Early colorectal cancer in older adults requires a balance between oncologic benefit and the risks of postoperative functional decline, loss of independence, and competing mortality. Chronological age alone is insufficient to guide this balance because physiological reserve, functional status, comorbidity, cognition, nutritional status, and life expectancy vary substantially among individuals of the same age. Frailty and sarcopenia provide complementary information regarding vulnerability to surgical stress, but frailty should not be used as an automatic indication for treatment de-escalation. Rather, frailty screening should identify patients who require multidimensional geriatric assessment to characterize clinically relevant vulnerabilities and guide individualized preoperative management. This review proposes an optimization-based framework for individualized surgical decision-making in older adults with early colorectal cancer. Patients with evidence of geriatric vulnerability should undergo comprehensive geriatric assessment, including evaluation of functional independence, physical performance, muscle strength, nutritional status, comorbidity, medication burden, cognition, and social support. When oncologically safe, a time-limited period of individualized optimization, including exercise, nutritional intervention, medical optimization, medication review, and psychosocial support, may be considered before definitive surgical planning. Reassessment should emphasize the direction of change in functional reserve and recovery potential rather than categorical reversal of frailty. Patients with a favorable trajectory after optimization may remain candidates for guideline-concordant oncologic surgery. In contrast, persistently limited reserve should prompt multidisciplinary and shared decision-making that considers tumor-specific oncologic benefit, functional consequences, competing mortality, and patient priorities. This approach reframes frailty assessment from static risk prediction toward an individualized, optimization-based strategy while preserving oncologic principles.

cards.title: Bushen Huoxue Formula promotes osteoporotic fracture healing by CGRP-mediated dual regulation of BMSCs-osteoclasts balance through modulating mitochondrial energy metabolism.
cards.abstract: Osteoporotic fracture (OPF) is a serious complication that severely impairs the quality of life. Bushen Huoxue Formula (BHF), a clinically established prescription based on the TCM principle of "tonifying the kidney and activating blood circulation," has been widely used to treat osteoporosis. However, its efficacy in OPF and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, using a rat OPF model, we found that BHF treatment significantly accelerated the fracture healing process and improved callus microstructure and mineralization. Multi-omics analysis revealed that its therapeutic effect was closely associated with the regulation of mitochondrial energy metabolism, identifying CGRP as a key differential target. Mechanistically, CGRP was upregulated in bone mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), where it enhanced mitochondrial energy metabolism and promoted osteogenic differentiation. Conversely, in osteoclast precursor RAW264.7 cells, CGRP was downregulated and inhibited osteoclast differentiation, demonstrating its dual regulatory role in bone remodeling via the same target. Further studies showed that taurine, a major component of BHF, could recapitulate the formula's effects by modulating CGRP to promote osteogenesis and suppress osteoclastogenesis. Importantly, corroborative clinical research demonstrated that BHF treatment effectively alleviated clinical symptoms and promoted fracture repair in OPF patients. In summary, BHF facilitates OPF healing through CGRP mediated mitochondrial energy metabolism, providing both mechanistic insight and clinical evidence for its repositioning from osteoporosis to fracture management.

cards.title: Infectious complications are preceded by specific longitudinal neutrophil cell surface patterns after polytrauma: Preliminary results of a prospective analysis.
cards.abstract: Alterations in neutrophil receptors provide valuable insights into the immune response after polytrauma. Point-of-care (POC) technologies enable rapid on-site analysis of neutrophils. Previous studies demonstrated individual neutrophil surface patterns after trauma, depending on injury severity and metabolic status. We hypothesized that infectious complications after polytrauma are preceded by specific neutrophil cell surface receptor alterations. A POC neutrophil analysis system (AQUIOS® Flow Cytometer) was implemented at a Level 1 trauma center. Polytrauma patients with an Injury Severity Score (ISS)≥25 were prospectively included. Neutrophil cell surface expression of CD10, CD11b, CD64, CD62L, and CD16 was analyzed immediately after admission and after 8 hours, 24 hours, 48 hours, and 5 days. Patients were grouped according to the occurrence or absence of infectious complications. Thirty-two polytrauma patients with a median ISS of 34.5 were included in this study. Trauma sequelae included spine fractures, long bone fractures, and traumatic brain injury. During hospitalization, 13 out of 32 patients developed infectious complications. Patients who subsequently developed infectious complications showed significantly higher CD64 expression throughout the observation period, and CD62L demonstrated a trend toward higher expression. In addition, CD11b expression was elevated 8 hours after trauma. Longitudinal assessment of multiple selected neutrophil markers draws an individual neutrophil surface profile, with specific patterns associated with the development of infectious complications. This offers a promising tool for early risk stratification and identification of trauma patients vulnerable to post-traumatic infectious complications and allows for future immune-protective trauma surgery. Prognostic and Epidemiological; Level III.

cards.title: Metabolic fitness of CAR T-cell therapy: an aging approach
cards.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy represents the cutting edge of modern cancer immunotherapy. However, aging impairs T-cell function and limits the applicability of CAR T-cell therapy in clinical oncology as the vast majority of patients with cancer are older than 60 years. To address this challenge, we must turn to a field that, paradoxically, is well recognized in clinical practice but has received relatively little attention in the context of this therapy: the CAR T-cell fitness. This review discusses how the relationship between metabolism and CAR T-cells can be leveraged to overcome current limitations. We examine this topic from two main perspectives: the impact of aging on CAR T-cell function; and the restructuring of CAR T-cell therapy to incorporate metabolic cues that enhance the CAR T-cell responses, including CAR design, manufacturing and clinical application. We describe how aging influences CAR T-cell biology through immunosenescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, and local and systemic inflammation. This evidence also supports the consideration of age as an important factor in clinical decision-making when selecting patients for CAR T-cell therapy, although additional meta-analyses will be needed to strengthen this concept. Finally, we highlight how redirecting basic research toward aging models will facilitate further advances and broaden the outlook of CAR T-cell therapy.

cards.title: Interferon-driven T-cell activation and a senescence-associated signature characterize clinically active adult localized scleroderma
cards.abstract: Background: Localized scleroderma (LS, morphea) is an immune-mediated fibrosing skin disease whose molecular basis in adults, and its variation with clinical activity and histological stage, are poorly defined. Objectives: To characterize transcriptional, cellular and senescence-associated programs in adult LS by clinical activity, histological stage and subtype, and to compare them with those of other inflammatory skin diseases. Methods: We performed bulk RNA sequencing of archival lesional skin from 60 adults with LS and 22 healthy controls (HC), with enrichment analyses, cell-type deconvolution, immune-module scoring, cross-disease comparison and p16INK4a immunohistochemistry. Results: LS lesions showed 704 differentially expressed genes versus HC, enriched for interferon signaling, antigen presentation and T-helper differentiation pathways; changes were extensive in clinically active (n = 49) and histologically inflammatory (n = 21) lesions but limited in fibrotic lesions (n = 33). Deconvolution inferred expansion of fibroblasts, macrophages and regulatory, cytotoxic and helper T cells, with co-expression of effector and checkpoint genes in T-cell profiles (IFNG, GZMK, LAG3, TIGIT). Th1 and Th17 activity was higher in inflammatory than in fibrotic lesions, whereas Th2 activity did not differ between them. A senescence-associated gene set was enriched in LS (normalized enrichment score 1.64), including fibrotic lesions (nominal P <0.05), and dermal p16INK4a-positive cell density was higher than in HC (median 113.9 vs 36.0 cells/mm^2; P = 0.003). LS signatures most closely resembled those of cutaneous lupus erythematosus and lichen planus. Conclusions: Adult LS shows interferon-associated T-cell activation, most pronounced in clinically active and histologically inflammatory disease, and a senescence-associated signature. Type-2 and senescence-associated programs persist in fibrotic lesions. These findings support Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) inhibition in active disease and trials of senescence-modulating therapies across disease stages.

cards.title: Lactate-Lactylation Signaling at the Macrophage-Disc Cell Interface: Immunometabolic Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities in Intervertebral Disc Degeneration.
cards.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) develops within an avascular, hypoxic, and lactate-rich microenvironment in which metabolic stress converges with cellular senescence, ferroptosis, oxidative injury, and chronic inflammation. Lactate is not only a glycolytic end product and signaling metabolite but also a substrate for lysine lactylation. This narrative review evaluates lactate-driven lactylation at the macrophage-nucleus pulposus (NP) cell interface and distinguishes disc-supported findings from correlative observations and cross-tissue mechanistic inference. Disc studies link AMPKα lactylation to impaired autophagy and senescence; H3K18 lactylation and ACSL4 K412 lactylation to ferroptosis; THBS1-associated H3K18 lactylation to inflammatory transcription; and SOD1 K123 lactylation to defective antioxidant defense. No study using intervertebral disc tissue has yet demonstrated NP-to-macrophage lactate transfer, lactate-induced lactylation in disc macrophages, or a complete macrophage-NP feed-forward loop. The possible reprogramming of disc macrophages by NP-derived lactate is therefore inferred mainly from other hypoxic and inflammatory tissues and requires direct testing in disc models. These observations motivate a proposed bidirectional lactate-lactylation interaction as a testable model while distinguishing disc-supported NP-intrinsic mechanisms from an unresolved immune arm. This framework highlights pharmacologically tractable nodes in lactate production and transport, lactylation writers and erasers, ACSL4-dependent ferroptosis, SOD1 dysfunction, senescence, and macrophage state control. It also emphasizes the risks of suppressing physiological NP glycolysis and the need for disc-restricted delivery. Cell-type-resolved validation in human tissue will be essential before lactylation-directed interventions can be translated into disease-modifying therapy.

cards.title: TRPM2-mediated Ca2+ entry drives cellular senescence to irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction.
cards.abstract: Aberrant Ca2+ signaling, mediated by multiple ion channels, is increasingly recognized as a central driver of irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction; however, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we identify the transient receptor potential melastatin-2 (TRPM2) channel as a key mediator of irradiation-induced Ca2+ entry that drives salivary gland dysfunction. Trpm2 -/- mice were resistant to irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction at the acute/early stage of post-irradiation. RNA sequence analysis further showed that cell cycle pathways were upregulated, along with a decrease in ROS and its associated pathways in irradiated Trpm2 -/- mice. Mechanistically, our data show that loss of TRPM2 decreases cellular senescence, restores mitochondrial Ca2+ handling and bioenergetics, along with DNA repair and protein synthesis. Finally, we show that pharmacological inhibition of senescence with quercetin or piperlongumine prevents irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction. Together, our findings provide a mechanistic link between TRPM2-dependent Ca2+ signaling and cellular senescence as a key driver of irradiation-induced salivary gland dysfunction.

cards.title: Same-Day TAVR and Femur Fracture Repair in a 103-Year-Old Woman: Beyond Chronologic Age.
cards.abstract: A 103-year-old woman with critical nonrheumatic calcific aortic stenosis was transferred to an academic medical center after an urgent femoral fracture fixation was deferred because of high perioperative cardiac risk. Why was transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) chosen before orthopedic surgery, and why was balloon aortic valvuloplasty not an optimal bridge? What was the severity and clinical impact of post-TAVR aortic regurgitation? How did procedural risk influence sedation and anesthesia? How did multidisciplinary teams coordinate expedited care? TAVR was performed to reduce intraoperative cardiac risk, followed by open reduction and internal fixation later the same day. Structural heart, anesthesia, orthopedic, rehabilitation, and social work teams coordinated expedited treatment and recovery planning. Severe aortic stenosis and acute fracture require coordinated, time-sensitive management. TAVR may facilitate timely orthopedic surgery and reduce immobilization-related decline. Candidacy should consider frailty, functional status, physiologic reserve, procedural risk, recovery potential, and patient goals, not age alone.

cards.title: The Cross-sectional and longitudinal association of metabolic obesity phenotypes with osteoporosis and fracture: from discovery in the REACTION study to evidence in the UK Biobank.
cards.abstract: The relationship between obesity and bone health has attracted increasing attention, yet findings remain inconsistent. Obesity often coexists with metabolic abnormalities and differences in metabolic state might therefore explain discrepancies across studies of obesity and bone health. We included 11,633 and 22,648 Chinese REACTION participants in the osteoporosis and fracture analyses, respectively. From the UK Biobank (UKB), 167,759 participants were included in the cross-sectional analysis, of whom 163,252 and 131,083 were followed up for osteoporosis and fracture, respectively. Logistic and Cox models were used to estimate associations. The analyses were further stratified by metabolic health status, and transitions in metabolic obesity status were also examined. In the cross-sectional UKB analysis, osteoporosis prevalence was higher in MHN (OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.40-1.81) and MUN (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.34-1.71) than in MHOO, with similar patterns for major osteoporotic fractures (MOFs); in REACTION, these associations did not reach statistical significance. In the longitudinal UKB analysis, over a median follow-up of 13.74 years, osteoporosis risk was 52% higher in MHN and 57% higher in MUN than in MHOO, and MOFs risk was also elevated in MHN and MUN. BMI was non-linearly associated with each outcome in the metabolically unhealthy subgroup. Deterioration from MHOO to MUOO was associated with higher odds of osteoporosis and fractures than stable MHOO. The risk of osteoporosis and fractures varied across metabolic obesity phenotypes and was not explained by BMI alone, suggesting that metabolic health status may also contribute to bone outcomes.

cards.title: Satellite cell attrition and skeletal muscle aging
cards.abstract: Abstract Skeletal muscle aging involves the progressive decline in mass and function of muscle tissue, significantly impacting mobility and quality of life in older adults. Central to this process is the functional deterioration of SCs, the primary muscle stem cells responsible for regeneration. Aging impairs SC self-renewal, activation, proliferation, and differentiation through mechanisms including telomere attrition, mitochondrial dysfunction, epigenetic dysregulation, and aberrant signaling pathways such as Notch/Wnt and TGF-β. Additionally, the aged microenvironment—marked by chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, fibro-adipogenic infiltration, immune dysregulation, and vascular decline—further suppresses SC activity. Recent advances in multidisciplinary research, encompassing single-cell genomics, epigenetics, and bioengineering, have deepened our understanding of these mechanisms. Emerging interventions, such as nutritional strategies, exercise, pharmacological agents, cell therapy, and gene editing, offer promising avenues for restoring SC function and rejuvenating muscle regeneration. Future efforts should focus on integrated, personalized approaches to combat sarcopenia and improve healthspan.

cards.title: Aging drives senescence in visceral adipose to a greater extent than obesity, instigating multicellular common signaling patterns that impair organ function and drive inflammation
cards.abstract: Abstract Obesity accelerates key hallmarks of biological aging in visceral adipose tissue (VAT), yet age-associated changes in cellular senescence against a background of sustained elevated adiposity remain poorly understood. To investigate these changes, we examined human omental VAT from younger (18-35 years), middle-aged (36-51 years), and older adults (52-75 years) with comparable BMI (40 ±5 kg/m 2 ) using a cross-sectional design. We integrated bulk and single- nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), Visium HD spatial transcriptomics, and three complementary computational approaches for senescent cell (SnC) identification. VAT from older adults exhibited increased expression of senescence-associated markers, including CDKN2A (p16INK4a) and CDKN1A (p21CIP1), as well as enhanced fibro-inflammatory and tissue-remodeling programs. snRNA-seq revealed a non-linear age-associated pattern, with relatively modest differences between younger and middle-aged adults and more pronounced senescence- associated changes in older adults. SnCs were increased primarily in adipose stem/progenitor cells and mesothelium, which also emerged as major intercellular communication hubs. CellChat analyses identified SnCs of multiple lineages converging on shared outgoing signaling programs, implicating inflammatory, extracellular matrix-remodeling, and adipogenic regulatory pathways, including IL-1, IL-6, TGF-β, and WNT signaling. These predicted interactions were accompanied by transcriptional programs involving HIF1A, NF-κB, SMADs, PRRX1, and TP53 in SnCs, as well as consistent upregulation of KDM6B a histone demethylase activating gene expression. Collectively, our findings suggest that aging drives the senescence program to a greater extent than obesity, potentiating tissue dysfunction through coordinated intercellular signaling mechanisms.

cards.title: MicroDUET: a dual-headed genomic foundation model for pathogen surveillance
cards.abstract: Pathogen genomic surveillance works from raw reads, assembled genomes and alignments, representations that are slow and costly to compare at scale. Compact embeddings from genomic language models offer an alternative, but surveillance requires resolving both evolutionary ancestry (phylogeny) and phenotypic capability (function) - which need not co-vary. Here we present MicroDUET, which adapts a 26.6-million-parameter ProkBERT backbone with two 3.5-million-parameter adapter heads: a phylogeny head trained contrastively on genome windows from the same microbes, and a function head trained to identify genes across taxa. On held-out retrieval benchmarks, the phylogeny head returned the correct species for 80.3% and 66.6% of cellular and viral queries, and the function head the correct gene family for 97.3% and 97.2%, reaching 74.4% accuracy on an independent antimicrobial resistance-class benchmark. Across all three benchmarks MicroDUET outranked 17 other genomic encoders. Without training on lineage, clade or drug-susceptibility tasks, MicroDUET identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis and mpox virus lineages and clades (0.965, 0.975 accuracy), discriminated rifampicin resistance without lineage adjustment (AUROC 0.985), and retrospectively identified an emerging mpox lineage as anomalous (AUROC 0.974). MicroDUET operates 10^3 - 10^4 times faster than single-threaded sequence-based alignments. MicroDUET therefore provides a compact, reusable representation for scalable pathogen surveillance and sequence triage.

cards.title: Real-world treatment patterns following denosumab discontinuation: a descriptive epidemiological study.
cards.abstract: This descriptive epidemiological study suggests that sequential osteoporosis therapy after denosumab discontinuation is underutilized in real-world practice. Within 1 year after discontinuation, approximately 30% of patients restarted denosumab, approximately half had no subsequent osteoporosis treatment, and only 16% initiated sequential osteoporosis therapy. To describe real-world treatment patterns following denosumab discontinuation, including delayed reinitiation, no subsequent osteoporosis treatment, and sequential osteoporosis therapy. This descriptive epidemiological study used a Japanese claims database (April 2014-March 2024). We included adults aged ≥40 years who newly initiated denosumab and discontinued it after ≥2 doses. Discontinuation was defined as the last administration before a gap of >240 days or final observed administration followed by ≥240 days without another administration. The primary outcomes within 1 year after discontinuation were delayed denosumab reinitiation, no subsequent osteoporosis treatment, and sequential osteoporosis therapy. We also described the type and timing of sequential therapy and estimated the 1-year cumulative incidence of fragility fractures. Among 37,526 eligible patients, the 1-year cumulative incidence of delayed denosumab reinitiation was 29.6%, the probability of no subsequent osteoporosis treatment was 50.9%, and the cumulative incidence of sequential osteoporosis therapy was 16.3%. Oral bisphosphonates were the most frequently used sequential therapy (26.7%), followed by romosozumab (22.2%), selective estrogen receptor modulators (21.3%), intravenous bisphosphonates (15.1%), teriparatide (14.6%), and abaloparatide (0.1%). Sequential therapy was most often initiated 180-209 days after discontinuation, particularly for romosozumab (45.7%), whereas selective estrogen receptor modulators were frequently initiated 0-29 days after discontinuation (39.8%). The 1-year cumulative incidence of fragility fractures was 5.4%. Within 1 year after discontinuation, approximately 30% of patients restarted denosumab, half received no subsequent osteoporosis treatment, and one in six initiated sequential therapy. These findings suggest a substantial gap in the continuity of osteoporosis care.

cards.title: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery in Gastrointestinal Cancer: A Narrative Review of Perioperative Evidence, Compliance-Associated Outcomes, and Geriatric Considerations.
cards.abstract: Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) has become an important component of perioperative care in gastrointestinal oncology, although its implementation remains challenging because of heterogeneous patient profiles. This review critically examines current perioperative evidence, integrates the 2025 ERAS Society guidelines, and discusses three key areas for future development in ERAS: frailty-stratified care, compliance-associated clinical outcomes, and the potential effects of ERAS on perioperative inflammation and oncologic recovery. Recent evidence highlights three key areas. First, frailty is an important determinant of perioperative vulnerability in older patients, and Geriatric 8 (G8) screening combined with geriatric co-management can help identify vulnerable individuals and guide individualized perioperative care. Second, ERAS compliance shows a graded association with postoperative morbidity, while machine learning-based analyses suggest that patient characteristics are associated with differences in adherence and recovery trajectories, supporting the implementation of risk-stratified pathways. Third, clinical studies have reported reductions in postoperative inflammatory markers following ERAS implementation, providing a biological rationale for further investigating its effects on perioperative immune function. ERAS implementation is also associated with earlier return to intended oncologic therapy (RIOT), although its impact on long-term oncologic outcomes requires further evaluation. The future development of ERAS lies in dynamic, risk-adapted decision-making rather than rigid protocol enforcement. Integrating continuous quality audits, frailty assessment, geriatric co-management, and individualized perioperative interventions provides an important framework for optimizing recovery across diverse patient populations. Further research should clarify the immunological effects of ERAS, determine whether improvements in short-term recovery translate into long-term oncologic benefits, and extend coordinated perioperative care beyond hospital discharge, as explored in the ERAS 3.0 paradigm.

cards.title: Underweight and obesity as outcome predictors after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: insights from the DOUBLE-CHOICE trial.
cards.abstract: An "obesity paradox" has been described after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), suggesting lower mortality in patients with higher body mass index (BMI) despite greater comorbidity. In contrast, underweight consistently predicts adverse outcomes. Whether these associations reflect a true biological effect or are primarily driven by residual confounding, frailty, and patient selection remains uncertain. This prespecified subgroup analysis included eligible patients from the randomized DOUBLE-CHOICE trial comparing two transcatheter heart valves and two anesthesia strategies (minimalist approach with local anesthesia only vs. standard care with conscious sedation). The primary endpoint was a 30-day composite of all-cause mortality, vascular and bleeding complications, infections requiring antibiotic therapy, and neurologic events. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, frailty, diabetes, hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and anesthesia strategy. Among 752 patients (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2, n = 192; BMI < 30 kg/m2, n = 560), obese patients had lower rates of the 30-day primary endpoint (15.2% vs. 27.6%; p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, obesity remained independently associated with lower risk (adjusted OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30-0.75; p = 0.002). In contrast, underweight (BMI < 20 kg/m2; n = 23) was associated with a higher incidence of the primary endpoint (55.0% vs. 23.4%; p = 0.003) and remained an independent predictor after adjustment (adjusted OR 3.74, 95% CI 1.30-9.52; p = 0.005). In this randomized TAVI population, obesity was independently associated with favorable 30-day outcomes, whereas underweight identified a small but high-risk subgroup with substantially increased procedural risk. These findings identify underweight as a potential high-risk phenotype requiring further investigation in future studies incorporating more detailed measures of frailty and body composition.

cards.title: Before late effects emerge: does ionizing radiation accelerate aging in cancer survivors?
cards.abstract: Cancer survivors can experience an earlier onset and a greater burden of age-related conditions, raising the question of whether cancer treatments alter underlying aging trajectories. Ionizing radiation causes persistent, organ-specific late effects and biological changes that overlap with the main hallmarks of aging, but whether these effects also reflect accelerated aging remains uncertain. This Debate distinguishes premature aging, defined as the earlier occurrence of age-related conditions, from accelerated aging, which requires a faster longitudinal accumulation of biological, functional, or multimorbidity-related deficits. Current radiation epidemiology provides evidence for dose-related late disease risks but does not determine whether ionizing radiation mainly advances the timing of otherwise expected events, increases their cumulative burden, or alters the underlying rate of aging. Earlier disease onset alone should therefore not be interpreted as evidence of accelerated aging, particularly because cancer, other treatments, baseline vulnerability, lifestyle, and socioeconomic factors can produce similar aging phenotypes. Testing this hypothesis requires longitudinal aging phenotyping initiated before treatment, individual-level dosimetry, clinically appropriate comparison groups, and causal analyses able to separate temporal shifts from changes in the slope of functional decline. Outcomes should integrate biomarkers of biological aging with clinical frailty, physical and cognitive function, multimorbidity, and disability-free survival. Systemic radiation-related accelerated aging is not yet established, but it represents a testable framework for clarifying the relationship between radiation exposure, late effects, and long-term physiological reserve.

cards.title: Type 2 angiotensin II receptor (AT2R) deficiency exacerbates cardiac senescence and fibrosis in aging mice.
cards.abstract: Cardiac aging increases susceptibility to cardiovascular diseases. Cellular senescence may be involved in the development of age-related cardiac diseases. Extensive evidence derived from both clinical and experimental studies suggests that the type 2 angiotensin II receptor (AT2R) exerts a potent cardioprotective effect; however, its potential contribution to age-related cardiac complications remains unknown. In the present study, we used AT2R knockout (AT2-KO) and wild-type mice (WT), both aged (18-21 months) and young (4-5 months), and evaluated the repercussions of cardiac aging. Old AT2-KO mice exhibited impaired systolic and diastolic cardiac function and exacerbated fibrosis accompanied by increased expression of fibrotic markers. The absence of AT2R accelerated the cardiac senescence process in old mice, evidenced by early increase in p53 and p21. In addition, aged AT2-KO mice showed increased expression of senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) components, activation of cardiac NF-κB and NLRP3-inflammasome followed by increased levels of cardiac IL-1β and IL-18 compared with aged WT mice. AT2R deficiency also resulted in significant DNA damage even in young animals, and it was associated with a 5-month reduction in median lifespan (26 months for AT2R-KO versus 31 months for WT). These findings suggest potential mechanisms whereby AT2R acts as a key mediator of cardiac senescence and cardioprotection during aging.

cards.title: Stem Cell-Based Regenerative Strategies for Bone Aging: Current Advances and Future Perspectives
cards.abstract: Bone aging is characterized by a progressive decline in skeletal regenerative capacity, driven by stem-cell senescence, chronic inflammation, impaired vascularization, metabolic dysfunction, and alterations in the bone marrow niche. These changes contribute to osteoporosis, delayed fracture healing, and reduced bone quality in older individuals. Stem cell-based therapies have emerged as promising strategies to restore bone regeneration, with investigations focusing on mesenchymal stromal cells, skeletal stem cells, adipose-derived stromal cells, induced pluripotent stem cell-derived osteogenic progenitors, and cell-free approaches such as extracellular vesicles and secretomes. This narrative review examines the biological mechanisms underlying bone aging, the impact of the aged microenvironment on stem-cell function, and current approaches to rejuvenate skeletal regeneration. We discuss advances in tissue engineering, including biomaterials, 3D-printed scaffolds, controlled-release systems, and multifunctional constructs designed to modulate inflammation, enhance angiogenesis, and improve osteogenesis. Preclinical studies consistently demonstrate beneficial effects on bone formation, microarchitecture, and repair; however, translation to clinical practice remains limited. Human studies have primarily focused on fracture nonunion and focal bone defects, showing encouraging safety and feasibility but insufficient evidence for systemic treatment of age-related skeletal fragility. Major barriers include cellular heterogeneity, manufacturing and regulatory challenges, inadequate potency assays, and the complexity of the aged bone niche. Future success will likely depend on integrated therapeutic strategies that simultaneously target progenitor-cell dysfunction and the local microenvironment while ensuring reproducible, scalable, and clinically meaningful outcomes. These advances may pave the way toward effective regenerative therapies for osteoporosis and age-related bone loss.

cards.title: The phenotypic spectrum of McCune-Albright syndrome: a report of four paediatric cases and a literature review.
cards.abstract: McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS) is a rare mosaic disorder caused by postzygotic activating variants in GNAS, resulting in constitutive activation of stimulatory G protein alpha subunit (Gsα) signalling. The phenotype classically includes fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait macules and hyperfunctioning endocrinopathies, but the clinical spectrum extends beyond this triad. We describe four paediatric cases and review the current literature, with emphasis on the diagnostic challenges of mosaicism, endocrine morbidity and evolving treatment. The four cases comprise a boy with polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, hyperthyroidism and Sertoli-cell hyperplasia; a girl with early fractures, peripheral precocious puberty, suspected phosphate wasting and craniofacial fibrous dysplasia; an adolescent with segmental pigmentation, pain and MRI-confirmed fibrous dysplasia after negative blood and skin testing; and a girl with very early gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty, transient hepatobiliary abnormalities and positive GNAS testing from a café-au-lait macule but no MRI evidence of fibrous dysplasia. MAS is a dynamic multisystem mosaic disorder in which manifestations may emerge at different ages and in no fixed order. Negative blood testing does not exclude the diagnosis. Longitudinal endocrine, skeletal, ophthalmological and multidisciplinary surveillance is essential, and treatment should be directed at both endocrine control and preservation of skeletal function.

cards.title: Nanoparticles reshaping graft-versus-host disease landscape.
cards.abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) is a major immune-mediated complication of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and remains the leading cause of non-relapse mortality. Glucocorticosteroids are the first-line treatment; however, there is a critical need for more effective and less toxic alternatives. Nanomedicine constitutes a promising approach by enabling a more tailored and safer drug delivery, although their use in GVHD remains very scarce. This review aims to systematically analyse the existing literature on nanomaterial-based approaches for the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of GVHD. Encouraging results have been reported across major nanomaterial subtypes, suggesting nanomedicine as a viable and versatile platform to improve GVHD outcomes compared with conventional approaches. However, this review also highlights the heterogeneity and frailty of the available data, and the urgent need for clinical translation and deeper exploration of alternative formulations. Finally, we advance as final remarks innovative encapsulation and targeting rationales, supported by an exploration of novel cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying GVHD, to increase therapeutic efficacy, reduce systemic toxicity, and eventually uncouple GVHD from the beneficial graft-versus-leukemia effect.

cards.title: Characterization of transcriptomic profiles underlying gross morphological changes observed in semelparous pink salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha).
cards.abstract: Pacific salmon undergo dramatic physiological remodeling during their terminal spawning migration, culminating in reproductive maturation, senescence, and death. To investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying these processes, we characterized transcriptomic changes in wild pink salmon (Oncorhynchus gorbuscha) sampled at three migratory stages (marine, riverine, and spawning ground) and across three tissues central to endocrine regulation and energy metabolism: gonads, head kidney, and skeletal muscle. Differential gene expression analysis was performed to identify biological pathways associated with maturation and semelparity. Transcriptomic changes were most pronounced during the final transition from river migrating fish to spawning, with the gonads exhibiting the greatest number of differentially expressed genes, followed by skeletal muscle and head kidney. Gene ontology analyses revealed coordinated upregulation of pathways associated with starvation responses, lipid mobilization, tissue catabolism, proteolysis, autophagy, and cell death across tissues. Immune and inflammatory processes were elevated in skeletal muscle and head kidney, while gonads showed strong enrichment of insulin signaling, steroid metabolism, and hormone-response pathways. Analysis of endocrine receptor expression identified tissue-specific and ohnolog-specific regulation of receptors involved in thyroid, growth hormone, insulin, gonadotropin, sex steroid, and glucocorticoid signaling, suggesting functional divergence among duplicated salmonid genes. These findings identified in pink salmon provide evidence for strong maturity induced molecular changes occurring at the time of final maturation rather than freshwater entry. The coordinated activation of endocrine, metabolic, and degenerative pathways supports a mechanistic link between reproductive development and semelparous senescence, providing new insight into the endocrine networks that govern spawning-associated physiological decline in Pacific salmon.

cards.title: Physical Performance After Acute Myocardial Infarction: Gait, Frailty, and Cardiovascular Prognosis.
cards.abstract: Physical performance and frailty have emerged as potential markers of physiological reserve and cardiovascular vulnerability after acute myocardial infarction (AMI). This review examines the prognostic significance of gait speed, lower-extremity physical performance, frailty, and sarcopenia after AMI and acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and discusses their underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical implications. Slow gait speed, impaired Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores, and frailty are associated with mortality, rehospitalization, heart failure, and adverse cardiovascular events after AMI or ACS. Gait speed and SPPB may provide incremental prognostic information beyond conventional cardiovascular risk assessment and established risk scores. These associations may reflect an interconnected cardiac-vascular-muscle axis involving reduced cardiac reserve, vascular dysfunction, impaired skeletal muscle perfusion, sarcopenia, and physical deconditioning. Importantly, emerging evidence suggests that targeted cardiac rehabilitation may improve gait speed, muscle strength, and overall physical performance in vulnerable patients. Physical performance represents a clinically relevant and potentially modifiable dimension of post-AMI cardiovascular vulnerability. Incorporating gait speed, SPPB, and frailty assessment into conventional risk stratification may improve patient phenotyping and identify individuals requiring more intensive rehabilitation and follow-up. Further prospective studies are needed to standardize assessment strategies and determine whether improving physical performance translates into better cardiovascular outcomes.

cards.title: Safety and tolerability of RJx-01 to maintain muscle integrity in patients following hospitalisation with an acute exacerbation of COPD (MINT-COPD): protocol for a phase IIa randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial
cards.abstract: Introduction Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is one of the leading causes of global disability and disability-adjusted life years. One of the key systemic features of COPD is impaired skeletal muscle mass and function, termed sarcopenia. The recognition of skeletal muscle dysfunction as a treatable trait in COPD opens a therapeutic avenue for pharmacological development, with the aim of improving physical function and reducing healthcare utilisation. A novel combination drug, RJx-01, was identified as a candidate therapy for sarcopenia based on preclinical evidence. The primary aim of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of RJx-01 compared with placebo following hospitalisation with an acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD), when acute deterioration of skeletal muscle integrity is observed. Exploratory efficacy analyses will assess differences in muscle function, mass, and multi-omic-derived outcomes. Methods and analysis The MINT-COPD trial is a phase IIa, single centre, randomised controlled trial (RCT). Eighty participants admitted to hospital with AECOPD will be randomly assigned 1:1 to receive either oral RJx-01 or placebo, once daily for 24 weeks. The primary outcome is safety and tolerability of RJx-01 compared with placebo in COPD patients. Exploratory objectives aim to assess the preliminary effects of AECOPD-associated hospitalisation and RJx-01 treatment on muscle mass, function, and fatiguability, as well as patient reported symptoms and frailty. The optional skeletal muscle biopsy sub-study aims to assess the effects of AECOPD on proteomic and transcriptomic markers of skeletal muscle.

cards.title: Age and Neuroimmune Diseases.
cards.abstract: With the aging population accelerating, age has become a core factor influencing the clinical phenotypes, treatment responses, and prognoses of neuroimmune diseases (NDs), including those affecting the central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS). This cross-disease review summarizes the shared and specific age-related characteristics of NDs, focusing on the pathological basis of immunosenescence and neurodegeneration underlying age-related ND progression. We extract the clinical manifestations, immune and neural mechanisms of elderly ND patients, and evaluate the challenges and individualized adjustment principles of therapeutic strategies for this population. We explore the age-related immune dysregulation features between NDs and other systemic autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), type 1 diabetes (T1D)). This review aims to construct a cross-disease framework for the precision management of NDs in the aging era, identify research gaps and future directions, and emphasize age-adapted intervention strategies for optimizing the prognosis of elderly ND patients.

cards.title: Treatment Patterns of Oral Glucocorticoids in Patients with IgG4-Related Disease: A Real-World Analysis based on a Japanese Claims Database.
cards.abstract: To describe the prescribing patterns of oral glucocorticoid and evaluate flares and glucocorticoid-related complications in patients with immunoglobulin G4-related disease. This retrospective observational study used a Japanese hospital claims database. Patients with a prescription for oral glucocorticoids, a diagnosis of immunoglobulin G4-related disease, and having at least two immunoglobulin G4 measurement tests were included. The index date was defined as the first oral glucocorticoid prescription recorded in the database (Day 0). Patients were followed for up to Day 1460 (4 years). The study included 3,167 patients. The mean dose of oral glucocorticoid was 28.76, 10.71, and 4.12 mg/day on Day 0, 90, and 1095, respectively. At Day 1460, 66.56% of the patients were still receiving oral glucocorticoid therapy and the dose exceeded 5 mg/day in 17.80% of patients. During the follow-up period, 453 patients (14.30%) experienced at least one flare. The incidence rates of hospitalized infections, osteoporotic fractures, and cardiovascular diseases, defined as serious glucocorticoid complications, were 7.46, 0.61, and 1.61 per 100 person-years, respectively. Over half of the patients continued glucocorticoid therapy at 4 years. Glucocorticoid withdrawal strategies could be associated with reducing the long-term glucocorticoid-related toxicity in patients with immunoglobulin G4-related disease.

cards.title: Multilayer regulation of osteogenic reprogramming in human aortic valve interstitial cells in calcific aortic valve disease.
cards.abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is an active fibrocalcific disorder in which human aortic valve interstitial cells (hVICs) undergo heterogeneous osteogenic reprogramming. This narrative review provides an hVIC-centered synthesis of four interacting regulatory layers: pathological microenvironmental cues, intracellular signaling, non-coding RNA regulation, and cellular heterogeneity. Lipid dysregulation, inflammation, hypoxia, oxidative and metabolic stress, cellular senescence, and abnormal mechanical loading alter hVIC behavior through interconnected developmental, inflammatory, metabolic, and mechanosensitive pathways. Non-coding RNAs add post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, although many proposed axes remain incompletely validated. Single-cell transcriptomic studies further identify distinct disease-associated hVIC states and challenge a universal linear transition from quiescent to myofibroblast-like and osteogenic cells. We compare conventional and advanced experimental models and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies according to the strength of human, functional, and translational evidence. Current data support a context- and stage-dependent network rather than a single dominant pathway. Integrating human valve tissue, cell-state-resolved analyses, complementary disease models, clinically meaningful endpoints, and targeted delivery may improve biomarker development and support disease-modifying strategies for CAVD.
