cards.title: Time- and posture-specific management of severe supine hypertension and neurogenic orthostatic hypotension in diabetic autonomic neuropathy: A case report.
cards.abstract: Coexistence of neurogenic orthostatic hypotension with supine or nocturnal hypertension creates a therapeutic challenge because treatment of either component may aggravate the other. This case illustrates a clinical management framework based on characterization of the full hemodynamic phenotype, repeated reassessment, and treatment adaptation according to posture and time of day, integrating postural blood pressure (BP) responses, 24-hour BP monitoring, symptoms, functional status, comorbidities, and safety findings. A 63-year-old man with hypertension and insulin-treated type 2 diabetes presented with orthostatic dizziness and presyncope. Antihypertensive therapy was intensified for elevated seated BP. After intensification, upright tolerance worsened, with recurrent syncope, a rib fracture, and loss of functional independence. Symptoms remained disabling despite antihypertensive withdrawal and nonpharmacological measures. Supine-to-seated-to-standing assessment showed a BP fall from 197/99 mm Hg supine to 122/81 mm Hg seated and 79/56 mm Hg standing, with presyncope and heart rate increasing from 72 to 86 beats/min. Supine measurements and 24-hour BP monitoring documented severe supine and nocturnal hypertension, reverse dipping, and mean asleep BP 203/107 mm Hg. Autonomic testing demonstrated combined cardiovagal and adrenergic dysfunction, supporting neurogenic orthostatic hypotension due to diabetic autonomic neuropathy. Management was tailored to upright and recumbent periods. A removable transdermal nitroglycerin patch was used overnight. Nonpharmacological measures included repeated encouragement to increase fluid intake, but daily intake generally remained below 2 L. Clinical assessment suggested relative volume depletion. Low-dose morning fludrocortisone was introduced cautiously despite severe supine/nocturnal hypertension. After upright tolerance improved, morning lercanidipine was added. Subsequent 24-hour BP monitoring showed a more balanced profile. Orthostatic symptoms and upright tolerance improved. No further syncope or falls occurred, and functional independence improved. Later 24-hour BP monitoring showed reduced nocturnal predominance, with mean awake/asleep BP 164/86 and 165/89 mm Hg, respectively. Mild peripheral edema was managed with intermittent torasemide. This case illustrates how integrating postural BP responses with 24-hour BP patterns can identify competing hemodynamic phenotypes that may require different management during upright and recumbent periods. Repeated reassessment and individualized treatment adaptation according to the documented BP pattern and clinical context may help balance competing risks of upright hypoperfusion and supine/nocturnal hypertension.

cards.title: Metformin alleviates dry eye-associated corneal epithelial senescence and oxidative stress via AMPK activation.
cards.abstract: Stress-induced premature senescence (SIPS) and oxidative stress play critical roles in the pathogenesis of Dry Eye Disease (DED), a chronic condition characterized by tear film instability and ocular surface damage. While metformin exhibits known anti-aging and antioxidative properties, its specific therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms in non-diabetic DED remain largely undefined. An in vitro hyperosmotic stress model using human corneal epithelial cells (HCECs) and an in vivo benzalkonium chloride (BAC)-induced DED mouse model were established. Cellular viability, senescence (SA-β-gal, p16, p21, p53), oxidative stress (ROS), and barrier integrity (ZO-1) were evaluated using CCK-8, Western blot, RT-qPCR, and immunofluorescence. The mechanistic role of the AMPK pathway was analyzed using transcriptomic data (GSE252984) and validated using the AMPK inhibitor Compound C and the NRF2 inhibitor ML385. Bioinformatics analysis identified the AMPK signaling cascade as a profoundly dysregulated pathway in DED-associated senescence. In vitro, metformin pretreatment significantly attenuated hyperosmolarity-induced cell death, ROS accumulation, and the expression of senescence and inflammatory markers. Mechanistically, metformin activated the AMPK/SIRT1 axis to suppress senescence and promoted NRF2 nuclear translocation to restore redox balance; these protective effects were reversed upon AMPK or NRF2 inhibition. In vivo, systemic administration of metformin preserved corneal epithelial thickness, decreased apoptosis, and reduced senescence markers in DED mice. Notably, co-administration of Compound C neutralized these therapeutic benefits. Metformin effectively alleviates corneal epithelial injury and SIPS in non-diabetic DED by modulating the AMPK/SIRT1 and NRF2 signaling pathways. These findings highlight metformin as a promising repurposable therapeutic agent for breaking the pathological cycle of ocular surface damage.

cards.title: Cellular senescence mediates facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy.
cards.abstract: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) is driven by aberrant expression of the early embryonic transcription factor Double Homeobox 4 (DUX4), yet the mechanisms linking low, sporadic DUX4 activity to progressive muscle degeneration remain unclear. Here, we identify cellular senescence as a central and early mechanism in FSHD pathogenesis. Analysis of patient muscle transcriptomes revealed strong enrichment of senescence and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) programs that correlated with DUX4 activity, clinical severity, and histopathological changes. Notably, these signatures were detectable even in STIR-negative muscles, defining a prodystrophic state characterized by early molecular alterations preceding overt MRI-detectable inflammation and highlighting their potential utility as early biomarkers of disease activity. Using an FSHD mouse model, we show that DUX4-induced muscle injury rapidly triggers senescence, which then progressively expands. Fibroadipogenic progenitors and macrophages emerged as the principal senescent populations and key sources of pro-inflammatory and profibrotic SASP signals. Importantly, senescence was therapeutically modifiable. Treatment with the nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor lamivudine (3TC), which inhibits LINE-1 reverse transcriptase activity, significantly reduced senescence, inflammation, and fibrosis while promoting muscle regeneration. These findings identify cellular senescence as a tractable driver of FSHD and warrant senotherapeutic strategies, particularly lamivudine, for clinical intervention in FSHD.

cards.title: Obesity, frail obesity, and outcomes after durable left ventricular assist device implantation: a pooled analysis of the MOMENTUM 3 trials.
cards.abstract: Obesity in patients supported by left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) is linked to excess mortality and haemocompatibility-related events. Whether this association persists with the fully magnetically levitated HeartMate 3 (HM3) pump is unknown. This analysis tested outcomes with obesity and the additive influence of co-existing frailty ('frail obesity') in the contemporary era. The study pooled 2200 HM3 recipients from the MOMENTUM 3 pivotal randomized trial (n = 515) and Continued Access Protocol (n = 1685). Obesity was defined as body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 and frailty by a 40-item Rockwood cumulative-deficit frailty index (FI), with clinically relevant frailty defined as FI ≥0.325 (moderate-severe frailty); BMI was excluded from the FI to avoid mathematical coupling. The primary endpoint was survival to transplant, recovery, or 24 months of support free of disabling stroke (modified Rankin score >3) or pump replacement reoperation. Obese patients (n = 887, 40.3%) were younger, less often with ischaemic aetiology, and more frequently women, but more often had diabetes and hypertension, than non-obese patients. Unadjusted 2-year outcomes were similar between groups (freedom from the primary endpoint: 75.1% vs 77.1%, log-rank P = .34; survival: 79.9% vs 81.2%, P = .57). After covariate adjustment, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (hazard ratio [HR] 1.30, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.07-1.58) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.35, 95% CI 1.10-1.67), as well as heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia, but not stroke, bleeding, or early right heart failure. Frailty affected 67.3% of obese recipients (571/849) and was associated with a higher adjusted risk of the primary endpoint (HR 1.51, 95% CI 1.09-2.10), overall mortality and non-haemocompatibilty-related morbidity endpoints. The obesity-by-frailty interaction was not significant for either the primary endpoint (P = .436) or mortality (P = .215), indicating additive rather than synergistic risk; frail-obese patients nonetheless carried the highest absolute risk of any subgroup. Frailty improved by at least one severity class by 6 months in 75.9% of frail-obese patients, and improvement was associated with better survival (adjusted HR 0.14, 95% CI 0.07-0.26). In the HM3 era, obese and non-obese recipients had similar unadjusted 2-year outcomes; however, after adjustment for baseline case-mix, obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of both the primary endpoint and all-cause mortality, together with heart failure hospitalization, infection, and arrhythmia. Frailty was independently associated with adverse outcomes across nearly all endpoints and was highly prevalent among obese recipients; the combination of obesity and frailty was additive but not synergistic, with frail-obese patients carrying the highest absolute risk. Frailty, however, proved substantially reversible after LVAD support, and its improvement was associated with markedly better survival. Obesity and frailty should therefore be assessed together, rather than through BMI thresholds alone, with recognition that frailty status is dynamic after implantation and that improvement in frailty is associated with markedly better survival.

cards.title: [Risk assessment and clinical strategies of muscle loss in weight loss therapy].
cards.abstract: Obesity is a chronic metabolic disease characterized by excessive fat accumulation, and scientific weight management is pivotal to its prevention and treatment. With the clinical application of novel anti-obesity medications and bariatric surgery, rapid weight loss is often accompanied by muscle loss, which increases the risks of falls and frailty. Clinical assessment should comprehensively evaluate physical function, mobility and quality of life to promptly identify and intervene in muscle loss. Developing multidisciplinary management regimens covering nutrition, exercise, pharmacotherapy and psychological support based on patients' age, baseline muscle function, comorbidities and nutritional status serves as a vital approach to fat loss while preserving muscle mass. In recent years, remarkable progress has been made in the research and development of muscle-protective drugs, offering new strategies for muscle preservation during weight management. Implementing muscle protection strategies throughout the entire weight management process to achieve high-quality weight loss is crucial for improving long-term prognosis of patients with obesity.

cards.title: Ginseng-Sanqi-Chuanxiong extract ameliorates hypertensive vascular aging through endothelial–smooth muscle cell crosstalk via the PPARγ/NF-κB axis
cards.abstract: Background Vascular aging is an important pathological basis of hypertension and hypertension-associated target-organ injury. Ginseng-Sanqi-Chuanxiong (GSC) extract has been shown to have protective effects against vascular dysfunction; however, its mechanisms in hypertensive vascular aging remain unclear. Objective In this study, we investigated the protective effects and mechanisms of GSC in hypertensive vascular aging. Materials and Methods The chemical compounds present in GSC decoction were identified through ultra-performance liquid chromatography–quadrupole time-of-flight–mass spectrometry with elevated energy data acquisition (UPLC-Q-TOF/MS E ) analysis. Network pharmacology was then used to predict the potential targets and signaling pathways. Ten-month-old spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs) were treated with GSC for 4 months to evaluate vascular aging and target-organ injury. Lastly, endothelial–smooth muscle cell (EC-SMC) co-culture, molecular docking, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assays were used to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Results UPLC-Q-TOF/MS E helped identify 55 compounds in GSC that were predominantly saponins, lactones, and phenolic-related constituents. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that PPARγ/NF-κB signaling could be a core regulatory pathway. GSC treatment reduced the systolic blood pressure while attenuating cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis, renal glomerular sclerosis and tubular injury, and hippocampal neuronal loss in the SHRs. GSC also alleviated vascular remodeling, vascular stiffness, and vascular senescence while decreasing inflammatory cytokine and senescence-related protein expression levels and regulating PPARγ/NF-κB signaling in vascular tissues. In the EC-SMC co-culture system, GSC intervention attenuated senescence in Ang-II-induced endothelial cells and inflammatory responses in co-cultured smooth muscle cells through endothelial-mediated paracrine regulation. The molecular docking and SPR assays further demonstrated direct interactions between PPARγ and GSC constituents, including kaempferol, senkyunolide H, and levistolide A. Conclusion GSC attenuated hypertensive vascular aging through its protective effects associated with endothelial-mediated regulation of the PPARγ/NF-κB signaling pathway, providing scientific evidence of the vascular protective effects of GSC in hypertension.

cards.title: Use of hospital care among centenarians in France: implications for health-system planning in extreme old age-insights from a nationwide study of temporal patterns, regional variation and care settings (2014-2023).
cards.abstract: To describe nationwide hospital care use among centenarians in France, including temporal and regional variation, emergency admission, surgical care, and inpatient rehabilitation. We conducted a retrospective nationwide observational study using French hospital discharge data on centenarian hospital stays from 2014 to 2023. Over the study period, 110,585 acute care hospital stays were recorded among centenarians, of which 12.1% were surgical. Acute care hospitalization burden decreased from 53.2 stays per 100 centenarians in 2014 to 45.4 per 100 in 2023. Overall, 70.0% of acute care stays followed an emergency department admission, with this proportion increasing from 68.0% in 2014 to 72.9% in 2023. In-hospital mortality was 14.9% per stay; among fatal acute care stays, 9.4% ended in death on the day of admission. Marked regional variation was observed. Musculoskeletal conditions accounted for 16.9% of acute care stays and represented an increasing proportion over time. A total of 21,012 inpatient rehabilitation stays were recorded; rehabilitation hospitalization burden decreased from 10.3 to 8.3 stays per 100 centenarians, while the proportion related to musculoskeletal conditions increased. These descriptive nationwide findings may help inform health-system planning as the centenarian population continues to grow. Our results suggest that centenarians remain a clinically vulnerable population with substantial hospital care needs, requiring system-wide readiness beyond geriatric services. These findings may support more integrated care pathways, broader responses to falls and fractures, spanning prevention, acute care, and rehabilitation, and explicit consideration of the oldest-old in strategies addressing territorial and social inequalities in healthcare access.

cards.title: Osteoporosis, sarcopenia, locomotive syndrome, and frailty in age-related spinal kyphosis.
cards.abstract: Age-related kyphosis is a common manifestation of musculoskeletal aging associated with falls, mobility decline, reduced participation, and respiratory compromise in severe cases. This narrative review summarizes its relationships with osteoporosis, sarcopenia, locomotive syndrome, and frailty. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched for English-language publications from database inception through December 31, 2025. Relevant evidence was reviewed narratively. Observational studies indicate that osteoporosis-associated vertebral fragility is an important structural contributor to kyphotic progression through clinically apparent or unrecognized vertebral fractures and progressive vertebral deformity. Degenerative disc changes and local trunk muscle dysfunction may also contribute through altered spinal loading and reduced active postural support. Evidence linking generalized sarcopenia to kyphosis remains inconsistent, whereas local trunk muscle dysfunction and poor paraspinal muscle quality may be more directly relevant. Kyphosis may coexist with locomotive syndrome and physical frailty, but these associations do not establish causality. Assessment should include bone mineral density, vertebral fracture status, regional and global sagittal alignment, trunk muscle function, and mobility. Management should combine appropriate osteoporosis treatment, trunk-focused exercise, posture training, and nutritional support. Further longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to clarify causal relationships and determine whether treatment preserves mobility and independence.

cards.title: Stemonine Alleviates UVB-Induced Keratinocyte Senescence by Activating SIRT3.
cards.abstract: Ultraviolet B (UVB) radiation is the primary environmental factor contributing to skin damage, largely by accelerating cellular senescence, which leads to impaired skin function and premature aging. Recent studies have indicated that Stemonine, a natural alkaloid, has therapeutic potential owing to its documented biological activities. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of Stemonine on immortalized human keratinocyte cell line HaCaT against UVB-induced cellular senescence and elucidated the underlying mechanisms. Our results demonstrated that Stemonine significantly improved cell viability, attenuated oxidative stress, and ameliorated mitochondrial dysfunction in UVB-irradiated HaCaT cells. Furthermore, Stemonine treatment reduced DNA damage signaling, downregulated key senescence executors such as acetylated p53 and p21, and decreased SA-β-Gal activity. Importantly, Stemonine upregulated both the expression and activity of SIRT3. Crucially, the protective effects of Stemonine were largely abolished upon SIRT3 knockdown, indicating that its actions are mediated via the SIRT3 pathway. These findings suggest that Stemonine is a promising candidate for mitigating UVB-induced skin aging.

cards.title: Improved range of motion following correction osteotomy for varus malunited proximal humerus fractures with 3-dimensional planned cutting guides: a case series.
cards.abstract: Varus malunion of the proximal humerus can lead to persistent pain and restricted shoulder mobility. When symptoms persist despite conservative treatment, valgus wedge osteotomy may be considered. This case series reports the outcomes of corrective osteotomy for varus malunion of 2-part proximal humerus fractures using patient-specific 3-dimensional (3D) cutting guides, fixed with a PHILOS plate (Synthes) in patients aged less than 65 years. We hypothesized that this technique would improve forward flexion, restoring at least 80% of the forward flexion of the contralateral, unaffected shoulder. All patients in this study were referred to our clinic for further treatment and had received at least 6 months of physiotherapy prior to this. The patients were dissatisfied with their shoulder after conservative treatment, for most primarily due to the limited elevation. Patients were eligible if they were aged less than 65 years, had closed epiphyses, and presented with an untreated varus malunion of the proximal humerus. Exclusion criteria included frozen shoulder, signs of rotator cuff tear, or neurologic abnormalities. The primary outcome measure was the difference in forward flexion, assessed by a single observer using a goniometer pre-operatively and at a minimum of 1-year follow-up. Secondary outcomes included the Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand score, the Oxford Shoulder Score, visual analog scale scores for pain and satisfaction, correction of the head-shaft angle, and complications. Eleven patients underwent 3D planned corrective osteotomy. At a 1-year follow-up, median forward flexion improved from 100° to 148°, corresponding to 94% of the contralateral side (P = .005), and median abduction improved from 80° to 145° (P = .005). Patient-reported outcomes improved significantly, with the median Oxford Shoulder Score decreasing from 25 to 17 (P = .01), the median Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand score from 34 to 13 (P = .02), and median visual analog scale satisfaction increasing from 3 to 9 (P = .02). The median humeral head-shaft angle increased from 95° pre-operatively to 121° post-operatively (P = .003). Three major complications (low-grade infection, hardware breakout, and frozen shoulder) and one minor complication (hypertrophic scarring) were observed. Seven patients (64%) experienced hardware irritation requiring removal. In this case series, 3D planned corrective osteotomy for varus malunited proximal humerus fractures resulted in clinically relevant improvements in forward flexion and overall shoulder range of motion. Post-operative anterior flexion was better than the presumed 80% of the contralateral side in most patients. These findings suggest that patient-specific 3D planning may be a valuable adjunct in the correction of proximal humerus malunions.

cards.title: Effect of Risedronate on Rib Cortical Thickness After Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy to Peripheral Lung Tumors: Results of a Randomized Phase 2 Trial.
cards.abstract: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to peripheral lung tumors is associated with radiation-induced bone effects that may predispose patients to chest wall pain and radiation-induced rib fractures. These effects may be inhibited by bisphosphonates. We aimed to determine the impact of risedronate on the radiologic biomarker of rib cortical thickness (CTh) in patients with peripheral lung tumors treated with SBRT. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 clinical trial enrolled patients with tumors within 2 cm of the chest wall, who were randomized 1:1 to receive risedronate 150 mg prior to SBRT or placebo. CTh was evaluated every 3 months for 1 year. The primary endpoint was the percent change in rib CTh from baseline to 3 months within the higher than 30 Gy isodose region. Seventy-three patients (78 tumors) were randomized and eligible for analysis. Baseline CTh was 1.46 (± 0.34) mm and 1.44 (± 0.42) mm in the placebo and risedronate arms, respectively. The mean percent change from baseline to 3 months within the 30 Gy isodose region was 6.4% (± 18.0) for placebo versus 3.1% (± 17.9) for risedronate (absolute difference: -3.3%; p = 0.44). The absolute differences in percent CTh change from baseline to 6, 9, and 12 months in the risedronate (versus placebo) group were -4.7%, -8.3%, and -11.8%, respectively. In patients with peripheral lung tumors treated with SBRT, risedronate did not result in statistically significant differences in CTh within the 30 Gy isodose region. This biomarker of bone changes after SBRT demonstrated increases over time within higher dose regions in the placebo group but remained similar to baseline in the risedronate group. Further studies are needed.

cards.title: Hybrid Osteosynthesis for Septic Humeral Shaft Nonunion in a Patient with Obesity: A Case Report.
cards.abstract: Septic humeral shaft nonunion represents a complex reconstructive challenge in orthopedic surgery, particularly in patients with obesity, in whom increased lever arms and greater mechanical loading of the upper extremity substantially compromise fixation stability. Recurrent failure of isolated fixation constructs, including intramedullary nails or compression plates, necessitates hybrid strategies that combine enhanced biomechanical stability with effective eradication of microbial infection. This article presents the case of a middle-aged man with obesity and a history of a left humeral shaft fracture initially treated with intramedullary nailing in December 2020 who developed persistent nonunion. Following revision surgery with dynamic compression plating, fixation failure occurred secondary to implant fatigue. A second revision procedure was performed through a posterior approach, including nerve neurolysis, extensive debridement, and hybrid fixation using a 240 x 8 mm Targon™ H intramedullary nail (B. Braun, Melsungen, Germany) combined with a narrow 4.5-mm dynamic compression plate (DCP; DePuy Synthes, Warsaw, IN, USA). Cancellous bone chip grafting was also performed. Intraoperative cultures yielded Staphylococcus epidermidis, establishing the diagnosis of septic nonunion, and targeted oral clindamycin therapy was initiated. Despite transient postoperative radial neuropraxia, which resolved with pregabalin treatment and structured physical rehabilitation, the patient achieved complete osseous union, eradication of infection, and an Upper Extremity Functional Scale (UEFS) score of 69/80, corresponding to 86% of maximal functional capacity. In conclusion, hybrid fixation combining an intramedullary nail with a narrow 4.5-mm DCP, together with pathogen-directed antimicrobial therapy, provides excellent axial and rotational stability and represents an effective salvage strategy for septic humeral shaft nonunion in patients with increased biomechanical demands.

cards.title: Aerobic Exercise Ameliorates Osteoarthritic Chondrocyte Degradation in Osteoarthritis via Regulating E2F8/NLRP14 Signaling Pathway.
cards.abstract: Although physical activity is known to mitigate disease risks, its protective molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. E2F8, a regulator of cell cycle and metabolism, showed significant differential expression between osteoarthritis (OA) and exercise models, suggesting it may link mechanical activity to OA alleviation. In vitro, Interleukin-1 Beta (IL-1β) simulated inflammation. In vivo, OA was induced in rats via Monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) injection. The effects of E2F8 and mechanical stress were assessed using moderate treadmill exercise, histology, and joint observation. Bioinformatic analysis, cyclic tensile strain, Western blot, immunofluorescence, and gene knockdown were used to investigate mechanisms. In OA rats, E2F8 was downregulated in cartilage while NLRP14 increased. In vitro, mechanical stress reversed the IL-1β-induced anabolic/catabolic imbalance by regulating the E2F8/NLRP14, mitigating OA progression. Mechanical stress enhances E2F8 expression in osteoarthritic chondrocytes, which in turn protects cartilage by suppressing the expression of NLRP14. These findings underscore the role of E2F8 as a mechano-sensitive mediator and highlight the potential of exercise or exercise-mimetic therapies as effective strategies for preventing and treating OA.

cards.title: S100A9 Induces RANKL Expression in Osteocytes Utilizing IL-6/sIL-6R Combination and gp130 Signaling Pathways.
cards.abstract: Calprotectin, a heterodimer of S100A8 and S100A9, is predominantly expressed in neutrophils, monocytes, and chondrocytes. Clinical studies demonstrate that elevated circulating calprotectin levels correlate with diseases followed by inflammatory bone loss, including rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and periodontitis. We previously reported that S100A9 directly increased RANKL and IL-6 expression in an osteocyte-like cell line. While RANKL is well-established as an essential factor for the formation and activation of osteoclasts, the role of S100A9-induced IL-6 in bone resorption remains unclear. On the other hand, osteocytes require sIL-6R to activate the gp130 signaling pathway. Therefore, we hypothesized that S100A9-induced IL-6 cooperates with soluble IL-6 receptor (sIL-6R) to increase RANKL through gp130-mediated signaling. Here, we show that S100A9 increases the bone resorption area and TRAP-positive cell number in the murine calvaria. In addition, Rankl and Il6 mRNA levels in osteocytes were upregulated by S100A9 treatment. In vitro results demonstrated that S100A9 increased not only Rankl and Il6 expression in osteocytes, but also sIL-6R secretion in macrophages. Since osteocytes strongly express gp130, the IL-6 complexed with sIL-6R enhanced gp130 downstream signaling, including JAK1 and STAT3 activation in osteocytes. Blockade of either Il6 or gp130 suppressed S100A-induced effects. Notably, gp130 antagonist treatment inhibited S100A9-induced bone resorption in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that S100A9 promotes RANKL-mediated osteoclastogenesis through IL-6/sIL-6/gp130 signaling in osteocytes.

cards.title: A multispecies foundation model for genome function prediction, gene annotation and sequence design
cards.abstract: Comparative genomics and synthetic biology require models that can interpret, annotate, and design DNA sequences across species, yet genomic models have not combined these capabilities beyond a few well-characterized organisms. Here we introduce Nucleotide Transformer v3 (NTv3), a long-context cross-kingdom foundation model that provides a common backbone for functional prediction, gene annotation and controllable sequence generation across phylogenetically diverse species. NTv3 is pre-trained on more than 128,000 genomes using sequences up to 1Mb and post-trained on 16,262 functional tracks across 15 animal and plant genomes. NTv3 performs comparably to AlphaGenome on matched human assays and matches or exceeds evaluated published models for functional-track prediction across 19 species spanning mammals, birds, fish, plants, fungi and protists. Ablation experiments show that both genome pre-training and expanding functional supervision from human and mouse to 15 species improve track prediction. Leveraging these learned functional representations, NTv3 outperforms leading ab initio gene predictors across mammals, plants and insects, with fewer spurious gene models and improved recovery and reduced fragmentation of long genes. Finally, the same representations can be used with discrete diffusion to design regulatory DNA sequences with specific activity levels. We demonstrate this in plant and fly promoters and enhancers, and experimentally validate the activity and promoter selectivity of the generated fly enhancers. Together, NTv3 unifies genome interpretation, gene annotation and regulatory sequence design across the animal and plant kingdoms, with direct relevance to agriculture, biodiversity research and biotechnology.

cards.title: Effects of Alendronate and Alfacalcidol on Preventing Bone Loss in Chemotherapy-treated Soft-tissue Sarcoma.
cards.abstract: Cancer treatment-induced bone loss (CTIBL) increases fracture risk and impairs quality of life, but little is known about CTIBL in soft-tissue sarcoma. This study aimed to investigate whether alendronate and alfacalcidol prevent doxorubicin-induced bone loss in a mouse model of soft-tissue sarcoma. Sarcoma S-180II cells were transplanted subcutaneously into 10-week-old female BALB/c mice using an air-pouch model. After tumor engraftment, mice received weekly intraperitoneal doxorubicin and were allocated to one of four groups: vehicle control, alendronate, alfacalcidol, and alendronate plus alfacalcidol. Alendronate was administered subcutaneously twice weekly, and alfacalcidol was administered orally three times weekly. Mice were euthanized 2 or 4 weeks after tumor transplantation. Body weight, tumor weight and volume, femoral microstructure by micro-computed tomography, histomorphometric indices by tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (TRAP) staining and osteocalcin immunostaining, and receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) expression were evaluated. Body weight and tumor parameters did not differ among groups. At 2 weeks, combination therapy had significantly increased trabecular bone volume fraction, thickness, and number compared with the vehicle control. At 4 weeks, alendronate alone and combination therapy had preserved trabecular bone volume and number and reduced trabecular separation; combination therapy resulted in higher bone-volume fraction and trabecular number than alendronate alone. Cortical bone area and thickness were also greater in all drug-treated groups than in the control at 4 weeks. TRAP staining showed significant suppression of osteoclast-related indices in the alendronate- and combination-treated groups, whereas no significant differences were observed in osteocalcin, RANKL, or RUNX2 expression. Alendronate may prevent doxorubicin-associated bone loss in soft-tissue sarcoma, primarily by directly suppressing residual osteoclast activity in vivo.

cards.title: Two-Year Outcomes of Casting vs. ORIF for Displaced Medial Epicondyle Fractures in Children.
cards.abstract: Randomized trials found similar 12-month outcomes after surgery and cast immobilization for displaced pediatric medial humeral epicondyle fractures. We report the prespecified 24-month follow-up of a multicenter noninferiority randomized trial. Children aged 7 to 16 years with medial humeral epicondyle fractures displaced ≥2 mm were randomized to open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) or cast immobilization. The primary outcome of the trial was the Quick Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (QDASH) score at 12 months. Twenty-four-month outcomes included patient-reported outcomes, clinical measures, radiographic healing, and complications. Sixty-six of 72 patients (92%) completed follow-up. Mean QDASH scores were 1.4 after ORIF and 0.6 after casting (mean difference, 0.8; 95% CI, -0.2 to 1.8), within the noninferiority margin. Secondary outcomes were similar. Four ORIF patients underwent implant removal, and 1 cast-treated patient underwent medial collateral ligament reconstruction. At 2 years, cast treatment remained noninferior to ORIF, supporting durable nonoperative management. Therapeutic Level I. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.

cards.title: Assessing the inclusion of frailty scores in either the methodology or results of clinical intervention trials of heart failure: A scoping review.
cards.abstract: Chronic heart failure is highly prevalent in older adults, in whom frailty is common and associated with poorer outcomes. Despite advances in guideline-directed medical therapy, concerns regarding tolerability and polypharmacy contribute to under-utilization in frail patients. This scoping review aimed to map the existing evidence on how clinical interventional trials of heart failure management have incorporated frailty, specifically, whether trials have (i) stratified outcomes according to frailty status and/or (ii) adjusted treatment strategies based on frailty. We searched MEDLINE, Ovid Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL and ClinicalTrials.gov for interventional trials of heart failure published up to August 2025 that incorporated frailty using validated assessment tools. Eligible studies stratified outcomes by frailty status and/or adjusted interventions based on frailty. Data were extracted and a narrative synthesis was conducted. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria. Seven were post-hoc analyses of randomized controlled trials, two were prespecified analyses, and one was a randomized controlled trial. Two studies evaluated exercise-based interventions, one on implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, and the remainder on pharmacological-based therapies. Nine studies used the Rockwood cumulative deficit approach to measure frailty, although the parameters used varied between studies. Available secondary analyses suggest preserved efficacy across frailty groups for most pharmacological interventions, whereas other modalities did not show convincing improvements in heart failure-specific outcomes among frail patients. Primary evidence of heart failure interventions incorporating frailty remains limited, with a large bulk of the evidence available being retrospective. Although several reported pharmacological interventions appear to have preserved efficacy across frailty levels, some of these therapies were not recommended in current guidelines, and heterogeneity in frailty measurement reduced the confidence of conclusions drawn. The gaps identified in this review highlight the need for further primary evidence that incorporates frailty, plus a standardized holistic method of measuring frailty in heart failure patients.

cards.title: Understanding factors that influence time to surgery for hip fractures in South Africa: A qualitative study using the Model of Pathways to Treatment.
cards.abstract: Although early surgery for hip fractures (HF) improves patient outcomes, in South Africa (SA) time to surgery often exceeds recommended durations. We explore factors influencing time to HF surgery in SA to inform interventions promoting earlier access. Data were collected through repeated in-depth interviews with 38 HF patients and their caregivers and 40 healthcare professionals (HCPs) and observations of clinical practice in five hospitals in Gauteng. Findings were informed by the four key "intervals" of the 'Model of Pathways to Treatment'. Appraisal: Personal beliefs that symptoms were due to other causes or that hospital visits were a "weakness", prompted initial self-management. Early care-seeking was prompted by pain intensity and further encouraged by family members. Help-seeking: Timely access to transport was impacted by ambulance shortages, long distances, and safety concerns for paramedics, and thus many patients relied on private transportation. High-impact trauma cases were prioritised over low-impact HF. Diagnostic: Patient pathways varied and were complicated by ambulance shortages and scheduling issues. Administrative requirements (referral letters) slowed referral processes, particularly for patients from outside hospital catchment areas. Caregivers found admission paperwork burdensome, while HCPs viewed it as helpful for coordinating care and avoiding later delays. While hospitals prioritised emergency cases (including HF), HCPs felt streamlining administrative processes could improve time to X-ray. Pre-treatment: Patients and caregivers reported long waits for surgery, with delays leading to complications and further setbacks. Surgeries were often postponed for other "emergencies", with HCPs describing difficulties with managing competing surgical priorities. This study, the first to explore factors that impact time to HF surgery in SA, highlights the agency of patients and caregivers in negotiating access to treatment, and health system processes that help or hinder access. Findings identify key leverage points for interventions targeted at each 'interval' in the care pathway to accelerate access to HF surgery.

cards.title: "Mind or machine?": Study protocol for a mixed-methods study evaluating the effectiveness and lived experience of active versus passive prophylaxis in older hip fracture patients.
cards.abstract: Hip fracture in older adults causes a "dual crisis" of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and rapid muscle atrophy. Pharmacological prevention is effective but carries significant bleeding risks for these frail patients. Current physical prophylaxis is often too weak to restore muscle pump function. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of two enhanced strategies, active resistance training and passive neuromuscular electrical stimulation, against standard care for VTE prevention and muscle preservation. A three-arm, assessor-blinded, parallel-group RCT will be conducted at a tertiary hospital in Qingdao, China. Older patients (n = 222) recovering from hip fracture fixation will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to: (1) the control group; (2) the control plus lower-limb resistance training group; or (3) the control plus neuromuscular electrical stimulation group. The primary outcome is the incidence of ultrasound-confirmed VTE within the intervention period. Secondary outcomes include venous hemodynamics, muscle architecture, self-reported fatigue, and cost-effectiveness. Quantitative data will be analyzed using intention-to-treat principles. Following the RCT, a qualitative interpretive phenomenological analysis study will be conducted with a purposive sample of 10-12 participants to explore the lived experiences, barriers, and facilitators associated with adhering to "active" versus "passive" rehabilitation models. This study addresses the lack of data comparing active versus passive therapies for hip fracture patients. Active training promotes voluntary muscle use, potentially boosting patient confidence. In contrast, electrical stimulation guarantees muscle pumping regardless of fatigue. If effective, this study will validate a new "dual protection" strategy. This will help establish an optimal rehabilitation model to solve the "dual crisis" of thrombosis and muscle loss. The study was pre-registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on March 17, 2026. Trial Registration Number: ChiCTR2600120624.

cards.title: Association between serum vitamin D levels and pediatric distal radius fractures: a case-control study.
cards.abstract: This study evaluated whether serum vitamin D levels are associated with distal radius fractures in children. In this case-control study, pediatric patients with confirmed distal radius fractures (cases) were compared to children visiting an orthopedic clinic for routine checks or minor muscular pain (controls). Serum vitamin D, phosphorus, and calcium levels were analyzed. We enrolled 98 children (mean age: 8.2 ± 2.6 years). Overall, 87.8% had serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] concentrations below 30 ng/ml, with a cohort mean of 22.04 ± 7.35 ng/ml. No statistically significant differences were found between the case and control groups regarding serum vitamin D ( P = 0.806), calcium, or phosphorus levels. Logistic regression confirmed none of these metabolic markers were significantly associated with fracture incidence. Serum vitamin D levels were not associated with pediatric distal radius fractures in this population. The generally low 25(OH)D concentrations observed in both groups suggest that other factors may have a greater role in fracture risk. The level of evidence is III.

cards.title: Pitfalls and pearls of geriatric trauma care.
cards.abstract: Geriatric trauma represents a growing public health concern as the population of adults aged 65 years and older continues to expand. Traumatic injury remains the fifth leading cause of death in this age group and is associated with significantly higher morbidity, mortality, and health care costs compared with younger trauma populations. Geriatric physiologic changes, comorbid disease burden, polypharmacy, and altered pharmacokinetics complicate the assessment and management of injured older adults and contribute to frequent undertriage and delayed recognition of life-threatening injury. Low-energy mechanisms, particularly ground-level falls, account for the majority of injuries in this population yet often result in disproportionately severe outcomes. Cognitive impairment, anticoagulant use, frailty, and limited physiologic reserve further increase vulnerability following trauma.This article examines the epidemiology and pathophysiology of geriatric trauma, highlighting common pitfalls in care, including medication-related complications, underrecognition of shock, delirium, elder abuse, and mental health disorders. Evidence-based clinical pearls are presented to guide assessment, resuscitation, and disposition decisions, with emphasis on adjustment for age for trauma activation criteria, early imaging, delirium screening, and interdisciplinary care. Current recommendations from the American College of Surgeons are discussed, including geriatric-specific trauma activation thresholds, frailty assessment, and use of structured screening tools such as the Confusion Assessment Method. The Geriatric 5Ms framework is introduced as a patient-centered approach to clinical decision-making.

cards.title: Early deep infection after operatively managed low-velocity tibial gunshot fractures is associated with older age, temporary external fixation, and longer time to definitive fixation.
cards.abstract: The aim of this study was to determine postoperative infection rates and identify factors associated with deep infection in low-velocity tibial gunshot wound (GSW) fractures managed operatively. This is a retrospective cohort study. The setting includes a Level 1 urban trauma center. The participants in this study are adult patients with operatively managed tibial fractures resulting from low-velocity GSWs treated between 2015 and 2024. Inclusion required operative fixation, 48 hours of postoperative intravenous antibiotics, and a minimum of 3 months of follow-up. A total of 113 patients with 116 tibial fractures met the inclusion criteria. Intervention included operative fixation of tibial GSW fractures with a uniform 48-hour postoperative intravenous antibiotic regimen. The primary outcome was deep infection, defined as infection requiring operative debridement, intravenous antibiotics, or positive deep tissue or hardware-associated cultures. The mean age of the patients was 33.9 ± 13.0 years, and 84.5% were male. Deep infection occurred in 13 patients (11.2%). Patients who developed deep infection were older (P = 0.046) and experienced longer intervals from injury to definitive fixation (P = 0.008). Temporary external fixation was strongly associated with deep infection (odds ratio 9.81, 95% confidence interval 2.06-46.66; P = 0.002). Temporary external fixation was associated with a longer overall time from injury to definitive fixation (P < 0.001). In operatively managed tibial GSW fractures treated with a standardized 48-hour antibiotic regimen, increasing age, temporary external fixation, and a longer interval from injury to definitive fixation were associated with increased risk of infection. These findings may help identify higher-risk patients and inform future strategies to reduce infection after ballistic tibial fractures.

cards.title: A Value-Driven Care Approach to Improving Time to Operation for Patients with Low-Impact Geriatric Hip Fractures.
cards.abstract: Timely surgical repair of hip fractures improves outcomes, yet many patients do not receive surgery within 48 hours of ED registration as a result of system-level inefficiencies. This 2-year case study (January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2024) consisted of a bundled, multidisciplinary intervention implemented within a value-based health care framework in a tertiary hospital in Singapore. The intervention included restructuring fragmented workflows by constructing a multidisciplinary task force that cocreated the bundle comprising revised preoperative cardiac guidelines, default surgical listing (formal scheduling of surgery) on admission from the ED, prioritization of operating theater access, real-time communication between departments of orthopedics, geriatrics, and anesthesia, and monthly performance feedback to improve patient-centered outcomes (namely timeliness of surgery, length of stay, and safety outcomes). Among patients 60 years of age and over with fragility hip fractures, the proportion undergoing surgery within 48 hours increased from 38.9% (among 149 patients in a preimplementation period from July to December 2023) to 68.4% (among 117 patients in a postimplementation period from July to December 2024) (P<0.001). In addition, median time to surgery decreased from 58.8 hours to 38.3 hours (P<0.001), and median length of stay improved from 11.0 days to 7.0 days (P<0.001), with more patients discharged within 10 days (from 48.3% to 67.5%; P=0.002). Complication rates, readmissions, and returns to the operating theater were unchanged. Overall, the intervention improved surgical timeliness and hospital efficiency (using bed-day utilization as a pragmatic proxy) without compromising patient safety. Although the Value-Driven Care program of the Singapore Ministry of Health does not include a specific cost component, its principles align clinical outcomes with resource utilization, which are associated with downstream consequences of operational and financial efficiency. Post implementation, for example, reduced length of stay led to 962 fewer bed-days over 1 year (366 days in 2024), with a related cost avoidance of nearly US$900,000. Key enablers of success included the establishment of a multidisciplinary task force that aligned stakeholders around a shared patient-centered goal, which contributed to the development of a shared platform for monitoring and assessing progress, subsequently leading to reduced variability through collaboration in codevelopment of care protocols, and supported implementation through structured workflow redesign, real-time communication, and continuous feedback. These elements most likely contributed to the observed improvements and may provide a practical framework for addressing similar system-level challenges in other health care settings.

cards.title: Cross-Sectional observational study of imaging findings in patients presenting with chronic non-bacterial osteomyelitis in the United Kingdom.
cards.abstract: Chronic non-infectious osteomyelitis (CNO) is a rare condition that presents with multifocal inflammation of bone in children and adolescents. The exact distribution, severity and identifiable patterns of disease are not fully understood. Describe the prevalence and pattern of radiological abnormalities present at the time of diagnosis in patients with chronic non-bacterial osteitis. Multi-centre national prospective cross-sectional observational study set in the United Kingdom. Patients with new diagnoses of CNO were recruited between 2020-2022. MRI was reviewed independently by two radiologists and disagreements were resolved by a panel of three. The anatomical location for each lesion was recorded by bone and within bone. The severity of the MRI findings was scored using CROMRIS. Hypothesis testing and agglomerative k-cluster analysis was used to identify patterns of disease. A total of 246 imaging studies were retrieved for 138 patients (87 female, 51 male, median age 10.5 years, IQR 9.0, 12.6) comprising 96 Whole Body MRI (WBMR), 67 MRI, 61 radiographic and 20 CT studies. Median time from diagnosis to imaging was -16 days (IQR -110, 14). In all 581 foci of disease were identified (inter-rater agreement 81.4%) most commonly affecting the pelvis and lower limb (62%). The clavicle was the 5th most common location but the most common single site location (9%) for single site disease. Abnormal vertebrae were identified in 55 patients (38%) and these were complicated by a fracture in 30%. There was no difference in the prevalence of abnormalities between the sexes. Patients with vertebral involvement had fewer sites of disease. Involvement of the head and mandible is often isolated. Four out of five lesions on WBMR were discordant with the patients' symptoms and 56% of all sites of disease were discordant. The pelvis and lower limb are the most common locations affected by CNO. Vertebral involvement is more common than previously reported and clinically silent disease is common. Apart from disease in the mandible and head there are no other discernible radiological phenotypes.

cards.title: Monoportal endoscopic intrapelvic versus conventional anterior intrapelvic approach for acetabular fractures: a retrospective comparative study of early postoperative and radiographic outcomes.
cards.abstract: The monoportal endoscopic intrapelvic (MEI) approach has recently been introduced as a minimally invasive alternative to the conventional anterior intrapelvic (AIP) approach for acetabular fractures. This study compared perioperative, radiographic, and early clinical outcomes between the MEI and AIP approaches. This retrospective comparative cohort study included 48 patients undergoing acetabular fracture fixation through an isolated intrapelvic approach (28 historical AIP and 20 MEI). Perioperative outcomes, radiographic reduction quality, postoperative pain, opioid consumption, mobilization, length of stay, and complications were compared. Multivariable regression analyses were adjusted for age, ASA score, polytrauma, both-column fracture pattern, and marginal impaction. Compared with isolated AIP, MEI was associated with lower postoperative pain on day 1 (adjusted mean difference - 2.07, 95% CI - 2.90 to - 1.25; p < 0.001), lower transformed cumulative opioid consumption (adjusted ratio 0.15, 95% CI 0.06-0.42; p < 0.001), earlier mobilization (adjusted ratio 0.59, 95% CI 0.39-0.89; p = 0.012), and shorter hospital stay (adjusted ratio 0.55, 95% CI 0.40-0.75; p < 0.001). Estimated blood loss was numerically lower with MEI but did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (adjusted ratio 0.71, 95% CI 0.48-1.05; p = 0.087). No statistically significant difference was detected in postoperative radiographic reduction quality. The MEI approach was associated with improved early postoperative recovery compared with conventional AIP, with no statistically significant difference detected in radiographic reduction quality. Larger prospective studies are warranted to confirm these findings and further define the role of endoscopic intrapelvic fixation in acetabular fracture surgery.

cards.title: Spatial and epigenetic programs underlie heterogeneous cellular senescence in the aging liver
cards.abstract: Abstract Aging is a complex biological process leading to tissue dysfunction, and driven in part by progressive epigenetic drift, widespread transcriptional dysregulation and cellular senescence. Senescent cells (SnCs) accumulate across tissues in a heterogeneous and cell type-specific manner, yet their molecular signatures and spatial organization within native tissue have not been systematically mapped. Here we combined single-nucleus transcriptomic, epigenomic, three-dimensional (3D) genome and spatial profiling to systematically characterize aging of the mouse liver and associated cellular senescence. Aging was marked by hepatocyte loss, immune cell expansion, erosion of repressive H3K9me3 heterochromatin, alteration of 3D genome organization, and activation of stress-response pathways known to promote senescence. Age-associated SnCs were spatially colocalized within discrete inflammatory microenvironments termed SenSpots. Different SenSpots were dominated by distinct hepatocyte senescence states (senotypes), driven by unique transcription factors, and exhibited distinct lobular zonation. Single-cell DNA methylation profiling revealed a subset of immune cells in aged livers with loss of DNA methylation at constitutive heterochromatin and elevated senescence signatures. AAV-mediated, p21-promoter driven Stat1 deletion in the aged liver selectively suppressed interferon-responsive senescence programs while pharmacological inhibition of MDM2 attenuated senescence-associated inflammatory signatures. Together, these findings reveal that hepatic senescence is not a uniform state but a set of diverse epigenetically reprogrammed, spatially organized, and pharmacologically modifiable inflammatory niches.

cards.title: A multi-platform analysis of paired well- and dedifferentiated liposarcoma identifies recurrent genomic alterations associated with progression and recurrence.
cards.abstract: Knowledge regarding genomic aberrations resulting in progression of low-grade well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDLS) to high-grade dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLS) is limited. We analyzed DNA sequence, copy number, and gene expression in 9 paired WD/DDLS or WD/WDLS serial surgical samples to identify potential drivers of progression. We validated the relevance of events using samples collected from 265 patients and in vitro studies. All WDLS exhibited characteristic amplification of 12q13-15; additional, novel 6q23-25 gains were observed in 18% of WDLS and associated with higher local recurrence risk (HR=11, p<0.001). The 6q23-25 amplicon encoded TAB2, which was 2.1-fold overexpressed in WDLS samples with the event; in vitro TAB2 was necessary to prevent senescence and allow for MDM2 accumulation in 6q23-25-amplified WDLS cells but not in non-amplified WDLS or amplified DDLS cells. WDLS progression to DDLS was not associated with 6q23-25 amplification but with pathogenic ATRX mutations (7.6% vs 0%), 13q losses (22% vs 3.4%), and 8q12-21 gains (21% vs 5%). Downregulation of 13q genes MYCBP2 and IRS2 was observed in DDLS; in vitro, these genes were essential for WDLS cell differentiation. This study defines a longitudinal model of liposarcomagenesis with initiation characterized by 12q13-15 amplification, early WDLS progression through inhibition of senescence by 6q23-25 amplification, and progression to DDLS driven by ATRX mutations and/or tertiary copy number events (e.g., 13q loss, 8q12-21 gain). Implications: This study defines the role of recurrent copy number alterations and gene mutations in WD/DDLS initiation and progression, creating a detailed map of molecular events regulating liposarcomagenesis, patient outcome, and dedifferentiation.

cards.title: 3D-DXA-based Finite Element Models Improve Hip Fracture Prediction versus aBMD in the Japanese Population-Based Osteoporosis (JPOS) Cohort Study
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Summary Hip fractures are among the most serious consequences of osteoporosis, yet many individuals who sustain hip fractures do not meet the diagnostic threshold based on areal bone mineral density (aBMD). Finite element (FE)-based mechanical descriptors may improve hip fracture prediction beyond aBMD. Purpose This study investigated whether FE-based mechanical descriptors derived from dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) improve hip fracture discrimination beyond aBMD in the Japanese Population-Based Osteoporosis (JPOS) cohort. Methods The study included 1,636 women, of whom 85 sustained hip fractures during 20 years of follow-up. Subject-specific three-dimensional femoral models were reconstructed from DXA images using statistical shape and appearance modelling, and nonlinear FE analyses were performed to derive mechanical descriptors under simulated sideways-fall loading. Predictive performance was evaluated using discrimination, model fit, reclassification, and hazard ratio analyses. Results Over two-thirds of women who experienced hip fracture were not classified as osteoporotic based on aBMD. Several FE-based descriptors significantly improved fracture prediction relative to total hip and femoral neck aBMD across the evaluation frameworks. The best-performing descriptor, combining femoral strength with residual energy (F_U + W_R), achieved a significantly higher AUROC of 0.797 compared with 0.763 (p = 0.026) and 0.757 (p = 0.040) for total hip and femoral neck aBMD, respectively, and the highest hazard ratio (3.577 per SD). The same descriptors consistently performed best across all evaluation methods. Conclusion These findings demonstrate that FE-based descriptors provide meaningful information beyond aBMD and may improve identification of women at elevated hip fracture risk.

cards.title: Flexible Organic Crystals toward Functional Devices: From Serendipitous Discovery to Rational Design.
cards.abstract: Organic small-molecule single crystals, owing to their long-range ordered packing structures and anisotropic physical properties, have long been regarded as important material platforms for the construction of high-performance optoelectronic devices. However, because of the densely packed molecular arrangements and the relatively fragile networks of noncovalent interactions, these rigid lattices are prone to local stress concentrations under external mechanical perturbations, which can further lead to macroscopic fracture. Over the past decade, the continuous emergence of flexible organic crystals has expanded the current understanding of the mechanical behaviors of organic crystals and contributed to the development of "crystal adaptronics", an emerging research direction centered on mechanically adaptive molecular crystals and their functional applications. Under appropriate molecular conformations and lattice symmetry conditions, some organic crystals can accommodate pronounced deformation, including bending, through reversible and cooperative lattice expansion-contraction or through interlayer slippage, thereby dissipating stress while preserving structural integrity and intrinsic optoelectronic functionality. In this review, we move beyond a simple categorization of recent works to critically summarize the mechanical mechanisms of flexible organic crystals, the corresponding molecular design strategies, and recent advances in their applications in functional devices, and further discuss the major challenges and future directions in this field.

cards.title: Stress Fracture Recovery and Return to Sports in Youth with Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis.
cards.abstract: To compare stress fracture recovery times in children with and without juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), and to evaluate JIA-related factors associated with recovery. This retrospective case-control study included children with JIA <19 years old with a first stress fracture treated at a single center from 2004-2024. Cases were matched 1:3 to children without JIA by age, gender, and fracture location. Recovery time was defined from imaging confirmation of a stress fracture to medical clearance to return to sports. We used a generalized estimating equations method to compare recovery times and evaluate associations with JIA-related factors, including JIA subtype, glucocorticoid and arthritis-directed therapy exposure, and proximity of arthritis to fracture location. The cohort included 260 children (65 cases, 195 controls; 53.8% female; median age 14.3 years [IQR 12.6, 16.2]). Pars interarticularis fractures accounted for 30.8% of injuries, followed by metatarsal (23.1%), and tibial fractures (14.2%). Among children with JIA who sustained pars fractures, 75.0% had an enthesitis-related arthritis (ERA) phenotype. Median recovery times were 10.6 (IQR 7.0, 19.4) weeks for children with JIA and 10.6 (IQR 7.1, 14.6) weeks for controls (P=0.197), with no significant differences for lower-extremity fractures. In contrast, children with JIA who sustained pars fractures had longer recovery times than controls (ratio of geometric means: 1.44, 95% CI 1.01, 2.05; P=0.045). Among children with active sacroiliitis, fractures occurred more frequently in the proximate pars or pelvis than at non-proximate sites (P<0.001). Recovery time was not associated with JIA subtype (all p>0.150), glucocorticoid exposure (P=0.365), or biologic therapy (P=0.625). Overall recovery times did not differ significantly between children with and without JIA. However, children with JIA and pars fractures had longer recovery times, and associations with ERA and sacroiliitis warrant further investigation. Additional research on spondylolysis recovery in young athletes with JIA may help inform individualized return-to-sports recommendations.

cards.title: INTERMITTENT ANDROGEN DEPRIVATION THERAPY PLUS COMPREHENSIVE STEREOTACTIC BODY RADIOTHERAPY FOR OLIGOMETASTATIC HORMONE SENSITIVE PROSTATE CANCER (CROP): MATURE RESULTS OF A PROSPECTIVE TRIAL.
cards.abstract: This phase I/II single-arm trial assessed the tolerability and efficacy of stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to all tumours plus intermittent androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) in patients with oligometastatic hormone sensitive prostate cancer (HSPC). Primary endpoint was the incidence of grade 3+ SBRT induced adverse events (AE's), including radiotherapy induced bone fractures. Secondary endpoints included failure-free survival (FFS), cumulative incidence of developing castration resistant prostate cancer (CRPC), and overall survival (OS). Eligible patients had synchronous or metachronous oligometastases (≤ 5 metastases, with ≤ 3 metastases in any one organ system) identified on conventional imaging. SBRT was delivered to all lesions, along with 1 year of ADT before stopping. Intermittent ADT (using 1 year cycles) was restarted when the prostate specific antigen (PSA) reached > 10 ng/mL, if new metastases developed, or earlier at the discretion of the physician. SBRT could be delivered to any new oligometastases that developed while off ADT in conjunction with restarting ADT. Eighty-nine evaluable patients with 171 metastases were enrolled. Median follow-up was 74.7 months. Thirty-three patients (37.1%) had synchronous disease presentation. Six patients (6.7%) experienced grade 3 AE's (5 patients with vertebral fractures and 1 patient with urinary tract obstruction). The 5-year cumulative incidence of restarting ADT and developing CRPC were 59.7% and 22.8% respectively. Five-year FFS and OS were 15.2% and 78.2% respectively. Higher PSA nadir after SBRT and 1 year of ADT was significantly associated with developing subsequent CRPC and worse OS. At time of last follow-up, 35 patients (39.3%) were alive with HSPC and not on ADT. SBRT and intermittent ADT for oligometastatic HSPC was safe and resulted in favourable long-term outcomes. A small proportion of patients did not progress in any way after SBRT and 1 year of ADT.

cards.title: The Use of Regional Anesthesia in Pediatric Orthopaedic Surgery-Review of the Literature, Controversies, and Current Status.
cards.abstract: Regional anesthesia (RA) has become an increasingly important component of perioperative care in pediatric orthopaedic surgery. RA utilization in pediatric patients is well documented as part of the management of upper and lower extremity trauma, both at the time of fracture reduction as well as during definitive surgical stabilization. Elective management of both upper and lower extremity deformities and reconstruction of chronic injuries with RA support are common practices in many centers. Use of RA to mitigate postoperative pain and improve patient mobilization after elective spinal deformity procedures in pediatric patients is also well established. Despite extensive studies reporting successful and safe use of RA in his patient cohort, questions remain regarding potential risks and complications, particularly potential issues with postprocedure neurologic evaluation. Continued modifications in anesthetic techniques, in combination with an increased use of peripheral nerve blocks in place of neuroaxial blockades, may further limit the risk of potential postoperative issues.

cards.title: Development and validation of severe muscle mass reduction cutoffs for GLIM Criteria in Japanese adults: A two-phase study.
cards.abstract: The Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition prioritizes instrument-based assessment of reduced muscle mass, but severity-grading cutoffs for appendicular skeletal muscle mass index and fat-free mass index are not established. We derived cutoffs for severe muscle mass reduction in older Japanese outpatients and examined their associations with mortality in hospitalized adults. A frailty clinic registry identified thresholds for appendicular skeletal muscle mass index by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry or bioelectrical impedance analysis and fat-free mass index by bioelectrical impedance analysis. Receiver operating characteristic analyses used 1-year hospitalization as the outcome, with thresholds refined according to hospitalization risk. Nationwide claims data were used for validation. Mortality was assessed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses adjusted for age, sex, comorbidities, and frailty. The development cohort included 1035 participants (mean age, 76.5 years). Severe muscle mass reduction cutoffs for appendicular skeletal muscle mass index were <6.4 kg/m2 in men and <5.0 kg/m2 in women using either method, and those for fat-free mass index were <16.0 kg/m2 in men and <13.4 kg/m2 in women. In the validation cohort (n = 242,464), severe muscle mass reduction was associated with higher mortality, with hazard ratios of 2.04 (95% confidence interval: 1.97-2.12), 1.95 (1.86-2.03), and 2.01 (1.94-2.09) for appendicular skeletal muscle mass index by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and bioelectrical impedance analysis and for fat-free mass index, respectively (all P < 0.001). These cutoffs may facilitate severity grading according to the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition criteria and improve prognostic risk stratification.

cards.title: Causal effects of connective tissue diseases on sarcopenia-related traits and the mediating role of immune cell phenotypes: a mediation Mendelian randomization study.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as a common comorbidity of connective tissue diseases (CTDs). However, the causal relationships between CTDs and sarcopenia-related traits, and whether immune cells mediate these effects, remain unclear. We performed a three-step Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis using genome-wide association study summary data of European ancestry. Step 1 evaluated the causal effects of seven CTDs on five sarcopenia-related traits. Step 2 screened 731 immune cell phenotypes for associations with these traits. Step 3 assessed the causal effects of the selected CTDs on the selected immune cell phenotypes. For each exposure-mediator-outcome triplet, the indirect effect and the mediation proportion were estimated using a two-step MR approach. Dermatomyositis (DM), mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD), polymyositis (PM), and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) were causally associated with at least one sarcopenia-related trait. Among 731 immune traits, 15 were significantly associated with at least three traits after FDR correction. In patients with RA, mediation analysis indicated that HLA-DR expression on CD14-CD16- cells partially mediated the effect on appendicular lean mass (mediation proportion = 9.76%, P = 0.040, q = 0.099) and whole-body-fat-free mass (mediation proportion = 5.76%, P = 0.039, q = 0.099), though these mediation findings did not survive FDR correction and should therefore be considered exploratory. This mediation MR study provides genetic evidence that DM, MCTD, PM and RA are causally associated with specific sarcopenia-related traits. The partial mediation of RA's effects through HLA-DR up-regulation on CD14⁻CD16⁻ cells suggests a potential immune pathway linking RA to muscle loss, though these findings require confirmation in independent cohorts. Key Points • The first mediation MR study to quantifies the mediating role of a specific immune cell phenotype in the causal pathway from CTDs to sarcopenia-related traits. • DM, MCTD, PM, and RA were causally associated with sarcopenia-related traits, with PM and RA showing the most consistent detrimental effects. • HLA-DR expression on CD14-CD16- cells may partially mediate the effect 3 of RA on appendicular lean mass and whole body fat free mass.

cards.title: Small bites for big risks: efficacy of the small-bites closure technique in a real-world laparotomy cohort.
cards.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of the continuous small-bites fascial closure technique compared to standard large-bites closure in an unselected, consecutive series of high-risk patients undergoing midline laparotomy. The primary objective was to investigate whether the small-bites approach remains effective and safe in a real-world surgical population burdened with systemic comorbidities. A retrospective analysis of a prospectively maintained clinical database was conducted on 101 patients assigned via an institutional protocol (53 small-bites, 48 large-bites). The primary outcome was the one-year incidence of incisional hernia (IH). Secondary outcomes included surgical site infections and operative metrics. Multivariable binary logistic regression was utilized to adjust for baseline confounding factors, specifically variations in abdominal muscle quality as measured by the L3 cross-sectional mass ratio. At the one-year follow-up, overall IH occurred in 7.5% of the small-bites group versus 12.5% of the large-bites group (p = 0.405). The small-bites approach required significantly longer fascial closure times (p = 0.016) but resulted in non-significant reductions in surgical site infections (30.2% vs. 39.6%, p = 0.322) and early evisceration (5.4% vs. 15.8%, p = 0.072). Additionally, baseline L3 cross-sectional mass ratio did not independently predict herniation (p = 0.142). Subgroup analyses revealed no significant differences in IH rates between the closure techniques in high-risk patients presenting with underlying malignancy (p = 0.632), sarcopenia (p = 0.689), or stomas (p = 1.000). However, in patients without malignancy, the small-bites technique yielded a significantly lower incidence of IH compared to the standard approach (p = 0.022). Adjusted multivariable regression indicated a non-significant decreased risk of IH development with small-bites (p = 0.360). The small-bites technique is a safe and comparably effective closure method for real-world cohorts. It maintains fascial integrity in high-risk patients and significantly reduces incisional hernia risk in non-malignant cases.

cards.title: Outcome Analysis of Distal Third Tibial Fractures Treated With Minimally Invasive Plate Osteosynthesis: Protocol for a Prospective Observational Study.
cards.abstract: Distal third tibial fractures are difficult to treat owing to the subcutaneous anteromedial border of the tibia, its tenuous periosteal vascularity, and the proximity of the fracture to the ankle joint. Minimally invasive plate osteosynthesis (MIPO) using a locking compression plate (LCP) preserves fracture biology by avoiding direct exposure of the fracture site. This study aims to describe the functional and radiological outcomes of closed distal third tibial fractures (Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Osteosynthesefragen/Orthopaedic Trauma Association [AO/OTA] types A, B, and C1) treated with MIPO-LCP in an Indian tertiary care setting. The study is descriptive and hypothesis generating and is not designed as a comparative effectiveness trial. This is a single-center, single-arm, prospective observational cohort study to be conducted at a rural tertiary center in India over 24 months (May 2026 to April 2028). Thirty adults aged 18 to 80 years with closed AO/OTA type A, type B, or type C1 distal third tibial fractures are to be enrolled consecutively. The primary outcomes are the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle-hindfoot score at 6 months, administered by an independent assessor, and the time to radiological fracture union, assessed using the Radiographic Union Scale for Tibia (RUST). Secondary outcomes include the Olerud-Molander Ankle Score (OMAS), complications, and time to full weight-bearing. Exploratory regression analysis will be performed. Follow-up is scheduled at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months. Ethics approval was obtained on July 8, 2025. Enrollment has been ongoing since May 1, 2026. As of September 2026, five participants have been enrolled. Results are expected between 2028 and 2029. This protocol will generate prospective, hypothesis-generating data on MIPO outcomes in India. Findings will be descriptive only and, given the sample size limitation (n=30), cannot support definitive claims. Results will inform future comparative trials. Clinical Trials Registry-India CTRI/2026/04/108996; https://tinyurl.com/2j9eh8kp. DERR1-10.2196/100325.

cards.title: Association between Alzheimer's disease and related dementias and postoperative outcomes after geriatric hip fracture surgery.
cards.abstract: Patients with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) represent a vulnerable subset of geriatric hip fracture patients, yet the extent to which ADRD influences postoperative outcomes remains incompletely characterized. The purpose of this study was to examine the association between Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) and outcomes. A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted of patients 65 years or older undergoing operative management for hip fractures at a multi-site urban academic medical center. Patients were stratified by ADRD status as documented in the electronic medical record. Univariate analyses compared demographic characteristics, injury and surgical variables, hospital quality metrics, and mortality using chi-square and Student's t-tests, as appropriate. Multivariable regression models controlling for age, sex, BMI, ASA class, Charlson Comorbidity Index, baseline functional status, and fracture classification evaluated the association between ADRD and study outcomes. A total of 3,312 patients were included: 829 (25.0%) ADRD vs. 2483 (75.0%) control. ADRD patients were older, had greater comorbidity burden, and had worse baseline functional status. ADRD patients had increased minor and major complications, ICU admissions, readmissions, 1-year mortality, and longer hospitalization (all p < 0.001). Variance inflation factor analysis confirmed no meaningful multicollinearity among covariates (VIF range 1.04-1.34). On multivariable analysis, ADRD was independently associated with major complications (OR 1.372, 95% CI 1.066-1.760), ICU admission (OR 1.581, 95% CI 1.231-2.025), length of stay (β 0.958, 95% CI 0.624-1.292), 30-day (OR 1.994, 95% CI 1.521-2.608) and 31- to 90-day readmission (OR 1.956, 95% CI 1.453-2.625), and mortality between 31 days and 1 year (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.18-2.01). ADRD is independently associated with worse postoperative outcomes after geriatric hip fracture. These associations persisted after adjustment for baseline comorbidity, functional status, and fracture classification, though residual confounding by unmeasured frailty domains cannot be excluded. Orthogeriatric co-management should be directed toward this vulnerable population to optimize outcomes.
