cards.title: Plasma exchange for acute and acute-on-chronic liver failure: A systematic review and patient-level survival data meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: Acute liver failure (ALF) and acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) are associated with high short-term mortality. Plasma exchange (PE) has been proposed as a therapeutic strategy, but its effect on survival remains uncertain. We conducted a systematic review and reconstructed patient-level survival data meta-analysis to assess the association between PE and transplant-free survival (TFS) and post-transplant survival in ALF and ACLF. PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus were searched through June 2026. Eligible studies compared PE with standard medical therapy (SMT) and reported Kaplan-Meier data suitable for reconstruction. Patient-level time-to-event data were reconstructed from curves using validated methods and analyzed with one-stage Cox proportional hazards models incorporating shared frailty to account for between-study heterogeneity. The endpoint was TFS. Sensitivity, subgroup, and restricted mean survival time (RMST) analyses were performed to evaluate robustness and clinical relevance. Eighteen studies including 1440 patients were analyzed: nine studies in ALF (n=617) and nine in ACLF (n=823). In ALF, PE was associated with improved TFS compared with SMT (HR 0.46, 95% CI 0.36-0.58). In ACLF, PE was also associated with improved TFS (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.51-0.73). Results were supported by sensitivity analyses and RMST estimates. PE was not associated with improved post-transplant survival. PE was associated with significantly improved TFS in ALF and ACLF compared with SMT. These findings support PE as a valuable supportive strategy to improve TFS in selected patients with severe liver failure, while its role specifically as a bridge to liver transplantation requires further prospective evaluation.

cards.title: A biofidelic Goat Model of Traumatic Optic Neuropathy with Optic Canal Fracture via Transnasal Endoscopy.
cards.abstract: Traumatic optic neuropathy (TON) is a major cause of irreversible vision loss following blunt cranial trauma. However, translational research has been significantly impeded by the lack of clinically relevant large-animal models that faithfully recapitulate the human condition. Current rodent models fail to reproduce optic canal fractures, which represent a key injury mechanism in many patients with TON. Here, we combined high-fidelity finite element analysis (FEA) with iterative engineering to establish a reproducible goat model of TON. We first developed a high-resolution finite element model of the human head to characterize force transmission to the optic nerve. During simulated clinically relevant periorbital impacts, stress preferentially concentrated in the intracanalicular segment, reaching a peak force density of approximately 500 N/m 2 at 50.6 ms-a magnitude approximately fivefold higher than that observed in the intraorbital segment. Further simulations demonstrated that direct impact to the optic canal reproduced comparable intracanalicular stress using a markedly lower input force (195 N) compared with periorbital impact (3 900 N). Guided by these insights, we developed transnasal endoscopic impact systems capable of inducing optic canal fractures in goats. The induction of TON was confirmed within 24 h by the presence of a characteristic relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD). At 1 month post-injury, the goats ( n=14) exhibited a 10%-20% reduction in ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness and 40%-65% reductions in flash visual evoked potential (FVEP) and pattern electroretinogram (PERG) amplitude ratios (all P≤0.001), while the structural and functional integrity of the fellow eye was preserved. This study presents a robust, standardized, and clinically relevant large-animal platform for investigating TON pathophysiology.

cards.title: Prevalence and Clinical Determinants of Frailty in Older Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Attending a Diabetes Centre in India.
cards.abstract: Diabetes and frailty are both increasing in prevalence due to population ageing. However, data on these comorbid occurrences and real-world outcomes are scarce. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of frailty and its metabolic, nutritional and clinical associations in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) attending a diabetes centre in India. A total of 1171 individuals aged 65 years and above with T2DM were assessed for frailty using the validated Frailty Assessment and Screening Tool (FAST) questionnaire. Dominant-hand grip strength (HGS) was measured using a Jamar dynamometer, utilizing the American Society of Hand Therapists (ASHT) criteria. Additionally, sensitivity analysis was done using the Sarcopenia-Chandigarh Urban Bone Epidemiological Study (Sarco-CUBES) criteria. Standardized definitions were employed to evaluate microvascular complications associated with diabetes. Individuals with T2DM had a mean age of 71.5 ± 5.4 years, and male participants constituted 65.3% of the study population. The overall prevalence of frailty was 59.0% (691/1171). Among the 691 individuals, FAST-defined frailty alone identified only 6.2% (43/691) individuals, whereas HGS-defined low muscle strength alone identified 80.7% (558/691), and 13.0% (90/691) met the FAST/HGS composite classification. Using Sarco-CUBES-derived cut-offs, the prevalence was 76.4% (895/1171). Logistic regression analysis showed that physical inactivity along with uncontrolled diabetes was associated with higher odds of frailty (adjusted odds ratio: 2.12, 95% CI: 1.48-3.03; p<0.001). Multivariable models identified advanced age,physical inactivity, lower protein intake, sulfonylurea use and uncontrolled diabetes as independently associated with frailty. The prevalence of diabetic retinopathy was higher in the cohort with frailty compared to those without (74.3% vs. 65.6%; p = 0.032),even after adjusting for age, sex, HbA1c, and diabetes duration. Among older Indian adults with T2DM attending a diabetes centre, 59.0-76.4% were classified as having frailty depending on criteria used. Increasing age, physical inactivity, inadequate protein intake and uncontrolled diabetes were significantly associated with frailty. Implementing routine screening along with targeted, comprehensive interventions and appropriate medications are essential to manage frailty in elderly patients with T2DM in India.

cards.title: Imaging evaluation of pediatric acquired hearing loss.
cards.abstract: Pediatric acquired hearing loss represents a clinical challenge, requiring prompt diagnosis in order to optimize normal language and psychosocial development. This review outlines a practical imaging framework categorizing acquired hearing loss etiologies into opacified and aerated middle ears. High-resolution computed tomography (CT) is the gold standard for delineating osseous anatomy, including ossicular discontinuity, fractures, and congenital or acquired bone erosion. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides soft-tissue characterization, and can evaluate labyrinth contents, cranial nerves, and for intracranial complications; non-echo-planar diffusion-weighted imaging (non-EPI DWI) can help to identify cholesteatomas. By leveraging these complementary modalities, radiologists can establish a precise diagnostic roadmap to guide clinical management and surgical intervention.

cards.title: Multi‐Trait Integration of Sarcopenia‐Related Phenotypes Identifies Genetic Loci and Biological Pathways Linked to Muscle Aging
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Sarcopenia is an age‐related syndrome characterized by progressive declines in muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. To investigate the shared genetic architecture of quantitative traits relevant to sarcopenia, we integrated genome‐wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for appendicular lean mass, hand grip strength, and walking pace from the UK Biobank. Significant genetic correlations among these traits supported multi‐trait integration, resulting in an integrated GWAS termed mtMuscleAging. A total of 405 associated loci were identified, including 78 loci with enhanced significance and 33 loci that did not reach genome‐wide significance in any individual trait GWAS. Fine‐mapping prioritized 538 candidate variants, while integrative post‐GWAS analyses identified prioritized genes and highlighted conserved coding regions and biological pathways related to muscle, heart, pancreas, fibroblasts, and aging. Single‐cell and single‐nucleus transcriptomic analyses further contextualized these genetic findings in aging skeletal muscle and identified alterations in midkine and pleiotrophin signaling and intercellular communication. Phenome‐wide association analyses identified genetic relationships between mtMuscleAging and multiple health phenotypes, including cardiovascular disorders. Machine‐learning analyses based on prioritized genes captured age‐associated skeletal muscle expression patterns, while drug repurposing analyses nominated candidate compounds for further experimental evaluation. Collectively, our findings characterize shared genetic variation across sarcopenia‐related traits and provide loci, genes, cellular contexts, and candidate compounds relevant to muscle aging.

cards.title: Off-Pump Versus On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Prefrail and Frail Patients: 30-Day and 1-Year Outcomes From the FRAGILE Randomized Trial.
cards.abstract: Frailty is associated with worse outcomes after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). However, the comparative effectiveness of off-pump CABG (OPCAB) versus on-pump CABG (ONCAB) in prefrail and frail patients remains uncertain. This multicenter, randomized, open-label trial enrolled patients ≥60 years of age classified as prefrail or frail, randomized 1:1, between January 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was a 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke, renal failure, acute respiratory distress syndrome, or reoperation for bleeding. Secondary outcomes included ventilation time, intensive care unit and hospital stay, transfusion requirements, completeness of revascularization, surgical wound infection at 30 days, and neurocognitive function preoperatively and at 1 year. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle; relative risks with 95% CIs were estimated. A total of 508 patients were included (OPCAB, n=258; ONCAB, n=250; median age, 68 years [interquartile range, 65.0-73]; 30.5% female). The primary composite outcome occurred in 28 patients receiving OPCAB (10.9%) and 40 patients receiving ONCAB (16.0%; relative risk, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.94-2.31]; P=0.09). Surgical wound infection was more frequent with ONCAB (20 [8.0%] versus 9 [3.5%]; P=0.04). No significant differences were observed in neurocognitive or quality of life outcomes at 1 year. Estimated 1-year survival probabilities were 96.1% and 92.8% in the OPCAB and ONCAB groups, respectively (P=0.099). In prefrail and frail patients undergoing CABG, OPCAB and ONCAB resulted in similar rates of the primary composite outcome. No significant differences between OPCAB and ONCAB were found in neurocognitive outcomes. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02338947.

cards.title: Management of hypertension in older persons: what do the 2023/2024 European Society of Hypertension, 2024 European Society of Cardiology and 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology guidelines tell us?
cards.abstract: Treatment of hypertension in older people is associated with significant health-related benefits. However, at very old age, in patients with frailty, multimorbidity, and polypharmacy, the benefits of treatment must be balanced against the potential for harm from adverse events. The evidence for treatment in such populations is limited because they typically have not been included in many clinical trials. In this article, we discuss the differences in the approach to management of hypertension in older patients between the three recent clinical guidelines: the European Society of Hypertension (2023-2024), European Society of Cardiology (2024) and the American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology (2025) guidelines. We conclude that the therapeutic approach to older persons should be personalized and should include a comprehensive evaluation of functionality and frailty. Balancing potential health-related benefits and harms should be the basis of all clinical decisions in this population, especially for individuals eluding simplistic classifications.

cards.title: Vertebral Augmentation for Osteoporotic Compression Fractures: Umbrella Review of Adjacent Vertebral Fracture Incidence and Risk Factors.
cards.abstract: To determine whether vertebral augmentation (VA) increases adjacent vertebral fracture (AVF) risk compared with conservative treatment and identify potential risk factors. PubMed, EMBASE, EBSCOhost, ScienceDirect, and Scopus were searched for systematic reviews and meta-analyses published between 2014 and 2025 evaluating AVFs following VA for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) [PROSPERO: CRD420251079382]. Methodological quality, evidence overlap, and certainty were assessed using AMSTAR-2, corrected covered area (CCA) and weighted CCA (wCCA), and an adapted GRADE framework, respectively. Narrative synthesis followed SWiM due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Reporting followed PRIOR and PRISMA 2020 guidance. Nine systematic reviews and meta-analyses were included. AMSTAR-2 confidence was low in 5/9 and critically low in 4/9 reviews. All 13 GRADE-assessed outcomes had low or very low certainty. Evidence overlap was 5.88% by CCA and 4.66% by wCCA. One review reported a pooled single-arm AVF incidence of approximately 14%, while other reviews reported incidences of 8%-18%. Comparative findings were heterogeneous, with increased, decreased, or no significant difference in AVF risk following VA versus conservative treatment. Lower bone mineral density, female sex, cement leakage, cement volume, and inadequate anti-osteoporosis treatment were reported as potential risk factors, although associations varied and were not consistently specific to adjacent-level fractures. Current evidence does not consistently demonstrate increased AVF risk following VA compared with conservative treatment. Heterogeneity, methodological limitations, and low to very low certainty limit definitive conclusions. Standardized fracture definitions, reporting of procedural factors and osteoporosis treatment, and adequately powered prospective studies are required.

cards.title: Tubular EZH2-HIF1α axis promotes mouse renal fibrosis after ischemia-reperfusion-induced acute kidney injury by accelerating cellular senescence.
cards.abstract: Maladaptive tubular repair and cellular senescence contribute to the transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD), but the associated regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the involvement of EZH2- and HIF-1α-associated signaling in tubular senescence and renal fibrosis. A murine unilateral ischemia-reperfusion injury model combined with contralateral nephrectomy was used to examine AKI-to-CKD progression, and DZNep was administered to evaluate its pharmacological effects. Hypoxia/reoxygenation- and TGF-β1-stimulated tubular epithelial cells were used for complementary in vitro analyses. EZH2 and HIF-1α remained elevated during post-ischemic kidney injury, whereas DZNep treatment improved renal function and attenuated tubular damage, fibrosis, and senescence-associated changes. In HK-2 cells, DZNep and 2-MeOE2 reduced injury-, fibrosis-, and senescence-related responses. To strengthen target-specific evidence, EZH2 knockdown attenuated H/R-induced HIF-1α expression, SASP production, and α-SMA and FN accumulation. Similarly, HIF1A knockdown reduced EZH2 expression and the induction of SASP and profibrotic proteins following H/R. These genetic findings support the involvement of both EZH2 and HIF-1α in the cellular response to ischemic stress, although they do not establish direct regulation or a feedback loop. Collectively, EZH2- and HIF-1α-associated signaling may contribute to maladaptive tubular senescence and fibrotic remodeling after AKI and warrants further mechanistic evaluation.

cards.title: Endogenous pain modulation after polytraumatic TBI and the impact of exercise.
cards.abstract: Polytraumatic brain injury (pTBI) involves concurrent injuries to the brain and other body regions, demanding a multidisciplinary approach to pain management and rehabilitation. Here, we evaluated pTBI-induced disruption of endogenous pain modulation in male and female rats, and therapeutic impact of monominergic drugs and voluntary exercise. We established a rat pTBI model combining the lateral fluid percussion model of brain trauma and tibia fracture with pin fixation. We then evaluated mechanical nociceptive reactivity, descending control of nociception (DCN) and response to selective noradrenergic (NRI) and serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRI), as well as α1-, α2-adrenoceptor, and 5-HT7 serotonin receptor antagonists. pTBI caused chronic hindpaw mechanical hypersensitivity up to 180 days post-injury (DPI) bilaterally in females and unilaterally in males. Acute NRI treatment elevated noradrenaline and reduced hindlimb hypersensitivity in both sexes, an effect reversed by an α1- adrenoceptor antagonist. While NRI pretreatment remained effective through 180 DPI in females, efficacy diminished in males by 49 DPI. In males, hindlimb hypersensitivity was instead reduced by enhancing serotonin signaling with an SSRI acting via the 5-HT7 receptor. DCN response was present in both male and female pTBI rats following SSRI or NRI pretreatment, respectively. In female pTBI rats, voluntary exercise initiated at 3 DPI restored normal sensitivity by 21 DPI and maintained an intact DCN response up to 180 DPI; these gains were reversed an α1- adrenoceptor antagonist. Overall, pTBI causes chronic mechanical hindlimb hypersensitivity treatable with sex-specific reuptake inhibitors, while early exercise restores long-term noradrenergic pain modulation in females.

cards.title: Neighborhood walkability, green space, and incident hip fracture among older U.S. adults: The cardiovascular health study.
cards.abstract: Neighborhood walkability and green space are associated with walking behavior and physical activity, but evidence linking them to fracture is limited and inconsistent, and potential sex differences remain understudied. We evaluated associations of neighborhood walkability and green space with incident hip fracture in older, community-dwelling U.S. adults. We conducted a prospective cohort study of adults aged ≥65 years from the Cardiovascular Health Study (CHS). Neighborhood exposures were defined using 1-km radial buffers around geocoded residential addresses from 1992 to 1993 (baseline). Walkability was the sum of standardized population and walkable destination densities. Green space was the proportion of satellite-derived green land cover. Hip fractures were prospectively ascertained over 12 years using International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision (ICD-9) codes from hospital discharge abstracts. Cox hazard models adjusted for individual-level (age, sex, race, weight, height, smoking status, current heavy alcohol use, medication use, diabetes, renal function, marital status, education level, annual household income) and neighborhood-level (median household income, median value of owner-occupied housing, proportion of persons in managerial/professional occupations) covariates evaluated associations, overall and by sex. Among 3676 participants (58% women), 359 experienced hip fracture over a median 10-years observation. Greater neighborhood walkability was significantly associated with lower hip fracture incidence among women (hazard ratio per 1 standard deviation increase of 0.72 [95% confidence interval, 0.53-0.98]), but not overall or among men. Neighborhood green space was not significantly associated with hip fracture. Greater neighborhood walkability, but not green space, was associated with lower hip fracture risk among older women.

cards.title: Akkermansia muciniphila alleviates osteoporosis by suppressing bone marrow adiposity through the gut microbiota-UDCA-TGR5 axis.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is characterized not only by progressive bone loss but also frequently by pathological bone marrow adiposity (BMA) expansion. Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK), implicated in lipid metabolic homeostasis, was previously found to be markedly depleted during estrogen deficiency-associated bone loss. However, whether AKK suppresses pathological BMA expansion and the corresponding receptor-mediated mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrated that AKK significantly attenuated bone loss and potently suppressed pathological BMA expansion in ovariectomized rats. Integrated untargeted metabolomics and targeted bile acid profiling revealed that AKK supplementation notably restored ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) levels in both serum and feces. Metagenomic analyses showed that AKK reshaped bile salt hydrolase (BSH)-related microbial functions, thereby promoting the intestinal deconjugation of tauroursodeoxycholic acid to generate UDCA. The enhanced UDCA-producing capacity of gut microbiota from the AKK-treated group was abolished by inhibition of microbial BSHs. Consistently, oral UDCA supplementation replenished circulating UDCA levels and reproduced the bone- and marrow-protective effects of AKK. In the host, elevated circulating UDCA activated TGR5-dependent TGF-β/SMAD2 signaling in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), thereby suppressing adipogenic differentiation and promoting osteogenesis. These effects were reversed by a TGR5 inhibitor and Tgfbr1 knockdown. Collectively, our study reveals a novel mechanism underlying the anti-osteoporotic effects of AKK, whereby AKK suppresses pathological BMA expansion through the gut microbiota-UDCA-TGR5 signaling axis. These findings provide a potential therapeutic strategy for osteoporosis and bone marrow lipid metabolic dysfunction.

cards.title: FABP3 regulates vascular remodeling and endothelial-mesenchymal transition through NF-κB activation in aged mice fed a high-fat diet.
cards.abstract: Aging and obesity synergistically promote pathological vascular remodeling mediated by endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT). Fatty acid-binding protein 3 (FABP3) maintains fatty acid homeostasis and cardiovascular function; however, its role in EndMT-driven vascular remodeling under combined aging and obesity remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate the regulatory mechanism of FABP3 in aging- and obesity-associated vascular remodeling. Young (6-week-old) and aged (18-month-old) C57BL/6J mice were fed normal chow or a 16-week high-fat diet (HFD). Carotid pathology, oxidative stress, inflammation, and EndMT were assessed via histological and immunostaining. Transcriptomic sequencing, qRT-PCR, and Western blotting were used to detect FABP3, NF-κB signaling, senescence, and EndMT markers. In vitro, palmitic acid (PA)-stimulated HUVECs with FABP3 knockdown, rhFABP3 rescue, or NF-κB inhibitor treatment were used for mechanistic validation. HFD induced body weight gain, increased epididymal fat mass, and elevated serum lipids, with more severe metabolic disorders in aged mice. Aging aggravated carotid intima-media thickening, fibrosis, lipid deposition, oxidative stress, and inflammatory infiltration; these abnormalities were further exacerbated by HFD. EndMT was activated in aged vasculature, with reduced endothelial markers (CD31, VE-cadherin) and elevated mesenchymal markers (α-SMA, TGF-β, COL1A1, N-cadherin). FABP3 and core NF-κB signaling components (NF-κB, p-NF-κB, IκBα, p-IκBα) were significantly upregulated in HFD-fed aged mouse carotids, paralleling EndMT severity. PA triggered HUVEC senescence and EndMT. FABP3 silencing or NF-κB inhibition alleviated these phenotypes, whereas rhFABP3 supplementation reversed the protective effects of FABP3 knockdown. This study demonstrated that FABP3 overexpression activates NF-κB signaling, aggravating endothelial inflammation, promoting abnormal EndMT, and accelerating vascular remodeling in aged obese mice. These findings provide novel mechanistic insights and potential therapeutic targets for aging- and obesity-related cardiovascular diseases.

cards.title: Gut microbiota-derived indole-3-propionic acid suppresses osteoclast formation by promoting IL-10+ Breg differentiation via AhR signaling.
cards.abstract: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites play pivotal roles in immune and bone homeostasis; however, the specific metabolites involved in postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the role of indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), a microbial metabolite of tryptophan, in estrogen deficiency-induced bone loss through integrated microbiome, metabolomic, and immunological analyses. Using 16S rRNA gene sequencing combined with targeted metabolomics, we identified significant alterations in gut microbial composition and dysregulation of tryptophan metabolism in ovariectomized (OVX) mice. Serum IPA levels were markedly reduced in both PMOP patients and OVX mice. IPA supplementation inhibited osteoclast differentiation, promoted osteoblast differentiation, improved trabecular microarchitecture, and increased bone mineral density (BMD), thereby alleviating OVX-induced osteoporosis. Mechanistically, IPA activated aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) signaling in B cells, promoting the differentiation of IL-10-producing regulatory B cells (Bregs) and enhancing IL-10 secretion, which in turn suppresses osteoclastogenesis. These effects were further confirmed by adoptive transfer experiments and pharmacological AhR inhibition. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the gut microbiota-derived metabolite IPA mitigates estrogen deficiency-associated osteoporosis by modulating immune-bone crosstalk, providing new mechanistic insights and a potential therapeutic strategy for PMOP.

cards.title: Predicting Military Training Outcome: A Prospective Cohort Study of Supervised Statistical Learning Classification Methods in British Army Recruits.
cards.abstract: Investigate predictors of failure and injury during British Army basic training and test the performance of statistical learning models to predict these outcomes. 968 male and 450 female recruits had demographics, lifestyle habits, mood, physical performance, body composition, micronutrient status, and bone metabolism measured at week 1 of training. Associations between predictors and training outcome (failure; lower limb overuse musculoskeletal injury) were assessed by logistic regression. Training outcome was predicted by logistic regression, elastic net, random forests, and gradient boosting. 66% of men and 76% of women passed with 20% and 34% developing an injury. For men, slower 2.4 km run time (odds ratio [OR]=1.004, p=0.011) and higher symptoms of depression (OR=1.173, p=0.001) were associated with higher risk of failing, and lower areal bone mineral density (OR=0.008, p=0.002), slower 2.4 km run time (OR=1.006, p=0.011), previous stress fracture (OR=3.267, p=0.002), lower parathyroid hormone (OR=0.783, p=0.009), and lower c-telopeptide cross-links of type I collagen (βCTX) (OR=0.255, p=0.041) were associated with higher risk of injury. For women, slower 2.4 km run time (OR=1.009, p=0.009) and higher total 25-hydroxyvitamin-D (OR=1.013, p=0.001) were associated with higher risk of failing, and slower 2.4 km run time (OR=1.007, p=0.009), higher alcohol intake (OR=1.006, p=0.017), and lower βCTX (OR=0.057, p=0.026) were associated with higher risk of injury. Training outcome was poorly predicted in men and women (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve≤0.68). All models had low sensitivity and high specificity, but application of an outcome-specific threshold determined using the Youden Index improved sensitivity. Interventions to improve military training outcome should address aerobic fitness prior to starting training. Prediction models may be useful in identifying some 'at-risk' recruits.

cards.title: Association between cognitive trajectories and subsequent hip fracture risk: a multinational prospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Using data from three nationally representative prospective cohorts, this study examined the association between cognitive trajectories and subsequent hip fracture risk. Moderate-decline and rapid-decline trajectories were significantly associated with higher fracture risk, highlighting that cognitive patterns may help identify hip fracture risk. Cognitive impairment is closely associated with hip fractures. However, evidence remains limited regarding whether cognitive trajectories influence hip fracture risk. This study investigated the association between cognitive trajectories and subsequent hip fracture risk. This study included 14,282 participants aged ≥ 45 years from three prospective cohorts in China, the United States, and the United Kingdom. The first three waves of each cohort were used to construct cognitive trajectories, while the subsequent two waves were used to assess hip fracture outcomes. The association between cognitive trajectories and the risk of hip fracture was assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression models. Participants were classified into three cognitive trajectories: high-stable (n = 8317, 58.2%), moderate-decline (n = 4725, 33.1%), and rapid-decline (n = 1240, 8.7%). In fully adjusted Cox models, relative to the high-stable trajectory, hip fracture risk was higher in participants following a moderate-decline trajectory (HR = 1.39, 95% CI: 1.05-1.84) and was further increased in those following a rapid-decline trajectory (HR = 1.86, 95% CI: 1.27-2.74). These associations remained robust in sensitivity analyses. Cognitive trajectories were related to subsequent hip fracture risk, particularly among individuals in the rapid-decline group. Early identification and targeted management of unfavorable cognitive trajectories may contribute to hip fracture prevention among middle-aged and older adults.

cards.title: Radiographic Accuracy of Identifying Anterolateral Tibial Plafond Involvement in Pronation External Rotation Ankle Fractures.
cards.abstract: To evaluate the rate of anterolateral tibial plafond involvement in pronation-external rotation (PER) ankle fractures and analyze the accuracy of radiographs, using CT as the reference standard among fractures with paired imaging, in detecting anterolateral tibial plafond involvement, impaction, and predicting surgeons' stated intent to pursue direct visualization and articular reduction, as determined by surgeon assessment of the imaging findings. Design: Multi-institutional retrospective chart review. Two level 1 trauma centers in the United States. Adult patients operative treated PER ankle fractures (AO/OTA 44C) from 2020-2022 and adequate preoperative radiographs, defined as an AP, mortise and lateral view of the injured ankle were included. A subset of these patients also had preoperative CT imaging of the injured ankle and were therefore evaluated with both imaging modalities. All images were reviewed by 4 fellowship-trained orthopaedic trauma surgeons. For this study, anterolateral tibial plafond involvement was defined as the presence of any fracture line or impaction involving the anterolateral plafond, and impaction (a subset of involvement) as where the anterolateral plafond was crushed and depressed. A finding was considered present if at least 3 of the 4 reviewers indicated its presents on first-round responses. The rates of involvement and impaction were determined among all fractures based on radiographs alone, and separately among the subset of patients with paired radiographs and CT. Using CT as the gold standard, we determined the accuracy of radiographs and compared surgeons' stated intent to pursue direct visualization and articular reduction of the anterolateral plafond fracture before versus after review of CT imaging. Eighty-three PER ankle fractures were included (mean age 43.3 years [range, 17-89]; 63.9% male), of which 37 also had CT scans (mean age 39.2 years [range, 17-83]; 73.0% male). Among all 83 fractures, anterolateral tibial plafond involvement and impaction were identified on radiographs in 14.5% and 4.8% of cases, respectively. Among the 37 PER ankle fractures with both plain radiographs and CT scans, anterolateral plafond involvement was identified in 13.5% of radiographs versus 37.8% of CT scans (p=0.346) and impaction in 5.4% of radiographs versus 8.1% of CT scans (p=0.005). The diagnosis of impaction using plain radiographs was correct in 66.7% of fractures compared with CT, resulting in a sensitivity of 67%, specificity of 100%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 100%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 97%. The diagnosis of anterolateral plafond involvement using plain radiographs had a sensitivity of 21%, specificity of 91%, PPV of 60%, and NPV of 66% compared with CT. Plain radiographs predicted surgeons' stated intent to pursue direct visualization and articular reduction in 66.7% of cases and had a PPV of 100% and NPV of 97%. In PER ankle fractures, the rates of anterolateral tibial plafond involvement and impaction were 37.8% and 8.1% on CT, respectively. Plain radiographs demonstrated high specificity but limited sensitivity for identifying both impaction (67%) and involvement (21%). Because anterolateral plafond impaction was relatively uncommon in PER fractures, a CT obtained for this purpose alone would yield a positive finding in only a minority of cases; nonetheless, CT should be considered for PER ankle fractures more broadly, given that plain radiographs miss a meaningful proportion of both involvement and impaction and interobserver reliability of radiograph-based assessment was poor. Prognostic level III.

cards.title: Cellular and Molecular Mechanisms of Wound Healing and Therapeutics Innovations.
cards.abstract: Chronic wounds are a significant and growing global clinical problem owing to increasing rates of diabetes, vascular diseases, ageing, and metabolic disorders. In contrast to acute wounds, which follow a coordinated sequence of haemostasis, inflammation, proliferation and remodelling, chronic wounds fail to progress through the healing process, leading to delayed or unfinished recovery. There is mounting evidence that this malfunction lies primarily in dysregulated intracellular signalling and is not necessarily in a lack of growth factors or cellular components. There is prolonged stimulation of pro-inflammatory pathways, disrupted angiogenic and regenerative signalling, excessive extracellular matrix degradation, cellular senescence and impaired immune resolution in chronic wound environments. The most important signalling networks, such as TGF-b/Smad, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, MAPK, NF-kB, Wnt/b-catenin, JAK/STAT, Hippo-YAP/TAZ, Notch, and hypoxia-inducible factor-1a, are crucial in the coordination of wound repair, but are functionally impaired in chronic pathological diseases. The pathways demonstrate a widespread crosstalk, forming a self-maintaining feedback loop that drives inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and a lack of cellular responsiveness. This review provides a detailed description of the physiology of normal wound healing, compares acute and chronic wound pathology, and critically discusses the molecular signalling defects that promote the persistence of chronic wounds. Additionally, it identifies emerging therapeutic approaches aimed at regulating dysregulated signalling networks, such as small-molecule modulators, biologics, biomaterials, gene- and cell-based therapies and exosome-mediated therapies.

cards.title: Proteomic Evaluation of the Progression from Acute Kidney Injury to Chronic Kidney Disease
cards.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are interconnected syndromes with substantial global burden, yet the molecular mechanisms driving the transition from acute injury to chronic fibrosis remain incompletely understood. We performed quantitative data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry (DIA-MS) proteomics on mouse models of AKI (ischemia-reperfusion injury) and CKD (unilateral ureteral obstruction), quantifying 5,985 protein groups. A conserved core injury response of 1,475 shared proteins (46%) was dominated by mitochondrial dysfunction, loss of solute transporters, and immune and extracellular matrix remodeling. AKI was marked by chromatin reorganization, DNA damage response, and acute inflammation, whereas CKD showed sustained fibrosis, complement activation, and coagulation. Peroxisomal proteins, including the {beta}-oxidation enzymes Acox1 and Ehhadh, were consistently down-regulated in both AKI and CKD, with no peroxisomal protein up-regulated. Both models also displayed a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-like signature, including Havcr1, Spp1, Igfbp7, Plau, and lysosomal cathepsins. We further identified 95 candidate progression markers, including Brat1 and Col3a1, 93 proteins with greater loss in CKD, 14 proteins changing in opposite directions, and seven disease-associated co-expression modules. These findings provide a proteomics resource for biomarker discovery and therapeutic targeting, including peroxisomal restoration and senolytic strategies, in AKI and CKD.

cards.title: Explainable AI to Guide the Design of Interpretable Prediction Models From High-Dimensional Data, Applied to Falls and Related Injuries in Adults Aged 50 Years or Older: Algorithm Development and Validation.
cards.abstract: Transparent prediction models, such as Cox regression, remain the standard for clinical risk prediction. However, they are challenging to design optimally by hand when tens or even hundreds of features require selection, transformation, or interaction modeling. While complex machine learning models offer high performance, their "black-box" nature limits the clinical trust, transparency, and interpretability required for decision-making. This study aimed to develop an explainable AI-based recommender that provides data-driven feature-related recommendations that, when incorporated, improve the predictive performance of existing interpretable statistical models on high-dimensional data, and to demonstrate it by developing and internally validating a Cox model for the 1-year risk of falls or related injuries (FRIs). We used linked primary and secondary care records from DataLoch (Lothian, Scotland) for adults aged 50 years or older registered with a contributing general practice between January 2015 and February 2020. The outcome was the first FRI within 1 year of the index date. A random survival forest was explained with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP), and its feature attributions were translated into recommendations for a Cox model: feature exclusions, nonlinear terms, and interactions. Data were split 80/20 into training and test sets. We compared the recommendations-augmented Cox model with the baseline Cox model, a Cox model with restricted cubic splines, and a penalized Cox model with all pairwise interactions. The metrics were Harrell concordance index (C-index), Uno C, calibration slope, and integrated Brier score. We repeated the analysis with all 409 available features and in 3 public datasets (German Breast Cancer Study Group 2 [GBSG2], AIDS Clinical Trial [ACT], and PeakVO2). Of 220,341 patients (mean age 64, SD 12 years), 8489 (3.85%) had an FRI within 1 year. From 59 candidate features, the recommender excluded 15 (8 medication classes and 7 comorbidities). The final model retained 44 predictors (demographic and lifestyle factors, frailty, 21 comorbidities, and 15 medication classes), with nonlinear terms for age, frailty, BMI, and area deprivation, and interactions of age with stroke, osteoporosis, loop diuretics, and frailty. The augmented model had a C-index of 0.719 (95% CI 0.708-0.731) compared with 0.715 (95% CI 0.702-0.727) for the baseline model (difference 0.004, 95% CI 0.001-0.007), with 70 vs 73 parameters, and similar calibration (slope 0.962 vs 0.961). With all 409 features, the recommender recommended 304 exclusions, 4 nonlinear terms, and 2 interactions. The augmented model had a C-index of 0.722 compared with 0.713, with 129 vs 423 parameters, and better calibration (slope 0.952 vs 0.846). The method also proved effective on 3 additional public datasets, demonstrating wider applicability. The proposed exploratory AI recommender demonstrates the potential of explainable AI to guide the design of transparent predictive models.

cards.title: NutriA-Senior, a Mobile App to Enhance Nutritional Awareness in Older Adults: Design and Pilot Usability Study.
cards.abstract: Mobile health is emerging as a ubiquitous paradigm for delivering health care interventions when self-management is feasible. However, interventions targeting older or frail participants should account for age-related cognitive, visual, and physical needs to optimize usability and long-term retention. This paper describes the rationale, design, and implementation of Nutritional App-Senior (NutriA-S), a theory-informed mobile app developed to enhance nutritional education in older adults with sarcopenia or probable sarcopenia. Moreover, we present the results of a usability study conducted in a cohort of age-matched healthy volunteers. NutriA-S was designed as a self-instructional app built on the Moodle e-learning platform. It includes 24 progression modules containing interactive quizzes and associated informational items aimed at engaging users by sustaining attention and improving nutritional knowledge. A 4-week pilot usability study was conducted with 35 healthy volunteers aged 65 to 85 years, recruited through flyers posted in 2 outpatient settings. After recruitment, participants used the app remotely at home with telemedicine-based monitoring and support. At the end of the study, usability was quantitatively assessed using the Italian version of the standard System Usability Scale (SUS) and the User Version of the Mobile Application Rating Scale (uMARS). The SUS questionnaire yielded a median total score of 80 out of 100 (IQR 55.00-92.50), indicating good perceived usability, with more than half of the participants rating the app as acceptable (above the threshold of 68). The overall median uMARS score was 4.083 (IQR 3.68-4.30), with the functionality and information domains achieving the highest median scores of 4.5 (with IQRs of 4.00-4.50 and 4.13-4.75, respectively), confirming that older adults perceived the tool as technically reliable and highly credible. This pilot usability study shows encouraging results, suggesting that NutriA-S is a highly usable, intuitive, and credible digital health tool for older adults. The identified limitations in items like customizability, willingness to pay, and willingness to use the app frequently, which received lower scores, will guide app refinements before deploying NutriA-S in an upcoming randomized controlled trial for older adults with sarcopenia or probable sarcopenia.

cards.title: Fracture risk in 85-year-old women: associations with volumetric bone mineral density, physical performance and falls.
cards.abstract: This prospective study demonstrates associations of volumetric BMD (vBMD) by pQCT, areal BMD (aBMD) by DXA, physical performance (one-leg balance, gait speed, and knee extension force), and fall history with fracture risk in 85-year-old women. A failed one-leg balance test was associated with both hip and any fracture independent of femoral neck aBMD. Total radial vBMD was associated with any fracture. Gait speed and previous falls showed associations with fracture risk of similar magnitude as femoral neck aBMD. These findings suggest that functional performance measures may enhance fracture risk assessment in older women. This prospective study evaluates associations between fracture risk and volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD) by peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT), physical performance tests, and fall history, in comparison with femoral neck areal BMD (aBMD) by DXA, in 85-year-old women. In the Osteoporosis Prospective Risk Assessment (OPRA) study, 382 women aged 85 years were followed for a mean of 4.3 years. Participants underwent pQCT of the radius and tibia and DXA of the hip and lumbar spine, performed physical performance tests (one-leg standing balance, considered failed if balance could not be maintained for 5 s; gait speed, analyzed continuously; and knee extension force, measured by isometric dynamometry), and reported fall history. Cox proportional hazards models estimated fracture risk, adjusting for BMI, previous fracture, smoking, and use of vitamin D, glucocorticoids, and bisphosphonates. During a mean follow-up of 4.3 years, 116 women (30%) sustained a fracture. Trabecular vBMD at the radius and tibia was associated with lower risk of any fracture (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.55-0.85 and HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55-0.86, respectively). Radial trabecular vBMD was also associated with lower hip fracture risk (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.42-0.98). Femoral neck aBMD was associated with lower risk of any fracture (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62-0.90), but not hip fracture (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.50-1.00). A failed balance test and low gait speed was associated with higher risk of any fracture (HR 1.55, 95% CI 1.04-2.29 and HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01-1.48, respectively). In multivariate analyses, a failed balance test remained associated with any fracture (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.12-2.56) and hip fracture (HR 2.30, 95% CI 1.05-5.02). Total radial vBMD remained associated with any fracture (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.996). Volumetric BMD by pQCT was associated with fracture risk independent of commonly recognized clinical risk factors in 85-year-old women. Physical performance tests were associated with fracture risk in unadjusted analyses, and the one-leg balance test additionally remained associated after adjustment for clinical risk factors and femoral neck aBMD.

cards.title: Surgical outcomes of single-stage posterior debridement combined with titanium mesh cage reconstruction and bone grafting for spinal infection after vertebral augmentation: a multicenter study.
cards.abstract: To investigate the surgical outcomes of single-stage posterior debridement combined with titanium mesh cage (TMC) reconstruction and bone grafting in the treatment of spinal infection following percutaneous vertebral augmentation (VA). A multicenter retrospective study was conducted, including patients who underwent surgery for spinal infection after percutaneous VA for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCF) between January 2018 and December 2023. All patients received single-stage posterior debridement, TMC reconstruction, and bone grafting. Operative duration, intraoperative blood loss, and clinical outcomes-including preoperative, immediate postoperative, and final follow-up visual analogue scale (VAS) scores, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), and local kyphotic Cobb angles-were recorded and analyzed. A total of 51 patients (17 male, 34 female; mean age: 68.35 ± 6.83 years) were enrolled, of whom 49 completed follow-up and were included in the final analysis; two patients died during follow-up and were treated as missing data. The average interval between VA and revision surgery was 7.51 ± 5.77 months. The preoperative American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) grade was C, D, and E in 2, 40, and 9 patients, respectively. The average operation time was 201.33 ± 84.38 min, with a mean intraoperative blood loss of 900.98 ± 507.99 mL. Pathogens were detected in 31 cases postoperatively. The mean follow-up duration was 19.65 ± 4.56 months. At the final follow-up of the 49 patients, VAS scores, ODI, and local Cobb angles significantly improved compared to preoperative values (P < 0.05). Bony fusion was achieved in 45 of the 49 patients (91.8%), with an average duration of 5.44 ± 1.18 months. Single-stage posterior debridement combined with TMC reconstruction and bone grafting was associated with favorable clinical and radiographic outcomes in patients with spinal infection following percutaneous VA.

cards.title: Environmental Chemical Exposures and Accelerated Epigenetic Aging: Links to Metabolic and Age-Related Health Outcomes
cards.abstract: Environmental chemical exposures may influence biological aging, but their relationships with epigenetic aging and related health outcomes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we evaluated the associations of 13 environmental exposures, including heavy metals, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), and volatile organic compounds (VOCs), with epigenetic aging in 666 older adults from the Forensic Research via Omics Markers in Environmental Health Vulnerable Areas (FROM) cohort. Among the evaluated epigenetic aging biomarkers, GrimAge acceleration showed the most prominent associations, with 2-hydroxyfluorene (2-HF), 2-naphthol (2-NAP), blood cadmium (bCd), and methylhippuric acid (MHA) exhibiting significant positive associations (strongest for 2-HF: beta = 0.491 years per doubling of exposure, P = 1.22 x 10-14). Quantile g-computation showed that combined environmental exposures were significantly associated with increased GrimAge acceleration (psi = 0.497, 95% CI: 0.013-0.981, P = 0.044), and Bayesian kernel machine regression identified 2-HF and 2-NAP as major contributors. Among clinical traits, white blood cell count (WBC) and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) were significantly and positively associated with GrimAge acceleration, and two-sample Mendelian randomization provided nominal support for a positive effect of GrimAge acceleration on GGT. Mediation analyses identified significant indirect effects through GrimAge acceleration for the associations of 2-HF, 2-NAP, bCd, and MHA with GGT. Exploratory disease analyses further suggested potential associations with diabetic nephropathy and osteoporosis, together with an inverse association with cardiac valvular disease. These findings suggest that environmental chemical exposures are associated with accelerated epigenetic aging, which may represent a biological pathway linking environmental exposures to metabolic and age-related health outcomes.

cards.title: Radial head injury and functional outcomes after adult Monteggia fracture dislocations.
cards.abstract: To evaluate radial head injury as a marker of functional recovery after adult Monteggia fracture-dislocations. Forty-four adults with ulnar fractures, documented proximal radioulnar joint disruption, and ≥ 6 months of follow-up were studied retrospectively. Whole-head non-reconstructability was distinguished from focal fragment excision. Exploratory Firth regression assessed fair/poor Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS < 75), adjusting for age. Postoperative events and subsequent unplanned surgical procedures were recorded. At median follow-up of 11 months, 32 patients (72.7%) achieved excellent/good MEPS. Fair/poor MEPS affected 7/14 patients with whole-head non-reconstructability versus 5/30 others (adjusted odds ratio 4.88; 95% confidence interval 1.08-27.50; p = 0.039). Ten patients had postoperative events and seven underwent reoperation. Restricting follow-up or broadening the injury definition yielded confidence intervals including the null. Following operative treatment of adult Monteggia fracture-dislocations with documented PRUJ disruption, whole-head non-reconstructability was associated with fair or poor MEPS outcomes in the primary exploratory analysis. The imprecision of this estimate and its sensitivity to injury definition and follow-up restriction limit its prognostic interpretation. Comprehensive assessment of Monteggia injury morphology and the postoperative course may inform individualized counseling. These findings do not establish a validated prognostic model or a causal adverse effect of radial head arthroplasty.

cards.title: Hydrogel-based local delivery of bacteriophages for infection control: a systematic review of in vivo evidence.
cards.abstract: Localized biofilm-associated infections remain difficult to treat with systemic antibiotics amid rising resistance. Hydrogel delivery may enhance bacteriophage (phage) therapy by protecting phages, prolonging residence, and enabling controlled release. This systematic review summarizes in vivo evidence for hydrogel-mediated phage delivery and its translational relevance. Following PRISMA 2020, PubMed, Web of Science were searched to 14 January 2026 using MeSH terms for bacteriophages, hydrogels/local delivery, and in vivo or clinical applications. Eligible studies reported original in vivo animal or human data; in vitro-only work was excluded. Nineteen studies met criteria: three clinical and sixteen preclinical. Clinical use included fracture-related infection, burn wound, and prosthetic joint infections treated with commercially available phage preparations in hydrogels. In a single compassionate-use fracture-related infection case managed with concurrent surgical debridement and systemic antibiotics, infection control without recurrence and good bone was were observed at one year; locally applied phages remained detectable for approximately 72 h, indicating in vivo release and surgical compatibility, although the independent contribution of the hydrogel-phage component could not be isolated. Preclinical studies tested 28 phages against six bacterial species via topical, injected, intraoperative, oral, or irrigation delivery. Consistent benefits occurred in burn wound infection (n = 6) and wound/soft-tissue infection models (n = 5) with lower bacterial load, improved healing, and increased survival in two burn wound infection studies. Bone/joint models (n = 4) showed partial reduction but inconsistent eradication. Other studies demonstrated ∼2000-fold pathogen reduction in colitis and decreased bacterial and inflammatory markers in endodontic infection. Hydrogel-based local phage therapy is a feasible strategy for infection control No major adverse effects were reported in the included studies, although safety reporting was limited. Standardized in vivo comparisons and clinical trials are needed to optimize delivery and dosing.

cards.title: Author Response: "Do PPIs Blunt the Treatment Effect of Romosozumab?".
cards.abstract: In response to the letter 'Do PPIs blunt the treatment effect of Romosozumab', we agree that PPI use is an important factor in taking care of osteoporosis patients, which is why we have reported on PPI use in our data. However, with only 11 PPI users in our cohort, the observed tendencies in aBMD gain are not conclusive and cannot be interpreted in either direction. In addition, we discuss the importance of a well-controlled calcium homeostasis in osteoporosis patients and do completely agree that PPI use should always be documented and taken into account in osteoporosis patients with and without anti-osteoporotic treatment as presented in our manuscript.

cards.title: DLAT/DLD-dependent cuproptosis disrupts osteoblast-macrophage crosstalk through mtDNA-associated STING signaling under delayed-healing-like inflammatory-hypoxic conditions.
cards.abstract: Impaired fracture repair is associated with sustained inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and disrupted osteoblast-macrophage communication. Cuproptosis involves copper-dependent aggregation of lipoylated mitochondrial proteins and loss of iron-sulfur proteins, suggesting a potential connection between mitochondrial injury and osteoimmune dysfunction. This study investigated this relationship in an in vitro inflammatory-hypoxic model. Human hFOB 1.19 osteoblasts and THP-1-derived macrophages were studied under delayed-healing-like stress (DHS; 1% O₂ with TNF-α/IL-1β). Elesclomol-Cu (ES-Cu) served as a mechanistic probe, while tetrathiomolybdate (TTM) and DLAT/DLD depletion were used to investigate copper-dependent injury. Assessments included copper accumulation, cuproptosis-associated markers, mitochondrial function, mtDNA abundance, and STING-associated signaling. Conditioned-medium transfer and three-dimensional fibrin co-culture examined inflammatory responses and osteogenic differentiation. DNase treatment and macrophage STING depletion assessed contributions from extracellular DNA and STING. DHS increased intracellular copper (P = 0.0009) and produced modest cuproptosis-associated changes, which were more pronounced following ES-Cu addition. TTM or DLAT/DLD depletion attenuated injury, mitochondrial dysfunction, and mtDNA accumulation. Conditioned medium from injured osteoblasts increased macrophage CD86 positivity and inflammatory cytokine secretion while reducing CD206 positivity. DNase treatment or macrophage STING depletion attenuated inflammatory responses. Macrophage-conditioned medium subsequently suppressed ALP activity, mineralization, and osteogenic gene expression in recipient osteoblasts. These endpoints improved following donor-cell interventions or macrophage STING depletion. Three-dimensional co-culture showed corresponding changes. The findings support a model linking experimentally induced copper-dependent osteoblast injury under DHS with mtDNA-associated STING signaling, macrophage inflammatory responses, and impaired osteogenic differentiation. They do not establish mtDNA-specific cGAS activation or cuproptosis-specific effects of DLAT/DLD depletion, and residual treatment carryover remains unresolved. Validation beyond these cell-line systems is required before extending the findings to clinical delayed fracture healing.

cards.title: Implementing a Group Education Model for People with Type 2 Diabetes in a Socioeconomically Deprived Primary Care Population: A Quality Improvement Report
cards.abstract: People with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) receiving injectable therapies require ongoing education and support to optimise self-management and glycaemic control. Group education may offer a cost-effective approach that combines professional guidance with peer support. Homewell Practice serves a socioeconomically deprived population in Hampshire with significant health inequalities. Many patients receiving insulin or GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy had poor glycaemic control, frailty, or increased risk of hospital admission. Traditional one-to-one consultations provided limited opportunities for peer learning and support. A 12-month quality improvement project was conducted between May 2022 and April 2023. Adults with T2DM receiving injectable therapy were invited to attend monthly community-based education sessions. Attendance data, HbA1c outcomes and patient feedback were collected and analysed descriptively. Patient-centred group sessions were delivered using adult-learning principles and peer discussion. Topics included insulin titration, hypoglycaemia management, nutrition, glycaemic targets and diabetes complications. Fifteen patients attended at least one session. Improvements in glycaemic control were associated with repeated attendance. Mean HbA1c reduction was 12.4% in patients attending four or more sessions, compared with 5.6% for those attending three sessions and 2.4% for those attending two sessions. Patients attending only one session demonstrated a 1.8% increase in HbA1c. All questionnaire respondents (9/9, 100%) reported improved understanding of diabetes and found the sessions useful; 8/9 would recommend the programme. Peer support was identified as the most valued aspect of participation. Attendance remained lower than anticipated, particularly among patients with multiple comorbidities and mental health needs. Group education for adults receiving injectable diabetes therapy was associated with high patient satisfaction and improved glycaemic outcomes among regular attendees. A hybrid model combining group education with individualised support may improve accessibility and engagement for higher-need patients.

cards.title: Association of sugar rationing during the first 1000 days with long-term risk of osteoporosis: A natural experiment study.
cards.abstract: The first 1000 days, from conception to approximately the second birthday, are important for skeletal development. We examined whether lower sugar availability during this period was associated with osteoporosis in adulthood. We studied 65,346 UK-born UK Biobank participants born between October 1951 and March 1956 (mean baseline age, 54.6 years; 55.9% women). Birth month defined four categories of early-life sugar rationing exposure: never exposed, in utero only, in utero plus up to 1year, and in utero plus up to 2 years. Cox models estimated associations with hospital-recorded incident osteoporosis. We also examined differences by sex and polygenic risk score (PRS) and tested alternative time scales. During a median 13.8 years of follow-up, 1606 incident cases occurred. Compared with never exposed participants, fully adjusted hazard ratios were 0.94 (95% CI, 0.80-1.11), 0.78 (0.66-0.93), and 0.77 (0.63-0.95) across the three progressively longer exposure categories (P for trend=0.006). We found no evidence of interaction with sex (P=0.385) or PRS tertile (P=0.816). When attained age was the time scale, the estimate for the longest exposure was 0.93 (0.81-1.06). Sugar rationing exposure extending into infancy was associated with a lower hazard of adult osteoporosis in the primary analysis. The association weakened when attained age was the time scale, limiting causal interpretation. We found no evidence of greater benefit among participants with higher genetic risk.

cards.title: MRI-derived OsteoSarcoScore (OSS): a composite bone-muscle quality indicator associated with prevalent vertebral fracture in postmenopausal women.
cards.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers detailed visualization of vertebral and paravertebral anatomy, enabling direct assessment of pathophysiological conditions. This study aims to introduce OsteoSarcoScore (OSS), an MRI-derived bone-muscle quality measure, to assess vertebral fracture risk. This retrospective study included 234 postmenopausal women (mean age: 66.94 ± 8.87 years) who underwent both MRI and QCT. For muscle quality, the psoas-muscle (PM-Score), multifidus-erector-muscles (MF-Score), and MyoScore (PM-Score + MF-Score) were defined as muscles' signal intensities (SIs) at the L2/3‒L4/5 levels divided by subcutaneous fat SIs. For bone quality, the F-score and vertebral bone quality (VBQ) were defined as the median L1‒L4-5 vertebrae SIs, normalized to relevant controls. The OSS was derived as composite of F-Score-MyoScore and compared with VBQ-MyoScore. Analyses included ANOVA with post hoc correction, DeLong's test for ROC comparison, and multivariable logistic regression with standardized predictors (odds ratios for OSS per 1-SD). Primary models adjusted for age, BMI, vendor, and field strength, with additional adjustment for vBMD; propensity score matching served as a secondary analysis. Incremental value beyond vBMD was assessed by ∆AUC, continuous NRI/IDI, and decision-curve analysis. Reliability was assessed by ICC for scores and Cohen's kappa for fractures. Among osteoporotic patients, MyoScore, VBQ‑MyoScore, and OSS were higher by 3.9%, 10.1%, and 10.2%, respectively, than in non‑osteoporotic patients. In fractured patients, OSS, MyoScore, and VBQ‑MyoScore showed an increase of 136.1%, 132.5%, 132.5%, respectively, compared to non‑fractured patients. Also, OSS was significantly higher in the fracture group (Mann-Whitney U test, p < 0.001). Muscles scores weakly correlated with patient age with r = 0.22‒0.23, (all p = 0.001). In osteoporosis, higher AUCs favored bone quality scores (F-score = 0.72 and VBQ = 0.69) than PM-Score and MF-Score (0.54‒0.56). In patients with fractures, OSS and QCT-vBMD did not differ significantly in diagnostic performance (AUC: 0.681 vs. 0.725; DeLong z = - 0.95, p = 0.341). Adding OSS to a base model of age, BMI, vBMD, vendor, and field strength significantly improved discrimination (∆AUC = 0.044, 95% CI 0.004-0.084, p = 0.033; NRI = 0.61; IDI = 0.079). OSS remained significantly associated with fracture after adjustment for scanner vendor and field strength (OR per 1-SD = 2.36, 95% CI 1.58-3.52, p < 0.001). OsteoSarcoScore, a composite biomarker integrating bone and muscle quality, showed discriminatory ability for vertebral fracture that did not differ significantly from that of QCT-vBMD, highlighting the potential of combined bone‒muscle assessment for fracture risk evaluation; however, further validation is warranted.

cards.title: Pathological Ossification of Spinal Ligament-Derived Fibroblasts in an Inflammatory Micro-Environment via Activation of the ECM/ITGA5/FAK/AKT Pathway in Ankylosing Spondylitis.
cards.abstract: Chronic inflammation and heterotopic ossification (HO) were typical hallmarks of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Although existing target inflammation inhibitors could reduce inflammation but failed to halt HO progression, highlighting the need for osteogenesis-specific treatments. However, the role of fibroblasts (Fbs) responsible for extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling in AS-associated pathological ossification remained unclear. In this study, osteogenic capacity, pathological condition and underlying molecular pathways for Fbs derived from AS spinal ligaments were validated. Fbs from uncalcified spinal ligaments of age-matched AS patients/controls were compared. AS-Fbs were treated with a gradient concentration of TNF-α during osteogenic induction. Meanwhile, specific inhibition of AKT phosphorylation was applied to confirm the role of PI3K/AKT in osteogenesis. Upstream signalling pathways were also explored via RNA-sequencing. Additionally, in vivo, subcutaneous cell transplantation was performed to simulate ectopic ossification. AS-Fbs possessed superior osteogenic capacity than controls. Moreover, osteogenic signs could be promoted by low concentration TNF-α-induced inflammatory micro-environment. Functional analysis revealed a crucial role of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Mechanistically, RNA-seq identified the ECM/integrin subunit alpha 5 (ITGA5)/focal adhesion kinase (FAK) upstream pathway. In detail, osteogenic induction increased ECM protein levels including thrombospondin-1 (THBS1) and fibulin-1 (FBLN1), activating ITGA5, subsequent FAK phosphorylation, osteogenic markers expression and eventually inducing Fb-to-osteocyte differentiation. ITGA5 knockdown or specific FAK inhibition attenuated osteogenic phenotypes and reduced osteogenic proteins expression. Regarding in vivo experiments, subcutaneous bone-like tissue formation derived from transplantation of AS-Fbs was identified and could be suppressed significantly via the AKT phosphorylation inhibition. In conclusion, the findings of this study revealed potential causes for HO progression derived from AS-Fbs in spite of effective anti-inflammation therapy. Furthermore, the crucial role of ECM/ITGA5/FAK/AKT axial signalling pathways in the aberrant osteogenesis of AS-Fbs was identified. Combined targeted intervention at the aforementioned signals and application of anti-inflammatory agents might be a novel potential strategy for the treatment of pathological ectopic ossification caused by AS.

cards.title: Opportunistic Computed Tomography-Derived Psoas Muscle Attenuation is Independently Associated With Achievement of Substantial Clinical Benefit After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
cards.abstract: Preoperative computed tomography (CT) obtained for surgical planning may provide clinically relevant information beyond anatomical assessment. We investigated whether opportunistically assessed CT-derived psoas muscle attenuation was associated with achievement of substantial clinical benefit (SCB) after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and examined its relationships with frailty and nutritional status. This retrospective cohort study included 280 patients who underwent primary THA for hip osteoarthritis. Psoas muscle attenuation was measured on preoperative CT images at the mid-vertebral level of L3. Frailty was assessed using the Clinical Frailty Scale and nutritional status using the Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score. The primary outcome was achievement of SCB at 24 months, defined as a ≥ 22-point improvement in the Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with SCB achievement, and restricted cubic spline analysis evaluated potential nonlinear associations. Model discrimination and calibration were also assessed for clinical and expanded models. The SCB was achieved in 184 patients (66%). Higher preoperative psoas muscle attenuation was independently associated with greater odds of achieving SCB (odds ratio 1.25 per 5-HU increase, 95% confidence interval 1.02 to 1.55; P = 0.031). Lower attenuation was associated with greater frailty, poorer nutritional status, and lower rates of SCB achievement (all trend P < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a nonlinear association between muscle attenuation and the probability of achieving SCB (P for nonlinearity = 0.021). Adding psoas muscle attenuation to the clinical model produced only a small, nonsignificant increase in receiver operating characteristic curve (0.711 to 0.732; P = 0.209). Preoperative CT-derived psoas muscle attenuation was independently associated with achievement of SCB after THA. Opportunistic assessment of psoas muscle attenuation from CT images already obtained for surgical planning may provide complementary information for preoperative assessment.

cards.title: Prevalence, clinical implications and prognostic impact of frailty and other geriatric conditions in patients with transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
cards.abstract: Frailty in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) remains poorly characterized. The aim of this study was to analyze the prevalence and prognostic influence of frailty and other geriatric conditions such as nutritional risk, cognitive status, depression, and dependence in patients with ATTR-CM. We performed an observational, prospective, single-center study of 110 ATTR-CM patients who underwent comprehensive geriatric assessment from October 2024 to April 2025 and were followed up to September 2026. Study endpoints were all-cause death and the combined event of all-cause death or worsening heart failure. Outcomes were assessed by the Kaplan-Meier method and multivariable Cox regression. The prevalence of frailty, based on 4 different criteria, varied from 32.7% to 62.7%. Dependence, depression, nutritional risk, and cognitive impairment were detected in up to 70.9%, 29.1%, 27.3%, and 15.5% of patients, respectively. Frailty, defined as a Clinical Frailty Scale > 4, a Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe-Frailty Instrument > 2, or a Short Physical Performance Battery < 10, was independently associated with an increased risk of both study outcomes. Dependence (Katz index < 6) and cognitive impairment (Mini Examen Cognitivo score < 23) were also independent predictors of both outcomes. Frailty diagnosis showed incremental prognostic value when added to United Kingdom National Amyloidosis Centre stages. Frailty is frequent in patients with ATTR-CM and is associated with impaired clinical outcomes.

cards.title: Bidirectional frailty transitions in community-dwelling older adults: longitudinal findings from the Queenstown cohort.
cards.abstract: Frailty in older adults is dynamic and shaped by clinical, functional, and social factors, yet longitudinal transitions in community populations are not well characterised. We examined one-year changes in frailty and identified factors associated with improvement and progression. We performed a longitudinal analysis of community-dwelling adults aged ≥65 years from the population-based Queenstown Health District cohort. Baseline (Wave 1, 2023-2024) demographic, clinical, and lifestyle data were collected, with reassessment at one year (Wave 2). Frailty was measured using the Clinical Frailty Scale. Ordinal logistic regression modelled overall direction of frailty transition, while multinomial logistic regression identified factors associated with improvement or worsening relative to stability. Alluvial plots illustrated transitions across frailty states over time. Among 1,153 participants (mean age 74.5 ± 6.6 years; 55.8% female), frailty remained stable in 627 (54.4%), improved in 211 (18.3%), and worsened in 315 (27.3%) over one year. Visualisation demonstrated predominant stability with bidirectional movement between frailty categories. In ordinal analyses, diabetes (OR 1.39, 95% CI 1.06-1.83), smoking (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.19-3.03), and iADL impairment (OR 1.56, 95% CI 1.01-2.41) were associated with worsening, while higher physical activity was protective (OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51-0.98). Multinomial models showed stroke history associated with improvement (OR 4.23, 95% CI 1.46-12.25), whereas iADL impairment reduced the likelihood of improvement (OR 0.48, 95% CI 0.28-0.82). Frailty was largely stable but exhibited meaningful bidirectional transitions. Functional impairment and modifiable behaviours were key predictors, underscoring the importance of repeated assessment and function-focused prevention to mitigate frailty progression.

cards.title: Inherited cardiovascular risk and its impact on healthspan and lifespan.
cards.abstract: Genetic disposition for cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major determinant of aging-related traits, such as healthspan, dementia, and frailty. While rare monogenic disorders provide important mechanistic insights, most CVDs and aging-related traits are driven by the cumulative effects of numerous common genetic variants, resulting in a polygenic risk architecture. Analyses of genes and pathways affected by these variants revealed significant correlations in the genetic architectures of CVD and aging, which appear to promote each other bidirectionally. Thus, CVD and aging share common genetic mechanisms, linking inherited cardiovascular risk to frailty, dementia, reduced healthspan, and shortened lifespan-and, conversely, explaining why aging is the strongest risk factor for atherosclerosis. Advances in genome-wide association studies have also enabled the construction of a polygenic risk score (PRS), which quantifies inherited CVD risk and facilitates early risk stratification beyond conventional clinical assessment. Importantly, individuals at high polygenic risk for CVD derive greater benefit from preventive strategies, which reduce their lifelong burden of CVD risk and ultimately promote healthy aging. Therefore, personalizing clinical risk assessment by integrating genetic testing for both CVD and aging-related traits may be of clinical importance. Specifically, lifestyle modification and preventive therapies based not only on conventional risk assessment, but also on polygenic risks may offer an individualized life-course approach for precision prevention, shifting cardiovascular care from reactive disease management toward the promotion of healthy aging.

cards.title: Fracture Liaison Services in Switzerland: current status and challenges.
cards.abstract: Switzerland is one of the very high-risk countries for osteoporosis. The Fracture Liaison Service is the internationally endorsed model for secondary fracture prevention and for reducing mortality after a person has sustained a fragility fracture. In this article, we describe current Fracture Liaison Service coverage and structure in Switzerland and the challenges Fracture Liaison Services are facing. Good interdisciplinary cooperation, especially with general practitioners, is a key factor. Artificial intelligence (AI) for the detection of vertebral fractures, shared electronic medical records, digital platforms and telemedicine are emerging and evolving approaches to overcome the existing barriers to osteoporosis treatment.

cards.title: In Vitro Blood Clot Mechanical Properties are Associated with Fibrinogen and White Blood Cell Subtypes in Addition to Hematocrit and Sex.
cards.abstract: Understanding the role of blood composition in clot mechanics may provide critical cues toward their diagnosis and treatment. To this end, we previously showed that sex and standard blood composition measures explain some variability in clot mechanics, but much remains unaccounted for. Ours and others' studies largely ignored the roles of fibrinogen and white blood cell (WBC) subtypes, which is surprising given their physiological importance. To develop a more complete understanding of what influences clots' mechanical properties, we now study the role of fibrinogen levels and WBC subtypes in addition to sex and standard blood composition measures. We drew blood from healthy young adults and prepared in vitro clot samples. Using pure shear and mode-I fracture tests, we measured clots' stiffness, fracture toughness, strength, and work to rupture. We then used linear regression to assess associations between blood composition and clot mechanical properties, reporting R 2 to describe the strength of these associations. Fibrinogen shows the strongest associations with clot mechanical properties, positively correlating with all four metrics and achieving the highest average R 2 . For example, fibrinogen is associated with 70% of the variance in stiffness and 78% in fracture toughness. Among WBC subtypes, neutrophils positively correlate with strength and work to rupture, whereas eosinophils negatively correlate with strength. Our work identifies strong associations between fibrinogen levels and WBC subtypes and in vitro clot mechanical properties, relationships that were largely unexplored in whole blood. Future studies should connect these findings to in vivo clot behavior and clinical outcomes.

cards.title: [Conservative treatment of non-unions : Options and limitations].
cards.abstract: Despite modern medical care, non-unions occur in 2-5% of all fractures. The burden on patients involves prolonged rehabilitation and potentially further surgery. Costs for healthcare systems increase substantially. While surgical intervention represents the standard of care, a range of non-surgical treatment options is available. A particular advantage of non-surgical treatment is the avoidance of surgery itself. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound therapy (LIPUS) and the use of pulsed electromagnetic fields (PEMF) are painless and applied by patients themselves once daily. With focused extracorporeal shockwave therapy (ESWT), administration by a physician-usually under general anesthesia-ensures the treatment takes effect precisely at the target site. Bony defects up to 5-10 mm in size can be treated without surgery, provided there is no infection and mechanical stability is adequate.
