cards.title: Is a Higher Modified Frailty Index Associated with Increased Complications in Breast Reduction? A Single Center Retrospective Analysis of 1716 Patients.
cards.abstract: Macromastia is associated with significant physical symptoms and reduced quality of life. Although reduction mammaplasty is an effective, the role of frailty in predicting postoperative complications remains uncertain. To evaluate whether the five-factor modified Frailty Index (mFI-5) predicts postoperative complications following reduction mammaplasty, and to identify independent risk factors. This retrospective cohort study included 1,716 consecutive female patients who underwent bilateral breast reduction at a single center (2005-2024). Patients were stratified into low (mFI-5 ≤1, n=1,589) and high (mFI-5 ≥2, n=127) frailty groups. The primary outcome was any postoperative complication within 30 days. Secondary outcome were specific complications requiring surgical intervention. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors. High frailty patients were older, had higher BMI, and more comorbidities. High frailty group had significantly higher overall complication rates (22.2% vs. 14.9%; p=0.031), including wound dehiscence, hemorrhage requiring transfusion, and nipple-areola complex necrosis. However, mFI-5 was not an independent predictor of complications (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.62-2.33; p=0.588). Higher BMI (OR 1.09; p=0.007) and active smoking (OR 1.68; p=0.008) were the only independent predictors identified. The mFI-5 was associated with postoperative complications in unadjusted analysis, but this association was substantially explained by the higher prevalence of obesity and smoking in the high-frailty group and did not persist after multivariable adjustment. BMI and smoking remain the principal modifiable risk factors for preoperative optimization, supporting the need for more comprehensive frailty assessment tools in future studies.

cards.title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence and Markers of Healthy Aging: A Systematic Review of Biological and Functional Outcomes.
cards.abstract: Aging involves molecular, cellular, and functional changes that increase vulnerability to chronic disease, cognitive decline, frailty, and loss of independence. Mediterranean-style dietary patterns are generally rich in plant foods, unsaturated fats, fiber, and bioactive compounds, but their composition varies across studies and may include modified or multicomponent interventions. This Systematic Review evaluated associations between Mediterranean-style dietary adherence and related interventions and markers of healthy aging, including biological aging biomarkers, cognition, frailty, physical performance, and overall health status. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published during 2013- 2025. Searches were conducted in April 2025 and updated in August 2025. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251107773). Randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies in adults were eligible if they assessed Mediterranean-style dietary patterns or interventions and reported aging-related biomarkers or functional outcomes. Two reviewers independently conducted study selection and data extraction. Eleven studies were included: 5 RCTs, 4 prospective cohort studies, and 2 cross-sectional studies. Greater adherence was associated with better cognitive performance and slower memory decline in some studies. Favorable findings were also reported for telomere dynamics, epigenetic age, and inflammatory biomarkers. Improvements in frailty and physical performance were mainly observed in interventions combining dietary modification with physical activity. Heterogeneity in dietary definitions, adherence measures, intervention components, and outcomes precluded meta-analysis. The evidence suggests that favorable associations exist between Mediterranean-style dietary patterns and selected markers of healthy aging but does not establish uniform or causal effects. Interpretation is limited by methodological heterogeneity, self-reported dietary exposure, and the inclusion of modified or multicomponent interventions. Long-term studies using standardized dietary definitions, harmonized outcomes, objective adherence measures, and designs capable of isolating diet-specific effects are needed. PROSPERO registration No. [https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251107773].

cards.title: Critical Validation of Deep Learning-Based Cervical Vertebral Fracture Detection on Computed Tomography Localizer Radiographs.
cards.abstract: Localizer radiographs are low-resolution two-dimensional overview images acquired prior to computed tomography (CT) scans. Their automated analysis could support the early detection of cervical vertebral fractures in trauma patients and thus enable immediate adjustment of imaging protocols. This study investigated to what extent deep learning-based methods can reliably detect such fractures on localizer radiographs, with a focus on critically validating model behavior beyond standard performance metrics. On a custom-annotated dataset of 346 trauma patients, two approaches were compared: a full-image binary classification and a two-step pipeline that first localizes the cervical spine and then classifies the cropped region. Model validity was assessed through a permutation test, occlusion testing, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, an analysis of potential confounders, and a subgroup analysis by anatomical fracture location. The full-image classifier formally achieved the highest test-set performance with a precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) of 0.477, compared with 0.349 for the cervical-spine-level classifier. Our validity analysis indicates that the full-image classifier does not primarily rely on the fracture region itself, rendering it unsuitable for clinical use. This work therefore presents a case study of shortcut learning and illustrates validation methods that may be of value for comparable studies on small datasets with visually subtle targets.

cards.title: From Hunterian to Hunterian: the posterior malleolar fracture.
cards.abstract: The posterior malleolar fracture (PMF) is now understood through three-dimensional imaging and mechanism-based classification, yet this understanding is not new. We argue that its central mechanism (rotation of an axially loaded talus within the ankle mortise) was inferred by Bonnin three-quarters of a century ago, obscured by an era of radiographic, size-based description, and later confirmed and made visible by computed tomography (CT). This continuity is frequently overlooked in the wider literature. We present a narrative review of the primary historical literature alongside contemporary CT-based and cadaveric studies. Bonnin's cadaveric experiments showed that a rotating, axially loaded talus behaves as a wedge within the mortise, splitting the posterior tibial margin (the injury we now term a rotational pilon fracture) and he held that damage to the plafond, not the size of the fragment, determined the prognosis. Attention later shifted to the proportion of articular surface involved - a quantity poorly measured on radiographs and divorced from mechanism. CT has since reintroduced the mechanism in living patients: the Mason-Molloy classification describes three pathomechanical types that confirm and refine Bonnin's observations, and management has moved from size thresholds to classification-guided fixation. Bonnin and Mason, two Hunterian Professors separated by more than half a century, performed essentially the same investigation with the tools available to them and reached the same conclusion. Recognising that the modern classification visualises a mechanism Bonnin had already inferred (rotation of a loaded talus) restores a continuity the wider literature has largely missed.

cards.title: Unraveling the Pathogenesis of Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw.
cards.abstract: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a serious complication associated with bone-modifying and antiangiogenic therapies. As the use of these agents expands in osteoporosis management and cancer care, the population at risk of MRONJ is increasing. Despite its substantial clinical burden, effective prevention and treatment remain limited by an incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis and of the biological features that may confer susceptibility to the jaws. This review critically synthesizes current evidence across five potentially interacting pathogenic domains: impaired bone remodeling, compromised vascular and lymphatic support, impaired oral soft-tissue healing, microbial dysbiosis and biofilm formation, and immune dysregulation. Systemic comorbidities and concomitant therapies are also considered as potential modifiers of disease susceptibility and clinical course. In addition, we examine jaw-specific susceptibility by integrating evidence from developmental biology, comparative anatomy, cellular pharmacology, and local osteoimmune biology. Together, these observations support a multifactorial model of MRONJ in which drug-specific effects interact with local tissue characteristics and host factors, while the temporal sequence and relative contribution of individual mechanisms remain incompletely defined. A more precise understanding of these interactions may improve risk stratification and inform future preventive and therapeutic strategies.

cards.title: Perioperative Single-Shot Regional Blocks and Associated Rebound Pain-Related Unscheduled Utilization of Health Care After Distal Radius Surgery.
cards.abstract: Perioperative single-shot regional blocks are commonly used for pain control in outpatient distal radius fixation surgery. While regional blocks provide initial postoperative pain control, patients often experience significant rebound pain as the block effect dissipates, which can lead to utilization of unscheduled health care (emergency department visits, phone calls, and messages sent via the electronic health record [EHR] to providers). We hypothesized that patients who received perioperative blocks are more likely to use unscheduled health care versus those who did not. A total of 619 patients underwent distal radius fracture fixation at a tertiary care academic center from 2013 to 2022. After excluding minors, inpatient and revision procedures, patients with insufficient records, and fixation of an impending pathologic fracture, 417 patients were included. Age, gender, mechanism, time to surgery, use of intraoperative local anesthetic, and whether a regional block was performed were collected. Returns to the emergency department, pain-related phone calls, and messages sent via the EHR system within 3 days of surgery were also collected. The adjusted relative risk of using unscheduled health care for pain was 4.0 (95% CI, 1.3-12.1; P = .01) on postoperative day 1 for patients who received perioperative blocks compared with those who did not. Similarly, the adjusted relative risk within 2 days of surgery was 3.9 (95% CI, 1.4-10.5; P = .007) and within 3 days was 3.2 (95% CI, 1.4-7.5; P = .008). Patients who receive perioperative regional blocks after distal radius fixation are more likely to use unscheduled health care within the first 3 days of surgery, compared with patients who did not receive blocks.

cards.title: Integrated multi-omics network by physical exercise across aging: molecular adaptation beyond single signaling pathways
cards.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive molecular dysregulation across interconnected biological systems, involving alterations in epigenetic regulation, gene expression, protein homeostasis, and metabolic function. Although physical exercise is widely recognized as one of the most effective nonpharmacological interventions to promote healthy aging, the integrative molecular mechanisms underlying its systemic effects remain incompletely understood. This review proposes a multi-omic framework in which exercise acts as a coordinated biological stimulus capable of remodeling age-associated molecular dysfunction across genomic, epigenomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic layers. We discuss evidence showing that exercise modulates DNA methylation patterns associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, and tissue regeneration. Epigenetically, exercise is associated with attenuation of age-associated hypermethylation in promoter regions and modulation of genes involved in oxidative stress defense and tissue regeneration. Transcriptomic studies further show that exercise is associated with more youthful expression patterns while attenuating inflammatory and senescence-related gene programs. Proteomic studies reveal that training is associated with mitochondrial metabolism, extracellular matrix remodeling, and muscle contractile protein abundance, reducing proteostatic dysfunction. Metabolomic analyses demonstrate that exercise improves metabolic flexibility and remodels cellular energy networks. Importantly, the unique contribution of this review lies in synthesizing emerging evidence that these adaptations are highly cell- and tissue-specific, involving immune cells, skeletal muscle satellite cells, endothelial cells, microglia, and intestinal stem cells. Rather than acting through isolated pathways, exercise may induce convergent adaptations across interconnected molecular systems, supporting the concept that healthy aging is dynamically regulated and that age-associated molecular dysfunction retains a degree of biological plasticity.

cards.title: Stochastic failure accumulation as a foundation for exponential mortality and selective disappearance
cards.abstract: Most organisms become increasingly likely to die as they grow older, a phenomenon known as demographic senescence. We develop a general mathematical framework for modelling senescence in which individuals are viewed as comprising a fixed number of interacting intra-organismal sub-systems, each characterised by stochastic failure and repair rates. In many organisms, `failure begets failure' because sub-systems are typically interdependent. We use diffusion approximations to derive an expression for population-level mortality curves in this setting, and demonstrate that greater interdependence leads to faster rates of senescence. Since individuals who die can no longer age, observed cohorts become increasingly composed of `lucky' individuals that avoided death by (stochastically) taking paths in failure space associated with lower mortality despite no intrinsic differences in their quality. Selective disappearance of `unlucky' individuals generates deviations of population-level measurements from individual-level trajectories, causing late-life mortality plateaus. We show that while these deviations must always exist, they may often be too small to detect, either because the failure accumulation process is stereotyped or because detection requires unreasonably large cohort sizes. We provide necessary and asymptotically sufficient conditions for Gompertz-Makeham mortality in our framework, with falsifiable predictions in terms of a scaling law for mortality near complete failure. We also show that the simplest null model in our framework leads to exact Gompertz-Makeham curves. Our work establishes a general framework for modelling demographic senescence and selective disappearance from biological first principles, and provides concrete predictions for when Gompertz-Makeham mortality emerges in such models.

cards.title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
cards.abstract: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength. Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Cross-sectional. Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728). CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3). Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis. Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated. Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women. In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

cards.title: Yi-Qi-Jian-Pi formula alleviates hepatic fibrosis in acute-on-chronic liver failure by regulating ferritinophagy-mediated hepatic stellate cell senescence.
cards.abstract: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) represents a severe clinical syndrome characterized by rapid exacerbation of chronic hepatic disease. Liver fibrosis (LF) significantly contributes to the advancement of ACLF pathology. The traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) preparation Yi-Qi-Jian-Pi formula (YQJPF) exhibits promising therapeutic effects on ACLF and LF; however, the underlying pharmacological mechanisms and active components remain incompletely understood. This study seeks to elucidate the pharmacodynamic properties, active constituents, and underlying mechanisms of YQJPF in treating liver fibrosis within an ACLF rat model, focusing specifically on ferritinophagy activation and the induction of hepatic stellate cell (HSC) senescence. A rat model of ACLF was induced via combined administration of CCl4 and LPS/D-GalN, and an in vitro model was established using human hepatic stellate cells (LX2). Liver-targeted active components were characterized using UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS analysis, with network pharmacology utilized to predict critical molecular targets. NCOA4 siRNA and ferrostatin-1 were used to validate mechanism specificity. The therapeutic effects and associated mechanisms were systematically evaluated through biochemical assays, histopathological examinations, and molecular and cellular analyses. YQJPF improved liver histopathology and attenuated fibrosis and ACLF in rats. It inhibited viability and proliferation of LX2 cells, decreased TGF-β1 secretion, and downregulated α-SMA and Collagen I expression. UHPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS identified 82 liver-tropic components (including 50 prototypes and 32 metabolites) in rat liver tissues. Network pharmacology revealed 257 potential targets, with 135 overlapping with hepatic fibrosis-related targets (core targets included TP53, NCOA4, and CDKN2A). YQJPF induced HSC senescence (upregulated p16, p21, and HMGA1; downregulated TERT; triggered cell cycle arrest) and activated ferritinophagy (upregulated NCOA4, Beclin1, LC3BII/I; downregulated FTH1 and p62; increased ROS/iron accumulation). NCOA4 knockdown or Fer-1 treatment reduced YQJPF-induced HSC senescence and antifibrotic effects. YQJPF reduces ACLF-related LF by NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy, which promotes HSC senescence. The 82 liver-tropic components and 135 overlapping targets highlight its multi-component, multi-target effects, providing a scientific foundation for its clinical application.

cards.title: 4'-Hydroxywogonin Attenuates Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression by Suppressing Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT Signaling.
cards.abstract: 4'-Hydroxywogonin, a bioactive flavonoid derived from Scutellaria baicalensis, has reported anti-inflammatory and anticancer activities; however, its therapeutic potential and molecular mechanism in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain unclear. This study investigated the anti-tumor effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin and its regulatory role in Gas6/Axl-associated signaling. Human HCC cells were used to evaluate proliferation, migration, invasion, cell cycle distribution, apoptosis, senescence, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Whole-transcriptome sequencing, western blotting, quantitative polymerase chain reaction, molecular docking, and thermal shift analysis were performed to explore the underlying mechanism, and antitumor efficacy and safety were further examined in a mouse xenograft model. 4'-Hydroxywogonin significantly inhibited HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inducing G1-phase arrest, apoptosis, and senescence. Transcriptomic and molecular analyses identified Axl as a key affected target. 4'-Hydroxywogonin reduced Gas6 and Axl expression, suppressed PI3K/AKT activation, and downregulated cell cycle and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related proteins. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between 4'-hydroxywogonin and Axl, which was supported by thermal shift analysis. Axl overexpression partially rescued the inhibitory effects of 4'-hydroxywogonin, suggesting involvement of Axl-dependent and additional pathways. In vivo, 4'-hydroxywogonin markedly reduced tumor growth with efficacy comparable to sorafenib and without evident hepatotoxicity. These findings indicate that 4'-hydroxywogonin suppresses HCC progression, at least in part, through inhibition of the Gas6/Axl-PI3K/AKT signaling axis, supporting its further development as a natural therapeutic candidate.

cards.title: Editorial Commentary: Arthroscopic Bony Bankart Fixation Stands the Test of Time-Preserve Native Glenoid Anatomy When You Can!
cards.abstract: Bony Bankart lesions provide an opportunity to restore native glenoid anatomy through direct fragment fixation. Arthroscopic bony Bankart repair can provide long-term shoulder stability, high patient satisfaction, and sustained participation in sport. Although we prefer double-row bridge fixation for its broad compression across the fracture bed, rotational control, and biomechanically stronger fixation, a properly indicated and well-executed single-row repair can achieve excellent results. Latarjet and other glenoid bone-augmentation procedures remain important options for patients with attritional or irreparable bone loss and high-risk bipolar lesions. However, increasing enthusiasm for these procedures should not displace anatomic repair when a viable bony Bankart fragment can be mobilized, anatomically reduced, and securely fixed. When native glenoid anatomy can be reliably restored, arthroscopic bony Bankart fixation is an effective and durable treatment.

cards.title: HCT-FS-Defined Frailty Is Associated With Lower Survival Across Diverse Hematologic Diagnoses After Allogeneic Transplantation.
cards.abstract: To evaluate whether Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation Frailty Scale (HCT-FS)-defined frailty predicts overall survival (OS), nonrelapse mortality (NRM), and relapse across diverse hematologic diagnoses undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (alloHCT), including nonmalignant disorders. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of 992 adults undergoing alloHCT at 16 centers in Canada and Spain (2018-2023). Frailty was assessed at consultation using the HCT-FS (fit, prefrail, frail). OS was estimated by Kaplan-Meier, competing-risks methods by cumulative incidence. Multivariable models assessed associations with OS and NRM. Frailty was assessed across six diagnostic categories, including nonmalignant disorders (4.8%). At consultation, 32.1% were fit, 54.7% prefrail, and 13.2% frail. Increasing frailty was associated with progressively lower 2-year OS (78.9%, 66.0%, 51.7%; p < 0.001) and higher 2-year NRM (10.5%, 18.9%, 33.2%; p < 0.001; HR 1.77 [95% CI 1.21-2.60] prefrail and 3.65 [2.36-5.65] frail vs. fit), while 2-year relapse incidence did not differ (19.0%, 23.5%, 22.3%; p = 0.229). Disease-specific estimates were exploratory and limited by small subgroup sizes. HCT-FS-defined frailty is associated with OS and NRM but not relapse in this multicenter alloHCT cohort. Larger disease-specific studies are needed to establish its prognostic value in less represented indications.

cards.title: A transient decrease in night-to-night variability of REM sleep before myocardial infarction
cards.abstract: Background. Myocardial infarction (MI) outcomes depend on time to treatment, and fatigue and sleep disturbance are often reported in the weeks before the event. Whether wearable-measured sleep changes within individuals before MI, and whether such change is specific to MI, is unknown. Methods. In the All of Us Research Program, adults with a first MI code and at least 180 valid Fitbit sleep nights in the preceding 360 days were matched to up to 10 controls on sex, comorbidities, sleep apnea, calendar time and a propensity score. The full matched cohort of all cases was the primary cohort, and cases with diabetes and/or hypertension formed a subgroup. The main endpoints were the within-person change in night-to-night variability (SD, RMSSD, CV) of the REM-sleep fraction at days 30-16 relative to each persons baseline (days 360-121) and from days 30-16 to days 15-1, tested against 10,000 randomly placed index dates with allowance for the choice of window (max-T). The same pipeline was applied to cases without recorded symptoms or treatment, to an index date at the first angina code, to a cohort including heart failure and to ischaemic stroke and admissions for heart failure, pneumonia, fracture or appendicitis and any cause, and the analysis was adjusted for nightly heart rate, wear and device. Results. The full matched cohort comprised 45 cases and 450 controls. REM-fraction variability changed transiently before MI, decreasing at days 30-16 and returning towards baseline over days 15-1; allowing for the choice of window, this decrease-then-return pattern was rarely matched at 10,000 randomly placed index dates (max-T p<0.001). Its components were the decrease in SD at days 30-16 (Cliffs {delta} -0.30, p=0.004; OR per SD 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.80; max-T p=0.0034) and the return in RMSSD over days 15-1 ({delta} +0.36, p<0.001; max-T p=0.0035); day by day, the decrease was not detected as a continuous change (cluster permutation test p=0.58). The decrease in SD was not seen at the same time before admissions for pneumonia (69 cases), fracture or appendicitis (130) or any cause (859) and was larger before MI than before each of them (difference in {delta} -0.25 to -0.34), whereas the rise over days 15-1 was shared with pneumonia; it was of similar size in the subgroup with diabetes and/or hypertension, in cases without recorded symptoms or treatment, with the index date at the first angina code, when people with heart failure were included and after adjustment for nightly heart rate, wear and device. Scoring each person against their own baseline discriminated cases from controls with AUCs of up to 0.66, probably an optimistic estimate because the decrease in RMSSD was attenuated in held-out halves of the matched sets. Conclusions. In adults who use consumer wearables, a first MI was preceded by a transient change in night-to-night REM-sleep variability, a decrease at days 30-16 and a return over the following two weeks. The decrease was not seen at the same time before other acute admissions, did not depend on recorded symptoms or treatment and was detectable against each persons own baseline with simple measures. The timing is an exploratory finding, to be confirmed in new cases.

cards.title: HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis drives astrocyte senescence and regulates endothelial function via GDNF/NRTN in diabetic retinopathy.
cards.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of blindness in working-age populations. Astrocyte senescence is highly prevalent in DR, but the underlying regulatory mechanism remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the role of the HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis in regulating retinal astrocyte senescence and endothelial function in DR. Mouse retinal astrocytes were exposed to high glucose (30 mM) to mimic diabetic conditions. Senescence was evaluated by β-galactosidase staining. Signaling pathways were manipulated using HIF-1α inhibitor (PX-478), PPAR-γ inhibitor (T0070907), SIRT1 agonist (SRT2104), and autophagy inhibitor (3-MA). Protein and mRNA levels of key factors were detected by Western blot and RT-qPCR. Astrocytes and retinal microvascular endothelial cells were co-cultured in Transwell systems to assess paracrine regulation on endothelial migration, proliferation, and apoptosis. High glucose induced astrocyte senescence, inflammatory activation, and downregulation of GDNF and NRTN, accompanied by elevated HIF-1α and PPAR-γ, and reduced SIRT1 expression and autophagy activity. Inhibiting HIF-1α or activating SIRT1 attenuated senescence, apoptosis, and inflammation, restored autophagy, and upregulated GDNF/NRTN secretion. HIF-1α negatively regulated SIRT1 expression via PPAR-γ. Senescent astrocytes impaired endothelial function through reduced GDNF/NRTN; overexpression of GDNF or NRTN in astrocytes preserved endothelial migration and proliferation, and inhibited apoptosis. HIF-1α/PPAR-γ/SIRT1 axis mediates high glucose-induced astrocyte senescence via autophagy dysfunction. Senescent astrocytes disrupt retinal endothelial homeostasis by reducing GDNF/NRTN secretion. Targeting this axis may represent a novel neurovascular protective therapeutic strategy for DR.

cards.title: The impact of social support on quality of life in patients with osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures after surgery in China: a longitudinal study with mental resilience as a mediator.
cards.abstract: Although surgical intervention is widely used to improve Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures (OVCFs) status, postoperative Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) can be influenced by a multitude of factors from the perspective of ecological and social systems. The study was to examine HRQoL in postoperative OVCFs patients and to further explore the correlations among HRQoL, mental resilience, and social support through a longitudinal study in China. This study assessed the HRQoL, mental resilience, and social support of patients at baseline 1 day post-surgery (T0), 3 months post-surgery (T1), 6 month post-surgery (T2), and 12 months post-surgery (T3) through questionnaire evaluation. A total of 155 postoperative OVCFs patients completed the baseline survey, with 152, 150 and 140 participants completing the follow-up surveys at T1, T2, and T3, respectively. Pearson correlation analyses were conducted to explore the correlation at each time point. We employed the parallel process model to investigate the complex correlations among social support, life quality and mental resilience as time went over. The latent growth curve mediation model was utilized to test the potential mediating role of mental resilience on the correlation between social support and HRQoL. Improvements in mental resilience and increases in social support were associated with enhanced HRQoL over time. There were positive correlations among HRQoL, mental resilience, and social support across time points (P < 0.05). Female sex was associated with a higher initial level of HRQoL (β = 0.192, P < 0.05) and a faster increase in mental resilience over time (β = 1.483, P < 0.05). Mediation analysis suggested that mental resilience mediated the association between social support and life quality (indirect effect of intercept = 0.447, P=.001, 95%CI (0.215, 0.689); indirect effect of slope = 0.244, P=.005, 95%CI (0.076, 0.421)). Correlation coefficients among the three key variables ranged from r = 0.257 to r = 0.876 across time points (all P < 0.05). cards.title: Associations of body roundness index and its trajectories with sarcopenia in middle-aged and older adults: a prospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: Body roundness index (BRI) describes abdominal body shape, yet evidence linking its longitudinal patterns to sarcopenia remains limited. We examined associations of baseline levels and trajectories with prevalent and incident sarcopenia. We analyzed China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study data from 2011 to 2015. The cross-sectional analysis included 12 671 middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and the longitudinal analysis included 5688 participants without baseline sarcopenia. Sarcopenia assessment combined anthropometrically estimated muscle mass with strength and physical performance, using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2019 framework. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations, restricted cubic splines evaluated nonlinearity, and group-based trajectory modelling identified longitudinal patterns. At baseline, 2104 participants had sarcopenia. Higher BRI was inversely associated with prevalent sarcopenia in the fully adjusted model (OR = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.23-0.27). The association was nonlinear, with elevated odds concentrated at lower values. During follow-up, 490 participants developed sarcopenia. Three BRI trajectories were identified: low-stable, moderate-stable, and high-rising. Compared with low-stable, adjusted odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) for incident sarcopenia were 0.12 (0.09-0.16) for moderate-stable and 0.04 (0.02-0.07) for high-rising. Lower baseline BRI and persistently low BRI trajectories were associated with greater sarcopenia vulnerability, possibly reflecting a low-reserve body habitus. These findings suggest that BRI warrants further investigation as a potential marker of sarcopenia vulnerability in population-based research.

cards.title: Spatially Decoupled Donor and Acceptor Gradient Brush Particle Blends for Mechanically Robust, Fatigue-Resistant, and Recyclable Elastomers.
cards.abstract: Combining high mechanical strength, fatigue resistance, and reprocessability in a single soft material remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a strategy based on spatially decoupled interparticle hydrogen bonding in architecturally controlled brush particle blends. Complementary hydrogen-bonding motifs, namely poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) as donor and poly(dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate) (PDMAEMA) as acceptor, were incorporated into poly(n-butyl acrylate) (PnBA)-based gradient brush particles via surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP). Upon blending, reversible interparticle hydrogen bonds were formed, functioning as dynamic physical cross-links. The resulting materials exhibited tensile strengths up to 18 MPa, Young's modulus of 95 MPa, and fracture strains exceeding 150-200%, a combination rarely achieved in physically cross-linked polymer networks. Hierarchical viscoelastic analysis revealed that the synergy between reversible interparticle bonding and architectural heterogeneity generates broad relaxation spectra and multiscale energy dissipation pathways. These features collectively underpin outstanding fatigue resistance, crack-propagation suppression, reprocessability, and thermally assisted self-healing, with annealing at 50 °C restoring approximately 90% of the original modulus and near-complete tensile strength. This work establishes spatial decoupling of hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors as a transferable design principle for durable, recyclable structural soft materials.

cards.title: Spatially Resolved 3D Mechanobiological Model of Rat Femoral Fracture Healing Integrating Mechanics, Vasculature, and Cell Migration.
cards.abstract: Fracture repair arises from the interaction of mechanical, vascular, and cellular processes whose spatial organization remains difficult to predict. We developed an image-derived three-dimensional mechanobiological framework that couples finite-element mechanics, strain-regulated vascularization, progenitor-cell redistribution, and tissue differentiation within a controlled rat femoral osteotomy-and-fixation construct. Model outputs were compared regionally and temporally with ex vivo micro-computed tomography (μCT) and histology over a 6-week healing period. The simulation reproduced several experimentally observed spatial features, including early peripheral/periosteal mineralization followed by later fracture-centered consolidation. Using a calibration/evaluation framework in which day 35 was used to map simulated regional stiffness to μCT bone area and days 14, 21, 28, and 42 were withheld for evaluation, the combined migration formulation showed the strongest overall held-out model-experiment correspondence (Pearson r = 0.57, Spearman ρ = 0.78, MAE = 0.70 mm2, RMSE = 0.88 mm2, R2 = 0.30). Correspondence was weaker for diffusion-only, mechanically guided only, and no migration control. Thus, the migration formulation influenced downstream predictions of regional mineralization, with the combined diffusion and mechanical-guidance formulation showing the strongest correspondence with held-out μCT measurements, although substantial regional error and imperfect absolute calibration remained. Data-driven analysis of simulated element-wise stiffness trajectories identified reproducible computational trajectory classes that exhibited distinct anatomical distributions. Early simulated mechanobiological features were also associated with later simulated stiffness; because this analysis operates entirely within the simulation, it characterizes internal predictive structure rather than independent biological outcome prediction. Together, these findings demonstrate the feasibility of coupling image-derived 3D geometry, mechanics, vascularization, and progenitor cell migration to study spatial heterogeneity during fracture repair in a single, well-controlled construct. Validation across additional geometries, fixation environments, and independent experimental datasets is required before broader biological or clinical generalization.

cards.title: A transcriptomic atlas of grass senescence reveals divergent underground sink networks promote nitrogen recycling in perennials.
cards.abstract: Senescence enables plants to remobilize and recycle nutrients from aging organs to support growth, reproduction, and survival. In annual crops like maize, nitrogen remobilization from leaves to grain is incomplete, with 30-50% of nitrogen remaining in crop residue where it may be subject to environmental loss. Mitigating nitrogen loss in annual crops could be achieved by leveraging the physiological strategies of perennial grasses, which remobilize nitrogen and other nutrients into underground organs at the end of the growing season, thereby preventing environmental leakage. To uncover the molecular basis of perennial nitrogen recycling to underground organs, we built a transcriptomic atlas from field-grown plants, comprising 2,685 RNA-seq libraries from 14 grass species within the Panicoideae (Poaceae), utilizing maize and sorghum as annual references for comparative analyses. The atlas spans leaves, roots, stalks, and rhizomes across two seasons, from mid-growing season to senescence. Using a photosynthetic index to align the leaf's transition from nitrogen sink to source across species, co-expression network analysis revealed that the subnetworks driving leaf nitrogen remobilization are preserved across annuals and perennials. However, we discovered that the subnetworks associated with underground sink establishment, specifically those associated with seed-like dormancy and desiccation tolerance pathways, have diverged among annual crop accessions. Our work identifies conserved gene candidates and networks that could reintroduce perennial-like nutrient recycling into annual crops to enhance long-term nutrient retention in the field.

cards.title: Endogenous Osteoblast-Osteocyte-Osteoclast Signaling Enables Bone Remodeling, Drug Response, and Cancer Invasion in a Nanoscale Calcified Bone-on-a-Chip
cards.abstract: Bone homeostasis depends on spatially orchestrated interactions among osteoclasts, osteoblasts, and osteocytes within a unique microenvironment characterized by an extracellular matrix that is mineralized on the nanoscale. Reconstructing these interactions to enable autonomous cell differentiation and tissue remodeling remains a significant challenge in faithfully modeling bone physiology and disease in-vitro. Here, we present an engineered bone-on-a-chip platform that recapitulates the spatial organization of bone-resident cells, the differentiation of immune cells into osteoclasts, and calcified tissue resorption. We demonstrate that nanoscale mineralization of cell-laden collagen hydrogels is associated with ossification- and matrix-associated transcriptional changes and an osteocyte-like phenotype in osteoblast-lineage cells, while establishing a multicellular microenvironment associated with pro-osteoclastogenic RANKL/OPG signaling and supporting osteoclastogenesis and remodeling without the need for exogenous growth factors. Mineralized niche-driven osteoclastogenesis on-a-chip supported greater osteoclast differentiation than conventional stimulation with RANKL and M-CSF and reproduced differential responses to clinically used anti-resorptive drugs. The model further supports the integration of vascular networks and reproduces features of established tumor-bone interactions, including distinct spatial distributions of different cancer types within the mineralized microenvironment. Together, the findings establish a robust, self-regulated, and versatile microphysiologic model for investigating bone remodeling, cancer-bone crosstalk, and therapeutic interventions.

cards.title: Healthcare Professionals' Priorities for Guidelines on Deprescribing Antihyperglycemics: A Mixed-Methods Study.
cards.abstract: For older adults living with frailty and type 2 diabetes, reassessing the appropriateness of medications is important. This may include consideration of deprescribing (reducing or stopping) antihyperglycemic medications. Our deprescribing.org team created a guideline for deprescribing antihyperglycemics in 2017. To inform a guideline update, we conducted a prioritization exercise to ensure our update addresses current healthcare professional (HCP) needs and priorities. The aim was to establish HCP priorities with regards to the guideline topics, outcomes, and knowledge translation materials included with the 2017 guideline and identify gaps in the content to be added to the update. We conducted a sequential explanatory mixed-methods study between April and June 2025, including a survey open to participants globally, followed by focus groups open to participants in Canada. Quantitative survey data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Qualitative data within the survey and focus group discussions were analyzed using summative content analysis and conventional content analysis, respectively. All guideline topics proposed in the survey were considered either "extremely important" or "important" by the majority of participants. The outcome considered most critical for decision-making when deprescribing was clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia (91%). As a knowledge translation tool, a decision-support algorithm was considered important or extremely important by 84% of respondents. Qualitative findings highlighted considerations for incorporating novel antihyperglycemic agents into deprescribing decisions, cost implications for the patient, and knowledge translation resources (e.g., reporting templates) to support clear communication between prescribers, and patient education materials. The topics and outcomes included in deprescribing.org's 2017 antihyperglycemic deprescribing guideline were all considered important or extremely important by HCPs and therefore we will recommend that these be carried forward into the new guideline. Next steps will include reporting HCP priorities to the guideline panel and updating the systematic review for the guideline.

cards.title: Fermented dairy intake and markers of musculoskeletal ageing on the island of Ireland: insights from the Northern Ireland Cohort for the Longitudinal Study of Ageing (NICOLA) and The Irish Longitudinal Study on Ageing (TILDA).
cards.abstract: Fermented dairy foods may support healthy musculoskeletal ageing via high-quality protein and gut-muscle axis modulation. Epidemiological evidence linking fermented dairy foods with physical function in older adults is limited. We examined associations between fermented dairy intake and physical function in older adults in Ireland using two independent population-based cohorts, to assess the consistency of associations across differing dietary assessment approaches. Cross-sectional analyses of data from the Northern Ireland Cohort for the Longitudinal Study of Ageing (NICOLA; n = 2791; mean age 64 ± 9 years) and The Irish Longitudinal Study on Ageing (TILDA; n = 3999; mean age 66 ± 9 years) was performed. Fermented dairy intake was calculated from cohort-specific food frequency questionnaires (FFQs) with outcomes including muscle strength, frailty and functional limitations. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models were applied, adjusting for demographic and health-related covariates. In NICOLA, fermented dairy intake was not associated with physical function outcomes after confounder adjustment. Associations observed in crude models were attenuated after adjustment, with no dose-response relationships. In TILDA, participants in the highest tertile of fermented dairy intake had higher odds of low grip strength compared with those in the lowest tertile (OR = 2.71; 95% CI: 1.12, 6.88; p = 0.030). However, analysis of individual fermented dairy foods indicated that this association was driven by yoghurt intake and was attenuated after covariate adjustment. Across two independently analysed cohorts, fermented dairy intake was not consistently associated with physical function after confounder adjustment. There is a need for longitudinal and interventional studies to better determine the role of fermented dairy foods in musculoskeletal ageing.

cards.title: Temporal Trends in the Prevalence of Frailty in England From 2002 to 2022, With Forecasts to 2040: Longitudinal Secondary Analysis of a National Cohort Study.
cards.abstract: The increasing life expectancy provides an opportunity for healthy longevity, but frailty is a potential challenge. Existing studies of frailty prevalence in England are largely cross-sectional, use heterogeneous frailty definitions, and rarely break down population-level drivers or project future burden, limiting their use for health and social care planning. This study aimed to explore temporal trends of frailty prevalence and project scenario-based future prevalence up to 2040 for the community-dwelling population aged 50 years and older in England. Prevalence of frailty (measured using a frailty index) in the overall sample and subgroups of age, sex, educational level, and marital status from 2002 to 2022 was estimated among the community-dwelling population aged 50 years and older using 10 waves of nationally representative data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA; n=6226 to 11,218 across waves). The number of individuals with frailty was also derived in each year. Joinpoint regression models were used to explore temporal trends of frailty prevalence. A linear probability regression model was performed using pooled data from 10 waves of the ELSA to explore driving factors and project future prevalence. Decomposition analysis was used to estimate the contribution of individual factors to the change in prevalence. A statistically nonsignificant (P=.61) increase of 2.3 percentage points from 15.5% (1738/11,218) in 2002 to 17.8% (1108/6226) in 2022 was observed, with the number of individuals with frailty growing from 2,560,122 to 3,791,038 among community-dwelling adults aged 50 years and older in England. Those with advanced age, who were female, had a lower educational level, and/or were single had a consistently higher prevalence of frailty. Opposing contributions netted to this overall change: improvements in sociodemographic conditions and educational attainment and healthier lifestyle behaviors offset 222.5%, 94.9%, and 51.6% of the observed increase, respectively. Under scenario-based projections, prevalence was estimated at 20.5% (95% CI 19.2%-21.9%) in 2040, corresponding to 5,213,689 people with frailty. Despite a modest increase in prevalence among the community-dwelling population aged 50 years and older, the substantial growth in the absolute number of individuals with frailty indicates a likely rise in future care demands. The study contributes a 20-year trend, decomposition, and forecast framework for community-dwelling older adults. Findings support prioritizing broader sociodemographic development alongside educational attainment and healthy lifestyles, with potential policy approaches including income and social protection, housing improvements, access to health care, and prevention. Key limitations include self-reported measures, exclusion of care home residents, and potential influence of unmeasured effects.

cards.title: [Silicone arthroplasty of the metacarpophalangeal joint].
cards.abstract: Pain relief through replacement of the degenerated joint using silicone arthroplasty. Advanced painful joint osteoarthritis and with restricted movement. Active local or systemic infection, insufficient bone stock for implantation, insufficient soft tissue coverage. Dorsal longitudinal access to the degenerated joint. Longitudinal tendon split and opening of the capsule, exposure and preservation of the collateral ligaments. Resection of the metacarpal head and opening of the shaft of the metacarpal bone and the proximal phalanx with awl and rasps, and insertion of the trial implant of adequate size. Switch to the definitive implant, suture closure of the capsule, the extensor apparatus and the skin. Early start with mobilization from a positioning splint that includes the wrist and metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint and immediately leaves the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) and distal interphalangeal (DIP) joints free. Immediate active mobilization of the PIP and DIP joints. Additional active mobilization of the MCP joint starting in the second postoperative week. Complete removal of the splint after 6 weeks, full weight-bearing after 8 weeks. Substantial and mostly lasting pain reduction (average 0.3/10 on the visual analog scale, VAS). Expected mobility on average 60° total range of motion. Revision rates of 3-5% after 15 years, radiologically after this time 12-65% implant fractures.

cards.title: Adjustment of Root System Architecture and Root Function in Response to Multifactorial Abiotic Stress.
cards.abstract: The root of land plants is a remarkably adaptive organ. Unlike the shoot with its main functions in light harvesting and photosynthesis, sexual reproduction and diaspore distribution, the root explores the soil for nutrient resources and water, while preferably avoiding zones of unfavorable conditions. Roots realize an extraordinarily flexible architecture and perceive and integrate environmental input parameters to optimize growth, architecture, and physiology. In nature, roots encounter a heterogeneous rooting environment characterized by combinations of negative and positive growth parameters, for example, nutrient availability, temperature, hypoxia, toxic metal ions, or compacted soil, necessitating research on multifactorial stress effects on roots. While many studies have addressed the combination of altered nutrient status, in particular nitrogen and phosphorus, and other environmental stress factors such as drought, temperature, and soil compaction, fewer studies addressed climate change-related combinations of stressors such as heat, drought, and hypoxia. The decisive mechanism of environmental input integration targets root growth and architecture, but also exudation. The adjustment is realized by altered activity of apical meristems for root elongation, the pericycle for lateral root initiation and formation, the development of adventitious roots, and root thickening by cambial activity and senescence. This review presents selective case studies to exemplarily summarize current experimental approaches and obtained knowledge on root responses to multifactorial environmental constraints with focus on assimilate-, redox-, and auxin-dependent regulation. The review pinpoints the need to advance and harmonize our experimental approaches by investigating the sensory role and growth response of roots at the local and systemic level.

cards.title: Irisin alleviates oxidative stress and osteoblast apoptosis in glucocorticoid-induced rat osteonecrosis of the femoral head via the integrin αVβ5/Bach1/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
cards.abstract: Glucocorticoid (GC)‑induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is associated with oxidative stress and osteoblast apoptosis. Irisin, the cleaved form of fibronectin type III domain‑containing protein 5, attenuates oxidative stress and apoptosis in numerous types of cells, including osteoblasts, osteocytes and cardiomyocytes. The present study aimed to investigate the role of irisin and the mechanism behind GC‑induced ONFH in vivo, as well as oxidative stress and osteoblast apoptosis in vitro. In the present study, GC‑induced ONFH was established in rats by intramuscular injection of methylprednisolone, with irisin administered by intraperitoneal injection; the FHs were then assessed by micro‑CT, histology, immunohistochemistry and TUNEL staining. In vitro, murine osteoblastic MC3T3‑E1 cells were treated with dexamethasone (DEX), and oxidative stress, apoptosis and Nrf2 signaling were evaluated by dihydroethidium/JC‑1 staining, flow cytometry, reverse transcription‑quantitative PCR and western blotting. Irisin prevented the development of GC‑induced ONFH in rats, and alleviated oxidative stress and apoptosis in DEX‑treated osteoblasts. To determine the underlying mechanisms by which irisin exerted beneficial effects on DEX‑treated osteoblasts, the present study investigated Nrf2 signaling cascades. Irisin induced Nrf2 signaling cascade activation in MC3T3‑E1 cells and Nrf2 silencing by targeted short hairpin RNA reversed the beneficial effects of irisin on DEX‑treated osteoblasts. Further mechanistic analysis revealed that irisin physically interacted with integrin (ITG) αVβ5 on osteoblasts, activating Erk1 signaling. This activation promoted nuclear export of Bach1, a competitive suppressor of Nrf2, thereby relieving Bach1‑mediated suppression of antioxidant response elements. Consequently, irisin enhanced Nrf2 nuclear accumulation and upregulated its target genes [heme oxygenase, NAD(P)H quinone oxidoreductase 1, glutamate‑cysteine ligase catalytic subunit], reducing reactive oxygen species and mitochondrial membrane potential loss. Pharmacological inhibition of ITG αVβ5 or Erk1/2 abolished irisin‑induced Bach1 export, Nrf2 activation and cytoprotective effects. Collectively, the present study indicated that irisin may mitigate GC‑induced ONFH and osteoblast apoptosis via the ITG αVβ5/Bach1/Nrf2 signaling pathway, highlighting its therapeutic potential.

cards.title: Vertebral fractures unmasking Cushing disease: an unexpected argument for secondary osteoporosis screening.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis poses a substantial health and financial burden. Although secondary causes are more common in men, they are screened less for osteoporosis than their female counterparts. We present the case of a 70-year-old man with a history of an adrenal incidentaloma with a recent diagnosis of 2 vertebral fractures. Initial workup revealed adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent hypercortisolism. Imaging confirmed a pituitary macroadenoma, suggestive of Cushing disease (CD). Lifestyle modifications, calcium and vitamin D supplementation, and intravenous zoledronic acid were initiated to treat the severe osteoporosis. Pituitary surgery was carried out, with pathology revealing a Crooke cell adenoma. This case illustrates the importance of screening for osteoporosis in men, including thorough evaluation to rule out secondary causes. Moreover, a critical evaluation of the current approach to bone health in CD is provided.

cards.title: Perioperative management of patients undergoing head and neck cancer resection and reconstruction with free flaps.
cards.abstract: Patients with head and neck cancer tend to be older, frailer and have more comorbidities than the general surgical population and frequently necessitate wide resections requiring complex reconstructions with free flaps. Preoptimization approaches, airway management protocols, intraoperative fluid administration, blood pressure goals, and use of pressors have been extensively evaluated, and while consensus has been substantially achieved on previously controversial aspects such as intraoperative use of vasopressors, standardized approaches to perioperative care are still evolving. Recent literature has focused on perioperative optimization and enhanced recovery pathways, especially in the care of frail and elderly patients. Airway management in adults and children and optimization of pain management to cover multilocalized pain (resection and free tissue donor site) have been additional topics of interest, as well as the value and applicability of risk scores for postoperative complications and predictive models of delayed recovery. The perioperative management of reconstructive head and neck cancer surgery presents unique challenges. The prevalence of frailty, elevated comorbidity burden and high-risk airway management in this patient population, combined with the complexity of the procedures, require careful individualized planning and specialized care.

cards.title: Comparison of 1-year costs of commercially insured patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing surgical vs. transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
cards.abstract: Patients with aortic stenosis (AS) have been shown to have lower costs at 1 year with transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared with surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in a Medicare population. The difference in costs between TAVR and SAVR in commercially insured patients with AS in the United States is unknown. Using the Optum claims database, AS patients receiving either TAVR or SAVR between 3/2019 and 9/2022 were identified. Patients were categorized into low, intermediate or high strata using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS). The primary outcome was total 1-year cost, defined as the sum of index AVR hospitalization and 1-year follow-up costs. Risk-adjusted generalized linear models were used to assess the difference in the costs between TAVR and SAVR. 3,623 patients (952 TAVR; 2,671 SAVR) were identified. TAVR patients had lower index hospitalization costs compared with SAVR patients across all HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $39,312, p < 0.01; intermediate: $42,006, p < 0.01; high: $39,431, p = 0.03). Cumulative costs through one year were significantly lower with TAVR in the low and intermediate HFRS strata (cost difference for low: $32,116, p < 0.01; intermediate $40,905, p < 0.01) and numerically lower in the high HFRS stratum (cost difference: $35,881, p = 0.15). When the analysis was restricted to isolated AVR, the 1-year difference was no longer significant in the low and intermediate HFRS strata ($8,064 and $11,314, respectively) and was numerically reversed in the high HFRS stratum (-$28,804). In a commercial payor population of real-world patients with AS, TAVR was associated with lower standardized index hospitalization costs across all HFRS strata and lower standardized 1-year costs in the low and intermediate HFRS strata. These findings demonstrate that baseline frailty and procedural scope are critical determinants of short and intermediate-term cost differences between TAVR and SAVR for the treatment of AS in commercial populations.

cards.title: Proximal Femoral Cancellous Bone Density Distribution and Internal Fixation Failure in Intertrochanteric Fractures: A Radiological Study and Internally Validated Prediction Model.
cards.abstract: To investigate proximal femoral cancellous bone density distribution and its association with fixation stability in intertrochanteric fractures, and to develop and internally validate a predictive model. This retrospective study included 220 patients with intertrochanteric fractures treated with proximal femoral nail anti-rotation (PFNA). Fixation failure was defined as cutout, blade migration >5 mm, neck-shaft angle loss >10°, rotational deformity >15°, implant failure, or revision surgery. Preoperative CT Hounsfield units (HU) were measured in the femoral head, intertrochanteric region, and calcar femorale. A predictive model incorporating age, tip-apex distance (TAD), and calcar HU was internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Fixation failure decreased across increasing density-gradient categories (P for trend = 0.037), although the overall difference was nonsignificant (P = 0.112). Age (OR = 1.17, 95% CI: 1.04-1.30), TAD (OR = 1.19, 95% CI: 1.08-1.30), and calcar HU (OR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.95-0.98) were independently associated with failure. The model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.84 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.83. Lower calcar HU was independently associated with fixation failure. The combined model showed good discrimination, but external validation is needed before clinical application.

cards.title: Risk factors for cognitive impairment in patients undergoing hemodialysis: an umbrella review and meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: Cognitive impairment is a common complication in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. This umbrella review and meta-analysis systematically evaluated the factors associated with cognitive impairment and, separately, cognitive frailty in adults receiving hemodialysis. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to January 2026. Five meta-analyses involving 97 associations were included; three evaluated cognitive impairment and two evaluated cognitive frailty. For cognitive impairment, older age, female sex, diabetes, cerebrovascular disease, multiple comorbidities, impaired physical performance, lower hemoglobin levels, and inflammatory markers were associated with increased risk, whereas higher educational attainment was associated with reduced risk (OR = 0.21, 95% CI: 0.13-0.34). For cognitive frailty, older age, female sex, depression (OR = 4.66, 95% CI: 2.98-7.27), stroke history (OR = 2.94, 95% CI: 1.72-5.03), comorbidities, malnutrition, longer dialysis duration (OR = 2.30, 95% CI: 1.49-3.53), low-flux hemodialysis (OR = 4.16, 95% CI: 1.97-8.79), and interdialytic hypotension (OR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.53-4.21) were associated with increased risk, whereas higher education and serum albumin were protective. Only two associations had moderate-certainty evidence; all others were rated low or very low. Cognitive impairment and cognitive frailty are associated with multiple demographic, clinical, and dialysis-related factors but represent distinct outcomes that should be interpreted separately. Further high-quality prospective studies are warranted.

cards.title: Sleep characteristics and sarcopenia in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis: nonlinear associations and a potential adiposity-related pathway.
cards.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD), yet the pathways linking sleep characteristics to sarcopenia remain poorly understood. We examined associations of sleep duration and quality with sarcopenia and whether these associations included an indirect component involving percent body fat (PBF), with albumin and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) as potential modifiers. This cross-sectional study included 562 patients receiving PD. Sleep was assessed by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Sarcopenia was defined by 2025 Asian Working Group criteria; PBF was assessed by bioelectrical impedance. Restricted cubic splines, mediation/moderated mediation analyses, and sensitivity tests (E-values) were used. Sleep duration showed a U-shaped association with sarcopenia (p-nonlinear < 0.001), with the lowest estimated odds at approximately 7.29 h/night. PSQI score was positively associated with sarcopenia (OR = 1.12 per one-point increase). An indirect association involving PBF was observed for PSQI (ACME = 0.002, p = 0.031) and short sleep (ACME = 0.026, p = 0.030), but not for long sleep. Albumin interacted with PBF in the sarcopenia model for the PSQI (p = 0.042) and short-sleep (p = 0.031) pathways, but the indices of moderated mediation were not statistically significant. NLR showed no evidence of interaction. Mediation sensitivity analysis suggested that the observed indirect associations were not readily explained by modest residual confounding. Sleep duration and quality are associated with sarcopenia in PD patients. An indirect association involving PBF was observed for poorer sleep quality and short sleep, but not for long sleep. Albumin interacts with PBF, yet does not significantly modify the overall indirect pathway. Due to the cross-sectional design, findings are hypothesis-generating and not causal.

cards.title: Real-World Deployment of a Web-Based Bone Health Self-Assessment Tool in Thailand: Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study.
cards.abstract: Public-facing digital self-assessment tools may provide a low-barrier way for individuals to engage with preventive health information outside clinical encounters. In osteoporosis, however, real-world use of such tools and the characteristics represented among completed assessments remain incompletely described. This study aimed to describe the real-world deployment of a public-facing web-based bone health self-assessment tool in Thailand and characterize the demographic, clinical, and lifestyle-related information captured in completed assessments. Exploratory analyses examined app-generated outputs, co-occurring unfavorable self-reported factors, and the sensitivity of descriptive findings to probable repeat assessments. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of eligible completed assessments generated during routine public use of the Bone Health Score (developed by Rathapoom Suwanaratana) web app from October through December 2025. The completed assessment was the primary unit of analysis because formal identity verification was not performed. Questionnaire data included demographic characteristics, fracture-related factors, glucocorticoid exposure, and lifestyle behaviors. The app generated a user-facing Bone Health Score, personalized recommendations, and a guideline-informed dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) consideration prompt. Analyses were descriptive. Sensitivity analysis evaluated probable repeat assessments and alternative assumptions for the DXA-consideration prompt. A total of 256 completed assessments were included. The mean age was 51.9 (SD 14.0) years, and 195/256 (76.2%) recorded female sex. The median Bone Health Score was 110 (IQR 90-120). Among 254 assessments with recorded sex, the DXA-consideration prompt was triggered in 94 (37%). Of these, 50/94 (53.2%) occurred below the sex-specific age threshold because at least one captured non-age criterion was present. DXA-prompt sensitivity estimates were 93/226 (41.2%) after excluding default menopause responses and 95/254 (37.4%) after removing the additional early-menopause age restriction. An exploratory 8-factor unfavorable self-reported factor count identified at least 2 factors in 151/256 (59%) assessments, although this proportion varied when individual components were removed. Eighteen repeated-nickname groups were identified, including 8 high-probability repeat clusters. Retaining only the first assessment from these clusters yielded 243 assessments, with principal descriptive estimates remaining similar. Routine deployment of a public-facing bone health self-assessment tool captured structured clinical and lifestyle-related information and translated it into individualized rule-based outputs. Non-age clinical factors contributed substantially to DXA-consideration prompts, showing that the deployed rule-based logic incorporated information beyond age alone. Further evaluation of usability, downstream behavior, clinical follow-up, and linkage with objective assessment is needed to define the broader public health role of this approach.

cards.title: Medical and surgical complication rates following conversion total hip arthroplasty for intertrochanteric femur fractures: a propensity-matched analysis.
cards.abstract: Intertrochanteric (IT) femur fractures are often managed with internal fixation, but subsequent complications may necessitate conversion to total hip arthroplasty (THA). Comparative outcomes remain incompletely characterized. We identified patients undergoing THA from January 2014 through September 2023 in the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Conversion THA followed prior IT fracture fixation; primary THA included all indications; and fracture THA was the index procedure for an acute IT fracture. We analyzed two comparisons: conversion THA (n = 1,790) versus primary THA (n = 209,902), and conversion THA (n = 1,732) versus fracture THA (n = 887). Following 1:1 propensity score matching, 1,788 and 883 pairs, respectively, were identified. Medical complications at 90 days, transfusion within 7 days, and surgical complications at 2 years were assessed. Compared with primary THA, conversion THA was associated with higher odds of anemia (odds ratio [OR] 2.65, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.22-3.17), periprosthetic fracture (OR 5.02, 95% CI 3.47-7.28), and periprosthetic joint infection (PJI; OR 4.73, 95% CI 3.22-6.94). Compared with fracture THA, conversion THA was associated with lower odds of respiratory failure (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.45-0.96) and urinary tract infection (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.48-0.94), and higher odds of periprosthetic fracture (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.23-2.60) and PJI (OR 2.87, 95% CI 1.70-4.82). Conversion THA was associated with higher odds of most measured complications than primary THA and higher odds of periprosthetic fracture and PJI than fracture THA. These findings suggest that the complexity of conversion procedures underscores the need for careful perioperative optimization, and support consideration of arthroplasty for selected IT fractures. Residual confounding and the exclusion of patients with successful fixation preclude conclusions about the superiority of arthroplasty over initial fixation. Future studies should directly compare arthroplasty with initial fixation to guide treatment selection. Level III Therapeutic Study.

cards.title: Hemodialysis and pin-site cranial bone injury following Mayfield three-pin fixation: a retrospective matched study.
cards.abstract: The Mayfield three-pin skull clamp is widely used for head immobilization during neurosurgical procedures. Although complications are uncommon, pin-related adverse events such as skull fracture have been reported. Evidence regarding pin-site cranial bone injury in hemodialysis patients remains limited. We conducted a single-center retrospective comparative study of adult patients who underwent craniotomy with Mayfield three-pin fixation between 2015 and 2025. Six hemodialysis patients were identified, and 28 non-hemodialysis patients were individually matched based on age, sex, surgical indication, and surgical position. Immediate postoperative CT scans, routinely obtained regardless of symptoms, were reviewed to identify pin-site cranial bone injuries, classified as outer-table cortical defects or full-thickness skull fractures. The association between hemodialysis and cranial bone injury was evaluated using an exact conditional test accounting for the matched sets. Pin-site cranial bone injury occurred in 4 of 6 hemodialysis patients (66.7%) and 3 of 28 non-hemodialysis patients (10.7%), indicating a statistically significant association with hemodialysis (two-sided exact p = 0.0044). One hemodialysis patient had a full-thickness fracture, whereas all other injuries were limited to outer-table cortical defects. No clinically apparent fixation-related complications or neurological deterioration were observed. These findings suggest that hemodialysis may be associated with increased susceptibility to pin-site cranial bone injury following Mayfield fixation. Although the clinical significance of minor cortical defects remains uncertain, careful pin-site selection may be warranted in hemodialysis patients.

cards.title: Trends in inpatient surgical treatment of multifragmentary proximal radius fractures in Germany, 2010-2024: a nationwide analysis of procedure statistics.
cards.abstract: Operative treatment of proximal radius fractures is reported to have increased, but it is unclear how much of the increase reflects demographic change and whether the balance between osteosynthesis and arthroplasty has shifted. We describe inpatient operative treatment of proximal radius fractures coded as multifragmentary in Germany, 2010-2024, and how coding, denominators and care setting affect its interpretation. DRG procedure statistics of the Federal Statistical Office identified osteosynthesis of multifragmentary articular fractures of the proximal radius (OPS 5-794.*4) and radial head arthroplasty (OPS 5-824.3). Rates were modelled with quasi-Poisson, the arthroplasty proportion with quasi-binomial regression; Kitagawa decomposition separated demographic change. Sub-period analyses, alternative denominators and a coding-drift indicator were added. Procedures rose from 5,351 to 7,163 (+ 33.9%), mainly before 2020 (rate ratio 1.026 per year, 95% CI 1.017-1.035); demographic change explained 6-13%. The share of multifragmentary codes among open reductions rose from 64.1% to 70.0%. The proportion of arthroplasty rose from 13.8% to 16.8% between 2010 and 2013, stayed at 15.6-17.3% until 2022 without a trend (odds ratio 0.994 per year, 95% CI 0.986-1.002) and reached 19.9% in 2024, probably inflated by a shift of osteosynthesis to the outpatient sector. The data do not show a steady shift from osteosynthesis towards arthroplasty. Code counts depend on coding, denominators and care setting; without indication, fracture classification and outcome, the statistics cannot show whether treatment decisions changed.

cards.title: TSP promotes ferroptosis in breast cancer cells to suppress osteolytic bone metastasis.
cards.abstract: Tiaowei Shenqi pill (TSP) is clinically applied for the treatment of osteoporosis and breast cancer (BC). This study aims to explore the effects and mechanisms of TSP in bone metastasis during BC. An experimental bone colonization model was established in BALB/c mice by injecting 4T1.2 cells into the left ventricle to evaluate BC cell bone metastasis and osteolytic bone destruction. A BC orthotopic tumor model was established by administering MDA-MB-231 cells into the fat pad of BALB/c nude mice. BC cells were co-cultured with osteoblasts MC3T3-E1 for an in vitro study. TSP inhibited orthotopic tumor growth and enhanced ferroptosis-related phenotypes, accompanied by downregulation of SREBF1, upregulation of RASSF1, increased phosphorylation of YAP1 at Ser127, and reduced YAP1 nuclear localization. TSP-containing serum (TSP-CS) reduced the response of BC cells to migration-promoting signals from osteoblast-conditioned medium. TSP treatment also reduced tumor burden in bone metastases, accompanied by a decrease in osteoblast-associated markers around cancer cells. Overexpression of SREBF1 suppressed RASSF1 expression, reduced YAP1 phosphorylation at Ser127, and promoted YAP1 nuclear localization. SREBF1 overexpression reversed TSP-induced ferroptosis and the suppression of bone metastasis and intrabone tumor burden, whereas subsequent RASSF1 overexpression could partially rescue these phenotypes. The YAP activator PY-60 further reversed the enhanced ferroptosis induced by RASSF1. TSP downregulates SREBF1 expression; this change is associated with increased RASSF1 transcription and is accompanied by reduced nuclear localization of YAP1. The findings of this study support the hypothesis that the SREBF1/RASSF1/YAP1 axis may be involved in TSP-induced ferroptosis in BC cells.

cards.title: ALKBH5-Dependent m6A Demethylation Promotes Cardiac Aging Through SLC38A3 Reduction and Glutamine Metabolic Alteration.
cards.abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification has been linked to various types of physiological and pathological bioprocesses. However, the exact role of m6A mRNA methylation in cardiac aging is largely unknown. Here, we show that ALKBH5 (alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase AlkB homolog 5), an m6A demethylase, plays a critical role in regulating cardiac aging. Physiologically aged and paraquat-induced mouse models of cardiac aging as well as senescent cardiomyocyte cell cultures were used to evaluate the expression and function of ALKBH5 in cardiac aging. The adeno-associated virus serotype 9 and small interfering RNAs were used to modulate ALKBH5 expression in vivo and in vitro, respectively. Cardiac aging and function were evaluated by histological analysis, immunostaining, and echocardiography. Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing and functional screening were performed to identify potential targets of ALKBH5 in regulating cardiac aging. ALKBH5 expression was increased in aged hearts and in senescent-like cardiomyocyte models, accompanied by reduced m6A levels. ALKBH5 knockdown attenuated senescence-associated phenotypes in cardiomyocytes and reduced aging-associated cardiac remodeling and dysfunction in physiological aging and paraquat-challenged mouse models when adeno-associated virus serotype 9-short hairpin RNA targeting ALKBH5 gene was delivered beginning in young adulthood, whereas ALKBH5 knockdown initiated in already aged hearts did not reverse established phenotypes. Mechanistically, ALKBH5-dependent m6A demethylation reduced the expression of SLC38A3 (solute carrier family 38-member 3), which suggested a YTHDC2 (YTH domain-containing protein 2)-dependent mechanism, thereby contributing to reduced glutamine accumulation, impaired mitochondrial homeostasis, and increased oxidative stress. SLC38A3 overexpression attenuated aging-associated cardiac phenotypes in vivo. In addition, glutamine supplementation reduced senescence-associated and cardiac aging-related phenotypes. Our study demonstrates that ALKBH5-SLC38A3 axis is an important regulator of m6A-linked, glutamine-associated pathways in aging-related cardiac phenotypes. These findings support a role for ALKBH5 as a contributor to cardiac aging-associated remodeling and dysfunction and suggest this pathway as a candidate target for further mechanistic and translational investigation.
