cards.title: Stressful life events recorded in 39.7 million clinical notes: associations with mental disorders, comorbidity, and frailty
cards.abstract: Abstract Background: Despite being harmful to both mental and physical health, stressful life events are not recorded in structured electronic health records. They appear sporadically in narrative clinical notes, where they are difficult to analyze at scale. Natural language processing (NLP) has made clinical notes more available for research, but applications to stressful life events remain limited, leaving their documentation patterns and prognostic value understudied. By applying NLP, we identified stressful life events from clinical notes and examined their associations with mental disorders, comorbidity, and frailty. Methods: We analyzed 39.7 million clinical notes, recorded between 2010 and 2023, from 202,988 patients in Central Finland Wellbeing Services County. NLP was applied to identify stressful life events in five categories: grief, divorce, financial distress, violence, and family problems. Associations with the risk of mental disorders (stress-related disorders, anxiety, and depression) were estimated using time-varying Cox proportional hazards models, and associations with physical health outcomes (comorbidity and frailty) using generalized linear mixed models. Results: Stressful life events were identified from clinical notes with high accuracy (F1 scores 0.81-0.95). Event prevalences ranged from 0.5% for family problems to 22.1% for grief. Most individual events were associated with mental disorders, comorbidity, and frailty. The number of different life events was associated with a higher risk of stress-related (hazard ratio [HR], 1.62; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.58-1.67), anxiety (HR, 2.08; 95% CI, 2.03-2.14), and depressive disorders (HR, 1.99; 95% CI, 1.94-2.03), and with higher comorbidity (rate ratio, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.56-1.59) and frailty (mean ratio, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.56-1.58). Conclusions: Stressful life events were accurately identified from clinical notes and were associated with a higher risk of mental disorders, comorbidity, and frailty. Even so, violence and financial distress, the two events with comparable national estimates, were documented substantially less often than those estimates, suggesting underrecording of stressful life events in clinical settings.

cards.title: Late HIV diagnosis and survival following AIDS diagnosis among people with AIDS in Italy, 2000-2024: an analysis of national surveillance data.
cards.abstract: Late diagnosis of HIV (LD) remains a major determinant of morbidity and mortality. Italy continues to report a high proportion of late HIV diagnoses. We investigated factors associated with LD among AIDS cases in Italy and examined survival after AIDS diagnosis. We analysed National AIDS Registry data for 2000-2024. LD was defined as HIV diagnosis within 90 days of AIDS diagnosis. Factors associated with LD were assessed using multivariable Poisson regression. All-cause mortality was assessed through linkage with the Causes of Death Registry using multivariable Cox models with shared regional frailty. Among 25,468 AIDS cases, 58.2% were LD, increasing from 48.2% (2000-2007) to 76.4% (2016-2024). LD was more frequent in older adults, males and foreign-born individuals, and less common among men who have sex with men and people who inject drugs. LD was not significantly associated with mortality within 3 months of AIDS diagnosis (aHR 0.94, 95% CI 0.85-1.04), but was associated with lower mortality after 3 months (0.60, 0.56-0.64). Late HIV diagnosis among AIDS cases remains highly prevalent in Italy, and its associations with mortality varied by time since AIDS diagnosis. Targeted testing strategies for populations at risk of missed diagnosis remains essential.

cards.title: Evolution and impact of sarcopenia and myosteatosis in the context of liver transplantation.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia and myosteatosis have a well-documented adverse impact on survival in liver cirrhosis patients. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and risk factors associated with muscle impairment before liver transplantation (LT), their evolution after LT, and to determine their prognostic value. All cirrhotic patients listed for LT at our center between 2006 and 2010 were included. Sarcopenia and myosteatosis were assessed on transverse L3 CT images at LT listing and at 12 (M12), 60, 120, and 180 months after LT. The study population consisted of 198 patients, 75.3% of whom were men, and 149 underwent LT. At LT listing, sarcopenia was diagnosed in 45.5% of patients and myosteatosis in 36.5% and 20.1% had both sarcopenia and myosteatosis. One year after LT, 56.1% of patients had persistent sarcopenia and 15.3% had de novo sarcopenia. Sarcopenia significantly improved at M12 post-LT (p=0.034). Post-LT patient survival was 89.2%, 76.3%, and 59.3% at 1, 5, and 10 years respectively. In multivariate analysis, at LT listing, MELD score ≥ 25 (HR: 2.549; p=0.001), sarcopenia (HR: 1.749; p=0.004) and myosteatosis (HR: 1.630; p=0.012) were found to be independent risk factors for overall mortality. The effects of sarcopenia and myosteatosis were additive: overall survival was significantly reduced in patients with both sarcopenia and myosteatosis compared to patients with isolated sarcopenia/myosteatosis (p=0.001). Sarcopenia and myosteatosis are common in cirrhotic patients listed for LT, persist after LT, and have a major and independent impact on overall mortality.

cards.title: Predicting prosthetic use and survival following transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease: a retrospective cohort study.
cards.abstract: To examine associations between BLARt, CFS, prosthetic use and 24-month survival after unilateral transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease. This retrospective cohort study included 168 adults aged ≥65 years who underwent unilateral transfemoral amputation between 2019 and 2023. BLARt was analysed as a continuous score and CFS as an ordinal measure grouped as ≤4, 5 and ≥6. Prosthetic-use analyses excluded participants who had died by the relevant time point. Logistic regression, exact tests, ROC analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analysis were used. At discharge, 23 of 132 survivors (17.4%) were using a prosthesis; at 24 months, 17 of 80 survivors (21.3%) were using one. Higher BLARt scores were associated with lower odds of prosthetic use at discharge (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.33-0.60) and 24 months (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37-0.69; both p<.001). Prosthetic use differed across CFS groups at both time points (p<.001), with no prosthetic users among participants with CFS ≥6. By 24 months, 88 participants (52.4%) had died. Compared with CFS ≤4, adjusted odds of death were higher for CFS 5 (OR 4.12, 95% CI 1.12-15.20) and CFS ≥6 (OR 8.40, 95% CI 1.97-35.80). CFS and the combined mortality model each had an AUC of approximately 0.71. BLARt was associated with prosthetic use among survivors, while increasing frailty was strongly associated with both lower prosthetic use and higher 24-month mortality. These measures may support multidisciplinary prognostic discussion but should not be used as rigid thresholds for prosthetic rehabilitation.

cards.title: Long-Term Outcomes After Left Ventricular Assist Device Exchange: Survival Rates and Postoperative Complications.
cards.abstract: Some patients require left ventricular assist device (LVAD) exchange because of pump thrombosis, infection, or pump failure. The aim of this study is to compare the long-term survival and postoperative complications between patients who did not require LVAD exchange and patients who required LVAD exchange. We included patients who underwent HeartMate II, HeartWare Ventricular Assist Device and HeartMate 3, LVAD implantation at our institution between December 2008 and November 2019. We compared survival rate and postoperative complications between the cases which did not require LVAD exchange (Group 1) and the cases which required LVAD exchange (Group 2). There were 333 cases which met our criteria. Group 1 included 296 cases; group 2 included 37 cases. Causes of LVAD exchange were pump thrombosis (n = 22), driveline fracture (n = 6) cases, driveline infection (n = 8), and pump failure (n = 1). There was no statistical difference between groups in cumulative incidence of death 5 y after surgery, or in postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding and neurological complications. The rate of postoperative device-related infection was higher in group 2. To the best of our knowledge, this report includes the longest follow-up period comparing patients who required LVAD exchange after surgery to those who did not require LVAD exchange. LVAD exchange can be performed safely without increasing mortality rates, gastrointestinal bleeding, or neurological complications.

cards.title: AtATO interacts with the senescence-related repressor AtWDS1 to negatively regulate age-dependent and dark-induced leaf senescence in Arabidopsis.
cards.abstract: Although many achievements have been made in understanding the mechanisms underlying age-dependent and induced leaf senescence, the precise regulatory pathway involved remains to be elucidated. AtWDS1, which is a nuclear-localized negative senescence regulator in Arabidopsis thaliana, was characterized in a previous study. In this study, AtATO, encoding an SF3a factor, was identified when AtWDS1-interacting proteins were screened and was further verified using yeast two-hybrid assays and bimolecular fluorescence complementation. YFP-tagged AtATO protein in A. thaliana mesophyll protoplasts revealed that AtATO localized to the nucleus and cytoplasm. An analysis of the AtATO T-DNA insertion mutant (atato) revealed a premature senescence phenotype, chlorophyll loss, and up-regulated expression of senescence-associated genes. Compared with those from the wild-type plants, the leaves from the atato mutant became chlorotic faster and had greater H2O2 accumulation under dark conditions. Phenotyping of the atato mutant indicated that AtATO suppressed developmental and dark-induced leaf senescence. In addition, atato mutants presented reduced tolerance to oxidative stress, accompanied by changes in the transcription levels of genes associated with the oxidative stress response and increased cell death. Taken together, these results suggest that AtATO functions as a novel modulator of leaf senescence in A. thaliana in response to developmental and stress signals.

cards.title: Species-level Torque teno virus abundance is associated with immune impairment, epigenetic aging markers, and clinical vulnerability in hospitalized older adults: the VIROMA study.
cards.abstract: Torque teno viruses (TTVs) are ubiquitous components of the human virome whose replication is tightly regulated by host immunity. While elevated total TTV load has been associated with increased mortality in older adults, the clinical relevance of species-level virome composition remains unclear. We profiled the circulating anellovirome in 251 hospitalized older adults using amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing and investigated associations with frailty, cognitive impairment, mortality, immune remodeling, and epigenetic aging. Reduced TTV species evenness was associated with 1-year mortality (p = 0.013, FDR = 0.052); however, differences in species composition accounted for less than 1% of the total variance (PERMANOVA: Ružička R2 = 0.0079, p = 0.021, FDR = 0.035; Bray-Curtis R2 = 0.0082, p = 0.035, FDR = 0.035), indicating that host-related factors rather than distinct clinical phenotypes primarily shaped the virome. Following multivariable adjustment, differential abundance analyses identified TTV19 enrichment in patients with 1- and 3-year mortality, frailty, and cognitive impairment, alongside TTV9 enrichment in frail patients. Bootstrap resampling confirmed a stable association between TTV19 and cognitive impairment (logFC = 2.39, 95% CI 0.59-5.43) and between TTV9 and frailty (logFC = 2.26, 95% CI 0.11-9.86). Conversely, multivariable Cox models showed no significant association between TTV19 abundance and 1-year or 3-year mortality, and only a nominal association with seven-year mortality (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.01-1.19) that did not pass multiple testing correction. Species-specific associations with DNA methylation-estimated immune cell subsets further supported links between selected TTV species and immune remodeling. TTV19 log-abundance showed a positive nominal association with Age Acceleration GrimAge (p = 0.024, FDR = 0.072), and with DNAm-estimated inflammatory and vascular markers. Overall, these findings suggest that the circulating anellovirome primarily reflects systemic vulnerability rather than disease-specific signatures in late life. A limited subset of viral species may represent candidate correlates of immune dysregulation and biological aging requiring further validation.

cards.title: Eriodictyol Modulates Cell-Type-Specific Stress Response Pathways In Vitro and Improves Visible Signs of Skin Aging
cards.abstract: Skin aging involves progressive disruption of redox balance, proteostasis, inflammation, and extracellular matrix integrity. Flavonoids have attracted interest for their ability to regulate cellular stress responses relevant to these processes. This study investigated the natural flavonoid eriodictyol (EDL) in human skin cells and evaluated whether topical application improved visible skin quality. Primary human keratinocytes and dermal fibroblasts were treated with EDL and profiled by RNA-sequencing to characterize cell-type-specific transcriptional responses. Functional validation assessed oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and senescence-associated markers, while a seven-flavonoid structure-function comparison contextualized EDL activity. Topical effects were assessed in a randomized, double-blind, vehicle-controlled cosmetic study (N = 60) using an EDL-containing formulation for 12 weeks. EDL induced distinct transcriptional changes in keratinocytes and fibroblasts, with enrichment of unfolded protein response pathways in both cell types. Keratinocytes showed increased expression of antioxidant and autophagy-related genes, whereas fibroblasts showed changes in gene expression pathways related to proliferation, metabolism, and senescence signaling. Functional assays further showed that EDL reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity. In a 12-week topical evaluation, EDL significantly improved overall skin quality across multiple parameters of visible aging compared with the vehicle. These findings demonstrate that EDL modulates stress-response pathways in human skin cells and improves visible skin quality following topical application.

cards.title: Feasibility of a lumbar CT-to-MRI image translation framework using a conditional CycleGANs for fracture stage determination in osteoporotic compression fractures.
cards.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides a reliable indicator of fracture stage. However, MRI scans can be expensive, time-consuming, and not readily accessible to all patients. With recent advances in artificial intelligence, translating lumbar CT images into MRI images has become feasible using cycle generative adversarial network (CycleGANs) based approaches. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of a model that translates lumbar CT images into MRI images (T1-weighted contrast-enhanced sequences) to predict the stage of osteoporotic compression fracture (OCFs) using conditional CycleGANs. A total of 652 patients diagnosed with OCFs who underwent both CT and MRI within 2 weeks were retrospectively collected. Of these, 552 patients were used for training, and an independent set of 100 patients was reserved for testing. CT and MRI volumes were aligned using segmentation-based rigid registration. The proposed framework consisted of two stages: generation of vertebra-specific acute fracture maps from CT images using a 3D ResNet-based model, followed by CT-to-MRI image translation using a 3D conditional CycleGANs with acute stage conditioning. Performance was evaluated using vertebra-level classification metrics, image similarity metrics, and qualitative assessment by five experienced readers, including three spine neurosurgeons, one orthopedic spine specialist, and one radiologist. Fractures were most common at the thoracolumbar junction. A total of 800 vertebral bodies were analyzed. Of 678 non-acute OCFs, 667 were correctly classified and 11 were misclassified as acute; of 122 acute OCFs, 106 were correctly identified and 16 were misclassified as non-acute. Acute fracture classification achieved a precision of 0.906, recall of 0.869, and F1-score of 0.887. Synthetic MRI images showed modest quantitative agreement with real MRI (Normalized MAE 0.094 ± 0.024; PSNR 18.7 ± 1.7 dB; SSIM 0.38 ± 0.04). Qualitative evaluation demonstrated high similarity in vertebral body morphology at the fracture level, with mean similarity scores of 87.2% for the conditional CycleGAN and 85.3% for the conventional CycleGAN. This study demonstrates the feasibility of a lumbar CT-to-MRI image translation framework using a conditional CycleGAN for determining fracture stage.

cards.title: Obliterative versus Reconstructive Surgery for Advanced Pelvic Organ Prolapse in Older Women: A Systematic Review for Preference-Sensitive Surgical Decision-Making.
cards.abstract: The choice between obliterative and reconstructive surgery for older women with advanced pelvic organ prolapse is preference sensitive. This review synthesized comparative evidence across perioperative safety, durability, urinary, bowel/anorectal, and patient-reported outcomes. PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 1 May 2026. English-language comparative studies in older advanced-prolapse populations were included. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, assessed risk of bias using Risk Of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions, and rated certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation. Findings were narratively synthesized because of heterogeneity. Of 664 records, 29 reports representing 27 study families were included. Safety outcomes were reported in 23 reports, durability/recurrence in 16, urinary outcomes in 12, bowel/anorectal outcomes in 9, and broad patient-reported outcomes/quality of life in 10. Twelve of the 14 non-overlapping comparisons reported shorter operative time after obliterative surgery; blood loss favored obliteration in 8 of the 12 comparisons and hospital stay in 5 out of 11. Overall complications were not consistently lower. Anatomical/composite durability numerically favored obliteration in 7 out of 10 comparisons, and recurrence-related reoperation was lower in 7 out of 8. Urinary, bowel, and patient-reported outcomes were inconsistent or similar. Certainty was low for operative time and very low for other key outcomes. Current evidence supports a more definitive conclusion about lower procedural burden, particularly shorter operative time, than about global complications, anatomical superiority, or functional outcomes. Findings should inform counseling that integrates frailty, comorbidity, sexual goals, functional symptoms, durability expectations, treatment burden, and patient preference.

cards.title: Trends in screening tools for sarcopenia: A bibliometric analysis.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia, characterized by the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass, strength, and function, poses a significant health challenge in aging populations. Early identification through effective screening tools is critical to mitigate risks such as falls, fractures, and frailty. This study aimed to analyze global research trends in sarcopenia screening tools using bibliometric methods to identify key contributors and emerging hotspots, thereby guiding future research directions. Data were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) for the period from January 2013 to March 2025. A total of 180 articles were analyzed using bibliometric tools such as the R package bibliometrix, VOSviewer, and CiteSpace. The analysis focused on publication trends, citation impact, co-authorship networks, and keyword co-occurrence to map research trends and identify influential studies and screening tools. The analysis revealed a steady increase in research output since 2013, with an annual growth rate of 38.16%. China emerged as the leading contributor, accounting for 30% of publications, followed by Japan and Brazil. Among the screening tools investigated, the Strength, Assistance in walking, Rise from a chair, Climb stairs, and Falls (SARC-F) questionnaire was the most studied tool, followed by SARC-F combined with calf circumference (SARC-CalF) and calf circumference measurements. Citation analysis highlighted pivotal studies on SARC-F validation, while emerging hotspots included tools like the Mini Sarcopenia Risk Assessment (MSRA) and Ishii test, reflecting a shift toward more practical and accessible screening methods. This bibliometric analysis maps global advancements in sarcopenia screening tools, highlighting China's prolific research output (30% of publications) and the development of culturally adapted instruments in Japan (Ishii test, Yubi-wakka method). The SARC-F questionnaire dominates research focus, spurring innovations including SARC-CalF and calf circumference metrics. The findings advocate standardized validation frameworks and integration of evidence-based screening into geriatric care policies, emphasizing tool accessibility and clinical utility to combat sarcopenia in aging populations.

cards.title: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of HMGB1 suppresses neuroinflammation and cellular senescence to alleviate diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
cards.abstract: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a devastating complication of diabetes. While neuroinflammation and cellular senescence are known contributors to DPN pathogenesis, the precise molecular mechanisms linking these processes remain unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that advanced glycation end products (AGEs) promote the nuclear-cytoplasmic translocation of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), enhancing its extracellular secretion. This extracellular HMGB1 functions as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP), recruiting inflammatory cells and inducing neuroinflammation and cellular senescence in PC12 cells. Consistent with these cellular findings, HMGB1 levels were markedly elevated in STZ-induced DPN mice. Notably, systemic neutralization of HMGB1 effectively suppressed neuroinflammation and senescence, thereby ameliorating DPN. Mechanistically, AGE treatment downregulated Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), resulting in increased HMGB1 acetylation, which facilitated its nuclear export and extracellular release. Consequently, SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of HMGB1 attenuated neuroinflammation and delayed cellular senescence, playing a pivotal role in alleviating DPN. Our findings unveil the critical role of the SIRT1/HMGB1 deacetylation axis in orchestrating neuroinflammation and cellular senescence, highlighting targeted inhibition of HMGB1 secretion as a promising therapeutic strategy for DPN.

cards.title: Sorcin phase separation restrains p53 translation via stress granules to prevent hepatic stellate cell senescence in liver fibrosis.
cards.abstract: Liver fibrosis (LF) is a dynamic process characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition driven by hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation. Inducing senescence in activated HSCs can limit fibrosis. The p53-p21 signaling axis is a key regulator of cellular senescence, however, how p53 activity is precisely controlled remains undefined. Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) has emerged as an important stress-adaptive regulatory mechanism, driving the formation of stress granules (SGs) that regulate mRNA fate. Here, integrative analyses of human and murine datasets revealed that Sorcin expression is upregulated during fibrosis progression. Functional studies showed that Sorcin suppresses HSC senescence, as evidenced by reduced senescence markers, decreased SA-β-Gal positivity, and enhanced proliferative capacity. Mechanistically, elevated intracellular calcium drives Sorcin-mediated LLPS, enabling cooperation with the RNA-binding protein TIAR to nucleate SGs-like condensates. RNA immunoprecipitation, polysome profiling, dual-luciferase assays and EMSA demonstrated that TIAR directly binds TP53 mRNA and represses its translation. Consequently, TP53 mRNA is sequestered within SG-like condensates, attenuating p53 signaling and delaying HSC senescence. In vivo, AAV-mediated Sorcin knockdown enhances HSC senescence and alleviates LF in a CCl4-induced mouse model. This study reveals a phase separation-mediated translational control mechanism governing HSC senescence. By restraining senescence, Sorcin sustains fibrotic persistence, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for LF.

cards.title: Revision Surgery After Total Temporomandibular Joint Replacement: A Case Series.
cards.abstract: Total temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) is an established treatment for end-stage temporomandibular joint disease. However, biological and mechanical complications may require revision surgery, and evidence guiding surgical decision-making remains limited. This study aimed to describe revision strategies for complications following TMJR, with emphasis on the underlying etiology and mechanical stability of the prosthetic system. This retrospective case series included four consecutive patients who underwent revision surgery for complications following TMJR between 2021 and 2025. Two patients developed heterotopic ossification with mechanically stable prosthetic components and underwent resection while preserving the prostheses. Two patients presented with mechanical failure, including component displacement, fixation loss, or prosthetic fracture, requiring complete revision with patient-specific prosthetic systems. During a follow-up period ranging from 8 to 24 months, all patients showed stable prosthetic reconstruction without reported postoperative complications. Revision surgery after TMJR should be guided by the etiology of the complication and the mechanical stability of the prosthetic system. Prosthesis preservation may be considered when the components remain mechanically stable and treatment can be directed toward the periarticular pathology. In contrast, loss of fixation or structural failure may require complete prosthetic revision.

cards.title: Polysaccharide-based dissolving microneedles reinforced by metal-polyphenol network: dual-enhancement of mechanical strength and photothermal-triggered drug penetration.
cards.abstract: Skin diseases affect approximately 30%-70% of the global population and significantly reduce quality of life. Although polysaccharide-based dissolving microneedles (DMNs) are a minimally invasive transdermal delivery platform with strong clinical potential, their loose molecular packing and weak intermolecular interactions often lead to insufficient mechanical strength, increasing the risk of bending or fracture during insertion into pathological skin. In this study, a metal-polyphenol network (MPN)-mediated dual-enhancement strategy was developed by incorporating an EGCG-iron ion self-assembled precursor into a hyaluronic acid (HA) matrix to generate the preferred MPN-enhanced DMNs (PMN). MPN incorporation regulated the molecular organization of the HA polysaccharide matrix through synergistic hydrogen bonding and metal-ligand coordination interactions, leading to enhanced structural integrity and mechanical robustness. Under 808 nm near-infrared irradiation (NIR), PMN generated localized photothermal heating that disrupted dense tissue barriers and promoted molecular transport, resulting in a 2.67-fold increase in transdermal drug penetration compared with conventional DMNs. In melanoma-bearing mice model, PMN combined with NIR irradiation achieves an 83.5% tumor inhibition rate in a B16 melanoma model with good biosafety. Overall, this work provides mechanistic insights into the structure-property relationship of MPN-regulated polysaccharide matrix and offers a versatile strategy for constructing mechanically robust and multifunctional polysaccharide-based transdermal delivery systems.

cards.title: Associations of muscle function with recurrent and injurious falls in adults aged 50 years and older: A systematic review.
cards.abstract: Falls are the leading cause of injury and injury-related mortality among older adults in the U.S. and a major contributor to fracture risk. Muscle function (strength and power) has been associated with risk of recurrent and injurious falls, yet studies vary by measurement methods and anatomical locations. This review synthesizes evidence on associations between muscle function and fall outcomes, identifies methodological limitations, and suggests directions for future research. PubMed and Embase were searched for peer-reviewed articles published between 2000 and September 16, 2026 examining associations of muscle function with recurrent or injurious falls among adults aged ≥50 years. Performance-based measures of muscle function (e.g., chair stands) were excluded to focus on direct strength and power assessments. Two reviewers screened abstracts and full texts, one extracted study characteristics, and one performed a risk-of-bias assessment. Seventeen studies were included, with eight rated 'good' and nine rated 'fair' quality. Most found that higher grip strength was associated with lower odds of recurrent and injurious falls, though sex-specific associations remain underexplored. Leg strength was evaluated in only one study, and leg power in two studies. Both reported associations of higher leg power with lower odds of injurious falls that were similar in magnitude to grip strength associations, but only one was statistically significant. Reduced upper-extremity strength may be a risk factor for recurrent and injurious falls, whereas evidence for lower-extremity power remains limited and inconsistent. Future research should incorporate multiple muscle function measures, standardize injury definitions, and examine sex-specific associations.

cards.title: Vitamin D receptor activator-associated calcium-alkali syndrome-like phenotype without calcium supplementation: a case series of seven patients.
cards.abstract: Vitamin D receptor activators (VDRAs) are widely prescribed for osteoporosis and CKD-mineral and bone disorder in Japan. Although hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury (AKI) are recognized adverse effects, metabolic alkalosis in these patients has received limited attention as a feature of calcium-alkali syndrome (CAS).We retrospectively reviewed patients with VDRA-associated hypercalcemia at our institution between April 2016 and June 2026, applying study-defined operational criteria for a CAS-like phenotype: hypercalcemia, elevated bicarbonate compatible with a metabolic alkalosis component (HCO₃⁻ ≥ 26 mmol/L), and AKI (KDIGO criteria). Seven elderly women fulfilled all criteria. Six received eldecalcitol (0.75 μg/day) and one received alfacalcidol (1.0 μg/day). Underlying CKD was present in six patients.Time from initiation to onset ranged from 1 to 120 months (median 18 months). Three cases had no identified exogenous alkali source. The serum Na-Cl difference was elevated in all patients (range 36-53 mEq/L). Renal outcomes were complete recovery in three patients, partial recovery in two, and non-recovery in one; one patient died of worsening heart failure.VDRA-associated hypercalcemia can present as a CAS-like phenotype even without calcium supplementation, and renal outcomes may be irreversible. Because the temporal relationship between hypercalcemia and metabolic alkalosis cannot be established from these retrospective data, the main clinical message is that elderly patients receiving VDRAs, particularly those with CKD or relevant concomitant medications, require periodic calcium monitoring and prompt evaluation when nonspecific symptoms, AKI, or an elevated Na-Cl difference are observed.

cards.title: Evaluating the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence for pediatric appendicular fractures: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: Pediatric fracture detection on plain radiographs can be challenging, and missed fractures can have important clinical consequences. Artificial intelligence has been increasingly investigated as a tool to support fracture detection in children. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence models for detecting appendicular fractures on pediatric radiographs. A comprehensive literature search was conducted from inception through February 1, 2026. Studies evaluating AI models for detecting appendicular fractures in pediatric populations using plain radiographs were included. Pooled sensitivities and specificities were calculated using bivariate random-effects meta-analysis, and subgroup analyses were performed based on anatomical site, unit of analysis, and comparator type. Sixteen studies were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity for standalone AI models were 92.0% (95% CI, 90.4-93.4%) and 87.9% (95% CI, 84.5-90.6%), respectively, with an hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) area under the curve of 0.96. Considerable heterogeneity was observed (I2, 49-78%). No significant differences were found between per-image and per-patient analyses (P=0.78). Differences in diagnostic performance among physicians using AI models, standalone AI models, and physicians without AI models were not significant (P=0.20). Fagan nomogram analysis demonstrated that at 50% pre-test probability, a positive AI result increased post-test probability to 90%, while a negative result reduced it to 7%. AI models demonstrate considerable diagnostic accuracy for detecting pediatric appendicular fractures on radiography. Considerable heterogeneity and concerns regarding real-life implementation highlight the need for prospective studies with standardized methodologies.

cards.title: Approaches to assessing functional outcome trajectories in old survivors of intensive care: a narrative review.
cards.abstract: Patients with critical conditions admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU) undergo one of the most extensive trials of resilience. In addition to considering survival as a crucial outcome, there is a growing awareness of the importance of recovering functional abilities in old ICU patients. In this narrative review, a group of geriatricians and intensivists will discuss previous studies and current approaches to assess functional trajectories in old ICU survivors with a focus on frailty, functional independence and intrinsic capacity. In previous studies, frailty as evaluated with the Clinical Frailty Scale or variants of the Frailty Index has been found to exhibit a dynamic course after a critical illness. Measures of functional independence show a similar pattern after ICU discharge depending on pre-existing impairments and frailty. Although the concept of intrinsic capacity could provide a holistic framework to predict functional impairments, there still is only limited data on its usefulness in the context of a critical illness. Assessing the post-discharge trajectory in old survivors of a critical illness is crucial to detect early signs of complications and adjust individual support. However, current approaches in this field lack validation. Considering the challenges and importance of functional recovery in old ICU patients, more intensive research in the future is imperative in order to determine the best approach to describe, monitor and optimise the health status amongst these individuals.

cards.title: Prognostic value of the red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio in alcohol-related sarcopenia.
cards.abstract: Chronic alcohol consumption is associated with sarcopenia, a metabolic disorder characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass and function. The red blood cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has emerged as a composite biomarker reflecting inflammation, oxidative stress, and nutritional status. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic value of RAR in patients with alcohol use disorder and sarcopenia. We conducted a prospective observational study including 231 patients with chronic alcohol consumption (mean intake 200 g/day) recruited at a tertiary hospital between 2008 and 2025. Clinical, analytical, and body composition variables were assessed using densitometry and handgrip strength. Probable sarcopenia was defined according to EWGSOP2 criteria based on low muscle strength. Cox and logistic regression models and ROC curve analysis were performed. RAR was positively associated with liver dysfunction and inflammatory markers, and inversely correlated with appendicular lean mass and handgrip strength. In patients with probable sarcopenia, RAR was independently associated with 12-month mortality (hazard ratio 1.67; 95% confidence interval 1.32-2.11; p < 0.001). The predictive capacity of RAR was high (AUC 0.81; 95% CI 0.67-0.94). In conclusion, RAR is a simple, low-cost, and independent prognostic biomarker that integrates inflammatory and nutritional status in patients with alcohol use disorder and sarcopenia.

cards.title: Fixation of patellar fractures using bioabsorbable hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide cannulated screws and subperiosteal nonabsorbable sutures.
cards.abstract: Bioabsorbable implants offer a promising alternative to metallic fixation for patellar fractures, potentially avoiding hardware-related complications. In 2023, a new generation of bioabsorbable hydroxyapatite/poly-L-lactide (HA/PLLA) cannulated screws was introduced, featuring a low-profile (2 mm) trident-shaped head and increased root diameter for enhanced strength. This study evaluates the clinical outcomes of a surgical technique combining these redesigned screws with subperiosteal nonabsorbable sutures. Between April 2023 and May 2025, 19 consecutive patients with transverse patellar fractures (AO/OTA 34-C1/C2) underwent open reduction and internal fixation. Two bioabsorbable cannulated screws were used. High-strength nonabsorbable sutures were passed through the screw channels and a central bone tunnel using a double-loop sliding knot for compression. The sutures were systematically routed subperiosteally to minimize tissue irritation. Full weight-bearing with a brace began on postoperative day one. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were assessed. This study was approved by the institutional review board of Kainan Hospital. The mean maximum articular surface gap was 8.7 ± 5.2 mm. The mean follow-up was 8.6 ± 3.0 months. Bone union was achieved in all cases. At the final follow-up, the mean knee flexion was 138.7° ± 13.0° and extension was - 1.6° ± 3.4°. No postoperative complications, including infection, loss of reduction, screw breakage, or symptomatic hardware irritation, were observed during the follow-up period. No reoperations were required during the follow-up period. All patients achieved bone union. No major complications or reoperations were observed during the follow-up period. These preliminary findings suggest that this technique may be feasible for transverse patellar fractures.

cards.title: Refining ECPR candidate selection: from fixed criteria to a dynamic probability-of-benefit framework.
cards.abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a rescue strategy for selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest. However, identifying patients most likely to achieve neurologically meaningful survival remains challenging. Conventional selection criteria, including age, initial rhythm, witnessed arrest, bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), and no-flow and low-flow duration, are clinically useful but may be insufficient when interpreted as isolated thresholds. We conducted a narrative review of contemporary evidence on ECPR patient selection, incorporating randomized trials, observational studies, registries, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and current guideline and consensus recommendations. Evidence was critically evaluated with particular attention to patient-level prognostic factors, arrest setting, dynamic physiological and metabolic variables, ECPR logistics, and system-level determinants of outcome. Current evidence supports a multidimensional rather than single-variable approach to ECPR candidacy. Favorable arrest characteristics, potentially reversible etiology, shorter low-flow duration, and preserved physiological reserve remain important; however, chronological low-flow time should be interpreted alongside the quality and effectiveness of ongoing CPR. Dynamic information-including transient return of spontaneous circulation, lactate kinetics, arterial pH, end-tidal carbon dioxide, and hemodynamic parameters-may further refine assessment of biological viability. Frailty, comorbidity burden, cerebral perfusion, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-related contraindications should also be incorporated into decision-making. Importantly, selection cannot be separated from system performance: Cannulation strategy, transport logistics, institutional experience, and the ability to establish extracorporeal circulation rapidly may substantially modify the likelihood of benefit. Differences between out-of-hospital and in-hospital cardiac arrest further limit the universal application of rigid eligibility criteria. Candidacy for ECPR should be viewed as a dynamic, probability-based assessment rather than a checklist of fixed thresholds. Integrating arrest characteristics, reversibility, evolving physiology, patient reserve, and system capability may provide a more clinically meaningful framework for identifying patients most likely to achieve neurologically favorable survival after ECPR.

cards.title: Operational end-of-life trajectory categories among patients who died in the emergency department: associations with resuscitative and palliative care in a five-year retrospective cohort.
cards.abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) increasingly care for patients approaching the end of life, yet the relationships between patterns of decline and final ED care remain poorly characterised. The objective was to describe the distribution of retrospectively assigned trajectory-oriented categories among ED decedents and examine associations with care processes. This single-centre retrospective cohort study included adults who died in the ED between 2018 and 2022. Categories were acute event/low comorbidity (T1), terminal malignancy or pre-existing exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care (T2), advanced chronic disease with acute decompensation (T3), frailty/dementia or high comorbidity with severe functional dependency (T4), and residual unclassified cases (T5). Primary outcomes were CPR and documented initiation of exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care; documented end-of-life recognition or discussion was secondary. Of 628 patients, 1.3% were T1, 10.8% T2, 10.0% T3, 49.4% T4, and 28.5% T5. CPR ranged from 75% in T1 to 24% in T2 and T4 (p<0.001). Exclusive palliative/comfort-focused care was initiated in 35% of T2 and 11% of T3-T5 patients (p<0.001). End-of-life recognition or discussion ranged from 12% in T1 to 51% in T2 (p=0.034). Frailty and dementia represented the main trajectory of death in the ED, while nearly one-third of patients could not be classified within the predefined categories. A pragmatic trajectory-oriented framework may help interpret observed patterns of care. However, retrospective assignment and the large residual group make these findings hypothesis-generating; prospective validation is required before decision-support use.

cards.title: Periprosthetic femoral fracture following primary hip arthroplasty : should the choice of femoral component design and fixation method vary according to the sex and age of the patient?
cards.abstract: Periprosthetic femoral fracture is a severe complication following hip arthroplasty, influenced by the design of the femoral component and the method of fixation. The aim of this study was to investigate the influence of sex and age on the risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture. We analyzed 204,041 primary hip arthroplasties from the Norwegian Arthroplasty Register and the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register (1 January 2005 to 31 December 2025). Femoral components were categorized as cemented composite beam (CB), cemented polished taper-slip (PTS), uncemented collarless (UCC-), and uncemented collared (UCC+). Cox regression analysis was used to compare the risk (adjusted hazard rate ratio (aHRR)) of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture stratified by sex and age. In males, PTS and UCC- had a nine-times higher risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture than CB. For UCC+, the risk was four times higher than CB. The risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture was increased in males aged > 65 years for UCC-; for UCC+ the risk was increased in males aged > 75 years, whereas PTS had higher risk for periprosthetic femoral fracture at all ages, compared with CB. In females, the risk of reoperation for periprosthetic femoral fracture was increased in those aged > 70 years for PTS and UCC+ compared with CB, whereas for UCC- the risk of periprosthetic femoral fracture was higher in those aged > 60 years, compared with CB. Our findings suggest that CB should be the preferred choice of femoral component, at least for males aged > 75 years and females aged > 70 years. UCC+ components were the best uncemented option, while the use of PTS components was associated with a high risk of periprosthetic femoral fracture among males of all ages.

cards.title: Outcomes of a long modular uncemented femoral stem for reconstruction in metastatic femoral disease.
cards.abstract: Cemented arthroplasty has previously been recommended for treating metastatic bone disease (MBD) around the hip. However, cementing has disadvantages, including restricted femoral component length, loosening due to disease progression, and bone cement implantation syndrome (BCIS). A long uncemented implant spanning the whole femur could negate these disadvantages; however, there is a paucity of data regarding their use. Our aim was to assess the outcomes of a long uncemented femoral component in MBD. A total of 205 patients with MBD underwent femoral reconstruction using the Restoration Modular Revision Hip System Plasma stem between January 2008 and December 2025. They were identified from the prospectively collected database of a tertiary MBD service. Any patient with symptomatic bone metastases involving the acetabulum or femur, with completed or impending pathological fracture, were included. The primary endpoint was reintervention for femoral implant failure, with exclusion of reintervention for deep infection and/or instability. Indications for surgery included pathological fracture (46 of 205; 22%) or lesions at risk of fracture (78%; n = 159). The mean follow-up was 45 months (12 to 131). A total of 140 patients (68%) died during the study period (mean 20 months (0.1 to 128) postoperatively). The mean distance from the centre of the femoral head to the most distal femoral metastasis was 126 mm (5 to 369). Using death as a competing risk, two-year probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and probability of death was 0.507 (95% CI 0.436 to 0.577). At five years, probability of reintervention was 0.010 (95% CI 0.000 to 0.025) and the risk of death was 0.703 (95% CI 0.629 to 0.776). Overall complication rate requiring further surgery was 8% (16 out of 205) with three reinterventions for femoral implant failure (all periprosthetic femoral fractures). This implant demonstrates promising short- to mid-term survivorship, with no patient requiring femoral revision for loosening and a comparatively low complication rate. A long uncemented femoral component may be an appropriate option in selected patients presenting with symptomatic bone metastases around the hip.

cards.title: Senescent Mesenchymal Stromal Cells Drive Stem Cell Aging Through Dysregulated Chemokine Synthesis.
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Aging is accompanied by a progressive decline in tissue regenerative capacity, driven by intrinsic stem cell dysfunction and age‐associated deterioration of the surrounding stem cell niche. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are ubiquitous components of stem cell niches, where they integrate structural, metabolic, inflammatory, and paracrine cues to regulate stem cell quiescence, activation, and differentiation. With age, MSCs undergo functional decline and senescence, altering their secretory and signaling profiles. Across tissues, MSC senescence emerges as an intermediate amplifier of aging: molecular, metabolic, epigenetic, and inflammatory stressors promote the senescent state, which converts these upstream insults into chemokine imbalance, chronic inflammation, and progressive loss of stem cell support. Here, we synthesize classical and emerging literature to examine how age‐associated changes in MSC chemokine synthesis contribute to stem cell aging, and we propose a synthesis‐based model in which MSCs translate age‐associated stressors into altered chemokine repertoires that disrupt stem cell‐supportive signaling. We also discuss therapeutic strategies, including chemokine‐directed therapies, senolytics, and MSC rejuvenation, that may restore regenerative capacity by normalizing MSC‐derived signals. Together, the evidence identifies dysregulated chemokine synthesis as a conserved mechanism linking tissue‐resident MSC aging to declining regenerative capacity.

cards.title: Peripheral and Placental KLRG1+ Senescence-Associated T Cells in Placenta Accreta Spectrum: Diagnostic and Clinical Correlations.
cards.abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) disorders are considered to be iatrogenic conditions. There is growing evidence for the role of T cell senescence in the pathophysiology of pregnancy complications. This study aimed to investigate peripheral and placental CD4/CD8 T cell subsets and senescence-associated/highly differentiated T cell frequencies in PAS and to explore their diagnostic performance and correlations with clinical, inflammatory, and proliferative (Ki-67) parameters. Placental tissue and maternal peripheral blood were obtained from PAS pregnancies and controls in their third trimester. Flow cytometric immunophenotyping was conducted for peripheral blood and placental CD4/CD8 T cell subsets, senescence-associated subsets, and their KLRG1 expression intensity. Immunohistochemical analysis of Ki-67 expression in placental tissue of subjects and controls was performed. PAS placental tissue showed an increase in CD28-CD57+ senescence-associated, KLRG1+ senescence-associated T cells, and KLRG1 MFI within all T-cell compartments. KLRG1 MFI increased progressively toward senescence-associated (CD28-CD57+) T cell phenotypes across all T-cell lineages in PAS placental tissue. In contrast, analysis of KLRG1+ percentages in PAS PB revealed limited, largely non-significant dysregulation of T cells. Ki-67 expression correlated positively with senescence-associated DP T cells and KLRG1+ senescence-associated CD4+ Th cells cells, linking the possible association of trophoblastic proliferation with T-cell senescence. This is the first study analyzing senescence-associated T cell subsets in PAS patients as well as the previously unexplored double-positive and double-negative lineages. Localized immunosenescence at the implantation site may contribute to the pathogenesis of PAS. Senescence-associated T-cell signatures show promise as exploratory tissue-based indicators of the immune dysregulation in PAS.

cards.title: Impact of body composition on toxicity and response in patients with advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma treated with BV-AVD.
cards.abstract: BV-AVD (brentuximab vedotin, doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine) has improved outcomes in advanced-stage Hodgkin lymphoma (ASHL); however, toxicity such as peripheral neuropathy (PN) remains a concern. Previous studies in oncology have demonstrated an association between sarcopenia and chemotoxicity. Therefore, we examined the effects of body composition parameters, including skeletal muscle (SM), subcutaneous fat (SF), and visceral fat (VF), along with quantitative biomarkers including metabolic tumor volume (MTV), on PN, treatment response, and progression-free survival. This study retrospectively reviewed the baseline, interim, and end-of-treatment (EOT) positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PET-CT) for 39 patients with ASHL treated with BV-AVD and assessed changes in MTV and body composition. MTV declined significantly from baseline to interim PET and EOT PET-CT (EOT PET), with no significant difference between the latter time points, indicating an early treatment response. SM:VF and SF:VF ratios followed a similar pattern, suggesting that changes in body composition including SM loss (sarcopenia) and changes in fat distribution (SF:VF), occurred early during treatment. Patients with stable SM:VF ratios were more likely to achieve a complete response (CR), whereas larger changes in SM:VF and SF:VF ratios and an early increase in VF were associated with failure to achieve CR, possibly due to increased inflammation. Stage IV disease and higher MTV were both associated with increased PN and may reflect the wider distribution of BV and an amplified inflammatory response. These findings demonstrate that body composition and PET-CT indices are relevant biomarkers in ASHL, and their integration with MTV may enhance risk stratification and deepen our understanding of toxicity risk.

cards.title: Optimizing Volar Lunate Facet Fracture Fixation: Finite Element Analysis and Cadaveric Testing.
cards.abstract: Volar lunate facet (VLF) fractures are prone to loss of reduction after volar plating. We used finite element analysis (FEA) and cadaveric testing to identify failure mechanisms and determine how screw configuration alters load transfer. A CT-derived radius model with a 10 × 15 × 5-mm VLF fragment was fixed with a 4-hole hook plate using locking and nonlocking (NL) screws. A 500-N radiolunate compressive load was applied, and von Mises stresses were quantified. Sensitivity analyses varied loading, bone density, fracture characteristics, and implant material. Ten distal radii underwent cyclic loading followed by load-to-failure testing; failure modes and locations were compared with FEA hotspots. FEA identified two stress concentrations: the distal plate contour/screw-hole region and the ulnar hook insertion into the VLF fragment. In the baseline 1[NL]&3[NL] construct, peak construct and radius stresses were 697.2 and 154.6 MPa. The 1[NL]&2[NL] configuration produced the lowest stresses (54.5 and 27.3 MPa), whereas locking hole 3 reduced construct stress to 587.2 MPa. Cadaver failure load was 1239.2 ± 438.5 N (range: 630.0-1990.1 N); failures were loss of reduction/fracture dislocation (4/10) or plate failure (6/10), with failure locations corresponding to FEA hotspots. Off-axis loading, reduced bone density, and fracture-line translation increased construct stress and altered hotspot location. FEA-predicted hook-fragment stress corresponded to loss of reduction, whereas distal plate stress corresponded to plate failure. Among modeled configurations, 1[NL]&2[NL] minimized construct and radius stress, although unbalanced cadaveric groups preclude claims of clinical superiority. These findings support fragment capture while minimizing distal plate stress.

cards.title: Nanoparticle delivery systems for gene therapy of degenerative musculoskeletal diseases.
cards.abstract: Degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs) are a group of chronic conditions characterized by the progressive deterioration of tissue structure and function, primarily affecting the articular cartilage, bones, tendons, and ligaments. With global aging populations, the rising prevalence of these disorders presents a growing public health challenge. Current treatments for DMDs are limited by substantial drug side effects and restricted therapeutic efficacy. Gene therapy has emerged as a promising alternative for addressing these conditions. Nanoparticles are essential for overcoming intracellular and extracellular barriers in nucleic acid delivery. Recent technological advances have led to novel nanomaterials and strategies, which have enabled safer and more efficient gene therapy. This review comprehensively analyzes the role of nanoparticle delivery systems in enabling effective gene-based interventions for major DMDs. First, we analyze the main gene therapies for various DMDs. Next, we systematically summarize recent advances in nanocarrier platforms and delivery strategies targeting osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, intervertebral disc degeneration, and tendon diseases. Finally, we discuss key challenges and future directions, offering a roadmap to advance nanoparticle delivery therapeutics toward clinical impact. This synthesis uniquely bridges nanoparticle delivery design with disease-specific pathophysiology, providing strategic guidance for overcoming translational barriers through emerging technologies including AI-driven carrier optimization and organ-on-chip platforms. Across these diseases, no carrier is universally optimal: systemic bone delivery prioritizes circulation stability and cell-selective targeting, whereas local delivery to cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons requires a balance among tissue retention, matrix penetration, cellular uptake, and controlled release. Current evidence remains predominantly preclinical and frequently demonstrates tissue accumulation without fully establishing intact-cargo delivery, functional target engagement, long-term safety, or manufacturability. This review therefore links nanoparticle design to disease-specific barriers and identifies the evidence required for clinical translation. The Translational Potential of this Article. This review focuses on the clinical translational potential of nanoparticle-based delivery systems for gene therapy in degenerative musculoskeletal diseases (DMDs). Addressing the unique physiological and pathological barriers of specific musculoskeletal tissues (such as bone, cartilage, intervertebral discs, and tendons), this article systematically summarizes targeting and sustained-release strategies designed to enhance delivery efficiency and overcome tissue-specific obstacles. Furthermore, this study highlights future perspectives, including artificial intelligence (AI)-driven carrier optimization, organ-on-a-chip models, and multimodal combination therapies integrating biomaterials and cells. By addressing the limitations of conventional therapies that merely alleviate symptoms without reversing tissue degeneration, this review provides a robust theoretical foundation and a clear translational roadmap for the development of precise, safe, and long-lasting gene therapy regimens for DMDs.

cards.title: Dual-stent decompression of an extensive orthokeratinized odontogenic cyst: a case report and technical innovation.
cards.abstract: Orthokeratinized odontogenic cyst (OOC) is a rare developmental entity with a low recurrence rate in pediatric patients, voluminous cysts can compromise mandibular integrity and displace teeth, necessitating conservative management to preserve vital structures. We report an extensive mandibular OOC in a 12-year-old female managed via a dual-stent decompression strategy. A 12-year-old female presented with an 8-cm midline-crossing OOC involving both mental foramina. To minimize risks of nerve damage and pathologic fracture, a two-stage protocol was initiated. Initial decompression was performed with a single stent; however, to optimize the drainage gradient across the midline, a dual-stent modification was implemented. This dynamic adjustment appeared to facilitate significant centripetal bone apposition over 8 months. The resulting volume reduction allowed for definitive enucleation under local anesthesia, completed within a 30-minute operative window to ensure pediatric cooperation. Histopathology confirmed OOC. Serial radiographic monitoring over 32 months demonstrated complete bone regeneration, spontaneous repositioning of incisors, and no recurrence. To our knowledge, this represents one of the first reported cases of dual-stent decompression in pediatric oral surgery. This technique may facilitate conservative intervention for extensive odontogenic cysts in children, supporting optimal healing, preservation of neurovascular integrity, and minimal morbidity while respecting pediatric behavioral management constraints.

cards.title: Cardiac-specific Lmpt knockdown induces heart dysfunction via mitochondrial quality decline and metabolic disturbance in Drosophila.
cards.abstract: Lmpt (Limpet, CG42679) is a Drosophila LIM domain protein homologous to human FHL2. Our prior work demonstrated it represses Wnt signaling during embryonic cardiac development. However, its role in adult cardiac homeostasis remains unclear. Here, we generated Hand-gal4-driven Lmpt knockdown flies (predominantly targeting adult cardiomyocytes) using the Hand-gal4/UAS-RNAi system and examined its function in adult flies. Lmpt knockdown significantly reduced climbing ability and triggered intrinsic cardiac contractile dysfunction, manifested as bradycardia, impaired fractional shortening and prolonged diastolic intervals in 3-week-old flies. These flies also exhibited systemic metabolic disorders and ATP depletion, decreased lipid accumulation in multiple tissues, and elevated ROS levels in the heart and gut. Meanwhile, Lmpt knockdown led to disorganized and fractured myocardial fibers and progressive age-dependent mitochondrial quality decline. qPCR analysis revealed abnormal expression of genes related to mitochondrial dynamics, respiratory chain, and quality control. In conclusion, Lmpt maintains adult cardiac function by preserving mitochondrial quality, energy metabolism, and myocardial structural integrity. This study provides new insights into the mitochondrial and metabolic mechanisms maintaining adult cardiac homeostasis, with potential implications for FHL2-related cardiomyopathies.

cards.title: Integration of network pharmacology, deep learning, and molecular biology reveals the efficacy of Citrus aurantium L. var. amara Engl. blossom extract in ameliorating diabetic osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Diabetic osteoporosis (DOP) is a type of metabolic bone disease. Blossom of Citrus aurantium L. var. amara Engl. (CAVA), a medicinal and edible herb widely employed in China which can alleviate indigestion and replenish qi, has been demonstrated to be effective in treating metabolic disorders such as obesity and diabetes. However, its effects on DOP remains uncertain. To explore the protective effects and mechanisms of blossom of CAVA against DOP. Ethanol extract of blossom of CAVA (CAVAE) was characterized using HPLC/MS. Network pharmacology, deep learning, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were employed to predict key constituents and possible pathways. High-fat diet and streptozocin-induced type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mice were established and Micro-CT, X-ray imaging, morphological analysis and molecular biology assays were performed to investigate the effects and underlying mechanisms of CAVAE on DOP. The 44 compounds identified by HPLC/MS analysis suggest that CAVAE may prevent DOP via PI3K/AKT and Wnt/β-catenin pathways. Experimental validation demonstrated that CAVAE significantly improved diabetes and osteoporosis in T2DM mice, as evidenced by the decreased blood glucose content, increased bone mineral density, enhanced trabecular bone number, improved femoral bone microstructure, restored femur stability, bone metabolism and reduced serum calcium ion levels, etc. Mechanistic investigations further confirmed that CAVAE probably alleviated DOP in T2DM mice by modulating PI3K/AKT and Wnt-3a/β-catenin pathways. CAVAE might exert anti-osteoporotic effects on T2DM mice through concurrent activation of PI3K/AKT and Wnt-3a/β-catenin pathways.

cards.title: Unraveling the shared genetic architecture of metabolic bone diseases via genomic structural equation modeling and multi-omics integration.
cards.abstract: The shared genetic etiology underlying the comorbidity of skeletal degeneration and metabolic dysregulation remains poorly understood. This study aims to decipher the pleiotropic genetic architecture of multivariate metabolic bone diseases (mvMBDs) through an integrative summary-statistics framework. We applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling (Genomic SEM) to integrate genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics for six complex traits: osteoporosis (OP), chronic kidney disease (CKD), type 2 diabetes (T2D), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), high-density lipoprotein (HDL), and C-reactive protein (CRP). Subsequent analyses incorporated robust fine-mapping (SuSiE/FINEMAP), transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), and partitioned heritability assessments to identify putative functional loci and regulatory mechanisms. Genomic SEM revealed significant genetic covariance among the six traits, successfully deriving a latent mvMBD construct. We identified 197 genomic risk loci, including 193 lead SNPs that did not achieve genome-wide significance in the six constituent univariate GWAS, predominantly localized in non-coding cis-regulatory elements (e.g., super-enhancers and intronic regions). Fine-mapping and TWAS prioritized critical pleiotropic genes (e.g., MACF1, CETP, SPP1, and HNF1A). Gene-set enrichment analyses identified enrichment for terms related to bone biology, lipid metabolism, and inflammation. Our findings robustly demonstrate that mvMBDs are not isolated clinical entities but rather interconnected systemic syndromes underpinned by glycolipid metabolic dysregulation and shared pleiotropic regulatory networks. This study establishes a novel theoretical paradigm for the genetic basis of metabolic bone diseases, offering promising functional targets for future precision medicine interventions.

cards.title: The surgical outcome among children with congenital pseudoarthrosis of Tibia: Our 12 years of experience.
cards.abstract: Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT) is a rare condition characterized by poorly perfused, invasive hamartomatous fibrous tissue that leads to fracture and pseudoarthrosis of the tibia. Management challenges include achieving union and preventing refractures. This study aims to evaluate surgical interventions and their outcomes in managing congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia in children. This retrospective study reviewed 70 CPT cases treated between 2010 and 2022 at Nepal's only specialized center for children with physical disabilities. It assessed demographics, surgical procedures, and outcomes, with techniques including periosteal grafting and the Masquelet method. Union was defined radiologically, and analyses were conducted using MS Excel and SPSS. This study included 70 CPT patients; 40 male (57.1%) and 30 female (42.9%). The mean age at presentation was 3.84 years, with the first surgery at 5.38 years. Most cases were Boyd type 5 (71.43%) and Crawford type 4 (71.43%). Of 35 patients who underwent surgery, the union rate was 41.93% (13/31), with a refracture rate of 23.08% among unions. Periosteal grafting had a 50% union rate, while the Masquelet technique achieved 41.67%. This study highlights the challenges in managing Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT), emphasizing the need for personalized surgical approaches based on patient age, limb length discrepancy, and classification. Effective patient counseling on risks and benefits is crucial for informed decisions.

cards.title: Co-designing a post-discharge intervention to improve mobility recovery among patients with lower limb fractures using human-centered design in greater Kampala, Uganda.
cards.abstract: Lower limb fractures are a major cause of functional limitation and require coordinated post-discharge care to support recovery and prevent complications. In low- and middle-income countries, including Uganda, continuity of care after discharge is often limited by health system constraints, socioeconomic barriers, and community barriers. This study aimed to co-design a post-discharge intervention to improve recovery among patients with lower limb fractures in Greater Kampala, Uganda, using a Human-Centered Design (HCD) approach. A qualitative exploratory study guided by the HCD participatory and iterative framework was conducted between July and December 2025. Stakeholders including healthcare providers, community health workers, patients, and caregivers participated in focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and in-depth interviews to explore their experiences, needs, and challenges related to post-discharge care. Stakeholders subsequently participated in an iterative co-design process to prioritize and refine intervention components. Data were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed thematically using NVivo version 15. Several interconnected barriers to post-discharge care were identified, including discontinuity of care after hospital discharge, inadequate discharge information, transportation challenges, community and family influences on treatment decisions, use of traditional bone setters, and health-system limitations. Through the co-design process, stakeholders proposed intervention strategies comprising structured discharge preparation, improved documentation of patient and caregiver contact information, strengthened linkages between health facilities and community health workers, community-based follow-up, and decentralized follow-up services at lower-level health facilities. Health-system and community-level factors influenced post-discharge care among patients with lower limb fractures. The study co-designed an integrated facility-community intervention comprising structured discharge processes, strengthened community health worker linkages, and community-based follow-up. Further studies should evaluate the feasibility and effectiveness of the intervention in improving post-discharge care and recovery outcomes.

cards.title: Senescence markers diverge in space, timing, and phenotypic relevance during skin aging in mice.
cards.abstract: The cell theory of aging posits that senescent cells accumulate with age, altering their environment and causing functional organ decline. The dynamics of their accumulation during normal aging and the extent to which it contributes to age-associated damage and disease remain unclear. Using the Study of Longitudinal Aging in Mice, which tracks two strains in both sexes, we identified skin health as a strong predictor of frailty. Quantification of three canonical senescence-associated markers (p16, p21, and γH2AX) in the skin of 320 animals showed variable effects of age on marker abundance: p16 increased with age, whereas p21 and γH2AX showed little or nonuniform changes. Associations between marker burden and age-related phenotypes were highly heterogeneous and varied by marker, sex, and strain. These findings underscore a complex, context-dependent relationship between senescence-associated markers and aging phenotypes, challenging the view that senescent cell accumulation uniformly drives organ decline.

cards.title: Conditions for runaway ruptures during reservoir operations: Magnitude-frequency distribution implications and application to Groningen.
cards.abstract: We present a theoretical analysis of an induced seismic rupture propagating from a gas reservoir into the underburden. We use linear elastic fracture mechanics to determine the conditions for self-arrested or runaway ruptures. We derive a phase diagram in which the model parameters (the reservoir thickness, the reservoir pressure depletion, background stress, and fracture energy) are combined into two dimensionless parameters. We apply the analysis to the seismicity induced by gas extraction from the Groningen gas field, where earthquakes have remained confined to the close vicinity of the reservoir. We invert the observations for the model parameters. They indicate subcritical initial stress on the underburden faults, meaning that runaway ruptures are possible in principle, but the conditions required for such events to have happened were most likely not met in reality. The model reproduces the spatial and temporal patterns of observed maximum earthquake magnitudes, and the significant deficit of M > 3.0 events compared to the expectation from the Gutenberg-Richter relationship. This tapering implies that the expected maximum magnitude is nearly insensitive to the total number of induced earthquakes and strongly controlled by the reservoir thickness and pressure depletion. Because the forecast is probabilistic and accounts for uncertainties in the model parameters, it does not exclude runaway ruptures; but such events are found to be unlikely. The model offers an operational framework to forecast earthquake magnitudes by constraining the physical model with measurable parameters.

cards.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake.
cards.abstract: Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude (Mw) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four Mw 7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

cards.title: Bilobetin Restores a TFRC-ACSL4 Ferro-Aging Barrier to Restrain Nickel-Refining Fume-Induced Bronchial Epithelial Transformation.
cards.abstract: Nickel-refining fumes (NiRF) are occupational inhalation hazards associated with lung carcinogenesis. We investigated whether TFRC-ACSL4-associated lipid oxidation and senescence contribute to bronchial epithelial adaptation during chronic NiRF exposure and whether bilobetin modulates these responses. Transcriptomic and machine-learning analyses, single-cell localization, human and mouse lung tissues, and a 180-day exposure model using the human bronchial epithelial cell line BEAS-2B were integrated. Chronic NiRF exposure reduced TFRC, ACSL4 and senescence-associated markers and increased colony formation, invasion, migration and anchorage-independent growth. TFRC or ACSL4 overexpression partially restored senescence-associated phenotypes. Ferrostatin-1 attenuated the increase in p53 and p21 abundance accompanying TFRC overexpression. Bilobetin partially restored TFRC-ACSL4/p21-associated protein expression and reduced transformation-associated behaviors. CETSA showed altered TFRC thermal stability after bilobetin treatment, supporting cellular target engagement. TFRC knockdown attenuated the bilobetin-associated lipid-oxidation pattern in the four-group experiment. These findings support a role for TFRC-ACSL4-associated cellular responses in chronic NiRF exposure and identify bilobetin as a candidate modulator.

cards.title: Network Analysis of Intergenerational Support and Social Frailty Among Older Adults With Chronic Diseases.
cards.abstract: To examine the item-level associations between intergenerational support and social frailty using network analysis. Existing evidence suggests that intergenerational support is negatively associated with social frailty. However, little is known about how specific components of intergenerational support relate to individual elements of social frailty. Network analysis offers a useful approach for examining these item-level interconnections. A cross-sectional survey. A total of 518 older adults with chronic diseases were recruited through convenience sampling from three hospital districts of a tertiary general hospital in Guangzhou, China, between December 2023 and October 2024. Intergenerational support and social frailty were measured using the Intergenerational Support Scale and the Social Frailty Index Scale, respectively. Network analysis was conducted to estimate and characterize the network structure linking intergenerational support and social frailty. The study was reported following the STROBE checklist. The network analysis identified SF3 (No confidant) and SF7 (Socioeconomic deprivation) as the most central nodes. IS3 (Children listen), IS7 (Financial support from children), and SF7 (Socioeconomic deprivation) showed potential bridging roles between intergenerational support and social frailty. No significant gender difference was observed in global network strength; however, the overall network structure differed between men and women. This study characterized the item-level associations between intergenerational support and social frailty among older adults with chronic diseases. Interventions targeting key central and potential bridge nodes may help strengthen intergenerational support and mitigate social frailty. No patient or public contribution. These findings provide insights for nursing practice by identifying potentially important aspects of intergenerational support and social frailty. Nurses may consider assessing intergenerational support and socioeconomic disadvantage when evaluating social frailty, facilitating intergenerational communication, and connecting socially vulnerable older adults with appropriate resources. In addition, exploratory gender-specific findings suggest the potential value of considering gender differences in the manifestation of social frailty among older adults.
