cards.title: Comparative phylogenomics reveals multilevel genomic differentiation between annual and perennial Hordeum species
cards.abstract: Annual plants complete their life cycle with a single reproductive episode, whereas perennials must balance reproduction with the maintenance of tissues that sustain future growth. Despite the fundamental importance of this distinction, the genomic differences associated with these contrasting life histories remain poorly understood. Here, we utilize independent occurrences of annuality in the grass genus Hordeum to identify recurrent differences between annual and perennial species. Combining transcriptomes from 82 accessions with recently published reference genomes, we compared protein-coding sequence evolution, gene copy number, gene expression and co-expression while accounting for evolutionary non-independence. We found widespread genomic differentiation, with several consistent patterns. Genes involved in cell division and genome maintenance showed evidence of stronger evolutionary constraint in perennials, while gene families associated with developmental regulation and senescence were more frequently retained in higher copy numbers in perennials. Differences in gene expression and coordination were particularly pronounced during reproduction, when perennials showed higher expression of genes involved in cell division, cytoskeletal organisation, cell-wall formation and resource transport, together with extensive reorganisation of gene co-expression relationships. Across these complementary analyses, processes involved in cellular proliferation, developmental regulation and tissue maintenance repeatedly distinguished the two life histories. Our findings suggest that annual-perennial differentiation extends beyond individual flowering regulators to broader genomic differences associated with a more complex coordination of processes balancing growth and senescence in perennials. By identifying these recurrent patterns across evolutionary lineages, this study provides a comparative framework for understanding the genomic differentiation underlying contrasting plant life histories.

cards.title: Hip Fracture Is Associated With Major Wealth Loss.
cards.abstract: The annual cost of hip fractures exceeds $6 billion in the United States. Although the direct healthcare costs related to these fractures are known, the full economic impact on individual families is not well studied. Understanding the economic impacts of disease informs policy and interventions. Therefore, we studied the socioeconomic effect of hip fractures on individual household wealth. Data were sourced from the Health and Retirement Study, a longitudinal panel survey. Individuals who sustained a hip fracture between 2000 and 2016 were identified, and total household wealth was tracked from 2 years before the fracture to 4 years after. Cases were matched with controls using propensity score matching based on age, sex, race, and initial wealth. Wilcoxon rank-sum and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used to evaluate wealth changes due to the non-normal data distribution. Median wealth declined by 50% after hip fractures. In contrast, the controls' median wealth remained relatively stable, decreasing by 4.8%. Cases had significantly less wealth after 4 years than controls (P = 0.025) and compared with their prefracture levels (P < 0.001). Most wealth loss in cases was due to declines in cash accounts and the value of the primary residence. The middle tertile of initial wealth was most affected, experiencing an approximately 50% decrease. Cases saw decreased stability in permanent housing, and cases without spouses faced an approximately 28% greater decrease in household wealth compared with those with spouses. Hip fractures are associated with substantial household wealth reductions, comparable with the financial burden of major illnesses such as cancer. These findings highlight the enormous value of hip fracture prevention and rapid hip fracture recovery. Sustaining a hip fracture is associated with losing half of household wealth, comparable with the amount lost by people who have cancer.

cards.title: Gamified spatial‑participatory model for urban social cohesion in a post‑conflict city: Bridging accessibility, inclusion, and intergroup trust through co‑design in Kabul.
cards.abstract: Post‑conflict cities exhibit profound socio‑spatial fractures, institutional weakness, and eroded public trust. Conventional planning repeatedly fails to address ethnic segregation, accessibility disparities, and social fragmentation. The aim of this study is to propose and empirically validate an integrated model, the Gamified Spatial-Participatory Model (GSPM), that combines spatial justice theory, participatory co-design, and conflict-sensitive gamification to foster social cohesion. Using Kabul, Afghanistan, as a paradigmatic case, a sequential mixed‑methods design was employed. Quantitative spatial diagnostics mapped severe accessibility deficits, while qualitative inquiry identified deep trust deficits and cultural barriers; these jointly informed gamified co‑design workshops as the intervention. Pilot results provide strong preliminary evidence of GSPM efficacy: 90% of participants reported substantially increased engagement; gamification correlated strongly with intergroup trust (r = 0.76, p < 0.01); perceived accessibility improved by 38% in intervention areas. Critically, 70% of women and 55% of ethnic minorities reported meaningfully stronger belonging. The study demonstrates that this approach shifts planning epistemology from technocratic to deeply human, operationalising spatial justice in fragile settings, and offers transferable principles for fostering inclusion in divided urban contexts.

cards.title: Vitamin D deficiency is associated with higher frailty risk among middle-aged and older adults: a national population-based analysis of NHANES 2007-2018.
cards.abstract: Although frailty is common in older adults, the relationship between vitamin D and frailty remains unclear. Using NHANES data, this study examined the association between frailty and serum vitamin D in middle-aged and older adults. Eight thousand and sixty-four participants aged 40 and older from NHANES (2007-2018) underwent cross-sectional analysis. Serum vitamin D was categorized as deficiency (<25 nmol/L), insufficiency (25-50 nmol/L), or adequate (≥50 nmol/L). Frailty was quantified using a 49-item Frailty Index (FI) based on the cumulative deficit model; frailty was defined as FI ≥ 0.21. Logistic regression and restricted cubic splines were used. The deficiency group had the highest frailty prevalence (55.9%), followed by insufficiency (42.9%) and adequate (37.2%). Frailty was significantly associated with deficiency (OR 2.15, 95% CI 1.42-3.25) after full adjustment, whereas insufficiency was not significantly associated with frailty (OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.95-1.38). Serum vitamin D and FI showed a U-shaped dose-response relationship, robust across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. In middle-aged and older adults, vitamin D deficiency, but not insufficiency, is associated with higher frailty risk. Serum vitamin D may have a U-shaped association with FI. Monitoring vitamin D levels may help inform frailty management in aging populations.

cards.title: Association between pancreatic ectopic fat deposition and QCT-assessed bone mass status in patients with chronic kidney disease: a cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are at increased risk of bone abnormalities. Beyond disturbances in mineral metabolism, ectopic fat deposition may also be associated with skeletal abnormalities in CKD. However, the relationship between pancreatic fat and bone mass status remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between mean pancreatic fat fraction and quantitative computed tomography (QCT)-assessed bone mass status in patients with CKD. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 327 patients with CKD. Vertebral volumetric bone mineral density was measured using QCT to classify bone mass status as normal bone mass, osteopenia, or osteoporosis. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was quantified from CT images. Ordinal logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate its association with bone mass status. Mean pancreatic fat fraction was highest in patients with osteoporosis (p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted model, each 5-percentage-point increase in mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with higher odds of a more severe bone mass category (OR = 1.481, 95% CI: 1.152-1.905, p = 0.002). RCS analysis showed a significant overall association (p = 0.009), with no evidence of nonlinearity (p = 0.290). No statistically significant interactions were detected for sex, age, diabetes status, or CKD stage. A higher mean pancreatic fat fraction was associated with more severe bone mass categories in patients with CKD after adjustment for the measured covariates. QCT-based pancreatic fat assessment may provide additional information on metabolic features associated with bone mass abnormalities in CKD.

cards.title: Dermatological complications after orthopedic casting of upper and lower extremities in a pediatric population: a single-center prospective study.
cards.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the incidence of dermatological complications after casting of upper and lower extremities in relation to moisture exposure and dermatological history. Eligible pediatric patients (≤18 years old) who presented for their first scheduled cast removal were evaluated for dermatological complications. Demographics, injury details, water/sweat exposure, and history of skin conditions were retrospectively collected. Chi-square analyses assessed associations between moisture exposure and dermatological history with skin complications. Of 200 patients (average age = 8.18 years; 56.5% male), 59.5% experienced forearm fractures, and 50% had long arm casts. Other casts included short arm (19.5%), short leg (3%), long leg (10%), thumb spica (3.5%), ulnar gutter (13%), and other (0.5%). Thirty-one patients (15.5%) had dermatologic findings, ranging from mild erythema (n = 24) and pruritus (n = 8) to more serious complications of maceration (n = 2) and blistering (n = 1). Moisture exposure (n = 17) was significantly associated with skin complications (P < 0.001). Having a history of atopic dermatitis (n = 13), psoriasis (n = 1), or urticaria (n = 1) was not significantly associated with skin complications (P = 0.21). Moisture exposure was significantly associated with skin issues, emphasizing the importance of family education on cast care and moisture avoidance. No significant association was found with preexisting dermatological conditions, suggesting standardized skin assessments are warranted for all cast removals.

cards.title: Longistylin C protects against glucocorticoid-induced osteo-porosis by preserving BMSC osteogenic function through redox homeostasis and mitochondrial homeostasis.
cards.abstract: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) is characterized by impaired bone formation and increased bone loss. Longistylin C (LLC), a natural stilbene isolated from Cajanus cajan leaves, has diverse biological activities, but its effects on GIOP remain unclear. This study investigated its bone-protective effects and underlying mechanisms. A dexamethasone (DEX)-induced rat model of GIOP was used to evaluate LLC by micro-computed tomography, histological analysis, serum bone turnover markers, and Cleaved caspase-3 immunohistochemistry. In vitro, DEX-treated rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) were assessed using osteogenic differentiation assays, ROS detection, JC-1 staining, Annexin V/PI flow cytometry, Western blotting, and RT-qPCR. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were also performed. LLC ameliorated DEX-induced trabecular deterioration, improved bone metabolism, and reduced Cleaved caspase-3 expression in bone tissue. In BMSCs, LLC improved cell viability, enhanced osteogenic differentiation and mineralization, and increased RUNX2 expression. LLC also reduced ROS accumulation, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and attenuated apoptosis. Mechanistically, LLC enhanced Nrf2/HO-1 signaling, increased Bcl-2 and Mcl-1 expression, and decreased Bax and Cleaved caspase-3 expression. LLC alleviates glucocorticoid-induced bone damage by reducing oxidative stress and apoptosis, preserving mitochondrial function, and promoting osteogenic differentiation. These findings support further investigation of LLC as a potential candidate for GIOP management.

cards.title: Cellular senescence in mammary gland remodeling and breast cancer evolution: dual roles and targeting strategies.
cards.abstract: Cellular senescence is a stable cell cycle arrest accompanied by a dynamic secretory program that shapes tissue remodeling and cancer behavior. In the mammary gland, post-weaning involution transiently generates senescent epithelial cells that support immune-mediated clearance and wound-healing-like remodeling. In contrast, chronic accumulation of senescent cells accompanied by impaired immune surveillance can create a tumor-promoting environment. This review integrates mechanistic, observational, and early clinical evidence to determine how the same senescence program produces opposite outcomes in mammary remodeling and breast cancer evolution. The evidence is organized around four contextual determinants: timing, cell type, immune clearance efficiency, and local microenvironment. Based on this, we propose a three-arm intervention framework that distinguishes enhanced physiological clearance, selective elimination of pathological senescent cells, and blockade of senescence escape. Most mechanistic data currently derive from mouse models and cell lines, and direct markers of human involution-associated senescence remain lacking. Clinical evidence for senescence-targeting agents is still at an early stage, with predominantly non-oncologic endpoints.

cards.title: Effect of short-course oral dexamethasone on acute phase response following intravenous zoledronate infusion: a randomized controlled trial.
cards.abstract: Zoledronate (ZA) is a potent aminobisphosphonate used in osteoporosis treatment. A common side effect is the acute-phase response (APR), which occurs in nearly 40-50% of individuals who receive the fi rst dose. This open-label randomized trial evaluated the efficacy of short-course oral dexamethasone in reducing APR following the first ZA infusion. Participants with osteoporosis (n = 51) were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive either intravenous ZA plus oral dexamethasone 4 mg on the day of infusion (D0) and two subsequent days (D1 and D2; intervention arm) or intravenous ZA alone (control arm). Oral temperature was measured by a digital thermometer at baseline, three times daily on D0-D2, and on the morning of D3. The primary outcome was the change in temperature from baseline over 3 days, estimated using a linear mixed-effects model. Fifty participants (62% diabetes; intervention, n = 26, and control, n = 24) were included in the analysis. The between-group difference in temperature change from baseline, averaged across all post-infusion timepoints, was 0.35 °C (95% CI: 0.19 to 0.51; p < 0.001), favoring the intervention group. The intervention effect was most marked on the evening of D1 (0.99 °C [95% CI: 0.71 to 1.27]; p < 0.001). Incident fever (temperature ≥37.8 °C) occurred in 26.9% of participants in the intervention group, compared with 66.7% in the control group (p = 0.01; NNT: 2.5). Rescue paracetamol was needed more frequently in the control group (79.2% vs. 46.2%; p = 0.022). Our findings support the use of a 3-day course of oral dexamethasone to reduce post-infusion fever in first-time ZA users. CTRI/2025/01/079301.

cards.title: Exercise management for sarcopenia among older patients with mental disorders in China: a best practice implementation project.
cards.abstract: The prevalence of sarcopenia is relatively high among hospitalized elderly patients with mental disorders. Without timely assessment and intervention, their condition may progress rapidly, elevating the risk of falls. This project intended to translate evidence into practice by implementing standardized exercise management for sarcopenia in psychiatric wards, with the goals of mitigating patients' risk of falls and optimizing their quality of life. This project utilized the JBI Evidence Implementation Framework. A baseline audit was undertaken to assess current practices related to exercise management for sarcopenia in elderly patients with mental disorders, followed by analysis of the audit results. JBI's Getting Research into Practice (GRiP) tool was used to identify barriers and facilitators influencing compliance with best practices. Based on these findings, a targeted exercise management plan was implemented, and a follow-up audit was subsequently performed. The baseline audit revealed generally low compliance, with rates for all seven audit criteria falling below 20%. Through strategies such as interdisciplinary collaboration, standardized protocols, professional training, and patient education, the follow-up audit demonstrated that compliance rates for all criteria improved to more than 85%. Evidence-based, audit-driven sarcopenia exercise management strategies were implemented and systematically monitored. Key strategies for enhancing compliance included reinforcing interdisciplinary collaboration and communication, establishing a structured exercise intervention protocol, providing systematic training and competency assessment for health care professionals, and delivering clear, practical operational tools. https://links.lww.com/IJEBH/A740.

cards.title: IOF-IFCC international survey of global laboratory practices for bone status indices.
cards.abstract: Bone status indices (BSIs) are increasingly used in metabolic bone disease, yet global laboratory practices remain poorly characterized. Building on recent IOF-IFCC nomenclature and ESCEO-IOF-IFCC recommendations, we conducted an international descriptive survey of BSI practices. A cross-sectional web-based questionnaire was distributed to laboratory professionals through IFCC and IOF networks, email invitations, and professional networks. It covered assay availability, specimen type, analytical platforms, external quality assessment (EQA), reference intervals or clinical decision thresholds, reporting units, interpretation, and reimbursement. Data were analyzed descriptively after duplicate screening, consistency review, and unit standardization. We received 231 responses, including 225 with geographic information from 41 countries across six continents. Marked heterogeneity was observed in analytical platforms, specimen types, reporting units, reference intervals or decision thresholds, EQA participation, and reimbursement. Reference intervals varied considerably, even among laboratories using the same manufacturer and instrument. EQA participation was high for total alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and parathyroid hormone (PTH), but lower for β-isomerized C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (β-CTX-I) and procollagen type I N-propeptide (PINP). Adoption of β-CTX-I and PINP was incomplete, although higher among laboratories following osteoporosis patients. Access to bone-specific ALP and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase 5b remained limited. PTH testing was poorly harmonized because second- and third-generation assays were used in parallel. Vitamin D decision thresholds varied widely, and misordering of 1,25(OH)2D instead of 25(OH)D was frequently perceived. Global BSI laboratory practice remains highly heterogeneous. Harmonized units, intervals or decision thresholds, interpretative practices, EQA participation, assay access, and clinician education are needed.

cards.title: Spike Sintering Tailored to Scrap Black Mass with a Low-Defect Crystal Structure for Direct Single-Crystal Upcycling of Layered Cathode Materials.
cards.abstract: Direct upcycling of black mass into single-crystal cathodes relies on calcination for several hours. Here, spike sintering (SS) is shown to convert scrap black mass (SBM) into single-crystal cathodes with an isothermal hold of only 1 min at 1040°C. SBM permits this because its lattice remains largely intact, with a lithium deficiency of 3% and an antisite occupancy of 4.52%, comparable to 4.26% for a pristine commercial NCM523. The thermal cycle combines Li restoration and partial recovery of cation order with grain growth, which temperature accelerates exponentially. The upcycled cathode (U-NCM) forms grain-boundary-free single particles with 3.89% antisite occupancy and doubled fracture strength. Relative to the conventional 950°C 5 h protocol, SS reduces the total furnace residence time, including the ramp, from 486 to 205 min and eliminates 99.7% of the isothermal hold. In graphite pouch full cells at 4.5 V and 45°C, U-NCM retains 76.9 ± 1.5% after 350 cycles compared with 51.5 ± 15.3% for commercial polycrystalline NCM523 (three cells each). Matching the thermal protocol to the crystallographic state of the feedstock therefore enables single-crystal upcycling within a 1 min isothermal hold, demonstrated here for NCM523 scrap black mass from a single industrial source.

cards.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Highly Sensitive Hydrogel Sensors for Underwater Breaststroke Motion Recognition.
cards.abstract: Ion-conductive hydrogels hold immense promise for flexible electronics, but their inherent swelling in liquid environments severely limits amphibious applications. Herein, a highly conductive, anti-swelling hydrogel designated as PASLC was developed via the one-pot photo-initiated copolymerization of acrylic acid (AA), lauryl methacrylate (LMA), sulfobetaine methacrylate (SBMA), and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB). When the molar ratio of hydrophilic to hydrophobic monomers was optimized to 150:3, the resulting PASLC-3 hydrogel achieved optimal swelling equilibrium, with a swelling ratio of only 4% after 7 days of immersion in water. Concurrently, this microenvironment effectively mitigates ion leakage and facilitates dynamic strain-induced conductive pathways, yielding an unprecedented seawater gauge factor (GF) of up to 12.974, which surpasses the value obtained in air. Furthermore, the hydrogel exhibits excellent stretchability (751.80% fracture strain), durable multi-substrate adhesion underwater, and superior biocompatibility (97% L929 cell viability at 24 h). Benefiting from this holistic design, PASLC-3 reliably enables real-time motion monitoring and Morse code transmission even after 7 days of seawater soaking. Integrated with deep learning neural networks, this sensor precisely decodes breaststroke kinematics, providing an attractive paradigm for robust, anti-swelling amphibious human-machine interfaces.

cards.title: Cyborg dementia: could structural disembodiment accelerate brain aging via loss of muscle-bone trophic signaling? A matter of perspective
cards.abstract: Advances in brain-machine interfaces and neuroprosthetics are often framed as a path toward overcoming the biological limits of the body, with the eventual replacement of failing limbs and organs by durable artificial substitutes. Interestingly, this optimistic narrative overlooks a challenge that is becoming increasingly apparent in aging neuroscience: brain health depends critically on a continuous supply of trophic signals originating from skeletal muscle and bone. Myokines and osteokines such as irisin, uncarboxylated osteocalcin, and cathepsin B act on the brain to sustain BDNF expression, synaptic plasticity, and neurogenesis, forming what has been described as a muscle-bone-brain axis; disuse and immobilization, even in the absence of any primary brain pathology, are sufficient to disrupt this signaling and accelerate cognitive decline. This raises a largely unaddressed question for cyborg technologies: could a robotic body, mechanically capable of movement but biologically inert and secreting none of the trophic factors that living muscle and bone normally provide, deprive the brain of signals it needs to remain healthy, thereby accelerating, rather than preventing, neural aging? We term this hypothetical condition cyborg dementia. Rather than a purely engineering problem of motor control and sensory feedback, this reframes brain-machine interface design as fundamentally about preserving the endocrine dialogue between brain and musculoskeletal system, extending the goals of neuroprosthetics beyond restoring action to protecting the neuroendocrine mechanisms that biological embodiment was silently providing all along.

cards.title: Oxidative Stress‐Induced Mitochondrial Translocation of <scp>NOX4</scp> Activates <scp>PINK1</scp> /Parkin‐Mediated Mitophagy in the Pathogenesis of Sarcopenia
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Sarcopenia is characterized by progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function, which seriously affects the health of the elderly. Although oxidative stress and mitophagy dysregulation have been confirmed to be involved in the disease process, the specific regulatory mechanism remains unclear. This study reveals that nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate oxidase 4 (NOX4) plays a core role in sarcopenia by regulating mitophagy. In the H 2 O 2 ‐induced oxidative stress C2C12 myotube model, NOX4 translocation from the cytoplasm to the mitochondria was triggered, accompanied by myotube atrophy and excessive activation of PINK1/Parkin‐mediated mitophagy. Transmission electron microscopy revealed autophagosome formation and mitochondrial structural abnormalities. Gene knockdown by Nox4 siRNA significantly alleviated the decrease in mitochondrial membrane potential and reactive oxygen species accumulation caused by oxidative stress, inhibited abnormal mitophagy, and alleviated myotube atrophy. In in vivo experiments, mice with muscle atrophy induced by dexamethasone showed significant improvement in muscle mass and atrophy phenotype after intervention with the NOX4 inhibitor apocynin (Apo). Further studies found that Apo treatment effectively inhibited the level of mitophagy in muscle tissue and reduced the degree of co‐localization of NOX4 and mitochondria. Mechanistically, oxidative stress‐induced mitochondrial translocation of NOX4 drives excessive activation of PINK1/Parkin‐dependent mitophagy, ultimately leading to muscle atrophy; inhibition of NOX4 can block this process. The findings of this study reveal a new regulatory mechanism in sarcopenia and suggest that NOX4 may be a potential therapeutic target for this disease.

cards.title: Development and Biomechanical Study of Micro Anatomic Universal Locking Plate for Talus Fractures.
cards.abstract: Talar fractures are associated with high complication rates, and existing internal-fixation devices often exhibit inadequate mechanical strength and suboptimal anatomical fit. This study aimed to design a novel Micro-Anatomical Universal Locking Plate (MAULP) for talus fractures and evaluate its biomechanical performance via mechanical testing and finite element analysis (FEA). The MAULP was pre-contoured based on CT data from 30 Chinese male tali and manufactured from Ti-6Al-4 V alloy. Fifteen synthetic talus fracture models were randomly assigned to three fixation groups (n = 5 each): Group A (two cannulated screws), Group B (MAULP alone), and Group C (MAULP plus one cannulated screw). Constructs underwent cyclic loading (400 N, 0.67 Hz, 20,000 cycles) followed by static loading. Interfragmentary displacement was recorded. FEA was performed under identical conditions. Three cadaveric tali (one per group) provided qualitative validation. One-way ANOVA was used for statistical analysis. Pre-loading fracture gaps showed no significant differences among groups (p > 0.05). After cyclic loading, Group A exhibited significantly greater displacement (1.759 ± 0.042 mm) than Group B (1.359 ± 0.037 mm) and Group C (1.354 ± 0.042 mm) (both p < 0.05), with no significant difference between B and C (p > 0.05). Cadaveric trends paralleled synthetic models. FEA predictions correlated well with experiments (relative errors: 7.4%-7.8%), with the plate bearing higher stress (~0.3 MPa) than the talus (~0.1 MPa). The MAULP, with or without an additional cannulated screw, provides significantly superior biomechanical stability compared to cannulated screws alone in a talar neck fracture model. Its anatomical design offers a promising fixation option, particularly for fractures requiring enhanced stability. Clinical studies are needed to confirm these findings.

cards.title: Successful management of a proximal femoral comminuted fracture occurring after total hip arthroplasty in a small-breed dog.
cards.abstract: Medical records of a 7-year-old neutered female Chihuahua were reviewed to describe the management of a proximal femoral comminuted fracture following total hip arthroplasty (THA). The dog underwent staged bilateral THA for hip dysplasia and concurrent orthopedic disease. Twelve days after the second THA, a fall resulted in a Vancouver type B3-like periprosthetic proximal femoral fracture. Revision surgery involved femoral stem replacement and fracture stabilization using an interlocking femoral stem system. Postoperative radiographs showed appropriate implant positioning. Radiographic evidence of bone healing was observed by postoperative day 132. The fracture followed a traumatic event, although the potential contributions of implant-related stress risers and femoral preparation could not be determined. This case suggests that interlocking stem revision may be an effective treatment option for periprosthetic femoral fractures in selected small-breed dogs.

cards.title: The Piezo1 Paradox in Aging and Age-Related Disease: Bidirectional Mechanosensory Dysfunction and Therapeutic Implications
cards.abstract: Aging is accompanied by profound changes in the mechanical properties of tissues, driving cellular dysfunction, and age-related diseases. Central to this process is Piezo1, a key mechanosensitive ion channel that converts physical stimuli into intracellular Ca 2+ signals. This review synthesizes current evidence illustrating the dual, context-dependent role of Piezo1 in aging—termed the “Piezo1 Paradox.” In certain tissues such as bone and bone marrow stromal cells, aging is associated with a loss of Piezo1 function, impairing mechanotransduction, and tissue maintenance. Conversely, in vascular, fibrotic, and some metabolic tissues, aging leads to Piezo1 overactivation, promoting inflammation, fibrosis, and cellular senescence. We explore how these divergent changes contribute to prevalent age-related disorders including osteoporosis, cardiovascular disease, neurodegeneration, and metabolic dysfunction. Furthermore, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies that aim to restore Piezo1 signaling within a tissue-specific “Goldilocks zone,” highlighting pharmacological modulators, biophysical interventions, and targeted delivery systems. By framing Piezo1 as a tunable mechanosensory node, this review underscores its potential as a therapeutic target for promoting healthy aging and mitigating age-related pathologies.

cards.title: Artificial intelligence in pediatrics.
cards.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is already part of pediatric practice, particularly for triage, early detection, documentation, and point-of-care decision support. Some currently available tools perform at an expert level, including bone age estimation and fracture detection. Ambient documentation is easing a persistent burden, and language models effectively draft notes and messages. However, the evidence for the technology in pediatrics lags behind adult medicine. Of the 876 AI and machine learning (ML) enabled devices currently authorized by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), only 149 carry labeling for patients younger than 18 years, and only 19% of those report validation in children. This review article examines where AI already exists in, or is approaching, everyday pediatric use. In each domain, the discussion pairs the strength of the technology with its present limitations. Notably, strong test set statistics do not always translate into better outcomes, and few pediatric tools have been validated externally or prospectively. The reasons for that gap are examined in depth: pediatric datasets are smaller and less representative, which leaves them more prone to bias, and a child's consent binds their data for longer than an adult's. In general, the argument is neither for swift adoption nor for resistance. Instead, it is for holding the technology to a high standard, which means keeping a human in the loop and training clinicians to be exacting judges of the currently available tools.

cards.title: Orthotopic Neobladder after Radical Cystectomy: Contemporary Patient Selection, Outcomes and Survivorship.
cards.abstract: Orthotopic neobladder should be actively discussed after radical cystectomy, but it should not be framed as the routine default. The best candidates are patients in whom urethral preservation is oncologically appropriate, renal and hepatic function are adequate, cognition and manual dexterity are intact, and the patient accepts rehabilitation, nocturnal leakage risk, and the possibility of clean intermittent catheterization. Age alone should not exclude patients; frailty, limited life expectancy, major neurocognitive disease, severe baseline incontinence, and unreliable follow-up weigh more strongly in favor of an ileal conduit. Prior high-dose pelvic radiation and marginal self-management capacity call for individualized assessment rather than routine exclusion. Bowel considerations are also nuanced: severe intestinal disease or markedly limited bowel reserve may preclude bowel-based reconstruction, whereas lesser bowel concerns should be judged case by case. We do not regard orthotopic neobladder as oncologically superior to ileal conduit. Its value lies in preserving body image and urethral voiding in carefully selected patients. Counseling therefore needs to be explicit about the trade-offs-slower functional recovery, nocturnal leakage, retention, catheterization burden, and lifelong metabolic, renal, and oncologic surveillance. In women, bladder neck and urethral assessment are decisive, and pelvic organ-preserving strategies should be considered only when cancer control is not compromised. In older adults, diversion choice should follow physiologic reserve and goals of care rather than chronology alone. Overall, orthotopic neobladder remains a valuable option for motivated, well-selected patients treated in centers that can deliver reproducible reconstruction and deliberate long-term follow-up; ileal conduit remains preferable when simplicity, safety, or self-management limitations dominate the decision.

cards.title: "My first thought was, I have to get up [from the floor] and get him back to the sofa, otherwise he'll fall too": fracture patients who are informal caregivers prioritize caregiving responsibilities over fracture recovery and bone health.
cards.abstract: Patients serving as caregivers at the time of their fragility fracture prioritized their caregiver role over fracture recovery and bone health management. Caregiver burden was exacerbated by the fracture event, making it difficult for patients to maintain their caregiver role while recovering from their injury and managing their bone health. Our objectives were to examine fragility fracture patients' experience of: (1) serving as a caregiver to a family member, spouse/partner, and/or friend; and (2) managing the fracture and bone health recommendations while having caregiver responsibilities. A phenomenological (qualitative) study was conducted. Eligible patients were English-speaking males and females, 50+ years old with a fragility fracture who: (1) were Fracture Liaison Service (FLS) outpatients in an urban hospital or FLS inpatients in an urban rehabilitation hospital in Canada; and (2) reported that they were informally caring (not paid) for at least one individual (spouse, family member, friend) at the time of fracture. Patients were interviewed within six months of the fracture. Analysis was guided by Giorgi's procedures. We interviewed 25 patients (22 females, 3 males) aged 50-83 years old. Participants reported that they prioritized caregiving responsibilities over fracture recovery and bone health management. Further, the fracture added to the burden of caregiving. Participants who were able to make alternative arrangements for care recipients reported feelings of guilt and anxiety with some suggesting that the fracture pushed them to the limits as a caregiver. Our results suggest that fracture patients who are caregivers experience challenges in continuing the caregiving role as well as looking after their own bone health. It is important that patients have access to supports that will relieve their caregiver burden so that they can focus on fracture recovery and bone health.

cards.title: Small and large earthquakes driven by inelastic deformation in weak fault zones.
cards.abstract: Earthquakes manifest across a wide range of magnitudes, corresponding to a diversity of rupture sizes and amounts of slip. Classical earthquake models consider rupture processes solely on the fault plane, but the surrounding fault zone rocks can host inelastic deformation. Here, we show, via a dynamic seismic cycle model incorporating spontaneous fault zone evolution through damage and healing, that both small and large earthquakes on a single fault emerge naturally from the interplay of fault slip and fault zone inelastic deformation. Our simulations reproduce key observations: frequency-magnitude distribution consistent with the Gutenberg-Richter law, magnitude-invariant static stress drop, and the dual-regime scaling of fracture energy density with earthquake magnitude. The results underscore the coevolution of earthquakes and fault zone damage as a fundamental mechanism governing earthquake behavior in nature. Fault zone deformation causing multiscale seismicity indicates that continuous monitoring of fault zone material properties may reveal fault stress states and earthquake potential.

cards.title: A physics-informed LLM agent for uncovering typhoon- and earthquake-induced turbine failures and offline yaw-pitch countermeasures.
cards.abstract: Extreme typhoons and earthquakes can cause severe damage to wind turbine structures, underscoring the need to better understand failure mechanisms and potential mitigation strategies. This study develops Iwind, a physics-informed large language model agent for wind-turbine engineering analysis. Supported by domain-specific training and multi-path retrieval-augmented generation, Iwind combines ReAct-style reasoning with the model context protocol to invoke the in-house physics solver Zwind for natural-language-driven load simulations. In the reported evaluations, Iwind outperformed its parent model on wind-turbine knowledge tasks and supported load-simulation execution and visual damage inspection. The collected cases showed blade fractures, tower buckling, and overturning under typhoon loading, while some earthquake-damaged turbines showed more pronounced damage in foundations or lower supporting structures. Parametric Zwind simulations further revealed W- and M-shaped offline yaw-pitch response manifolds for the investigated typhoon and earthquake cases, respectively, providing simulation-derived references for parked-state comparison and hazard-region identification.

cards.title: Metabolic exhaustion underlies sarcopenic obesity susceptibility in aging mice as revealed by multi-omics factor analysis.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenic obesity (SO) affects up to 40% of older adults with obesity, yet many remain protected despite comparable metabolic burden. The molecular basis for this heterogeneity remains unknown. We exposed 12-month-old female mice to high-fat diet (HFD) or standard diet for 7 months. Multi-omics factor analysis integrated muscle transcriptomics and metabolomics to identify factors explaining phenotypic variation. Despite uniform obesity development, aging HFD mice showed marked heterogeneity in muscle outcomes. Factor 3 uniquely distinguished dietary groups and predicted muscle dysfunction independent of adiposity severity. It revealed metabolic exhaustion: lipid overload-induced upregulation of fatty acid oxidation genes and oxidative markers, long-chain acylcarnitine accumulation, and free L-carnitine depletion, indicating incomplete β-oxidation. Activation of p53, TNF/NFκB, and oxidative stress pathways indicated comprehensive metabolic decompensation. Plasma acetylcarnitine and pantothenol achieved area under curve (AUC) 0.91 for discriminating sarcopenia phenotypes. Individual susceptibility to SO reflects differential metabolic exhaustion rather than obesity severity, detectable through circulating biomarkers.

cards.title: Inhibition of asparagine endopeptidase extends the lifespan and improves health span during aging.
cards.abstract: Asparagine endopeptidase (AEP), also known as legumain, is a lysosomal cysteine protease whose activity increases with age and contributes to age-related tissue dysfunction. We tested whether chronic AEP inhibition could slow aging phenotypes in naturally aged mice. Here, we show that chronic treatment with the AEP inhibitor #11a extended lifespan and improved health span in aged C57BL/6 mice, together with reduced frailty and improved physical and cognitive performance. #11a treatment also attenuated several senescence- and inflammation-associated readouts in multiple organs. Mechanistically, #11a treatment suppressed AEP-dependent cleavage of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), accompanied by an increased NAD+/NADH ratio and higher SIRT1 levels. These findings support further investigation of pharmacological AEP inhibition as a strategy to promote healthy aging.

cards.title: Bifunctional Pt/CeO2 Nanozyme-Mediated Metabolic Regulation Promotes NAD+ Regeneration and ROS Clearance to Ameliorate Age-Related Osteoporosis.
cards.abstract: Age-related osteoporosis is characterized by progressive loss of bone mass and deterioration of trabecular microarchitecture, driven by chronic inflammation, redox imbalance, mitochondrial dysfunction, and osteoblast senescence that uncouples bone formation from resorption. During aging, declining nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) availability further exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction and stress responses, suggesting that restoring NAD+ redox homeostasis could be a viable therapeutic strategy. Here, we reported a bifunctional nanozyme-mediated metabolic regulation strategy to promote NAD+ regeneration and scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS) for the treatment of age-related osteoporosis. The bifunctional nanozyme (Pt/CeO2) was constructed by in situ growth of platinum nanoparticles on cerium oxide nanorods and was designed for ROS scavenging and NAD+ regeneration via NADH (reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) oxidation. In senescent osteoblasts, Pt/CeO2 reduced ROS, restored mitochondrial integrity, and alleviated senescence, thereby promoting osteogenic differentiation. In vivo results confirmed that systemic administration of Pt/CeO2 preserved trabecular architecture and increased bone mineral density in naturally aged mice. These findings demonstrated that coupling ROS scavenging with the restoration of NAD+ redox homeostasis via Pt/CeO2 nanozyme provided a promising therapeutic strategy to counteract osteoblast senescence and slow the progression of age-related osteoporosis.

cards.title: Clinical characteristics across graded frailty status in older public hospital outpatients: An exploratory cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: Frailty is a multidimensional geriatric syndrome, but practical clinical indicators that reflect vulnerability across graded frailty status in routine outpatient care remain insufficiently characterized. This exploratory cross-sectional study included 28 community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or older who attended outpatient clinics at a public hospital in Seoul, Republic of Korea. Frailty status was classified as robust, pre-frail, or frail using a modified Fried frailty phenotype. Physical performance, anthropometric measures, sarcopenia-related indicators, nutritional status, depressive symptoms, and cognitive function were compared across frailty status, and trends across ordered categories were examined. Multiplicity was assessed in exploratory sensitivity analyses. Pre-frail status was the most common category, with 21 pre-frail, 4 robust, and 3 frail participants. Median calf circumference was 35.4, 34.5, and 30.5 cm in the robust, pre-frail, and frail groups, respectively (unadjusted P = .038). The overall difference did not remain significant after false discovery rate adjustment (q = 0.215). Gait speed and depressive symptom scores showed descriptive variation across frailty status (unadjusted P = .065 and P = .069, respectively). Gait speed contributed directly to frailty classification, while depressive symptoms may overlap conceptually with the exhaustion criterion. Simple clinical measures, including gait performance, anthropometric measures, and depressive symptom burden, may provide descriptive information on multidimensional vulnerability across graded frailty status in older public hospital outpatients. However, these exploratory findings do not establish independent associations or demonstrate the clinical superiority of the 3-category classification.

cards.title: The causal relationship between frailty and pneumonia: A two-sample Mendelian randomization study.
cards.abstract: Epidemiological studies have revealed a relationship between frailty and pneumonia; however, the causal relationship remains controversial. This study aims to explore this relationship through Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. This study utilized large-scale genome-wide association summary data to evaluate the potential causal relationship between frailty and pneumonia through two-sample bidirectional MR analysis. The inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method was employed as the primary approach, and the robustness of the results was validated using Cochran's Q test, MR-Egger regression intercept test, and MR-PRESSO test. In the forward MR analysis, the IVW results indicated that a 1-unit increase in genetically predicted frailty on the quantile-normalized frailty-index scale was associated with higher odds of all pneumonia (odds ratio [OR] = 1.295, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.151-1.457, P < .001), bacterial pneumonia (OR = 1.346, 95% CI = 1.095-1.655, P = .005), and asthma-related pneumonia (OR = 2.044, 95% CI = 1.588-2.631, P < .001). There was no causal association between frailty and viral pneumonia (OR = 1.719, 95% CI = 0.882-3.349, P = .112); sensitivity analysis showed no heterogeneity or horizontal pleiotropy (P > .05). In the reverse MR analysis, the IVW random-effects model results indicated a causal association between asthma-related pneumonia and frailty (OR = 1.039, 95% CI = 1.014-1.065, P = .002). No causal associations were detected between all pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia, or viral pneumonia and frailty (P > .05). Heterogeneity was detected in the reverse analysis of asthma-related pneumonia, whereas the MR-Egger intercept tests provided no evidence of directional horizontal pleiotropy in the examined analyses (P > .05). This study demonstrates that frailty has a causal association with all pneumonia, bacterial pneumonia, and asthma-related pneumonia. The reverse MR results indicate that asthma-related pneumonia also increases the risk of frailty.

cards.title: Need for removal of flexible intramedullary nails used to treat femoral shaft fractures in children: an observational study of 55 children with a minimum of 5-year follow-up.
cards.abstract: Removal of flexible intramedullary nails (FIN) in children with femoral shaft fractures has been considered unnecessary when nails are left unbent flush to the bone. We aimed to evaluate the frequency and timing of nail removal on demand. This is an observational follow-up study including consecutive 3-14-year-old children with femoral shaft fractures treated during 2011-2018 with FIN. The instruction was to leave the distal ends of the nails unbent above the distal femoral physis. Alignment of the fracture and position of the nails were assessed after nailing and during follow-up. Data on nail removal rates and timing was collected with at least 5 years of follow-up. The outcomes for children with correctly placed nails were compared with those with nails that were too long, defined as cut at or below the distal femoral physis evaluated from postoperative radiographs. 55 consecutive children were included. All fractures healed in satisfactory alignment. FINs were too long in 24 patients (20 distally, 4 proximally). Hardware was removed in 37 (67%) children at a median of 2.4 years from surgery because of pain (range 0.3-9.3). Removal occurred in 21/24 of those with too long nails, and in 16/31 patients with correctly applied FIN, RR 1.7 (95% confidence interval 1.2-2.5, P = 0.005). Half of the children with unbent FIN placed flush to the bone in femoral shaft fractures had removal of nails. Extending the nail to or below the distal femoral growth plate leads to hardware removal in nearly all cases, mainly due to pain.

cards.title: PLC-γ1 promotes the formation of slow-twitch skeletal muscle fibers via increasing the expression of PGC-1α.
cards.abstract: Improving skeletal muscle strength and mass is an essential strategy to prevent and treat sarcopenia, which can be achieved by increasing the number of muscle fibers. Here, we report that phospholipase C-γ1 (PLC-γ1), a member of phospholipase C family that functions as signal transducer by hydrolyzing membrane lipids to generate second messengers, was highly expressed in skeletal muscle fibers. PLC-γ1 expression in the skeletal muscle of elderly individuals was significantly lower than that in young individuals. Conditional knockout of PLC-γ1 in the skeletal muscle in mice showed decreases in the expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1α (PGC-1α), mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, number of slow-twitch skeletal muscle fibers, and exercise endurance. Overexpression of PGC-1α rescued decreases in mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, number of slow-twitch skeletal muscle fibers, and exercise endurance induced by conditional knockout of PLC-γ1 in the skeletal muscle. These findings suggest that PLC-γ1 is required for maintaining slow-twitch fiber content and exercise endurance in mice, and that it exerts these effects by sustaining PGC-1α expression.

cards.title: The Modified Frailty Index (mFI-11) Predicts Adverse Outcomes After Surgery for Lower-Extremity Nonmelanoma Skin Cancer.
cards.abstract: The lower extremity is a high-risk site for complications after dermatologic surgery, yet validated tools for preoperative risk stratification are lacking. The 11-item modified Frailty Index (mFI-11) predicts surgical morbidity across numerous specialties but has not been studied in dermatologic surgery. To determine whether the mFI-11 predicts adverse outcomes after surgery for lower-extremity nonmelanoma skin cancer (NMSC). Retrospective review of 103 cases of biopsy-proven invasive lower-extremity NMSC treated with excision or Mohs micrographic surgery at a single academic center between 2023 and 2026. Outcomes were analyzed with cluster-robust logistic and Poisson regression. Adverse events occurred in 38% of cases, increasing monotonically across frailty categories (23% to 67%). Frail patients (≥3 mFI-11 items) had greater odds of any adverse event (67% vs 29%; OR 4.87; 95% CI 1.81-13.07), more complications per case (rate ratio 1.32 per item), longer wound-care episodes (median 48 vs 21 days), and more frequent wound-care escalation (54% vs 15%). Frailty remained independently predictive after adjustment for defect size, age, and sex (adjusted OR 1.69 per item; 95% CI 1.17-2.43). The mFI-11 is a low-cost, graded, independent predictor of adverse outcomes after lower-extremity NMSC surgery and may aid preoperative risk stratification and counseling.

cards.title: Inorganic Ionic Polymerization toward Fracture-Resistant, Self-healable Functional Hydrogels.
cards.abstract: Fracture-resistant, self-healable functional hydrogels hold promise for soft robotics, wearable electronics, and intelligent devices. However, integrating these properties within a single structure remains challenging. Persistent load-bearing constraints hinder molecular rearrangement for repair, whereas excessive network dynamics can disrupt functional organization. Here, we uncover a reciprocal assembly mechanism based on bidirectional regulation between inorganic ionic oligomers and polymer chains. The acrylic acid/poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) environment suppresses calcium carbonate oligomer (CCO) aggregation, while CCO organizes PAA chains into birefringent acicular domains through multisite coordination and cooperative hydrogen bonding. These domains provide persistent load-bearing constraints and exchangeable interactions, enabling a fracture energy of 38.3 kJ m-2 and 87% tensile-strength recovery after 6 h of ambient healing. The same assembled network further exhibits 4.5% AM1.5G solar-weighted absorptivity and strong mid-infrared emission, remaining 5.1 °C cooler than neat PAA under simulated sunlight while retaining its cooling response for 21 days. This work establishes inorganic ionic oligomers as active reciprocal regulators of polymer organization, coupling dynamic network reconstruction with mechanical reinforcement and functional stability.

cards.title: Mapping Internal Damage Fields Induced by Stress Softening in Dissipative Nanocomposite Elastomers.
cards.abstract: The pronounced stress-softening effect (SSE)─a consequence of strain-induced invisible internal damage─is a defining feature of nanocomposite elastomers. However, SSE under real-world, heterogeneous deformation remains poorly understood due to a historical focus on simple uniaxial testing. Here, we propose a methodology to quantify and map this elusive internal damage entirely within an experimental framework, operating completely independently of any specific constitutive model. By calibrating an invariant-based damage function (IDF) for a nanocomposite elastomer from cyclic loading-unloading tests across various uniform deformation modes, we convert strain fields measured by digital image correlation (DIC) into full-field internal damage maps. This DIC-IDF approach is applied to two representative two-dimensional heterogeneous deformation scenarios in thin-film geometries: (i) notch opening, and (ii) stretching with a circular defect. The former reveals teardrop-shaped damage zones that drive stress redistribution and enhance crack-growth resistance. The latter highlights a shift of the maximum SSE zone from the lateral edge to the diagonal region as the applied stretching increases. We also verify that local principal-stretch axes exhibit no substantial net rotation during these heterogeneous deformations, particularly within active damage zones, validating the scalar IDF─where the induced damage anisotropy is not explicitly incorporated─as a reasonable first-order approximation. This DIC-IDF approach provides a powerful tool for decoding SSE and elucidating the fracture and toughening mechanisms of dissipative nanocomposite elastomers.

cards.title: Long-term low-intensity vibration attenuates age-associated adipogenic bias and enhances osteogenic potential in mesenchymal stem cells
cards.abstract: Aging impairs mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) function and regenerative potential, contributing to a shift in MSCs differentiation away from osteogenesis and toward adipogenesis. This study investigated the effects of in vivo low-intensity vibration (LIV) on bone characteristics, exercise performance, and the functional, mechanical, and molecular phenotypes of bone marrow-derived MSCs from 24-month-old mice. LIV (90 Hz, 0.7 g) was initiated at 5 months and administered twice daily until 24 months. Outcomes were compared with age-matched, non-vibrated controls. LIV was associated with improved voluntary wheel-running performance, including increased running distance and velocity, alongside a trend towards increased trabecular bone volume fraction and trabecular number. MSCs isolated from LIV-treated mice (+LIV) exhibited reduced senescence marker p16 and increased Ki67 proliferation index. +LIV MSCs had increased osteogenic differentiation and mineralization along with upregulated Runx2 and Col1a1 expression. +LIV MSCs exhibited decreased adipogenic differentiation and lipid accumulation, showing downregulated Fasn and Ap2 expression. +LIV MSCs exhibited increased F-actin fiber number, altered vinculin-associated focal adhesions, and increased apparent whole-cell stiffness. Nuclear characterization revealed increased lamin A/C levels and a shift in the storage-loss crossover frequency from 68 to 94 Hz, indicating that elastic-dominant behavior persisted to a higher frequency. These mechanical changes coincided with increased global H3K4me3 and decreased H3K9me3 and H3K27me3 in +LIV MSCs. Collectively, these findings suggest that in vivo LIV is associated with enhanced osteogenic potential in aged MSCs, accompanied by coordinated changes in cytoskeletal organization, nuclear mechanics, and histone modifications, although causal relationships among these changes remain to be established.

cards.title: Icariin Ameliorates Postmenopausal Osteoporosis by Modulating Phosphodiesterase 5A-Mediated RANKL/OPG Signaling.
cards.abstract: To investigate the effects of icariin on postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP) and its underlying molecular mechanisms. A PMOP rat model was established by ovariectomy and treated with icariin alone or combined with estrogen. Bone mineral density (BMD), serum estradiol (E2), osteocalcin (OCN), and CTX-I were measured. Bone histomorphology was assessed using HE staining and immunohistochemistry. In vivo safety was evaluated by body weight, organ indices, serum ALT, AST, BUN, CREA, and liver/kidney HE staining. In vitro, a co-culture system of MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts and RAW264.7 osteoclasts was constructed to evaluate icariin's effects on osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis, with CCK-8 and lactate dehydrogenase assays for safety. Mechanisms were further explored via ALP/ARS staining, molecular docking, RT-qPCR, Western blot, dual-luciferase assays, and PDE5A knockdown/overexpression. Icariin significantly increased BMD, elevated serum E2 and OCN, reduced CTX-I, and improved trabecular microarchitecture in PMOP rats. Icariin promoted osteoblastic differentiation/mineralization while suppressing osteoclast activity in vitro. PDE5A was highly expressed in PMOP; icariin downregulated PDE5A, inhibited RANKL, and upregulated OPG, thereby blocking NF-κB activation, enhancing Runx2 and OCN expression, and reducing cathepsin K and NFATc1. PDE5A overexpression partially reversed icariin's effects. Icariin at high doses showed no hepatorenal or osteoblast toxicity in vivo or in vitro, as per serum, histopathology, and LDH. Icariin promotes osteogenesis and inhibits osteoclastogenesis by downregulating PDE5A and modulating RANKL/OPG signaling, thereby restoring bone metabolic balance and exerting osteoprotective effects against PMOP, with a synergistic action when combined with estrogen and a favorable safety profile both in vivo and in vitro.

cards.title: Sodium alginate-based environmentally stable tough ionogel sensors integrated with machine learning for high-accuracy static gesture recognition.
cards.abstract: Gel materials with exceptional mechanical property, environmental stability, and reliable sensing performance are highly desirable for intelligent human-machine interfaces. However, conventional hydrogel systems generally prone to fail under load-bearing applications due to their poor mechanics, progressive dehydration, and freezing-induced performance deterioration. Herein, we report a mechanically tough ionogel with remarkable environmental stability via a facile solvent-replacement strategy: incorporating a non-volatile halometallate ionic liquid composed of CaBr2 and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium bromide ([BMIM]Br) into a polyacrylamide/sodium alginate (PAAm/SA) hydrogel network. Synergistic coordination and ion-dipole interactions reconstructed the network structure and solvent-polymer microenvironment, facilitating efficient energy dissipation. Consequently, the optimized ionogel exhibited remarkable environmental stability and mechanical properties, including 2860% stretchability, 0.68 MPa tensile strength, 9.46 MJ/m3 toughness, and 16.02 kJ/m2 fracture energy. Moreover, the ionogel demonstrated stable electromechanical response across a broad strain range (1-500%). Benefiting from these merits, the ionogel-based sensor enabled accurate monitoring of complex human motions and achieved 99.45% recognition accuracy for eight static gestures when integrated with a machine learning algorithm. Collectively, this work provides a facile strategy for constructing environmentally stable yet mechanic tough ionogels through coordination-ionic co-regulation paradigm, offering a viable pathway towards reliable and field-deployable gel systems for wearable electronics.

cards.title: Magnetically Reconfigurable Liquid Metal Microdroplet Networks Enable High Thermal Conductivity and Self-healing in Dynamic Polymer Composites.
cards.abstract: The integration of high thermal conductivity and autonomous self-healing capability in thermal interface materials remains a critical challenge for next-generation electronic devices. Herein, we design a liquid metal (LM) magnetic droplet composite: TA-coated iron particles (Fe@TA) are compounded with Ga68.5In21.5Sn10, ultrasonicated into LM magnetic droplets, and dispersed in a dynamic polymer matrix. The TA shell architecture serves a dual function: it prevents deleterious alloying between iron and gallium-based LM, while the polyphenolic moieties of TA establish coordination interactions with Fe2+/Fe3+ and Ga3+/In3+ ions, synergistically ensuring interfacial structure and the stability. Under magnetic actuation, Fe@TA enables the directional migration and controlled deformation of LM droplets within the matrix, promoting droplet-droplet contact and the formation of efficient thermal pathways. Meanwhile, the magnetic field guides the droplets toward the damaged region, inducing matrix displacement to close the fracture gap and facilitating dynamic bond reformation, which substantially enhances the self-healing capability. Remarkably, the healed LMMC70 composite exhibits a 100% enhancement in thermal conductivity compared to its pristine sample, attributable to the synergistic magneto-thermal effect that drives droplet aggregation at damage sites, reinforces interfacial thermal contacts, and restores structural continuity through effective dynamic bond reorganization. In addition, the LMMC90 composite integrates high thermal conductivity (5.6 W·m-1·K-1), ultralow contact thermal resistance (0.1 K·cm2·W-1), excellent electrical insulation (1011 Ω·m), and effective self-healing capability. This work offers a viable strategy for designing intelligent thermal interface materials with magnetic-field-assisted thermal management and autonomous damage healing, holding great promise for reliable thermal management in advanced electronics.

cards.title: Prevalence and associated factors of sarcopenia among community-dwelling older adults in Vietnam: A cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is a geriatric syndrome characterized by age-related declines in skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. Despite its clinical relevance, it is frequently under-recognized because it is often considered a normal consequence of aging, even though it is associated with adverse outcomes such as functional impairment, falls, hospitalization, and mortality. Therefore, early identification and targeted nutritional and physical interventions are essential. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and its associated factors among community-dwelling older adults in a developing-country setting. A cross-sectional study was conducted in January 2024 among 660 community-dwelling older adults in Can Gio District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Sarcopenia was defined according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2019 criteria, incorporating handgrip strength, 6-m walking speed, and skeletal muscle mass assessed by bioelectrical impedance analysis. Participants underwent standardized anthropometric measurements, physical performance assessments, and nutritional evaluations using body mass index and Mini Nutritional Assessment. Sociodemographic, clinical, frailty, and lifestyle data were collected. Associations with sarcopenia were examined using prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sarcopenia was identified in 42.4% (280/660; 95% CI: 38.6%-46.3%) of the participants. In the fully adjusted model, sarcopenia was independently associated with frailty (adjusted PR [aPR] = 1.72; 95% CI: 1.07-2.76), multimorbidity (aPR = 1.23; 95% CI: 1.04-1.45), and underweight status (aPR = 1.46; 95% CI: 1.27-1.68). A lower prevalence of sarcopenia was observed among participants who were overweight or obese (aPR = 0.45; 95% CI: 0.36-0.54), physically active (aPR = 0.81; 95% CI: 0.69-0.95), or reported no low family economic status (aPR = 0.82; 95% CI: 0.70-0.97). Sarcopenia was highly prevalent among community-dwelling older adults and independently associated with frailty, multimorbidity, and nutritional status, underscoring the need for early community-based screening and integrated nutritional and physical interventions.

cards.title: Explainable deep learning localizes age-discriminative candidate regions on hand radiographs of adult women.
cards.abstract: To determine whether deep learning can distinguish younger from older adult women on hand radiographs and to identify candidate anatomical regions for age-group discrimination using explainable artificial intelligence and quantitative cortical measurements. This retrospective, single-center, exploratory study included 2,221 women sampled consecutively within each age group during 2020-2023 (1,134 aged 20-45 and 1,087 aged 55-80 years at radiography). Patients contributed one posteroanterior radiograph and were assigned to mutually exclusive training, validation, or test sets. Five architectures were evaluated on the same 334 held-out test radiographs (171 younger; 163 older), with performance averaged across five random-seed runs. DenseNet121 was selected by descriptive comparison for gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) and ray-based analyses with retraining. Manual cortical measurements of test radiographs yielded metacarpal and proximal phalangeal indices for candidate rays identified by Grad-CAM. DenseNet121 achieved the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC, 0.996; 95% CI, 0.992-0.999). Grad-CAM showed prominent activation around the third proximal phalanx, with additional activation in the second and fourth rays. Performance remained high after ray masking; the third-ray-only model achieved the highest mean accuracy among single-ray models. The third proximal phalangeal index had the highest AUC among the six indices (0.956; 95% CI, 0.937-0.976). Grad-CAM, ray-based analyses, and quantitative cortical measurements support the third proximal phalanx as an anatomically interpretable candidate region for age-group discrimination in adult women. Integrating explainable artificial intelligence with quantitative radiographic assessment provides an exploratory workflow for investigating hand skeletal aging, with potential relevance to broader musculoskeletal imaging research.

cards.title: Increased demographic turnover and isolation precede social fragmentation in Asian elephants.
cards.abstract: Humans and many other animals live in interconnected social communities that are essential for survival and well-being. In principle, communities can persist despite changes in constituent members. However, gradually accumulating changes to membership could push systems past critical thresholds into alternate states, restructuring patterns of connectivity. Such changes can further affect systemic resilience against disturbance. We investigated social network dynamics for 443 wild female Asian elephants over 12 years by tracking community membership and structure. Following accumulated demographic turnover, networks fractured into smaller and more isolated communities. Connections changed not only owing to loss of members but also modifications in relationships among remaining individuals. This provides empirical evidence of a persistent state change in the social network of a long-lived terrestrial mammal following gradually accumulating demographic turnover.

cards.title: DYRK1B overexpression promotes senescence-like transcriptional and secretory programs in A549 lung cancer cells.
cards.abstract: The dual-specificity tyrosine-regulated kinase DYRK1B is frequently expressed at elevated levels in solid tumors and has been implicated in cancer cell survival, therapy resistance, and cell cycle arrest. While DYRK1B is best known for maintaining quiescence, its broader impact on cancer cell phenotypic plasticity remains incompletely understood. Using a doxycycline-inducible A549 lung adenocarcinoma model, we show that sustained overexpression of catalytically active DYRK1B induces senescence-related phenotypic changes. DYRK1B overexpression led to increased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, cell enlargement and granularity, and robust induction of the cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p21Waf1/Cip1. RNA-sequencing revealed extensive transcriptional reprogramming, with strong overlap to established cellular senescence signatures. Gene set enrichment analysis further identified suppression of E2F target genes, consistent with durable proliferation arrest. Senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) components, including PAI-1 (SERPINE1), CCL2, IGFBP7, were significantly upregulated at both mRNA and protein levels. These effects were not observed with a kinase-impaired DYRK1B mutant. Gene set enrichment analysis further identified enrichment of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) transcriptional programs, consistent with EMT-associated phenotypic effects of DYRK1B overexpression that we have reported previously. These findings identify DYRK1B as an inducer of senescence-like transcriptional and secretory programs when expressed at elevated levels in A549 lung cancer cells in vitro. Although currently speculative and awaiting in vivo validation, we hypothesize that DYRK1B-induced senescence might contribute to tumor cell persistence and therapy resistance, highlighting DYRK1B as a potential target for modulating cancer cell plasticity and senescence-associated phenotypes.

cards.title: The AIM2 inflammasome drives age-dependent cardiac dysfunction following ischemia-reperfusion in mice.
cards.abstract: Cardiac aging increases susceptibility to cardiovascular diseases (CVDs), particularly myocardial infarction. Although evidence suggest an association between activation of the absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) inflammasome and CVDs, its contribution to age-related cardiac complications remains unknown. We investigated the role of the AIM2 inflammasome and the cardiac response to ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury in aged mice. Male wildtype (C57BL/6) and AIM2-deficient (AIM2-/-) mice were subjected to natural aging (21 months), using 3-month-old mice as controls, and human cardiomyocytes (AC16) were stressed by hydrogen peroxide to mimic senescent. AIM2 expression was up-regulated in the aged myocardium and senescence AC16 cells, coinciding with increased levels of cleaved caspase-1 (p20), IL-1β, and IL-18. Functional assays in Langendorff-perfused hearts revealed that AIM2 deficiency significantly attenuated post-I/R dysfunction in aged mice, restoring left ventricular developed pressure (LVDP) and pressure derivatives (+dP/dTmax and -dP/dTmin) toward pre-ischemic levels. While AIM2 absence did not alter age-associated hypertrophy, fibrosis, longevity, or senescence markers (p53 and p21), it reduced the baseline pro-inflammatory and pro-pyroptotic profile of the aged heart (IL-1β, IL-18, GSDMD-N, and ASC speck). In vitro, AIM2 activation using Poly(dA:dT) elevated IL-1β, GSDMD-N, ASC speck, and cell death in senescent cells, whereas pharmacological inhibition with A151 prevented these effects. Concurrently, age-dependent AIM2 up-regulation was confirmed in human cardiac datasets. Together, these findings suggest that age-dependent AIM2 induction primes a pro-inflammatory cardiac microenvironment, exacerbating post-I/R injury and highlighting this pathway for future investigation in the context of cardiac aging.

cards.title: MLL, TERRA, and telomere chromatin dynamics in replicative senescence and aging.
cards.abstract: Replicative senescence links telomere shortening to irreversible proliferative arrest and is widely recognized as a major tumor-suppressive mechanism. At the organismal level, however, progressive accumulation of senescent cells contributes to tissue dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and aging. Accumulating evidence suggests that telomere shortening influences telomeric and subtelomeric chromatin organization and transcription through mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Building upon the telomere position effect model of cellular senescence and the subtelomere-telomere theory of aging, this review proposes a chromatin-sensing telomere theory of aging in which telomere shortening contributes to senescence through epigenetic and transcriptional changes at chromosome ends. Central to this model is TERRA, a long non-coding RNA that regulates telomeric chromatin structure, telomere maintenance, and DNA-damage responses. The lysine methyltransferase MLL/KMT2A is a key regulator of TERRA transcription. MLL associates with telomeric chromatin in a telomere length-dependent manner and promotes TERRA transcription through H3K4 methylation. Shelterin components, particularly TRF2, can repress TERRA transcription in certain experimental contexts, and we propose that telomere shortening progressively remodels the shelterin-dependent telomere-subtelomere chromatin environment, potentially reducing access of MLL and RNA polymerase II to subtelomeric promoters. A biphasic model of TERRA regulation is proposed in which early TERRA upregulation in aging tissues promotes telomere protection, while subsequent critical shortening of TERRA-dominant telomeres contributes to reduced TERRA expression, telomere dysfunction, and senescence. This theory proposes a mechanistic link between telomere shortening, chromatin regulation, and quasi-programmed aging.

cards.title: Mitochondria-targeted drug delivery systems for aging-related diseases: Mechanisms, strategies, and advances.
cards.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction, characterized by increased oxidative stress, impaired energy metabolism, disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, abnormal quality control, and activation of apoptosis, represents a critical pathological basis for a wide range of aging-related diseases (ARDs), including neurodegenerative diseases, cardiovascular disorders, sarcopenia, and osteoarthritis. Mitochondria-targeted drug delivery systems increase the effective concentration of bioactive molecules within these dysfunctional organelles, offering novel strategies for the precise modulation of mitochondrial function. This review summarizes structural and functional changes in mitochondria during aging and their associations with major ARDs. We comprehensively review key advances in the design principles, mechanisms of action, and applications of passive targeting, stimuli-responsive systems, active targeting, and biomimetic drug delivery platforms. In addition, emerging interventions such as NAD+ supplementation, mitochondrial gene delivery, EV-mediated mitochondrial delivery and mitochondrial transplantation are discussed. Despite the demonstrated potential of these systems to restore mitochondrial homeostasis and tissue functionality in various disease models, their clinical translation remains constrained by obstacles including unstable targeting efficacy under pathological conditions, insufficient long-term safety of materials, manufacturing complexity, and a lack of standardized evaluation criteria. Future efforts should focus on integrating disease heterogeneity, advanced materials, and multi-omics technologies to advance mitochondria-targeted therapies toward standardization, individualization, and diagnostic-therapeutic integration.

cards.title: Prevalence and severity of frailty in patients admitted to Hospital-at-Home: a scoping review.
cards.abstract: Hospital-at-Home (HaH) is increasingly promoted as an alternative to hospitalization, particularly for frail older patients. However, how frailty is assessed and reported in current HaH research, as well as its prevalence and severity among HaH patients, remains unclear. We conducted a scoping review of published articles and conference abstracts involving adult HaH patients assessed with a validated frailty measure. We searched Embase, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews from inception to 9 July 2025, and updated the search on 31 December 2025. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data on HaH model characteristics, frailty assessment, and prevalence/severity. A narrative synthesis was performed. Of 9,753 records screened, 269 underwent full-text review. Twelve papers (eight full-text articles and four conference abstracts), representing 10 studies, met inclusion criteria (n = 637 patients). Frailty assessment was highly heterogeneous, with six instruments used, including the Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS, n = 4 studies) and PRISMA-7 (n = 3 studies). No study used the frailty phenotype model. Only three studies reported frailty prevalence, with non-comparable estimates because of heterogeneous instruments and cutoffs, including a nonstandard CFS ≥ 3 threshold (range: 10-70.5%). Most studies reported mean or median frailty scores without severity distributions, and methodological and organizational reporting was incomplete. Frailty is infrequently and inconsistently assessed in HaH research, limiting robust conclusions on its prevalence and severity among HaH patients. Standardized frailty assessment and reporting should be incorporated into HaH research to improve comparability across HaH programs and settings, and inform future clinical and policy decisions.
