cards.title: The lncRNA SEPT5-GP1BB-encoded peptide ARP, upregulated by 17β-estradiol, retards H2O2-induced senescence of human umbilical vein endothelial cells by promoting autophagy.
cards.abstract: Vascular endothelial cell (VEC) senescence is a key contributor to vascular aging and atherosclerosis. Increasing evidence suggests that long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) can encode functional micropeptides involved in cellular regulation. In this study, we investigated whether 17β-estradiol (17β-E2) delays endothelial senescence through an lncRNA-encoded peptide associated with autophagy. RNA sequencing was performed in H2O2-induced senescent human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) treated with or without 17β-E2, and differentially expressed lncRNAs with coding potential were identified through GO/KEGG analyses and bioinformatics prediction. LncRNA SEPT5-GP1BB was found to encode a 453-amino-acid peptide termed ARP, whose expression was reduced during endothelial senescence but restored by 17β-E2 treatment. Functional experiments demonstrated that 17β-E2 promoted autophagy through ARP rather than through the lncRNA transcript itself. ARP overexpression increased LC3B expression, reduced p62 accumulation, decreased senescence-associated β-galactosidase activity, suppressed SASP-related gene expression, and alleviated oxidative stress in senescent HUVECs. Furthermore, these protective effects were largely abolished by chloroquine treatment, indicating that autophagy mediated the anti-senescent effects of ARP. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that 17β-E2 delays endothelial senescence by upregulating the lncRNA SEPT5-GP1BB-encoded peptide ARP, which promotes autophagy, suggesting that ARP may serve as a potential therapeutic target for vascular aging.

cards.title: Skeletal muscle aging drives sex- and compartment-specific protein insolubility that is modifiable by proteostasis-directed treatments
cards.abstract: Protein aggregation and altered protein solubility indicate proteostatic decline, yet their roles in skeletal muscle aging remain poorly understood. We combined light and electron microscopy, quantitative proteomics, and stable-isotope labeling of skeletal muscle to investigate age-associated changes in protein insolubility, and their responses to exercise and rapamycin. Aged muscle accumulated distinct aggresome and amyloid-positive aggregates despite unchanged bulk insoluble protein content. Instead, aging altered the abundance and soluble-insoluble shifts of lower-abundance proteins across cellular components, particularly mitochondrial, nuclear and extracellular matrix proteins, with greater changes in females. These changes were not broadly explained by intrinsic protein aggregation propensity. Exercise and rapamycin partially reversed age-associated changes in abundance and partitioning without increasing protein synthesis. Together, these findings highlight sex- and cellular component-dependent changes in protein insolubility as important, modifiable aspects of skeletal muscle proteostasis, and indicate that proteostatic maintenance may be a more important target than anabolism for muscle aging.

cards.title: Interpretable digital multimodal evaluations for sarcopenia in aging populations
cards.abstract: Background The multimodal nature of sarcopenia complicates its assessment in older adults. The Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2025 consensus simplifies diagnosis by requiring concurrent low muscle mass and strength, improving clinical utility. However, quantitative and interpretable assessments remain constrained by limited well-normalized data and challenges in multimodal alignment. Methods Here, we introduce three-level balancing assessment (TLBass), an interpretable AI model integrating multimodal sensing data with human dynamics models to evaluate sarcopenia. Data from 355 older adults in Hong Kong were collected for model development and validation. Results TLBass achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.92 for surrogate evaluations in the internal dataset. Only its behavioral base model (SBA) underwent external validation, independently achieving an AUC of 0.81 in an external clinical dataset, supporting its potential for rapid clinical screening. Conclusions TLBass provided interpretable associations between sensing data and clinical outcomes, including surrogate markers of fast-twitch muscle fiber characteristics, declining muscle strength, and impaired balance. These findings highlight the potential of interpretable AI to support personalized sarcopenia assessment.

cards.title: The impact of the gut microbiome on skeletal muscle in health and disease.
cards.abstract: The gut microbiome, the community of bacteria residing the lower gastrointestinal tract, is increasingly recognized as an important influence on skeletal muscle physiology, with critical implications for muscle disorders such as sarcopenia and muscular dystrophy. Researchers have uncovered multiple microbiome-derived metabolites that alter skeletal muscle protein synthesis, mitochondrial biogenesis, protein degradation, and glucose transport. Moreover, the microbiome mediates systemic cytokine release of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor alpha, which can drive muscle loss. These studies have led to the identification of gut bacterial species (such as Veillonella atypica and Roseburia inulinivorans) that improve muscle endurance and strength when administered as probiotics in animal models. Several clinical trials of microbiome-focused therapies have also been conducted, with suggestion of benefits as well as potential harms. Taken together, the gut microbiome plays a key role in modulating skeletal muscle physiology, and may serve as the basis for novel therapeutics targeting muscle disease.

cards.title: Factors associated with skeletal muscle mass in patients with Behçet's disease: An exploratory study.
cards.abstract: To investigate the prevalence of low skeletal muscle mass and factors associated with skeletal muscle mass index (SMI) in Japanese outpatients with Behçet's disease (BD), while assessing sarcopenia according to the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia 2025 criteria. This cross-sectional study included ambulatory outpatients with BD aged ≥40 years. SMI was measured using multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis. Sarcopenia was defined as low SMI with low handgrip strength. Clinical characteristics, physical functions, nutrition- and body composition-related measures, rectus femoris ultrasonography, and laboratory parameters were compared between the low- and normal-SMI groups. Associations with SMI were examined using age- and sex-adjusted and domain-specific multivariable linear regression models. Among 48 patients (mean age: 65.4±11.8 years; 45.8% women), 52.1% had Low SMI, and 10.6% of 47 participants with available SMI and handgrip strength data had sarcopenia. In multivariable analyses, higher SMI remained associated with higher body mass index, greater handgrip strength, larger calf circumference, higher phase angle, and greater rectus femoris muscle thickness. Low skeletal muscle mass is common in BD ambulatory outpatients and is associated with muscle-, nutrition-, and body composition-related measures. However, clear associations with disease activity and current systemic glucocorticoid use were not observed.

cards.title: Skeletal Responses to Unilateral Tibial Loading During Disuse in Male and Female Mice: Bilateral Skeletal Responses and HPG-Axis-Associated Gene Expression.
cards.abstract: Disuse osteoporosis induced by immobilization, bed rest, or spaceflight remains an inadequately treated condition. Whether local mechanical stimulation on a single limb can exert systemic anabolic effects during disuse, and whether such mechanotherapy is sex-dependent, are unknown. Here, male and female C57BL/6J mice (28-week-old) were assigned to ground control (GC) or 14-day hindlimb unloading (HU) groups. In both conditions, the left tibia received daily unilateral axial compressive loading, whereas the contralateral right tibia served as the non-loaded reference limb. Bone microarchitecture of both loaded and contralateral non-loaded tibiae was assessed using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT), while targeted analysis of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG)-associated and osteogenic genes was performed to investigate underlying molecular responses. Compared with GC, female HU mice had lower contralateral cortical thickness, cortical area, and trabecular bone volume fraction of the tibiae, whereas male HU mice had higher mean contralateral cortical thickness and cortical area. The findings revealed sex-associated differences in selected skeletal responses. In male HU mice, preservation of selected cortical and trabecular parameters was observed in both the loaded and contralateral non-loaded tibiae within the combined unloading and unilateral-loading paradigm. In contrast, female mice exhibited a different structural response pattern, with no comparable preservation of selected parameters in the contralateral non-loaded tibia. Gene expression analysis in male non-loaded tibiae demonstrated coordinated upregulation of HPG-associated and osteogenic genes, including NR5A1, LHR, FSHR, AR, BMP2, RUNX2, and TGF-β1, whereas the female RNA-seq analysis did not identify a comparable pattern of changes in the selected genes. The contralateral structural findings and accompanying transcriptional changes in male bone raise the possibility of systemic skeletal effects during combined unloading and unilateral loading. However, the study does not establish a systemic effect caused specifically by unilateral loading or demonstrate systemic HPG-axis activation. The results highlight the potential importance of sex-specific mechanobiological pathways in the development of therapeutic strategies for disuse osteoporosis.

cards.title: Demographic, comorbidity, and temporal trends in anterior (ALIF) versus posterior (PLIF/TLIF) single-level lumbar interbody fusion: a retrospective analysis from 2015 to 2023.
cards.abstract: The aim of this study is to characterize national demographic and comorbidity profiles associated with anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF) versus posterior interbody fusion (PLIF/TLIF) and evaluate temporal utilization patterns. Using a commercial insurance database from 2015 to 2023, adults undergoing single-level ALIF or posterior interbody fusion were identified. Univariate tests compared baseline characteristics. Annual utilization trends were estimated with Poisson regression or negative binomial regression if overdispersion was present. Significance was set at P < 0.05. Among 407,319 patients, 133,323 underwent ALIF and 273,996 underwent posterior interbody fusion. Mean age was higher for posterior interbody fusion (61.8 vs. 59.5 years; P < 0.001), as was mean Elixhauser Comorbidity Index (5.3 ± 3.6 vs. 5.2 ± 3.6; P < 0.001). Sex distribution and rheumatoid arthritis were similar (P > 0.05 for all). Posterior interbody fusion patients more frequently had obesity, diabetes, hypertension, COPD, chronic kidney disease, congestive heart failure, coronary artery disease, osteoporosis, and tobacco use (P < 0.001 for all). ALIF procedures increased at an average annual rate of 6.66% (95% CI, 4.60-8.47; P < 0.001), whereas posterior interbody fusion increased 1.98% per year (95% CI, -0.19-4.19; P = 0.075); the annual growth-rate difference (ALIF - posterior interbody fusion) was 4.68% points (95% CI, 1.71-6.98; P < 0.001). In this national sample, posterior interbody fusion was more commonly used in older, more medically complex patients, while both approaches grew over time with faster growth for ALIF and increasing ALIF share. These descriptive patterns outline contemporary selection of anterior versus posterior approaches and motivate outcome-focused, risk-adjusted studies in key subgroups.

cards.title: Adult-onset Still's disease and sarcopenia-related traits - muscle mass, strength, and function: A bi-directional Mendelian randomization study.
cards.abstract: The causal relationship between adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and sarcopenia remains unclear. Therefore, we employed Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the causal link between these 2 conditions. This study investigated the causal relationships between AOSD (n = 201,947) and sarcopenia-related traits, including low handgrip strength (n = 256,523), left handgrip strength (n = 406,552), right handgrip strength (n = 461,089), appendicular lean mass (ALM, n = 450,243), and walking pace (WP, n = 459,915). In the first stage, AOSD served as the exposure variable, while the sarcopenia-related traits treated as the outcome variables; in the second stage, the roles were reversed. MR analysis employed inverse variance-weighted, weighted median, weighted mode, and MR-Egger methods. Cochran's Q statistic was used to assess heterogeneity, while MR-Egger regression and MR-PRESSO were utilized to evaluate pleiotropy. The robustness of the findings, risk of bias, and causal direction were assessed using leave-one-out analysis, funnel plots, and R2 statistics. AOSD may contribute to reduced muscle mass and strength, but not to impaired muscle function. Genetically predicted AOSD is causally associated with reduced ALM (odds ratio [OR] = 0.971, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.951-0.991; P = .005) and increased risk of low hand grip strength in individuals over 60 (OR = 1.046, 95% CI: 1.001-1.091; P = .048). It also reduces left hand grip strength (OR = 0.984, 95% CI: 0.976-0.992; P < .001), with no significant effect on right hand grip strength (OR = 0.995, 95% CI: 0.987-1.003; P = .240). with no effect on WP is also observed (OR = 0.994, 95% CI: 0.988-1.001; P = .080). Genetically predicted sarcopenia-related traits (ALM and bilateral grip strength) had no robust causal effect on AOSD. While inverse variance-weighted suggested nominally significant associations of reduced grip strength (≥60 years) and slower WP with AOSD, these results were inconsistent across MR methods and warrant cautious interpretation. AOSD leading to a decline in muscle mass, strength However, it does not significantly affect muscle function, whereas most sarcopenia-related traits showed no convincing causal effect on AOSD. Nominally significant associations observed for low hand grip strength in participants over 60 years and WP were not robust across sensitivity analyses and await further validation.

cards.title: InSafeLock endopin versus conventional distal locking screws for femoral shaft fractures: A comparative laboratory biomechanical study.
cards.abstract: The InSafeLock femoral nail is a recently developed implant that uses endopin instead of screws in its distal locking mechanism. This study aimed to compare the biomechanical features of the distal locking mechanisms of InSafeLock and conventional nails. Twenty-four artificial femoral bones were used for mechanical tests. InSafeLock nails with endopin (Group 1) and conventional nails with distal locking screws (Group 2) were inserted into the artificial bones. The biomechanical features were evaluated using axial compression and rotational performance tests. There was no statistically significant difference between Group 1 and Group 2 in the axial compression displacement tests (P = .683). No visual damage was observed on the artificial bones or intramedullary nails after axial compression fatigue tests in either group. During axial compression failure testing performed after fatigue testing, the mean failure load of Group 1 was significantly lower than that of Group 2 (1132.5 ± 15.5 N vs 11,965.5 ± 9.5 N, respectively; P = .002). Rotational performance tests showed that the torsional yield strength of the groups was not statistically different (P = .333). While the InSafeLock endopin offers ease in distal locking, it exhibits a significantly lower failure load under high axial compression forces than conventional screws.

cards.title: Berberine attenuates cigarette smoke extract-induced stress and senescence-associated changes in human brain microvascular endothelial cells.
cards.abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the protective effects of berberine (BBR) against cigarette smoke extract (CSE)-induced injury in human brain microvascular endothelial cells and to identify candidate molecules and associated candidate molecules. hCMEC/D3 cells were exposed to 4% CSE and/or 7.5 μM BBR for 24 h. Inflammation, oxidative stress, and senescence-associated phenotypes were assessed. Previously generated CSE-responsive transcriptomic data were integrated with ChEMBL-derived candidates, followed by enrichment, weighted prioritization, protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, and docking. Compared with CSE alone, BBR co-treatment increased cell viability (P < 0.001), attenuated NF-κB-associated inflammation. IL-1β and TNF-α levels were significantly reduced (P < 0.05). BBR also reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and increased the reduced/oxidized glutathione (GSH/GSSG) ratio from 8.74 to 12.74 (P < 0.001). Senescence-associated β-galactosidase positivity decreased from 15.00% to 1.39% (P < 0.001), accompanied by reduced p16/p21 expression and G0/G1 accumulation (P < 0.01). Integrated analysis identified 23 overlapping candidates and prioritized GDF15, HMOX1, NQO1, IL1B, and CDKN1A. Docking predicted potential interactions with BBR; RT-qPCR and Western blot showed differential expression responses to BBR. BBR attenuates CSE-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and senescence-associated alterations in hCMEC/D3 cells. These effects may be associated with modulation of interconnected cellular stress responses.

cards.title: The epidemiology of frailty in urban and rural KwaZulu Natal, South Africa; a cross-sectional study.
cards.abstract: We investigated the prevalence and clinical risk factors associated with frailty, and frailty's relationship with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) in urban and rural South Africa. In a population-based cross-sectional study, using age- and sex-stratified random sampling of adults aged ≥40 years, researcher-administered questionnaires collected socio-demographic and clinical data. Physical assessments included body mass index (BMI), grip strength, short physical performance battery (SPPB), vision and hearing, and EuroQol 5-Dimensions 5-Levels measured HRQoL. A modified Fried's Frailty Phenotype defined frailty. Multivariable logistic regression calculated the odds of frailty for associated risk factors, and logistic and quantile regression examined HRQoL by frailty status. Amongst 1,893 participants, median age 60 years [IQR 50-70], 54% female, the overall study prevalence of frailty was 16.4%. Frailty was more common in those ≥70 years than those 40-49-years old (32.5% vs. 7.5%; OR 6.0 [95%CI 3.7,8.4], p < 0.001), and in females compared to males (19.2% vs. 13.1%; OR 1.6 [1.2,2.0], p < 0.001). Older age (≥60 years), urban residence, low educational attainment, moderate to severe food insecurity, visual and hearing impairments, self-reported disability, BMI<18kg/m2, and impaired SPPB were all independently associated with frailty. Compared to being robust, frailty was associated with a lower HRQoL utility score (median 0.81(IQR 0.71-0.86) in frail vs. 0.86 (0.83-0.90) in robust/prefrail, β -0.05 ([95%CI -0.07,-0.03], p < 0.001). Frailty is common and associated with poorer HRQoL. The identified clinical risk factors can be used to prioritise individuals for referral for clinical assessment of frailty in SA.

cards.title: Mechanisms and disease implications of inflammaging and potential therapeutic strategies.
cards.abstract: Inflammaging is a chronic, low-grade inflammatory state associated with aging and age-related diseases. This review examines the mechanisms underlying inflammaging, emphasizing the interplay between oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage, cellular senescence, and immune dysregulation. Persistent cellular stress promotes senescence and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), while impaired immune clearance allows senescent cells to accumulate, sustaining a self-amplifying inflammatory cycle. We further discuss the involvement of inflammaging in neurodegenerative, infectious, autoimmune, cardiometabolic, and musculoskeletal diseases. Finally, we summarize current and emerging interventions, including lifestyle modifications, pharmacological approaches, senolytics, senomorphics, and strategies targeting mitochondrial quality control and cellular metabolism. Understanding the interconnected mechanisms and tissue-specific effects of inflammaging may facilitate the development of targeted interventions to mitigate age-related diseases and promote healthy aging.

cards.title: [Supramalleolar osteotomy for correction of malunited malleolar fractures : When and how?].
cards.abstract: Malunion after malleolar fractures most often results from a malunited fibula but can also involve the tibial plafond. Axial deviation of the talus and residual joint incongruity lead to destabilization of the ankle joint, asymmetrical loading and accelerated focal cartilage loss. Supramalleolar corrective osteotomy aims to restore the mechanical axis, improve tibiotalar congruity and redistribute loading toward preserved cartilage. The preoperative planning requires weight-bearing standard radiographs of the foot and ankle and, when needed, whole leg radiographs. Comparative radiographs of the contralateral unaffected ankle may be helpful. Computed tomography is useful for assessing the position of the talus in the malleolus as well as the position of the fibula in relation to the tibia, especially the rotational deformity, intra-articular step-off, syndesmotic incongruity, and fibular shortening. The plan should identify the apex of deformity, the correction angle and the osteotomy level. The surgical technique should be individually adapted to the deformity. Supramalleolar osteotomy is placed just proximal to the ankle joint while preserving distal bone stock for fixation. Guidewires inserted under fluoroscopy guidance are used to define the cut, hinge and planned correction. Closing-wedge supramalleolar osteotomy requires precise wedge removal, cortical compression and stable fixation, whereas opening-wedge gaps are supported with bone grafts and rigid plate fixation. After tibial realignment, the fibula and syndesmosis must be reassessed because persistent fibular shortening, malrotation or malposition can maintain talar incongruity. Fibular osteotomy, lengthening, and derotation are often needed to correctly reposition the talus in the ankle mortise and to restore joint congruity. Calcaneal osteotomy may be added if heel malalignment persists. In the treatment of malunited ankle fractures, supramalleolar osteotomy has been shown to be effective in restoring joint mechanics and balancing the ankle and to yield highly satisfactory results in the mid-term to long-term, making it a viable option for preserving the ankle.

cards.title: From cave adaptation to ageing resilience: the Mexican cavefish Astyanax mexicanus.
cards.abstract: The Mexican cavefish, Astyanax mexicanus, is a powerful evolutionary model for investigating how adaptation to extreme environments reshapes vertebrate physiology. Multiple cave populations have independently evolved under subterranean conditions, acquiring traits including insulin resistance, persistent hyperglycaemia, increased adiposity, altered sleep patterns, hypoxia tolerance and extensive metabolic reprogramming. Despite these differences, cavefish exhibit lifespans comparable to those of surface fish, while selected traits, including fertility and locomotor performance, appear to be better preserved with age. These observations challenge the assumption that persistent metabolic dysfunction necessarily entails accelerated functional decline and raise the possibility that cavefish have evolved mechanisms of ageing resilience. This narrative review examines evidence linking cave adaptation to biological processes relevant to ageing, focusing on nutrient sensing, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, redox homeostasis and immune regulation. Rather than eliminating metabolic stress, cave-associated adaptations may buffer some of its downstream consequences, preserving selected physiological functions. Evidence is evaluated within the framework of the hallmarks of ageing, considering genomic instability, telomere dynamics, deregulated nutrient sensing, mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation, while identifying major knowledge gaps regarding epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, macroautophagy, cellular senescence, stem-cell exhaustion, altered intercellular communication and dysbiosis. The available evidence supports A. mexicanus as a comparative model for investigating how chronic environmental and metabolic stress can be uncoupled from selected aspects of functional decline. Distinguishing delayed ageing from enhanced tolerance or compensation in response to accumulated damage will be essential to establish the extent and mechanisms of ageing resilience in this species.

cards.title: Osteoclastogenesis associated gene signatures in postmenopausal low bone mineral density: cross-dataset transcriptomics and whole-blood validation.
cards.abstract: Osteoporosis is characterized by reduced bone mass and increased fracture risk, yet minimally invasive molecular correlates of postmenopausal low bone mineral density remain limited. We independently reanalysed two human osteoclastogenesis RNA-seq datasets, GSE225974 and GSE246769, using differential-expression, Gene Ontology, KEGG, Hallmark gene set enrichment, and cross-dataset concordance analyses. Six candidate genes, LGALSL, FAXDC2, DHCR7, MYL9, RHOC, and ITGB5, were subsequently evaluated by RT-qPCR in whole blood from 100 postmenopausal women with normal bone mineral density (n=30), osteopenia (n=30), or osteoporosis (n=40). Across the two RNA-seq datasets, 1,782 differentially expressed genes were shared, including 1,240 concordantly upregulated and 385 concordantly downregulated genes, with strong cross-dataset effect-size correlation (r=0.74). GO and KEGG analyses identified replicated sterol/lipid, skeletal-development, adhesion/integrin, and actin-cytoskeletal programs, while Hallmark GSEA identified 22 concordantly enriched gene sets, including oxidative phosphorylation, fatty-acid metabolism, and cholesterol homeostasis. BMD was positively correlated with calcium intake and physical activity. Conversely, deteriorating bone health was positively associated with high cholesterol, low BMI, early menopause. All six candidate genes were significantly and concordantly upregulated during osteoclastogenesis in both datasets. Whole-blood RT-qPCR analysis demonstrated progressively higher relative expression across normal-BMD, osteopenia, and osteoporosis groups for all six candidates. Expression analysis from the serum validated LGALSL, RHOC, MYL9 and ITGB5 elevated expression in osteoporosis cases. These findings identify reproducible osteoclastogenesis-associated transcriptional programs and support the six candidate genes as candidate signature correlating with the postmenopausal BMD status.

cards.title: A strain-insensitive multiplexed soft microneedle patch for robust interstitial fluid biomarker monitoring.
cards.abstract: Wearable microneedle sensors analyze biomarkers in situ from interstitial fluids (ISF), enabling minimally invasive, precise, and continuous monitoring of metabolic diseases. However, conventional designs either lack adequate conformability to skin or suffer from electrode fractures during skin penetration and body motion, leading to signal instability that undermines reliable multiparameter acquisition. Here, we present a fully integrated system with a soft microneedle sensor array featuring nano-hill topographies on strain-resilient electrodes to delocalize strain via geometric confinement. This design reduces signal variability by 14-fold compared to conventional designs, enabling stable, simultaneous in situ monitoring of multiple ISF biomarkers. It achieves clinical-grade accuracy for continuous glucose monitoring (mean absolute relative difference of 10.8%) and captures dynamic synchronized variations in glucose, local tissue pH, and temperature in a living subject in real time. The system integrates a reusable electronic module with a disposable microneedle array with a sensor footprint of just 1.8 cm2. By combining high signal stability with multiparameter synchrony in a compact form factor, this system offers a practical solution for reliable, real-time ISF analysis under dynamic in vivo conditions.

cards.title: Healthy Eating Index and Bone in Obesity.
cards.abstract: Individuals living with overweight or obesity have a higher bone mineral density, however bone quality may be compromised, leading to an increased susceptibility to fractures and impaired skeletal integrity. Nutrition is a potentially modifiable factor that may influence both body weight and bone metabolism through effects on inflammation, body composition, and metabolic regulation. In particular, dietary quality indices such as the Healthy Eating Index (HEI) provide a comprehensive assessment of adherence to dietary guidelines and may offer insight into how overall eating patterns influence bone quality among individuals with excess body weight. In this review, we have summarized the impact of dietary quality using the HEI on bone health in individuals who are living with overweight or obesity. Recent studies show a positive relationship of high HEI with bone parameters in overweight and obese individuals. Specifically, studies report on a higher Trabecular bone score (TBS), lumbar and femoral neck BMD, lower osteoporosis risk and higher serum 25 hydroxy vitamin D levels in populations with a higher HEI. Currently studies assessing impact of HEI on bone health in obesity are cross sectional in nature. Future studies should assess the impact of increasing HEI on bone health in a prospective design and the impact of weight loss and increasing HEI on bone quality in individuals living with overweight and obesity.

cards.title: Revitalizing aging muscles: harnessing NAD⁺, sirtuins, and exercise to combat sarcopenia.
cards.abstract: Aging is associated with systemic metabolic dysfunction that contributes to geriatric syndromes such as sarcopenia-the progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass and function. Evidence from preclinical models suggests that age-associated depletion of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺) may contribute to this decline by limiting the activity of sirtuin deacetylases (SIRT1-7). These enzymes act as metabolic sensors regulating mitochondrial biogenesis, oxidative capacity, DNA repair and pathways related to muscle atrophy. Physical exercise enhances NAD⁺ salvage through upregulation of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT). Pharmacological approaches including NAD⁺ precursor supplementation (nicotinamide riboside or nicotinamide mononucleotide) and inhibition of NAD⁺-consuming enzymes have shown benefits in preclinical models. However, clinical translation remains inconsistent. Recent meta-analyses have found no significant effect of these precursors on muscle mass or strength in adults aged over 60 years. Moreover, experimental evidence indicates that even profound NAD⁺ depletion in adult mouse skeletal muscle does not necessarily compromise function or accelerate aging. We conclude that pharmacological NAD⁺ restoration alone is currently insufficient to reverse sarcopenia in humans. A synergistic approach combining exercise with targeted NAD⁺ support, together with emerging strategies involving precursor transporters, trigonelline and hypothalamic NAD⁺-sirtuin circuits, represents a testable avenue that requires rigorous, stratified clinical evaluation.

cards.title: Joint-preserving correction of malunited anterior and posterior malleolar fractures.
cards.abstract: The posterior and anterior rims of the distal tibial are essential for overall ankle function. They are referred to as third and fourth malleolus, respectively, which are commonly injured in the wake of ankle fractures. Residual displacement, malunion, or nonunion may cause fibular malposition in the tibial incisura (fibular notch), syndesmotic (tibiofibular mortise) instability, and joint incongruency leading to posttraumatic arthritis. Computed tomography scanning is required to assess the three-dimensional outline of the deformity and to make an appropriate treatment plan. Correction of anterior and posterior malleolar malalignment aims at restoring the following: (1) articular tibiotalar congruency, (2) sagittal ankle bone stability and talar containment, (3) the anatomy of the tibial incisura (fibular notch) to enable correct positioning of the distal fibula, and (4) tibiofibular alignment and syndesmotic (mortise) stability. To date, there is little evidence in the literature regarding the outcome of realignment of anterior and posterior malleolar malunions, and further studies are needed to establish evidence-based guidelines for surgical correction.

cards.title: Nontraumatic orbital roof blowout fracture following nose blowing: illustrative case.
cards.abstract: Orbital blowout fractures generally involve the floor or medial wall and usually result from blunt trauma. Nontraumatic orbital roof fractures associated with nose blowing are exceptionally rare. An 84-year-old man developed immediate left orbital swelling, epistaxis, diplopia, and impaired downgaze after forceful nose blowing. CT demonstrated fractures of the left medial orbital wall and orbital roof, with intracranial herniation of orbital tissue. MRI showed herniation of the superior rectus muscle and orbital fat through the roof defect and an adjacent inferior frontal lobe hematoma. During an extradural transcranial operation, herniated orbital fat was found to have penetrated the dura and adhered firmly to the frontal lobe. The adherent tissue was released, the dura and periorbita were repaired, and the orbital roof was reconstructed. Diplopia and downgaze limitation improved postoperatively. An orbital roof fracture should be considered when orbital swelling and diplopia develop immediately after forceful nose blowing, even without trauma. Intracranial herniation and adhesion of orbital tissue may contribute to persistent ocular motility disturbance and may warrant surgical treatment. https://thejns.org/doi/abs/10.3171/CASE26847.

cards.title: The clinical use and applicability of magnetic resonance spectroscopy of the discovertebral segment: a scoping review.
cards.abstract: To map the available evidence on the clinical use and applicability of MRS applied to the spinal discovertebral segment. A systematic search was performed in PubMed, CINAHL, and EMBASE for articles that applied MRS to the discovertebral segment. Both in vivo and ex vivo studies (without immersion or preparation) in humans and animals were included, while studies were excluded if they employed non-clinical MRI scanners (e.g. small-bore scanners or ultra-high field MRI systems), or focused solely on the bone marrow (e.g., osteoporosis, anorexia). Two reviewers independently screened the articles and extracted data. The findings were reported descriptively. Eleven articles from eight studies applying proton (1H)-based MRS and published between 2009 and 2025 met the inclusion criteria. Seven studies were conducted in vivo in human participants, while one ex vivo study included human cadaveric and bovine discs. Substantial variations in methodologies were observed across the included studies in terms of MRI field strength, acquisition parameters, and post-processing software. MRS was used to quantify biochemical markers, such as water content, proteoglycans, lactate, and lipid peaks that may be related to intervertebral disc health and disc degeneration. Three studies assessed associations between MRS findings and clinical outcomes in patients with low back pain (LBP). MRS is an emerging technology in LBP research and has been used to non-invasively assess biochemical markers in the spinal discovertebral segment; however, the limited number of studies and the methodological heterogeneity preclude firm conclusions regarding its clinical relevance in LBP. Further large-scale in vivo studies with standardised MRS protocols and methods are required to evaluate the clinical significance of metabolic markers in the discovertebral segment.

cards.title: Gel Electrolytes With Regulated Ion Channels and Stabilized Zn Interfaces Enable Durable Flexible Zinc-Air Batteries.
cards.abstract: Flexible zinc-air batteries require gel electrolytes that simultaneously reconcile rapid ion transport, mechanical robustness, and stable Zn interfacial chemistry. Here, a trehalose-regulated L-PAT/PVA gel electrolyte is developed through hierarchical bulk-interface regulation. Hofmeister-induced PVA crystallization provides a mechanically reinforced framework, while trehalose-mediated competitive hydrogen bonding moderates excessive chain association, reconstructs the local hydration environment, and preserves continuous low-tortuosity ion-transport pathways. Simultaneously, sulfonate groups from L-carrageenan regulate the Zn/electrolyte interfacial microenvironment, homogenize local ionic flux, and direct Zn electrocrystallization toward the (002)-preferred orientation. DRT analysis further reveals suppressed slow-polarization contributions and more stable interfacial kinetics during cycling. The optimized electrolyte exhibits a tensile strength of 609 kPa, a fracture strain above 1200%, and an ionic conductivity of 154.5 mS cm-1. The resulting flexible Zn-air battery delivers 77 mW cm-2 peak power density, ≈200 mAh cm-3 volumetric capacity, and stable cycling for 250 h at 1 mA cm-2, while maintaining reliable operation from -15 C to 55°C and under mechanical deformation.

cards.title: Effects of a Nurse-Led Multicomponent Exercise Intervention for Haemodialysis Patients With Possible or Confirmed Sarcopenia: A Cluster Randomised Trial.
cards.abstract: To assess the potential effects, safety and feasibility of a nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention on skeletal muscle function and quality of life in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia. A cluster randomised trial with clusters defined by fixed haemodialysis schedules. A total of 56 eligible participants were enrolled and allocated through cluster randomisation. The intervention group (n = 28) received a 12-week nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention in addition to standard care, whereas the control group (n = 28) received standard care. The primary outcomes included skeletal muscle mass index (SMI), handgrip strength, gait speed and short physical performance battery (SPPB) scores. Secondary outcomes included scores on the Kidney Disease Quality of Life 36-Item Short-Form Survey (KDQOL-36) and C-reactive protein levels. Handgrip strength, gait speed, SPPB scores and KDQOL-36 scores were assessed at baseline and at Weeks 4, 8 and 12 during the intervention period, whereas SMI and C-reactive protein were assessed at baseline and Week 12. An intention-to-treat analysis was employed, and the effects of the intervention were evaluated using linear mixed models. Of the 56 participants, 50 completed the study. The intervention group showed favourable trends in handgrip strength, gait speed and SPPB scores, with moderate-to-large effect sizes; however, these differences were not statistically significant after Bonferroni correction. Furthermore, no significant between-group differences were found in skeletal muscle mass index, health-related quality of life, or C-reactive protein levels. No serious intervention-related adverse events were reported. The nurse-led multicomponent exercise intervention was safe and feasible and showed favourable trends in muscle strength and physical function, although statistically significant between-group differences were not retained after correction for multiple comparisons. A nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention may have the potential to increase muscle strength and physical function in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia. What problem did the study address? This study assessed the potential effects, safety, and feasibility of a nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention designed for haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia. What were the main findings? A nurse-led exercise intervention appeared safe and feasible and may help to improve muscle strength and physical function in haemodialysis patients with possible or confirmed sarcopenia. However, future studies with larger sample sizes and longer follow-up periods are needed to assess the long-term effects. Where and on whom will the research have an impact? The results of this study may inform the development and future implementation of nurse-led exercise interventions for haemodialysis patients with sarcopenia. Patients and family members were invited to collaborate with healthcare professionals in designing a nurse-led, multicomponent exercise intervention programme. Their contributions helped improve the feasibility and practicality of the exercise intervention. The CONSORT 2025 checklist was used in the reporting of the study. This trial was registered at www.chictr.org.cn (registration number: ChiCTR2200065863).

cards.title: A Novel Peptide Targeting the USP25-SIRT1 Interaction Activates SIRT1 to Suppress Cell Senescence.
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT The deacetylase SIRT1 is a critical regulator of cellular senescence, and the excessive accumulation of senescent cells can further drive the onset of organismal aging. SIRT1 activity is tightly governed by posttranslational modifications, including ubiquitination. While ubiquitination has been well documented to control SIRT1 protein stability, the precise regulatory pathway underlying SIRT1 activity remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the deubiquitinase USP25 as a central regulator of cellular senescence. Specifically, USP25 deficiency in mice mitigates age‐related phenotypes and improves overall physiological function. Mechanistically, USP25 directly interacts with SIRT1 and mediates its deubiquitylation via K63‐linked polyubiquitination, specifically targeting SIRT1 lysine residues K506 and K513, which ultimately suppresses SIRT1 deacetylase activity. Reduced SIRT1 deacetylase activity, in turn, increases P53 or PGC1α acetylation, which further increases the transcriptional activation of downstream target genes and consequently accelerates cellular senescence. Furthermore, we developed a cell‐penetrating peptide, pSirt1‐4, that efficiently disrupts the USP25–SIRT1 interaction, increases SIRT1 deacetylase activity, and attenuates cellular senescence. Collectively, our findings establish USP25 as a critical regulator of aging and highlight the USP25–SIRT1 axis as a promising therapeutic target for treating senescence‐related diseases.

cards.title: Is the annular ligament disrupted in Monteggia fracture-dislocations? A cadaveric mechanistic study.
cards.abstract: Monteggia fracture-dislocation is characterized by an ulnar fracture with radial head dislocation. The mechanisms of dislocation and annular ligament integrity remain unclear. This study established a cadaveric Monteggia fracture-dislocation model to investigate radial head dislocation and associated annular ligament injury. Twelve upper limbs from 6 fresh-frozen cadavers (mean age at death, 83 years; 1 male, 5 females) were examined. Soft tissues were removed while preserving the bones, ligaments, capsules, forearm interosseous membrane, and biceps tendon insertions. The humeroulnar joint was fixed at 90° flexion, and the ulna was manually fractured to create a Bado type I (direct-blow) Monteggia fracture-dislocation model. The annular ligament, quadrate ligament, oblique cord (Weitbrecht ligament), and forearm interosseous membrane were evaluated. Ulnar fracture created forearm deformity, causing the radius to contact the triangular fulcrum. Continued manual loading caused the radius to pivot around the fulcrum. The annular ligament remained intact in 11 of 12 limbs; 1 specimen showed injury at the annular ligament-capsular junction. In 11 limbs, the radial head was dislocated beneath the distal margin of the annular ligament. One quadrate ligament rupture occurred; the oblique cord and forearm interosseous membrane remained intact. In this standardized cadaveric direct-blow model, anterior radial head dislocation occurred in 11 of 12 limbs, beneath the distal margin of an intact annular ligament. These findings demonstrate that annular ligament rupture is not required for radial head dislocation in the described experimental setting. This mechanism provides a possible anatomic explanation for difficult reduction in selected cases.

cards.title: Laser-programmed anisotropic hierarchical host bone interfaces for mechanotransduction-guided osseointegration.
cards.abstract: Conventional mechanical osteotomy often induces thermal and mechanical damage, which compromises the biological quality of the host bone interface and impairs subsequent osseointegration. This study aimed to develop a 9.3 μm CO2 laser-based osteotomy strategy that integrates precise bone cutting with in situ regenerative interface engineering. A 9.3 μm CO2 laser osteotomy platform was developed by combining controlled pulse-overlap scanning with gas-atomized water-mist cooling. The generated osteotomy interfaces were characterized in terms of surface topography, thermal response, microstructural preservation, and local mechanical integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSC) alignment, focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, osteogenic differentiation, and osteoclast formation were evaluated in vitro. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were performed to investigate the underlying molecular programs. The optimized interface was further assessed in a rat femoral defect model with porous titanium scaffold implantation. The laser osteotomy strategy generated deterministic microscale grooves and graded nanoscale roughness, forming anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano osteotomy interfaces. Compared with mechanical cutting, laser osteotomy reduced thermal accumulation, limited microstructural disruption, and better maintained local mechanical integrity. The engineered interfaces directed hMSC alignment and activated focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, as indicated by enhanced pFAK activation, Lamin A/C reinforcement, and YAP nuclear translocation. These responses promoted osteogenic differentiation and suppressed osteoclast formation, with the Laser III group showing the most favorable biological response. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed enrichment of adhesion-, cytoskeleton-, and PI3K-Akt-related osteogenic programs. In vivo, the optimized interface enhanced peri-implant bone regeneration, mineral apposition, and osseointegration. This study provides proof-of-concept evidence that 9.3 μm CO2 laser osteotomy may enable bone cutting to be coupled with in situ regenerative interface engineering. By reducing cutting-associated damage and actively programming the host bone interface, this approach shows translational potential for improving peri-implant bone healing and implant integration. 9.3 μm CO2 laser-enabled osteotomy interface engineering integrates precise bone cutting with in situ programming of the host bone surface. This study reveals that laser-generated anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano interfaces can reduce cutting-associated damage, activate adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, promote osteogenic differentiation, suppress osteoclast maturation, and enhance peri-implant osseointegration. These findings provide a regenerative osteotomy strategy for improving the biological quality of surgically created bone interfaces, which holds translational potential for orthopedic implant surgery, fracture reconstruction, and the repair of bone defects in clinical practice.

cards.title: TOP2A Maintains Heterochromatin Stability by Sustaining LMNB1 Expression to Counteract Senescence
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Chromatin stability and nuclear architectural integrity constitute the primary defense against cellular senescence. Their collapse precipitates genomic disarray, epigenetic misregulation, and functional decline in stem cells. Although TOP2A is conventionally known for resolving DNA topological stress, its role in aging remains largely unexplored. Here, we found that TOP2A expression progressively decreased in senescent mesenchymal stem cells ( MSCs ), and its depletion initiated a catastrophic nuclear remodeling process characterized by the loss of Lamin B1 , heterochromatin erosion, and senescence‐associated phenotypes. Mechanistically, TOP2A directly regulated the expression of Lamin B1 to maintain nuclear architecture. TOP2A depletion set off a domino effect involving nuclear membrane rupture, loss of heterochromatin‐associated factors ( H3K9me3 , KAP1 , and LAP2 ), deterioration of cellular functions and acceleration of senescence. Notably, overexpression of TOP2A restored Lamin B1 levels, mitigated nuclear protein loss, preserved nuclear integrity, and counteracted cellular senescence. The in vivo relevance of these findings was further underscored by TOP2A inhibitor‐induced brain aging in murine models. Our study establishes TOP2A as a novel modulator of cellular senescence, which stabilizes heterochromatin and nuclear structure, and provides new perspectives for targeting chromatin‐based mechanisms in aging.

cards.title: Artificial intelligence in fruit and vegetable preservation: innovations and applications of intelligent technology.
cards.abstract: Fruits and vegetables are highly susceptible to post-harvest quality deterioration, and traditional preservation technologies can hardly meet the modern industry's demands for precision management and green development. By deeply integrating with sensors, the Internet of Things (IoT) and big data technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) enables full-link refined management covering signal collection, intelligent analysis, scheme formulation and automatic regulation, and facilitates precise control under controlled postharvest experimental conditions. Although research on AI-assisted postharvest handling is expanding rapidly, few studies systematically connect technological innovation to full-scale industrial application scenarios. Existing reviews have largely focused on individual technologies such as machine learning (ML) or only analyzed separate segments of postharvest workflows; rare efforts comprehensively analyze the integrated application of these tools across sorting, storage, cold chain monitoring and shelf-life prediction to realize targeted whole-process preservation regulation. In addition, prior literature has not fully summarized the industrial bottlenecks limiting large-scale on-site deployment. This paper sorts out targeted AI solutions for typical postharvest quality degradation of fruits and vegetables, including water loss, chilling injury, microbial contamination, and senescence caused by respiration and ethylene accumulation. Nevertheless, industrial promotion still faces multiple obstacles: inconsistent data quality, poor algorithm adaptability, high hardware costs, and the lack of unified industry standards and specifications. Looking forward, breaking bottlenecks such as cross-variety generalizable models, lightweight edge hardware and reliable data ecosystems will transform this field from scattered, experience-reliant operations into integrated intelligent decision-making systems. This can also provide technical references for global food security and sustainable agricultural development.

cards.title: Heterogenous Aging of Local Tissues Is a Major Contributor to the Age-Related Decline in Glycosaminoglycans and Fracture Toughness of Cortical Bone
cards.abstract: Abstract Bone fragility fractures increase with age as bone toughness declines, potentially in part due to the loss of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). However, the mechanisms linking GAG depletion to bone quality remain unclear, partly due to the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of bone remodeling during aging. During bone remodeling, newly formed secondary osteons and older interstitial tissue are randomly distributed throughout the bone, each with distinct material properties. This microstructural heterogeneity adds complexity to studying age-related changes in bone quality that cannot be explained by donor age alone. This study hypothesized that the age-related decline in bulk bone fracture toughness originates from changes in local tissue GAGs with tissue aging and is amplified by an increasing proportion of old tissue relative to new tissue with advancing donor age. To test this, local tissues in human cortical bone samples across different ages and sexes were analyzed using Raman spectroscopy, DMMB, Alcian blue, histomorphometry, microcompression, and fracture toughness testing. The results showed that compositional and mechanical properties of local tissues changed significantly with tissue age, but not with donor age or sex. The volume fraction of old tissue as well as GAG heterogeneity (FWHM) increased significantly with donor age. Furthermore, age-related changes in bulk bone GAG content were strongly correlated with bone fracture toughness. These findings suggest that age-related loss of bone quality arises from the combined effects of tissue age-dependent deterioration in local properties and donor age–dependent accumulation of older tissue.

cards.title: A Novel Peptide Targeting the <scp>USP25</scp> – <scp>SIRT1</scp> Interaction Activates <scp>SIRT1</scp> to Suppress Cell Senescence
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT The deacetylase SIRT1 is a critical regulator of cellular senescence, and the excessive accumulation of senescent cells can further drive the onset of organismal aging. SIRT1 activity is tightly governed by posttranslational modifications, including ubiquitination. While ubiquitination has been well documented to control SIRT1 protein stability, the precise regulatory pathway underlying SIRT1 activity remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the deubiquitinase USP25 as a central regulator of cellular senescence. Specifically, USP25 deficiency in mice mitigates age‐related phenotypes and improves overall physiological function. Mechanistically, USP25 directly interacts with SIRT1 and mediates its deubiquitylation via K63‐linked polyubiquitination, specifically targeting SIRT1 lysine residues K506 and K513, which ultimately suppresses SIRT1 deacetylase activity. Reduced SIRT1 deacetylase activity, in turn, increases P53 or PGC1α acetylation, which further increases the transcriptional activation of downstream target genes and consequently accelerates cellular senescence. Furthermore, we developed a cell‐penetrating peptide, pSirt1‐4, that efficiently disrupts the USP25–SIRT1 interaction, increases SIRT1 deacetylase activity, and attenuates cellular senescence. Collectively, our findings establish USP25 as a critical regulator of aging and highlight the USP25–SIRT1 axis as a promising therapeutic target for treating senescence‐related diseases.

cards.title: Bone Organoids Across the Development-to-Remodeling Continuum: From Tissue Formation to Functional Competence and Translation.
cards.abstract: Bone organoids are emerging as three-dimensional skeletal models that reproduce selected aspects of bone development, organization, and function under controlled conditions. Physiologically relevant models require more than cellular aggregation and mineral deposition; they must progressively acquire organized matrices, multicellular interactions, vascular and metabolic support, and mechanical responsiveness. In this review, we examine developmental principles guiding bone-organoid construction, including skeletal hierarchy, cellular niches, ossification pathways, and spatiotemporal signaling. We then discuss current strategies based on skeletal, mesenchymal stromal, and pluripotent stem cells, together with advances in biomaterials, three-dimensional bioprinting, perfusion, and microfluidic culture. To organize these developments, we introduce the development-to-remodeling continuum (DRC), which distinguishes tissue formation from multicellular integration, adaptive responsiveness, and remodeling competence. We assess collagen-mineral organization, osteocyte-network formation, vascular and metabolic maturation, osteoblast-osteoclast coupling, marrow and immune integration, and mechanical adaptation. We further evaluate applications in developmental and disease modeling, drug assessment, personalized modeling, and bone regeneration. Current limitations include variability, incomplete maturation, transport constraints, and insufficient functional benchmarking. By linking construction strategies to specific bone-related functions and the evidence supporting them, the DRC provides a framework for evaluating functional claims in relation to intended application and translational readiness.

cards.title: DUSP26 Regulated by YY1 Lactylation Couples Osteogenesis and Angiogenesis by Dephosphorylating PMPCB at Y141 and Activating Mitophagy in BMSCs.
cards.abstract: Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) support bone formation through osteogenic differentiation and pro-angiogenic paracrine activity, but the mechanisms coordinating these functions remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified dual-specificity phosphatase 26 (DUSP26) as a regulator of BMSC osteogenesis and mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 expression increased during osteogenic differentiation and was reduced in osteoporotic femoral tissues. p300 gain- and loss-of-function experiments, together with analysis of the Yin Yang1(YY1) K183R mutant, supported the conclusion that p300-regulated YY1 lactylation contributes to DUSP26 transcriptional activation. DUSP26 interacted with the mitochondrial processing peptidase subunit beta(PMPCB) and reduced its tyrosine phosphorylation, with mass spectrometry and mutational analyses implicating Y141 as involved in this regulation. Functional assays supported a model in which DUSP26 limits mitochondrial processing peptidase (MPP)-mediated PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) processing and promotes PINK1-dependent mitophagy, thereby supporting mitochondrial homeostasis. DUSP26 enhanced osteogenic differentiation and the pro-angiogenic activity of BMSC-conditioned medium(CM), whereas its knockdown impaired bone formation and reduced type H vessels in vivo. Furthermore, BMSC-derived exosomes carrying a runt-related transcription factor 2 (RUNX2) promoter-driven DUSP26 plasmid produced preferential transgene expression in osteogenic-lineage cells and attenuated ovariectomy-induced bone loss in mice. These findings link lactylation-associated transcriptional regulation to mitochondrial protein processing and support further preclinical evaluation of DUSP26-directed approaches for osteoporosis.

cards.title: PHGDH-Mediated Serine Metabolism in Nucleus Pulposus Cells Is a Potential Therapeutic Target for Intervertebral Disc Degeneration.
cards.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a major cause of low back pain, driven largely by nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence under chronic hypoxia and nutrient stress. Serine metabolism regulates senescence, but its role in IVDD remains unclear. Here, transcriptomic profiling reveals that the glycine-serine-threonine pathway is downregulated in senescent NPCs, with marked reduction of the serine synthesis rate limiting enzyme PHGDH. This is confirmed by single cell RNA sequencing of human discs, aged rat tissues, and degenerated human samples, accompanied by decreased intracellular serine. PHGDH silencing or serine deprivation inhibits NPC proliferation, induces senescence, and suppresses matrix anabolism. Mechanistically, PHGDH deficiency lowers α ketoglutarate, impairing histone demethylation and increasing H3K27me3 occupancy at the Rap1b promoter, which silences Rap1b and activates mTORC1, thereby blocking autophagic flux. Additionally, serine starvation depletes glutathione, elevates ROS, and promotes apoptosis. In vivo, AAV mediated PHGDH overexpression alleviates puncture induced IVDD, while a serine deficient diet exacerbates degeneration. Collectively, we uncover a PHGDH/Rap1b/mTORC1/autophagy cascade linking serine deprivation to NPC senescence, and propose that restoring PHGDH or serine availability may be a viable strategy to combat age related disc degeneration.

cards.title: The impact of interventions combining nutrition and physical exercise on frailty in old age: A systematic literature review and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM).
cards.abstract: BackgroundFrailty is common in older adults and associated with inadequate nutrition, reduced physical function, and increased vulnerability. While physical exercise benefits frailty outcomes, evidence on combined nutrition and exercise interventions remains unclear.AimTo systematically review evidence on the impact of interventions combining nutrition and physical exercise on frailty status among community-dwelling frail older adults (≥65 years).MethodsThe review followed the Cochrane Handbook, Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020, and Synthesis Without Meta-analysis guidelines. Searches were conducted in PubMed, CINAHL, and Scopus. Randomised controlled trials explicitly defining frailty were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened and assessed methodology using RoB 2.0. Certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Due to heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis without meta-analysis was performed.SummaryOf 2447 records identified, 10 publications met the inclusion criteria. Two trials directly assessed frailty reversal and reported improvements favouring structured exercise, with one showing additional benefit when combined with a nutritional supplement. Odds of frailty reversal ranged from two- to fivefold. Additional studies reported modest improvements in mobility disability risk, lean body mass, and functional performance. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to high, limited by small samples and heterogeneity.Although some studies reported favourable effects of combined nutrition and exercise interventions, the available evidence is insufficient to determine whether nutrition adds benefits beyond exercise alone. Structured exercise consistently benefited frailty-related outcomes. However, due to few studies and substantial heterogeneity, firm conclusions cannot be drawn. Further standardised trials are needed to clarify the role of nutritional components within combined nutrition-exercise interventions in frailty management.

cards.title: PPARγ/P21 Signaling Mediates Butyrate-Driven Protection against Aging-Related Endothelial Dysfunction: A Novel Effect of Soybean Polysaccharide via the Gut-Vascular Axis.
cards.abstract: Aging-induced endothelial dysfunction is a core driver of age-related cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). In 20-month-old naturally aged mice, 12-week soybean polysaccharide (SP) supplementation restored endothelium-dependent relaxation, reduced aortic reactive oxygen species and VCAM-1 in the aortic endothelium, and attenuated colon senescence, improved gut barrier integrity, and reduced systemic inflammation, as shown by decreased serum LPS, IL-1β, TNF-α, and fecal and serum TMA/TMAO levels. SP enriched butyrate-producing gut bacteria, including Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group, and increased gut and serum butyrate, consistent with enhanced microbial short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis capacity predicted by PICRUSt2. Direct butyrate supplementation reproduced these vascular and colonic benefits. It activated PPARγ signaling and downregulated p21, ICAM-1, VCAM-1, and p16, whereas PPARα and PPARδ remained unchanged. These findings support a gut microbiota-butyrate-PPARγ/p21 axis through which SP protects against aging-related endothelial dysfunction, providing a nutritional basis for targeting the gut-vascular axis in cardiovascular aging.

cards.title: Rethinking the functional relevance of posterolateral tibial plateau fractures in anterior cruciate ligament injury.
cards.abstract: Posterolateral tibial plateau fractures (PLTFs) are increasingly recognised in anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)-injured knees, yet their functional relevance remains unsettled. In our view, the recent study by Willinger et al. adds valuable prospective data on the association between PLTFs and lateral-sided soft-tissue pathology, but its findings should be interpreted with caution. The main concern is that PLTFs were analysed as a relatively uniform lesion despite substantial morphologic heterogeneity. Small cortical impressions are unlikely to have the same biomechanical significance as deeper depression defects associated with loss of submeniscal bony support or altered local slope geometry. In addition, preoperative pivot shift is an incomplete surrogate for the functional effect of PLTFs within a multifactorial instability pattern influenced by meniscal, anterolateral, and osseous restraints. The imaging framework also does not quantify structural variables likely to determine mechanical relevance. We therefore believe the study supports only a narrow conclusion: PLTF presence alone is not a reliable surrogate for greater preoperative pivot-shift laxity, whereas the significance of high-grade PLTF phenotypes remains unresolved.

cards.title: Association of runoff risk with private well contamination in a fractured dolostone aquifer.
cards.abstract: In the United States, private well owners are responsible for monitoring and maintaining their drinking water but have little control over neighboring contamination sources and limited information about daily water quality. Potential for rapid contamination in karst settings exacerbates the challenge. The Runoff Risk Advisory Forecast (RRAF) is a real-time online tool available in five US states that helps nutrient applicators avoid times and locations of high runoff risk. We wanted to determine if RRAF could be repurposed in areas susceptible to groundwater contamination to inform well owners of conditions when contamination is likely. Private wells were repeatedly sampled on seven dates (32-36 wells per date) and analyzed for nitrate-nitrogen, total coliforms, and bovine manure markers. Three-day windows of RRAF risk prior to sampling were selected post hoc, ranging from 1 to 3 days prior for manure markers to 10-12 days prior for nitrate. Contaminants were associated with RRAF values of ≥75% within these windows based on observed weather. A hydrologic association between RRAF risk and groundwater depth was also apparent. Overall, results suggest the RRAF model anticipates conditions of elevated contamination risk for susceptible wells. For nitrate, between-well variation and delayed peak concentration suggested that well location and construction factors may be more informative than runoff events. Microbial contamination was rapid and distributed among wells, with one or more detections of coliforms in 31% of wells and bovine markers in 61% of wells. Thus, a warning system based on the RRAF model could help identify conditions of acute pathogen exposure.

cards.title: Study on hydration cementation and enhancement mechanism of grout-rock interface of PVA modified grouting material.
cards.abstract: The weakly cemented sandstone aquifer in coal mine is prone to particle softening under mining disturbance and water-rock interaction, which induces the decrease of rock integrity and the development of water conducting channel, leading to the instability and failure of aquifer. To address the low early-age hydration activity of grouts containing a high proportion of coal gangue, discontinuous grout-rock interfacial bonding, and limited adaptability to weakly cemented sandstone, this paper uses cement and coal gangue(CG) as raw materials to prepare modified grouting materials with different polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) content. The uniaxial compression, XRD, FTIR and SEM test methods were used to systematically study the influence of PVA content on the performance of solid waste based slurry, the bearing characteristics of slurry-rock composite, the evolution of hydration products and the interface micro structure. The synergistic enhancement mechanism of PVA induced hydration cementation film coating and slurry-rock interface was revealed. The results show that: (1) High content of CG weakens the early hydration activity of cement slurry system. After PVA is added, the fluidity of slurry increases, the initial and final setting time is further prolonged, and the bleeding rate decreases, indicating that PVA can improve the flow stability and water retention performance of coal-based solid waste slurry. (2) PVA content has obvious dosage dependence on the bearing capacity of the grout rock complex. The peak stresses of the 0%, 0.3%, 0.6% and 1.0% PVA groups are 4.87 ± 0.14 MPa, 5.35 ± 0.06 MPa, 6.04 ± 0.09 MPa and 5.12 ± 0.09 MPa, respectively. The 0.6% PVA group shows relatively better mechanical properties within the test range of this paper. (3) Appropriate amount of PVA can promote the filling of C-S-H gel, AFt rod crystals and C-H flake crystals on the surface of sandstone particles and in the pores and fracture, and adsorb and coordinate through hydroxyl groups to form hydration products and flexible polymer film. The hydration products provide a rigid skeleton, and the PVA flexible film plays a buffering role in the interface bonding and deformation, and synergistically realizes the densification, continuity and toughness enhancement of the weakly cemented sandstone-grout interface. The experimental results show that 0.6% PVA content can achieve a better balance between slurry performance, water retention stability, interface hydration cementation and mechanical bearing capacity, which can provide material design basis for grouting reinforcement of weakly cemented aquifer, thickening of aquiclude and prevention and control of mining-induced water disasters.

cards.title: Crack identification and detection in mine boreholes using deep learning: A case study of hexi coal mine.
cards.abstract: The internal cracks in deep rock masses are an important factor determining the safety of coal mining. The borehole peeping technology is an important method for obtaining the distribution of coal and rock fractures in deep geological engineering. However, there are often problems such as strong background interference and complex joints in real mines, which bring greater challenges to obtaining the distribution of cracks. Therefore, this study proposes a deep learning-based method for identifying internal cracks, which is used for the intelligent identification and analysis of cracks in drilled rock masses. The experimental verification was carried out based on the real borehole peeping images of the tunnels in Hexi Coal Mine as the data set. By embedding the ResCBAM attention mechanism into the YOLOv8 head network, the reliability and accuracy of identifying internal cracks in rock were further enhanced. The test results show that, the proposed Res-YOLOv8 algorithm can more accurately suppress the interference of complex backgrounds and present the morphological characteristics of rock cracks to compare with the fusion of typical attention mechanisms SE and CBAM with YOLOv8. The ResCBAM-YOLOv8 algorithm demonstrates strong performance in the evaluation indicators of confusion matrix, loss rate, precision, recall and MPA. The proposal of method has improved the efficiency of detecting and identifying cracks in coal and rock masses in real mines, and provided more reliable technical support for the stability evaluation of coal mine roof.

cards.title: Stabilization of canine ilial body fractures using an anatomically contoured locking iliac plate: A short retrospective case series.
cards.abstract: To report the clinical outcomes of canine ilial body fractures stabilized with a newly designed, anatomically 3.5 mm Steelvet Iliac Locking Plate. Retrospective case series. Ten client-owned dogs treated between 2023 and 2024. Medical records and orthogonal pelvic radiographs were reviewed for signalment, fracture configuration, surgical findings, time to radiographic union, postoperative sacral index (SI), complications, and limb function. Continuous variables were summarized as median (interquartile range, IQR), mean ± standard deviation (SD), and range; categorical variables as counts and proportions with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Median age was 3.5 years (IQR 2.25-5.75; range 0.75-10) and median body weight 32.0 kg (IQR 28.3-38.5; range 21-52). Median time to radiographic union was 60 days (IQR 60-62.5; range 60-97). Six of ten dogs (60%; 95% CI 31.3-83.2%) achieved union by 60 days. One dog (10%; 95% CI 1.8-40.4%) developed a cutaneous fistula that resolved within seven days of plate removal after fracture healing. The SI was within normal limits in all dogs at final follow-up, and limb function was normal in 10/10 dogs. In this small case series, stabilization of canine ilial body fractures with the dedicated 3.5 mm Steelvet Iliac Locking Plate was associated with reliable bone healing, a low complication rate, and preserved pelvic canal dimensions. Clinical significance: A dedicated, anatomically contoured locking plate is a feasible option for fixation of canine ilial body fractures, conforming to the iliac surface with no or minimal intraoperative contouring and allowing straightforward application. Larger comparative studies are warranted.

cards.title: Prolonged length of stay in the Italian emergency departments: A competing risks frailty model.
cards.abstract: Emergency department (ED) overcrowding has increased worldwide in recent years. This paper provides quantitative information based on data collected immediately before the COVID-19 outbreak, which can serve as a baseline for developing systematic approaches to prolonged length of stay (LoS) in EDs. We analysed a random sample of 10,077 ED accesses drawn from the 503,797 eligible accesses recorded in 2019 in the 16 largest hospitals of Sicily, Italy. LoS was modelled using a cause-specific competing-risks Cox frailty model with Discharge and Hospitalization as competing endpoints. Two log-normal frailty components were included to account for unobserved heterogeneity between EDs and between patients. Non-proportionality was addressed by stratifying on pathology and by including time-varying effects for triage. Cumulative incidence functions (CIFs) were computed to estimate the probability of each endpoint and strata over time. Median LoS was 1.70 hours for Discharge and 3.77 hours for Hospitalization, and the gap widened markedly in the upper tail (90th percentile: 7.10 vs 34.95 hours). Discharge was associated with pathology, age, triage, sex and season; Hospitalization with pathology, age, triage and season. The hazard of Discharge decreased by 2% per additional year of age (HR = 0.98, 95% CI 0.977-0.983) and was 10% higher for accesses in summer (HR = 1.10, 95% CI 1.03-1.16). The hazard of Hospitalization increased by 0.4% per year of age (HR = 1.004, 95% CI 1.001-1.007). The effect of triage was time-dependent: at 10 hours of LoS, red-coded accesses had a 69% lower hazard of Discharge (HR = 0.31) and a 53% higher hazard of Hospitalization (HR = 1.53) than other codes. Circulatory and respiratory diseases and blood diseases showed the highest CIFs for Hospitalization and prolonged LoS for both endpoints, whereas skin and musculoskeletal diseases, injuries and poisoning, and nervous system diseases showed the highest CIFs for Discharge. Prolonged LoS in Sicilian EDs was driven mainly by pathology, and the exit process differed systematically across disease groups: patients with circulatory and respiratory diseases and with blood diseases waited longest before both Discharge and Hospitalization.The large between-ED heterogeneity in the hazard of Hospitalization, indicates that admission delays reflect organisational as well as structural constraints. Interventions to reduce overcrowding - in particular any expansion of inpatient capacity - should therefore be targeted at the specific wards receiving these patients, rather than applied uniformly across the hospital.

cards.title: Bioelectrical impedance analysis versus dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry for sarcopenia assessment in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia is common in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA) is cheaper and more accessible than dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). We assessed whether BIA can replace DXA for measuring muscle mass and classifying low muscle mass in adults with T2DM. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and CINAHL were searched to March 2026 (updated 7 October 2026) for studies measuring muscle mass with both methods in adults with T2DM. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-C. The primary outcome was Bland-Altman agreement (bias, DXA - BIA; population limits of agreement); classification, diagnostic accuracy and correlation (association only) were secondary. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp intervals; certainty was rated with GRADE. Seven studies (646 participants, six countries) were included. For whole-body fat-free mass (three studies), the pooled bias was +0.82 kg (95% CI -0.69 to +2.34; population limits of agreement -6.4 to +8.0 kg). For appendicular lean-mass indices (three studies), the bias was -0.13 kg/m2 (95% CI -1.32 to +1.06; I2 = 98%; limits -1.8 to +1.5 kg/m2). In three studies classifying low muscle mass by both methods, the pooled difference in proportions (BIA - DXA) was +3.6 percentage points (95% CI -8.6 to +15.7). With the same thresholds for both methods (two studies), BIA sensitivity was 71% and 91% and specificity 94% and 64%. Estimates were strongly correlated (r = 0.90), reflecting association, not agreement. Certainty of evidence was low or very low. In adults with T2DM, BIA and DXA showed no clear average difference, but individual estimates and classifications differed too much for interchangeable use. Where DXA is unavailable, standardised BIA may support initial assessment, but results that would change management, particularly near diagnostic thresholds, should be confirmed with DXA.

cards.title: Aggressive Hepatic AL Amyloidosis Encountering Therapeutic Frailty: Rapid Organ Reversal With Tailored Daratumumab-Based Therapy and Low-Dose Corticosteroids in a Patient With Steroid-Induced Psychosis.
cards.abstract: Hepatic AL amyloidosis can cause severe cholestasis independent of marrow tumor burden. In patients with absolute contraindications to high-dose steroids-such as steroid-induced psychosis-tailored daratumumab regimens with low-dose corticosteroids can drive rapid, life-saving organ reversal. However, intensive antimicrobial vigilance remains mandatory.
