cards.title: [Expression of Concern] D‑galactose induces astrocytic aging and contributes to astrocytoma progression and chemoresistance via cellular senescence.
cards.abstract: Following the publication of the above paper, it was drawn to the Editor's attention by a concerned reader that the p16 antibody that the authors reported to have used for the western blot experiment shown in Fig. 1C (cat. no. ab51243) is specific for the protein known as P16 ARC (or ARPC5), not the apoptosis‑associated protein p16INK4a, as was intended. The authors were contacted by the Editorial Office to offer an explanation for the apparent selection of an unsuitable antibody in this paper, and although they have replied, they have been unable to present the proof of purchase of the antibody in question given the lengthy time period that has elapsed since this study was published. Therefore, owing to the fact that the Editorial Office has been made aware of potential issues surrounding the scientific integrity of this paper, we are issuing an Expression of Concern to notify readers of this potential problem. [Molecular Medicine Reports 20: 4111‑4118, 2019; DOI: 10.3892/mmr.2019.10677].

cards.title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis shapes brain T-cell immunity in accelerated aging.
cards.abstract: The bidirectional communication between the gut microbiota, immune system, and central nervous system-the gut‒brain axis-plays a vital role in maintaining brain health. Its disruption can lead to neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. However, the relationship between the gut microbiota and age-related changes in brain immunity remains unclear. This study examined gut microbiota composition and T-cell profiles in senescence-accelerated SAMP8 mice and senescence-resistant SAMR1 controls at young adult and aged stages. The accelerated-aging phenotype of SAMP8 mice was confirmed by reduced behavioral performance and brain transcriptomic alterations. Fecal microbiota profiles were obtained using culture-dependent plating and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. T-cell phenotypes were determined by flow cytometry on brain and splenic leukocytes. Strain, age, and sex were drivers of microbiota composition variation. Microbial diversity differed between strains independently of age. Several bacterial genera had altered abundances in young SAMP8 mice, with only Intestinimonas remaining higher in aged SAMP8. T-cell profiling revealed strain- and age-specific immune signatures. In the brain, SAMP8 mice exhibited a higher CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio, and higher levels of pro-inflammatory cytokine-producing CD4⁺ T cells compared to SAMR1. In contrast, the spleens of SAMP8 mice had a lower CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio. Only the spleens of aged SAMP8 mice showed increased T-cell activation (effector/naïve ratios) and higher levels of pro-inflammatory cytokine-producing CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells, suggesting age- and tissue-specific immune alterations. Nine bacterial genera correlated with immune cell frequencies and ratios. Notably, Intestinimonas showed a discordant association with the CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio in the brain (negative) and spleen (positive). Furthermore, CD8⁺ T cells correlated with microbiota composition variation more strongly than strain, age, and sex. Together, these findings link the gut microbiota to age-dependent immune remodeling in the brain and imply that altered microbial communities could influence pro-inflammatory T-cell responses, thereby contributing to accelerated brain aging.

cards.title: Ultrasound Identification of Calcific Patellar Tendinitis After Patellar Fracture Fixation.
cards.abstract: Calcific tendinopathy most commonly affects the rotator cuff, whereas involvement of the patellar tendon is exceedingly rare. Persistent anterior knee pain following patellar fracture fixation is usually attributed to postoperative stiffness, hardware irritation, or altered biomechanics, potentially leading to underrecognition of concomitant tendon pathology. Musculoskeletal ultrasound is well suited for evaluating postoperative tendon disorders because it enables detailed assessment of tendon abnormalities while simultaneously depicting adjacent soft tissues and surgical implants. This presentation highlights intratendinous calcification accompanied by active tendinopathic changes after patellar fracture fixation and emphasizes the diagnostic contribution of ultrasound in the evaluation of persistent postoperative anterior knee pain.

cards.title: Chairside frailty screening in hemodialysis patients: diagnostic accuracy of the Kihon Checklist combined with calf circumference.
cards.abstract: Frailty screening is important in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD), but routine implementation is limited by time, space, and mobility constraints. Self-reported tools such as the Kihon Checklist (KCL) are feasible but may not fully capture physical vulnerability. This study evaluated whether adding calf circumference (CC) to the KCL improves chairside frailty screening performance. This cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study included 200 MHD patients at a tertiary medical center. Frailty was defined using the Physical Frailty Phenotype (PFP). Multivariable models compared a baseline KCL model with the primary KCL + CC model using bilateral mean CC. Prespecified sensitivity analyses examined bilateral maximum CC and a modified PFP reference standard without the weakness criterion. HGS-containing models were additionally evaluated as exploratory analyses. Model performance was assessed using AUC, continuous net reclassification improvement (cNRI), integrated discrimination improvement (IDI), decision curve analysis, and bootstrap internal validation. Overall, 120 patients (60.0%) were frail. The baseline KCL model showed strong discrimination (AUC, 0.923; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.885-0.961), with 80.0% sensitivity and 91.3% specificity. Adding CC improved discrimination (AUC, 0.953; 95% CI, 0.928-0.979), sensitivity (86.7%), reclassification (cNRI, 0.850; IDI, 0.085; both p < 0.001), and net benefit while maintaining specificity (91.3%). Findings remained robust in sensitivity analyses using bilateral maximum CC and a modified PFP without the weakness criterion. The internally validated AUC of the KCL + CC model was 0.942. Adding CC to the KCL provides a feasible, non-ambulatory chairside approach for improving frailty screening in MHD patients.

cards.title: Gap test-inspired crack-parallel tension tests of fracture of soft-knitted polymer composites simulated by microplane triads.
cards.abstract: Soft composites are increasingly used in wearable and soft robotic systems, as advances in material architecture enable greater damage tolerance under large deformation. In these mesoscale architectures, the crack-parallel stresses modify the crack initiation and growth in the opening-mode fracture. Emulating the gap test, we introduce a fracture test to quantify how the superposed crack-parallel tension affects the maximum load (i.e., the load capacity) and the load-deflection curve. A Mode I (opening mode) center-notched tensioned strip is used because its advantages in generating crack-parallel tension outweigh its hypothetical disadvantages with possible instability of crack jumps at two competing crack fronts. We develop and experimentally validate a continuum model that captures the nonlinear behavior and progressive damage of knitted composites. To this end, we introduce an ensemble of oriented microplane triads tangential to the yarn at characteristic points of the yarn loop within a repetitive unit cell of the knit. The triads ensure the yarn-polymer transfer of all normal and shear stress components at each characteristic point. The experimentally calibrated computational model provides a tool to predict the effect of crack-parallel tension on the changes of load capacity and of the effective fracture energy of knitted polymer composites, enabling rational design of these composites in engineering applications such as wearables and soft robotics.

cards.title: A genome-wide senescence synthetic lethality screen identifies PARP16 as a senolytic target.
cards.abstract: Accumulation of senescent cells is increasingly viewed as a significant contributor to aging and age-related diseases. To date, the elimination of senescent cells through small molecule senolytic agents has largely relied on a limited number of repurposed agents, often leveraged from previous oncological applications. Here, we describe a CRISPR-based, genome-wide, synthetic lethal screen for senescent cells. From this screen, we identify a number of genes whose deletion appears to be well tolerated in normal proliferating cells, but whose deletion is lethal in the context of senescence. We further characterize one promising candidate gene encoding the ER-resident protein PARP16. Knockdown of PARP16 does not affect the viability of mouse or human cells but results in the death of a wide range of senescent cells. Furthermore, two distinct small molecule PARP16 inhibitors have little effect of normal cell growth but result in the selective death of senescent cells in culture and in freshly isolated human donor lung tissue explants. Together, these results demonstrate a rational strategy to identify novel senolytic therapies that could have potential applications for a wide range of age-related conditions.

cards.title: Progerin‐Induced Premature Aging Depends on Both Its Farnesylation and Polymerization Status
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Hutchinson‐Gilford Progeria (HGPS) is a severe premature aging syndrome caused by a mutation in lamin A (LA). Pre‐LA is initially farnesylated, tethered to the inner nuclear membrane (INM), and subsequently proteolytically cleaved to liberate mature LA from its farnesylated tail. In HGPS, the truncated LA mutant progerin lacks this cleavage site and remains permanently farnesylated and INM‐tethered. We previously demonstrated that progerin's permanent farnesylation, and not its truncation, is responsible for inducing heterochromatin loss, DNA damage and premature senescence. These findings raised the question how permanent tethering of progerin to the INM causes senescence. To address this, we repurposed the FRB‐FKBP two‐component dimerization system to solely express progerin's farnesylated C‐terminal tail or N‐terminus, or to dimerize both domains using a rapalog. We find that dimerized full‐length progerin is required to cause heterochromatin loss, raising the question how progerin's N‐terminus contributes to perturbing cell function. We demonstrate that introducing mutations that disrupt N‐terminal polymerization avert progerin‐induced defects. In agreement with these findings, reducing the pool of endogenous LA available for polymerization with progerin recapitulates this rescue. Finally, we propose a two‐anchor model where LA/progerin must be tethered to the INM and polymerize with other A‐type lamins to cause premature senescence. To validate this, we tethered LA to the INM by fusing it to the permanently farnesylated C‐terminus of lamin B1 (LB1). These LA/LB1 chimeras recapitulate progerin‐induced cellular defects, confirming this model. Collectively, these findings provide unprecedented molecular detail into premature cell aging and have implications for other laminopathies.

cards.title: Genome architecture and duplication-associated functional diversification in the carnivorous plant Sarracenia purpurea
cards.abstract: The repeated evolution of complex traits raises the question of how genomes generate ecological novelty while preserving developmental organization. We present a chromosome-scale genome assembly and annotation for the carnivorous purple pitcher plant, Sarracenia purpurea, and investigate how two contrasting modes of gene duplication have shaped its genome and functional repertoire: ancient polyploidy, which leaves duplicated genes in conserved chromosomal regions (syntenic duplicates), and local tandem duplication, which generates neighboring gene copies. We compare these duplication classes across nine angiosperms. The genome shows a mosaic of conserved and fractionated duplicated regions reflecting differential retention and loss of genes following ancient polyploidy and later restructuring. Comparison with noncarnivorous Actinidia (kiwifruit) identifies 18 syntenic and nine tandem Gene Ontology (GO) Biological Process term-duplication-class combinations enriched in Sarracenia but not significantly enriched in Actinidia. Syntenic enrichments include meristem maintenance, organ-boundary specification, cuticle development, and hormonal regulation; tandem enrichments include defense responses, oxidative stress, jasmonic-acid biosynthesis, leaf senescence, and oligopeptide transport. Across the carnivorous genera Sarracenia, Nepenthes, Utricularia, and Pinguicula, we identify 19 syntenic and two tandem-associated biological processes showing significant enrichment in all four lineages, revealing striking functional commonalities across multiple evolutionary origins of carnivory despite their divergent trap morphologies and ecological strategies. Among Sarracenia genes differentially expressed in at least one comparison of flower, pitcher-leaf, and root tissues, tandem-class genes exhibit larger maximum absolute expression differences and greater GO richness and effective breadth at matched numbers of annotated homologs. These results highlight the complementary evolutionary contributions of ancient genome duplication and local gene-family expansion to the developmental and ecological diversification of carnivorous plants.

cards.title: Quantifying age-associated differences in the durability of Shingrix-induced immunity using mathematical modelling
cards.abstract: Understanding the durability of vaccine-induced immunity is critical for evaluating long-term protection and vaccine scheduling, particularly in aging populations where immunosenescence may alter immune response dynamics. In this study, we used a novel mathematical modelling pipeline to quantify age-related differences in the contraction and persistence phases of gE-specific CD4+ T cell and anti-gE antibody responses following Shingrix vaccination. Specifically, we developed a semi-mechanistic model to expand virtual populations that captured inter-individual variability in peak concentrations and waning dynamics. To compare immune responses across age groups, we introduced a time varying, age-related immune advantage metric that measures the probability of a randomly selected younger individual exhibiting a stronger immune response than one from an older group. By evaluating this metric across multiple simulated virtual populations, our results demonstrate clear and sustained age-related differences in both gE-specific CD4+ T cells and anti-gE antibody responses, with younger age groups consistently exhibiting higher responses. Given these age-related differences, we used our model to explore alternative vaccine schedules in older age groups. These exploratory simulations suggest that booster doses administered between 6 and 12 months following the second dose may mitigate age-related differences in antibody dynamics. This work highlights the use of mechanistic mathematical modelling to disentangle age-associated differences in vaccine outcomes and lead to designing of plausible improvement in age-specific vaccine schedules.

cards.title: Unified Machine Learning Model for Early Detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment, Frailty, and Fall Risk Using Multimodal Motor-Function Data
cards.abstract: Background: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI), frailty, and fall risk often co-occur in older adults and share motor signs, yet they are screened and modeled separately. A unified model that predicts all 3 conditions from 1 sensor-based assessment could support earlier and more efficient screening, but such a model has rarely been developed or rigorously compared with separate models. Objective: This study aimed to develop a unified machine learning model that predicts MCI, frailty, and fall risk together from sensor-based motor-function data, compare it with separate single-label models, explain its predictions, and test its robustness. Methods: Community-dwelling older adults (n=79) completed a multimodal motor-function assessment with the Mizzou Point-of-Care Assessment System (MPASS), covering gait, sit-to-stand, static balance, step-down, and reaction time, with some tasks repeated under a dual-task condition. With demographic and family-history data, this yielded 59 features. Unified classifier-chain and single-label models were built with 5 algorithms across 6 modeling stages, evaluated with repeated nested cross-validation, and compared using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and paired bootstrap tests. The final model was explained with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP), and its robustness and the sufficiency of the sample size were tested with chain-input, chain-order sensitivity, domain-ablation, learning-curve, and power analyses. Results: With class weighting, the unified model had a higher mean AUC than the single-label models in 17 of 20 configurations and was never significantly worse, and it performed at least as well under nested model selection (0.615 vs 0.605; P=.58). The final extra trees model achieved a mean AUC of 0.645 (95% CI 0.569-0.722); discrimination was best for MCI (AUC 0.779, 95% CI 0.680-0.872) and lower for frailty (0.606) and fall risk (0.551). The model overestimated risk for all 3 outcomes, most for frailty. Most features (43/59, 73%), led by stride length, were shared across the 3 conditions, with consistent SHAP rankings in training and test participants ({rho}=0.99). Predicted frailty was the most important input for fall risk, and the 45 sensor features alone performed as well as the full model. Learning curves suggested that fall-risk prediction would benefit from more participants. Conclusions: A unified model predicted MCI, frailty, and fall risk together from one sensor-based assessment and performed as well as 3 separate models. It identified motor features shared across the conditions and used the link between frailty and fall risk. It performed best for MCI; with improvement for frailty and fall risk, recalibration, and external validation, such a model could support efficient screening of older adults for several conditions at once. KEYWORDS mild cognitive impairment; frailty; fall risk; machine learning; multi-label classification; classifier chain; gait; dual task; explainable artificial intelligence; Shapley additive explanations.

cards.title: Seasonal spectral separation of shrub and herbaceous vegetation using in situ hyperspectral and Sentinel-2 data.
cards.abstract: Shrub encroachment is reshaping alpine grasslands on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and requires reliable remote sensing approaches to separate shrubs from herbaceous vegetation across seasons. We combined in situ Analytical Spectral Devices (ASD) hyperspectral measurements with Sentinel-2 multispectral observations to characterize canopy spectra and quantify separability during early-growing, peak-growing, and senescence stages using band sensitivity analysis, univariate separability metrics, vegetation indices, and satellite-scale evaluation. Green (505-570 nm) and near-infrared (750-900 nm) regions provided strong separation, while Sentinel-2 retained diagnostic contrast in visible (B3-B5) and near-infrared (B8) bands, with June emerging as the most favorable period. Vegetation indices showed phenology-dependent performance: Corrected Transformed Vegetation Index (CTVI) and Transformed Vegetation Index (TVI) were effective in early and late seasons, IPVI performed well at peak and senescence, and Transformed Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (TNDVI) remained stable across stages. Although Sentinel-2 was less discriminative than hyperspectral data, selected bands and indices still supported effective shrub-herbaceous separation for landscape-scale monitoring.

cards.title: Geophysics-informed hydrologic modeling reveals contrasting regolith and bedrock responses of headwater catchments to warming.
cards.abstract: Predicting how warming reshapes headwater streamflow requires distinguishing shallow and deep subsurface contributions, which remain difficult to constrain in catchment-scale models. We use seismic P-wave velocity to partition the critical zone into regolith and fractured bedrock domains within a three-dimensional physically based model and develop a particle-based attribution method to quantify their streamflow contributions and source-water ages across realizations spanning diverse hydraulic configurations. Across these realizations, warming produces contrasting subsurface hydrologic responses: Regolith-sourced streamflow generally becomes slightly younger, whereas fractured bedrock-sourced streamflow generally ages. This contrast arises because warming increases evapotranspiration and alters snow accumulation and melt timing, reducing effective recharge and lowering fractured-bedrock saturation. Declining recharge slows water transit and shifts fractured-bedrock-sourced water toward longer flow paths. Our results suggest that warming may reduce fractured-bedrock water renewal, with implications for the buffering role of bedrock water storage and for prolonged retention of legacy contaminants.

cards.title: Anatomical Handling Properties of Costal and Auricular Cartilage in Fresh-frozen Cadaveric Models for Revision Rhinoplasty.
cards.abstract: Revision rhinoplasty is among the most technically demanding procedures in facial surgery, requiring mastery of complex anatomy, advanced surgical skills, and proficiency in structural grafting. Cadaveric dissection remains a fundamental component of surgical training, yet the suitability of fresh-frozen anatomical specimens for simulating graft preparation has not been systematically assessed. This study evaluates the handling characteristics and graft-preparation feasibility of costal and auricular cartilage harvested from fresh-frozen cadavers used in structured revision rhinoplasty dissection. Ten fresh-frozen cadaveric heads and two thoracic specimens were dissected. Costal cartilage was harvested bilaterally from ribs 5-8, and auricular cartilage bilaterally through a posterior conchal approach. Graft length, width, thickness, preparation time, carvability, laminar fragmentation, and suturability were assessed. Because multiple samples were obtained from the same donor, donor-level means were used for inferential comparisons. Costal cartilage was rigid and brittle, with macroscopic and handling characteristics consistent with calcification. Laminar thinning resulted in fragmentation in 85% of attempts, and intentionally thicker slices displayed macroscopically visible microfractures and fractured during suturing. No costal graft was suitable for spreader or septal extension graft simulation. Auricular cartilage maintained elasticity, allowed reproducible laminar carving, and withstood suturing without fracture. Preparation time differed significantly between graft types. In the specimens examined, costal cartilage was unsuitable for laminar graft-preparation simulation because of fragmentation and fracture, although rib harvesting remained valuable for thoracic-exposure training. Auricular cartilage was more consistently suitable for graft-shaping simulation. These findings describe distinct roles for the two cartilage sources within fresh-frozen cadaveric simulation of revision rhinoplasty.

cards.title: Involvement of abscisic acid in the regulation of postharvest senescence in cut roses.
cards.abstract: Abscisic acid (ABA) is a major hormonal regulator of senescence in ethylene-insensitive flowers, but its involvement in ethylene-sensitive flowers remains unclear. This study examined the involvement of ABA in the postharvest senescence of cut roses (Rosa hybrida) from two cultivars differing in ethylene sensitivity, 'Deep Purple' and 'Iguana'. Senescence indicators and endogenous ABA levels were monitored throughout vase life. The effects of exogenous ABA and 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (ACC), the direct precursor of ethylene, were also assessed. Results showed that endogenous ABA contents increased as senescence progressed in both cultivars. However, basal ABA levels were one order of magnitude higher in 'Deep Purple', the more ethylene-sensitive cultivar, which also had the shortest vase life. ABA content was strongly correlated with flower neck bending, petal dehydration, ion leakage, and color changes in 'Iguana', but only with petal dehydration in 'Deep Purple'. Exogenous ABA accelerated senescence in both cultivars, although its effects differed: it increased petal dehydration and flower neck bending in 'Deep Purple', whereas it affected all measured parameters in 'Iguana', suggesting greater ABA sensitivity in this cultivar. ACC also accelerated senescence in both cultivars but increased endogenous ABA content only in 'Iguana'. These results indicate that ABA is involved in regulating postharvest senescence in cut roses, particularly through its effects on water homeostasis, with a more prominent contribution in the cultivar less sensitive to ethylene.

cards.title: High-intensity interval training reduces obesity-induced renal inflammation, oxidative stress, dysfunction, and histopathology despite no effect on telomere related genes in male rats.
cards.abstract: Obesity is a key driver of renal senescence, affecting oxidative stress, chronic inflammation and telomere shortening, and as a consequence induces senescence. This study aimed to investigate the effects of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on obesity-induced renal senescence in male rats. Twenty male Wistar rats were randomly allocated into four experimental groups: control diet non-training (C), control diet with HIIT (E), high-fat diet non-training (O), and high-fat diet with HIIT (OE). Obesity was induced using a high-fat diet for 8 weeks in the O and OE groups. Subsequently, the E and OE groups underwent an 8-weeks treadmill HIIT protocol (5 sessions per week, 4-10 intervals at 80-100% of their maximal speed). We assessed renal oxidative stress markers (MDA, SOD, and CAT), inflammatory markers (IL-1β, and IL-10), serum and urine parameters, KIM-1 , Resolvin (Rv)D1, mRNA expression of telomere-related genes (TERT, TRF1, and TRF2), and renal histopathology. The O group showed significantly higher weight gain than the C group (p<0.001), with increased oxidative stress (MDA; p<0.001) and inflammation (higher expression of IL-1β and lower expression of IL-10 and RvD1; p<0.001), along with reduced antioxidant defences (SOD, CAT; p<0.001). It also exhibited higher urinary renal injury markers (glucose, albumin, KIM, protein; p<0.001) and serum urea (p<0.01), with decreased GFR (p<0.01 vs C and OE). Expression levels of TERT (p<0.001), TRF1, and TRF2 (p<0.01) were also lower in the O group compared with the C group. OE group partially reversed these alterations, improving oxidative stress, inflamtion and renal function parameters (p<0.05-0.001). Histopathology revealed marked portal inflammation and adipose penetration in the O group, which was significantly attenuated in the OE group. These findings demonstrate that 8-week HIIT can effectively counteract obesity-induced oxidative stress, inflammation, and kidney histopathology and dysfunction, but not telomere shortening. .

cards.title: Cranial Injuries due to Misuse of Infant Carriers.
cards.abstract: Infant carriers (car seats, bouncy chairs) can cause injuries when used for other than their intended purpose. We studied children aged 0-24 months with carrier related injuries reported to the Pennsylvania Trauma Outcome Study (PTOS) dataset (2001-2022 inclusive). There were 562 injured children, averaging 23 injuries per year. Mean age was 3.3 months; 54.3% were male. Most (82.7%) fell from an elevated surface; 88.7% fell an estimated 2-5 feet. Head injuries (intracranial injury/hemorrhage and/or skull fracture) were present in 85.6%. Admission Glasgow Coma Scores were most commonly 15 (79.1%); 7 had GCS <12. Average Injury Severity Score was 9.3 (range 1-30). Average length of stay was 1.4 days; 30% spent >1 day in the intensive care unit. Two children underwent cranial operations. There were no deaths, and 82.9% were discharged home. Falls in, or from, infant carriers are a significant public health concern. Education, advocacy, and changes in carrier design may help reduce the frequency of these injuries.

cards.title: Public Acceptability of Self-Payment for Community Pharmacists' Services: A National Online Survey
cards.abstract: Background The traditional business model for sustaining United States (U.S.) community pharmacies has relied on income generated by product sales. A fee-for-service model could help alleviate insufficient profit by monetizing conventionally free pharmacy services if patients are willing to pay out-of-pocket. Objectives This study evaluated public acceptability of out-of-pocket payment for community pharmacist-provided services, variation in payment acceptability across services, and assessed whether payment acceptability differed by respondent characteristics and trust constructs. Methods This study represents a cross-sectional online survey of U.S. adults conducted during spring 2026 using a non-probability sampling approach. Primary outcomes were binary stated payment-acceptability judgments for a variety of pharmacist and health services. The survey used a between-subjects randomized payment-framing design, where participants were assigned to either a stated-price condition or an any-payment condition. Secondary outcomes included trust designations and participant demographic characteristics. Results A total of 1069 respondents completed the survey. A $20 fee was viewed more favorably than a general "any amount of money" fee. In the $20 stated-price condition, agreement was highest for osteoporosis screening (75.8%) and travel-related vaccines (69.0%), and lowest for antibiotic use consultation (23.9%) and wound care (32.1%). Older respondents and Hispanic respondents were less likely to view payment as acceptable, whereas men and respondents with greater pharmacist trust were more likely to view payment as acceptable. Conclusion Although patients historically have received many community pharmacy services at no cost, this study demonstrates that the concept of self-payment ifor certain services is considered acceptable, especially for services not typically provided.

cards.title: A stochastic developmental framework for maize leaf area dynamics.
cards.abstract: Maize developmental models have traditionally focused on crop growth, biomass production, or architectural traits, whereas fewer studies have integrated leaf development, expansion, and senescence within a single dynamic framework. Here, we present a stochastic developmental framework for the dynamics of the maize leaf area that combines temperature-driven plant development with a dynamic representation of the total, green and senesced leaf area. The framework extends a stage-structured model previously developed by generalizing leaf area development to plants producing between 6 and 29 final leaves, incorporating a structural delay between leaf appearance and full expansion, and introducing a parsimonious two-parameter senescence module. Sensitivity analyses identified distinct roles of the senescence parameters in controlling the timing, magnitude, and persistence of the green leaf area. Simulated senesced leaf-area trajectories were compared with published experimental data for six maize hybrids, capturing the main temporal trends, although the agreement varied among hybrids. The proposed framework provides a parsimonious and developmental description of the dynamics of the maize leaf area. Beyond its relevance for maize development, the model establishes a basis for future ecological applications in which the temporal availability of the green leaf area governs interactions between maize plants and specialized herbivorous insects.

cards.title: Tough cellulose nanofiber-based nanocomposite films incorporating Ag-decorated TiO₂ nanoparticles with low cytotoxicity and visible-light response for antibacterial applications.
cards.abstract: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO₂NPs) are widely used photocatalysts for antibacterial applications and environmental remediation. However, their UV-dependent activity and powder form limit practical applications. To address these issues, Ag-decorated TiO₂NPs (ATs, Ag/TiO₂ = 8 wt%) were synthesized by sonicating TiO₂NPs in an AgNO₃ solution, followed by hydrothermal reduction and oven drying. Subsequently, the ATs with visible-light response were incorporated into a TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofiber (TOCNF) dispersion via sonication, followed by oven drying to fabricate TOCNF-AT (TF-AT) composite films. The properties of the well-designed TF-AT films can be tuned by varying the AT content and light irradiation. In particular, the TF-AT10 film (AT/TOCNF = 10 wt%) exhibited a high work of fracture (WOF, 3.5 MJ m-3), over three times that of the pristine TOCNF film, indicating effective reinforcement of the TOCNF matrix by the ATs. Furthermore, owing to its controlled Ag+ release behavior, the TF-AT10 film showed low cytotoxicity (cell viability >90%) and strong antibacterial activity, achieving 100% and 90.1% inhibition against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus under visible-light irradiation, respectively. This performance may result from Ag-induced localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) and the release of Ag+ species. Although the TF-AT5 film (AT/TOCNF = 5 wt%) exhibited slightly lower WOF and antibacterial activity, its higher transparency (61% transmittance at 550 nm) offers advantages for practical applications. Therefore, the TF-AT films are promising candidates for advanced antibacterial applications.

cards.title: Carboxymethyl cellulose-regulated poly(vinyl alcohol) ionic networks for recyclable strain sensing.
cards.abstract: Conductive hydrogels are promising soft materials for flexible sensing, electronic skins, and human-machine interaction; however, integrating mechanical robustness, stable ionic transport, environmental adaptability, and reprocessability within a fully physically crosslinked network remains challenging. Here, we report a Hofmeister-effect-assisted multi-interaction strategy for constructing a physically crosslinked ionic hydrogel based on polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), termed P-MC. Freeze-thaw-induced PVA microcrystals serve as reversible load-bearing junctions, while concentrated MgSO₄ simultaneously provides mobile ions and promotes polymer-chain association through the Hofmeister effect. CMC forms a semi-interpenetrating network with PVA, and ethylene glycol regulates water-polymer interactions to improve environmental stability. The resulting P-MC hydrogel exhibits a tensile strength of 0.87 MPa, a fracture strain of 525.09%, favorable biosafety, anti-drying and anti-freezing performance, and thermal reprocessability. Distinguishable electromechanical responses are retained after five recycling cycles. By mounting two P-MC sensors on the index finger and thumb and processing the resulting dual-channel resistance signals using a one-dimensional convolutional neural network, six hand gestures are classified with a test accuracy of 99.44%; direct testing of the trained model on two additional volunteers yields accuracies of 95.00% and 96.67%. Additional demonstrations include joint-motion monitoring and core-sheath fiber-based triboelectric output. This work establishes a Hofmeister-regulated physical-network design strategy for recyclable, environmentally adaptable, and intelligently interactive flexible electronics.

cards.title: Integrating biomass production platform and identification approach for stereochemical assignment of super-carbon-chain compounds.
cards.abstract: Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. The modular fragment-based identification (MFBI) approach is successfully employed to establish the relative and absolute configurations of SCCCs. As an example, 157.7 mg of a minor SCCC, named amphidiketol A, featuring a highly-flexible C76-linear carbon backbone and thirty-three carbon stereocenters, is obtained from Amphidinium sp. in our platform. Its hybrid architecture contains eleven‌ distinct modular fragments. Its relative and absolute configurations are successfully established by the MFBI approach. Collectively, an undescribed paradigm for stereochemical assignment of SCCCs is presented. Nine senescence-associated protein targets of amphidiketol A in lung cancer A549 cells are identified.

cards.title: Cellulose-Derived Water-Free, Anti-Freezing, and Self-Initiated Ionogel for Flexible Wearable Electronics.
cards.abstract: The growing demand for sustainable flexible electronics has positioned cellulose as a promising candidate, yet its efficient dissolution and functionalization remain challenging due to its highly crystalline structure and strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding. While a wide variety of cellulose dissolution systems have been reported in the literature, most systems still depend on toxic initiators or complex processes. Herein, we report a sunlight-driven, initiator-free green synthesis of cellulose-based ionogels that enables direct cellulose dissolution and in situ photopolymerization, which provides a facile and sustainable route to anti-freezing ionogels via the direct in situ polymerization of ionogel precursors without initiators or crosslinkers. Notably, the incorporation of cellulose, along with the intrinsic properties of the 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride ([Bmim]Cl) and ethylene glycol (EG) significantly enhanced the mechanical properties of the conductive ionogel, which exhibited outstanding mechanical performance (fracture strain of 935%, fracture stress of 166.5 kPa), robust adhesive properties (1.48 MPa), excellent conductivity (0.028 mS·cm-1) and wide work temperature range (-20∼60 °C). These properties enabled the ionogel to function not only as a wearable strain sensor for motion detection but also as a self-powered controller for operating a remote-controlled car via human-computer interaction. This work provides a versatile and sustainable strategy for fabricating high-performance cellulose ionogels, paving the high value-added way for future soft electronic systems with multifunctional integration.

cards.title: Development of Long-Acting Teriparatide Analogues through Iterative Peptide Scanning and Site-Specific Modification by Serine/Threonine Ligation.
cards.abstract: Teriparatide, the only FDA-approved osteoanabolic drug for osteoporosis, suffers from poor metabolic stability and requires frequent subcutaneous injections, leading to suboptimal patient compliance. To find optimized teriparatide derivatives, we herein report an iterative peptide scanning strategy followed by a serine/threonine ligation (STL) chemistry for site-specific modifications. Using our 2-hydroxyphenol-pseudoproline (ψ2-hydroxyphenolpro) modification (HPM) method, two series of teriparatide analogues with different types of substituents were successfully prepared for scanning the modifiable sites and their expansibility. Through chemoselective acylation of embedded serine/threonine residues, several fatty acids of unequal lengths were introduced to further improve the pharmacokinetic properties of scanning derivatives. Among the 12 lipidated analogues, 54, 55, 62, and 63 exhibited potent antiosteoporotic activities in vitro and in vivo close to those of native teriparatide. The most effective compound, 62, also demonstrated significantly enhanced serum stability and may serve as a promising candidate for further development of long-acting antiosteoporotic pharmaceuticals.

cards.title: Aging Remodels the Female Skeletal Muscle Proteome Toward Matrix, Chromatin and Lysosomal Programs that Track Loss of Physical Function
cards.abstract: Loss of skeletal muscle strength and mobility is among the most consequential features of human aging, yet the molecular programs that accompany this decline in women remain poorly understood. Here, we performed deep comprehensive data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomic profiling of vastus lateralis biopsies from 10 younger (24-30 years) and 10 older (70-84 years) healthy women enrolled through the NIH Common Fund Cellular Senescence Network (SenNet), with matched measurements of grip strength and gait speed. Of 2,391 quantified protein groups, 163 were significantly altered with age, and partial least squares-discriminant analysis completely separated the age groups (cross-validated AUC = 1.00). Older muscle showed increased extracellular matrix and vascular remodeling proteins (TIMP3, COL8A1, ELN, FBN1), nuclear, chromatin and RNA-binding proteins (HMGB1, HMGB2, histone H1.0, MATR3, NCL), and lysosomal and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-associated proteins (CTSZ, CTSD, PSAP), together with reduced glycolytic and energetic proteins (GAPDH, ENO3, PHKA1, CYCS). Age effects were robust to adjust for body mass index (BMI). Integrating differential abundance, multivariate importance and participant-level consistency, we defined a 24-protein skeletal muscle aging signature whose score separated all younger from all elderly women. Combining grip strength and gait speed into a combined function score, we found that 23 of the 24 signature proteins correlated with physical function (FDR < 0.05), and the signature score correlated strongly with function (r = -0.79). The senescence-associated alarmins HMGB1 and HMGB2 emerged as lead proteins: HMGB1 showed the strongest association with function (r = -0.86), and both remained associated after adjustment for age group. Together, these data define a senotype proteomic program in aging female skeletal muscle and a molecular signature of muscle function that, after validation, may serve as a readout for interventions that aim to preserve physical performance in elderly women.

cards.title: Enzymatically triggered in situ gelation of a multifunctional peptide for localized controlled release and conformal fracture repair.
cards.abstract: Irregular fracture edges and gaps present significant challenges to bone healing. As versatile scaffolds for bone regeneration, hydrogels can effectively guide and facilitate tissue repair. Compared to preformed hydrogels, in situ gelation via a responsive sol-gel transition at the defect site offers superior flexibility, adaptability, and conformity, minimizing void cavities and establishing a more favorable environment for healing complex fractures. Peptides, as biogenic building blocks, can self-assemble into hierarchically structured hydrogels under specific stimuli. Given that alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is a key enzyme in bone mineralization and is highly expressed at the fracture site, we developed a phosphorylated peptide (NfFpYO) that undergoes ALP-triggered dephosphorylation, enabling direct in situ gelation on irregular fracture surfaces. Our results show that the resulting nanofibrous three-dimensional scaffold, functionalized with Gly-Pro-Hyp (GPO) motifs, promotes the migration, proliferation, and osteogenic differentiation of human bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (hBMSCs) in vitro. Moreover, the resulting nanofibrous hydrogel, which presents peptide-bound naproxen and fluorinated motifs, was associated with a less inflammatory and more repair-supportive macrophage-associated marker profile, enhanced osteogenic marker expression, and improved radiographic and histological fracture repair in a murine model. This study adapts a promising ALP-instructed peptide self-assembly strategy to the fracture-repair microenvironment through a multifunctional precursor design, providing a local shape-conformal and bioactive hydrogel platform with potential for complex fracture repair.

cards.title: Hybrid PLGA nanoparticles outperform SLNs in intracellular delivery of an anti-inflammatory lipid mediator to skeletal muscle cells.
cards.abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation (CLGI) contributes to several skeletal muscle disorders as sarcopenia, still lacking disease-specific therapies. Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) is a natural anti-inflammatory mediator with proven safety, but its high lipophilicity and poor solubility limit bioavailability and muscle delivery. The intrinsic difficulty of actively targeting skeletal muscle cells further supports the need for biomaterial-based strategies to enhance PEA delivery and therapeutic potential. Here, solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) and hybrid polymer-lipid PLGA nanoparticles (hyPLGA) are directly compared to identify a nanocarrier optimized for PEA delivery and bioactivity in skeletal muscle tissue. Both carriers exhibited favorable physicochemical profiles and maintained dimensional features after lyophilization, with PEA-SLNs achieving higher encapsulation efficiency. Despite this, PEA-hyPLGA nanoparticles demonstrated superior functional performance in vitro. In C2C12 myoblasts, both formulations were internalized efficiently, yet PEA-hyPLGA nanoparticles exhibited faster uptake kinetic. Notably, PEA-hyPLGA significantly reduced IL-6 and TNF-α transcript levels, enhanced PPAR-α nuclear localization, and mitigated LPS-induced cytotoxicity more effectively than Native PEA or PEA-SLNs. The efficient internalization of PEA-hyPLGA nanoparticles was also observed in human 3D muscle constructs, where the nanoparticles exhibited the ability to penetrate differentiated myofibers. Their behavior was further validated in vivo, where a prolonged retention of PEA-hyPLGA nanoparticles and their ability to reduce inflammatory markers in mouse skeletal muscle, upon intramuscular injection, was observed. Altogether, these findings indicate that hyPLGA nanoparticles represent a convenient nanostructure platform for PEA delivery and anti-inflammatory function in skeletal muscle, supporting their envisaged use as systemic administered targeted therapy toward translational strategies for sarcopenia.

cards.title: Nitinol continuous-compression staple fixation for selected complex patella fractures: a technical note.
cards.abstract: Nitinol continuous-compression staples may provide low-profile, fragment-specific fixation in selected complex patella fractures. This technical note describes two applications: a comminuted Gustilo IIIB open stellate fracture with small intermediary articular fragments and inferior-pole involvement, and a displaced distal-pole fracture with a coronal split component. After articular reduction, staples were positioned to apply compression across selected fragment interfaces while preserving bone stock and corridors for adjunctive fixation. Compression between staple tines may be useful for coronal split patterns and for small or comminuted fragments where conventional implants require unfavourable trajectories or excessive bone purchase. Potential advantages include reduced hardware prominence, avoidance of K-wire migration, continuous compression compared with static implants, improved capture of small inferior, anterior cortical, marginal, or coronal split fragments, and preservation of limited patellar bone stock.

cards.title: Maize Parenchyma to Nanocellulose: A Facile Preparation through High-Speed Shear Induced during Coagulation.
cards.abstract: Developing environmentally friendly and energy-efficient routes to nanocellulose remains challenging. Herein, we developed a gentle bottom-up strategy to prepare nanocellulose from maize parenchyma by combining concentration regulation with high-speed shear during coagulation. This approach directed cellulose chain aggregation and produced regenerated cellulose particles with irregular edges and sizes of 10-50 nm. The resulting nanocellulose film exhibited a favorable balance of mechanical properties, with a Young's modulus of 3.10 GPa and a work of fracture of 39.83 MJ m-3. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations showed that constrained shear promoted cellulose chains from random-coil conformations to extended and oriented states, facilitating hydrogen-bond reconstruction and cellulose II ordering. Solid-state 13C CP/MAS NMR further confirmed enhanced molecular ordering, with CrINMR increasing from 48.90% for CF-1.0 to 60.06% for CF-0.2. This work provides a sustainable route for valorizing agricultural waste into high-performance nanocellulose materials.

cards.title: Role of metabolites in mediating the effect of lipidomes on osteoporosis: A Mendelian randomization study.
cards.abstract: We investigated the causal relationships between the plasma lipidomes, osteoporosis (OP), and potential metabolite mediators using Mendelian randomization (MR). Using summary-level data from a genome-wide association study, bidirectional MR analyses to explore the causal relationships between the plasma lipidomes and OP, and two-step MR to discover potential mediating metabolites. Sensitivity analyses were performed to validate the robustness of the results further. After primary analysis and a series of sensitivity analyses, 7 inflammation-related proteins were identified that have a causal relationship with OP. Ceramide (d40:1) levels (odds ratio [OR] = 0.923; 95% confidence intervals (CI): 0.854-0.999; P = .046 < .05), phosphatidylcholine (16:0_18:2) levels (OR = 0.932; 95% CI: 0.883-0.985; P = .012 < .05), phosphatidylc holine (16:1_18:2) levels (OR = 0.939; 95% CI: 0.882-0.999; P = .047 < .05), triacylglycerol (48:3) levels (OR = 0.920; 95% CI: 0.854-0.971; P = .027 < .05), and triacylglycerol (51:4) levels (OR = 0.914; 95% CI: 0.840-0.995; P = .038 < .05) were negatively associated with OP, whereas phosphatidylcholine (O-17:0_15:0) levels (OR = 1.121; 95% CI: 1.019-1.233; P = .019 < .05), and triacylglycerol (48:0) levels (OR = 1.130; 95% CI: 1.042-1.226; P = .003 < .05) were positively associated with OP. Subsequently, we conducted a two-step MR to discover potential mediating metabolites. This study found that 14 plasma metabolites may play a mediating role in the relationship between plasma lipidomes and OP, such as 5alpha-androstan-3alpha,17beta-diol monosulfate (1) levels, N6-methyllysine levels, 5-oxoproline levels, 2-hydroxyhippurate levels, glycosyl ceramide (d18:1/20:0, d16:1/22:0) levels, spermidine to 5-methylthioadenosine ratio, serine levels, phosphate to serine ratio, proline to trans-4-hydroxyproline ratio, 1-palmitoyl-GPC (16:0) levels, 7-methylxanthine levels, arachidonoylcholine levels, and spermidine to choline ratio. In conclusion, our study identified a causal relationship between plasma lipidomes and OP, with a proportion of the effect mediated by plasma metabolites.

cards.title: Profile of Barbara Sherwood Lollar.
cards.abstract: In a laboratory nearly 2.4 kilometers under the Canadian Shield, geochemist Barbara Sherwood Lollar has tracked the sustained release of enough hydrogen gas from Earth's crust to produce 4.7 million kilowatt-hours of energy per year. Elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2022, Sherwood Lollar revisited the Kidd Creek Mine in Ontario, Canada where, in 2013, her explorations found that waters flowing from deep fractures were 1.6 billion years old. Reported in her Inaugural Article, the findings, aided by studies of noble gases in the samples, pushed the age of Earth's oldest waters back by hundreds of millions of years.

cards.title: A feasible and cost-effective method to induce distal radius fractures in full-length forearm human cadaveric specimens.
cards.abstract: Reported rates of loss of reduction in nonoperatively treated distal radius fractures (DRF) range from 17 to 71%. Thus, realistic biomechanical models are warranted to test novel immobilization devices that prevent loss of reduction in nonoperative fracture management. Currently available human cadaveric specimen models have several limitations: (i) disrupted soft tissue integrity, (ii) difficulty in replicating complex fracture patterns, and (iii) high technical demands and costs. Therefore, the aim of this study was to establish a feasible and accessible method for inducing DRFs, that accurately reflects in-vivo biomechanical fracture conditions in tissue-intact cadaveric specimens, suitable for testing of novel immobilization devices. Fifteen upper extremity cadaveric specimens were included. Specimens were prepared as full‑length forearm models. Using a repurposed strength training tower as a vertical drop tower, fractures were induced by proximally administering 120-135 J impacts. CT scans were performed pre- and post-fracture induction. All fractures were classified according to the AO/OTA classification. DRFs were successfully induced in all 15 specimens. A single 120 J impact produced a DRF in 11 out of 15 cases (73%). A second impact was administered in 4 out of 15 specimens (27%). Eleven of the 15 induced DRFs (73%) were classified as AO/OTA type C fractures, most commonly 2R3C3.2. Concomitant distal ulnar fractures were present in 6 cases, concomitant carpal fractures in 9 specimens. The overall cost of the setup amounted to 947 €. This study presents a feasible, cost-effective method to induce DRFs in tissue-intact, full-length human cadaveric forearm specimens. The setup consistently produces DRFs, predominantly AO/OTA type C, which can, with certain limitations, be utilized for biomechanical testing of immobilization devices, while also being uited for surgical and anatomical education.

cards.title: Low-cost and scalable synthesis of α-poly(L-glutamic acid) for superficial skin wound repair.
cards.abstract: Superficial skin repair demands high-performance, biocompatible medical dressings, drawing widespread attention to poly(glutamic acid) (PGA) in cosmetics and biomedicine. While γ-PGA, linked by γ-peptide bonds distinct from those in human proteins, is widely produced via scalable fermentation, it suffers from poor molecular weight control and cumbersome endotoxin removal. In contrast, α-PGA with native-like α-peptide bonds offers superior properties and biosafety but faces synthetic challenges. Here, we achieved a concise, hundreds-gram synthesis of well-defined, high-purity α-PGA via the ring-opening polymerization of unprotected glutamic N-carboxyanhydride. α-PGA-Na with a degree of polymerization of 20 displays superior hydration capacity compared with commercially fermented high-molecular-weight γ-PGA-Na and delivers comprehensive bioactivity in regulating cell viability, relative proliferative activity, migration, and alleviating UVB-induced cellular senescence. Furthermore, α-PGA-Na causes no acute skin or eye irritation in vivo, mitigates erythema, relieves pain-related behavioral responses, and facilitates early superficial wound healing. This work highlights α-PGA's dual potential as a cosmetic ingredient and liquid dressing, advancing tailored polypeptide materials for skincare and wound care.

cards.title: Nrf2 Activation Induces Fibroblast Senescence and Promotes Melanosome Accumulation in a Fibroblast-Keratinocyte Co-Culture Model.
cards.abstract: Solar lentigo (SL) is an age-associated hyperpigmented skin disorder linked to oxidative stress, impaired autophagy, and cellular senescence. However, experimental systems that recapitulate the senescence-associated skin microenvironment remain limited. In this study, we investigated the role of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) in fibroblast senescence and pigmentation-related responses using transcriptomic analyses and a fibroblast-keratinocyte co-culture model. Public transcriptomic datasets revealed increased NFE2L2 expression together with altered autophagy-related and senescence-associated signatures in hyperpigmented skin lesions. In dermal fibroblasts, Nrf2 overexpression induced senescence-associated phenotypes, including increased SA-β-gal activity and elevated expression of SASP-related genes. In a fibroblast-keratinocyte co-culture system, Nrf2-activated fibroblasts promoted melanosome accumulation in keratinocytes, suggesting that senescence-associated dermal-epidermal interactions contribute to pigmentation-related alterations. SENOMUNE, a formulation with autophagy-modulating activity, enhanced LC3 puncta formation in keratinocytes and attenuated melanosome accumulation in the senescence-associated co-culture system. Collectively, these findings suggest that sustained Nrf2 activation contributes to fibroblast senescence and pigmentation-related responses and provide a useful co-culture platform for evaluating senescence-associated pigmentation modulators.

cards.title: Use of thigh-based recipient vessels for free flap reconstruction in gustilo anderson type IIIC lower extremity open fractures: Description of two cases.
cards.abstract: Free tissue transfer is central to reconstruction of Gustilo IIIC lower-extremity injuries, but recipient vessel selection is challenging when local vasculature is compromised. We describe two Gustilo IIIC injuries reconstructed using thigh-based recipient vessels. Case 1: A 50-year-old man sustained an open tibial fracture with popliteal artery thrombosis and extensive tibial vessel injury. Following revascularization and serial debridement, a 25 × 15 cm tibial defect was reconstructed with a contralateral anterolateral thigh (ALT) free flap to the descending genicular artery (DGA), using an interposition great saphenous vein graft. The flap survived without complication.Case 2: A 35-year-old man sustained an open tibial fracture with complete popliteal artery transection requiring vascular reconstruction. A 20 × 14 cm defect was initially reconstructed with a free latissimus dorsi flap to the DGA using an interposition vein graft, complicated by venous thrombosis and flap loss. Subsequent reconstruction with an ALT flap and radial forearm flow-through flap to the superficial femoral vessels (SFA) achieved successful soft-tissue coverage. The DGA provides an accessible recipient outside the primary zone of injury, with consistent anatomy and suitable calibre for microsurgical anastomosis. Its location facilitates a two-team approach, avoids popliteal fossa exploration, and may reduce interference with subsequent skeletal procedures. The SFA is a valuable alternative recipient vessel, offering robust and reliable inflow with a good arterial pressure head. Thigh-based recipient vessels, particularly the DGA and SFA, should be considered in severe lower-limb trauma when conventional below-knee recipient vessels are unavailable or compromised.

cards.title: Refinement and initial characterization of a murine mandibular distraction osteogenesis model.
cards.abstract: To establish and initially characterize a reproducible mouse mandibular distraction osteogenesis (DO) model using a modular precision device. An external distractor was designed based on micro-CT data of C57BL/6 mouse mandibles. Fifty-four mice were randomized into sham, fracture, acute distraction, and gradual distraction groups. The gradual group underwent osteotomy, 5-day latency, 10-day distraction (0.15 mm/12 h, total 3 mm), and 4-week consolidation period. The acute group underwent 5-day latency and single 3 mm distraction on postoperative day 6 (POD 6). Fracture group underwent osteotomy only, while the sham underwent surgical exposure only. Samples were collected from the gradual group at POD 6, 10, 15, 22, 29, 43; other groups at POD 43. Bone regeneration was evaluated by micro-CT and histology. The distraction gap reached 3.02 ± 0.13 mm, consistent with the 3.0 mm target. Body weight recovered favorably. Micro-CT revealed that the gradual group exhibited characteristic DO temporal patterns: limited bone formation during distraction with low BV/TV (0.94 ± 0.44% at POD 6), followed by marked mineralization during consolidation, reaching 38.07 ± 2.86% at POD 43 (P < 0.0001 vs. POD 6). Histology showed ordered collagen deposition along the distraction vector during distraction, with subsequent trabecular maturation during consolidation. At POD 43, the gradual group had significantly higher BV/TV, Tb.Th, and Tb.N than both the fracture and acute groups (all P < 0.05). A reproducible mouse mandibular DO model was established, providing a reliable platform for investigating mechanically induced craniofacial bone regeneration.

cards.title: Serum Metabolomic Profiling Reveals Disrupted Amino Acid and Fatty Acid Metabolism in Older Adults with Sarcopenia.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia, an age-related syndrome characterized by progressive loss of muscle mass, decreased muscle strength, and/or reduced physical performance, is associated with disruptions in amino acid and lipid metabolism. This study aimed to investigate serum metabolic alterations associated with sarcopenia in older adults. In this cross-sectional study, 50 patients with sarcopenia (diagnosed per 2014 AWGS criteria) were matched 1:1 by age and sex with non-sarcopenic controls from a pool of 2,965 individuals. Assessments included skeletal muscle mass, grip strength, and gait speed. Serum metabolomic profiling was conducted using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). The screening of differential metabolites: variable importance in the projection (VIP) > 1 derived from the OPLS-DA model, and adjusted p-value based on false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05 calculated by two-sample t-test. Among 100 participants aged 60-87 years, individuals with sarcopenia showed significantly lower BMI, grip strength, albumin, and ASMI than controls (all p < 0.05), whereas lipid levels were comparable. PCA suggested weak group separation, whereas PLS-DA achieved clearer discrimination by sex and sarcopenia status. Differential metabolites identified in the sarcopenia group included arginine, leucine and histidinyl-histidine, the latter of which exhibited decreased abundance. Concomitant alterations in the levels of lipid metabolites collectively suggest disrupted amino acid and lipid metabolism. Patterns of dysregulated amino acid and fatty acid metabolism were observed in older adults with sarcopenia. Such metabolic disturbances might serve as candidate biomarkers to inform early detection and nutritional intervention strategies.

cards.title: Anatomic Considerations of Retrograde Intramedullary Nail Placement in Distal Ulna Fractures.
cards.abstract: To characterize the anatomic relationship between retrograde intramedullary nail placement in distal ulna fractures and important surrounding structures, with particular focus on the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC). Eight fresh-frozen cadaveric upper extremity specimens underwent simulated distal ulnar neck fracture fixation using a 4.5 mm retrograde intramedullary threaded nail. Pre- and postinsertion arthroscopy was performed to assess TFCC integrity. Dissection was used to evaluate proximity to surrounding structures, including the extensor retinaculum, extensor carpi ulnaris, extensor digiti minimi, and dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve. TFCC involvement was classified by location and quantified using surface area analysis. The nail path disrupted the distal extensor retinaculum in all specimens, with no direct injury to the extensor carpi ulnaris, extensor digiti minimi, or dorsal cutaneous branch of the ulnar nerve, although these structures were in close proximity. The superficial TFCC and the deep radioulnar ligament footprint were involved in the majority of specimens, with the dorsal peripheral region most commonly penetrated. However, the overall surface area of the TFCC impacted was minimal. Retrograde intramedullary nail placement for distal ulna fractures frequently involves both the superficial TFCC and deep radioulnar ligament footprint, with perforations most common in the dorsal peripheral region rather than the central disc of the TFCC. Despite this, the overall surface area of involvement is limited. Surgeons should be aware of the proximity of important surrounding structures and the likelihood of TFCC involvement when using a retrograde intramedullary approach for distal ulna fractures.

cards.title: A Bi‐Adjuvant Senolytic Nanovaccine Modulating Dendritic Cell Senescence Ameliorates Aging‐Related Metabolic Dysfunction
cards.abstract: ABSTRACT Senolytic vaccines hold promise for eliminating senescent cells, but their efficacy is limited by poor seno‐antigen immunogenicity and age‐related dendritic cell (DC) dysfunction. Here, we engineered an active biomaterial‐enabled bi‐adjuvant senolytic nanovaccine (CK5‐GC‐NV) by co‐assembling CpG oligodeoxynucleotide with a fusion protein of the seno‐antigen Gpnmb and a cationic spider silk protein variant (CK5). Beyond antigen delivery, the CK5 scaffold acts as an intrinsic senomodulator associated with the downregulation of mitotic kinases Aurka/b and a concomitant decrease in senescence‐associated PI3K/AKT phosphorylation in DCs. This intervention attenuates aged DC phenotypes, restores antigen cross‐presentation, and synergizes with CpG to elicit potent cytotoxic T‐lymphocyte responses against senescent targets. Across multiple aging mouse models, CK5‐GC‐NV immunization orchestrated targeted clearance of Gpnmb + senescent adipocytes, profoundly ameliorating metabolic dysfunction and extending lifespan. This multifunctional biomaterial platform integrates seno‐antigen immunogenicity enhancement with the restoration of aged DC function, providing a promising proof‐of‐concept for antigen‐directed gerotherapeutics.

cards.title: Research on the design and mechanical properties of extended constant resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolts.
cards.abstract: To address the premature fracture of anchor bolts caused by the mismatched yielding distance between anchor bolts and hydraulic supports in the advanced support section of rock burst-prone roadways, an elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt was designed-with its yielding distance specifically coordinated to match that of hydraulic supports. ABAQUS numerical simulation was utilized to investigate the mechanical characteristics of this novel anchor bolt under static loading, as well as under varying impact energies and impact velocities. A comparative analysis was further performed against the mechanical performance of conventional anchor bolts. The results reveal the following: Under static loading, the elongated constant-resistance energy-absorbing anchor bolt exhibits a fracture load of 160.6 kN, a fracture displacement of 523.2 mm, an elongation rate of 20.93%, and an energy absorption capacity of 69.7 kJ. Under impact velocities within 9 m/s, the impact velocity has little effect on the fracture load, elongation, and energy absorption of constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolts, while the impact resistance time exhibits a nonlinear decreasing trend with increasing impact velocity. Under both static and dynamic loading conditions, the extended constant-resistance energy-absorbing bolt exhibits superior impact resistance and can effectively address the problem of premature bolt fracture caused by the mismatch between the bolt yielding distance and that of the hydraulic support in the three-level energy-absorbing support system. The findings provide a new perspective for bolt design.

cards.title: Numerical study on infill fracturing of mature wells under free-drainage boundary conditions.
cards.abstract: Infill fracturing of mature wells involves re-fracturing within previously stimulated clusters, targeting unstimulated regions of the parent well's fracture network. This strategy sustainably enhances hydrocarbon recovery from depleted reservoirs without the environmental footprint of new drilling. Establishing a numerical simulation model for this process is essential for optimization. In this study, a numerical model for mature well infill fracturing was developed based on the extended finite element method and a free-drainage boundary module. The results indicate that prior production from mature wells primarily affects the fracture length and curvature in the infill wells. As infill fracturing-induced fractures propagate toward the far-field region, they are significantly influenced by the heterogeneous pore pressure distribution in the reservoir. This leads to a pronounced increase in fracture curvature. Compared with conventional fracturing, the curvature of fractures under infill fracturing is approximately 30% higher within the same simulation time, while the fracture length is notably shorter. With the increase in production time, fractures in infill wells tend to exhibit greater tortuosity. This enhanced complexity allows for more effective contact between the fractures and the reservoir, thereby improving the production potential of the infill wells to some extent.

cards.title: Prevalence of sarcopenia among community-dwelling older adults in an urban district in Penang, Malaysia and its associated factors.
cards.abstract: Sarcopenia refers to a progressive decline in skeletal muscle mass, strength, and physical performance that commonly occurs with ageing, and is associated with adverse outcomes such as frailty, disability, and mortality. Despite its growing public health importance in ageing populations, limited data are available on the prevalence of sarcopenia in Penang, Malaysia. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of sarcopenia and its associated factors among community-dwelling older adults in an urban district in Penang. A cross-sectional study was conducted among community-dwelling adults aged 60 years and above in the Seberang Perai Utara district, Penang. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Sarcopenia was diagnosed using the Asian Working Group for Sarcopenia (AWGS) 2019 criteria based on muscle mass, muscle strength, and physical performance. Data on sociodemographic characteristics, comorbidities, and physical activity levels were collected using a structured questionnaire and the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) short form. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with sarcopenia. A total of 226 participants were included in the study. The overall prevalence of sarcopenia was 32.7%, including 15.0% with severe sarcopenia and 17.7% with sarcopenia. In multivariate analysis, higher body mass index (adjusted OR 0.794, 95% CI 0.723-0.873, p < 0.001) was associated with lower odds of sarcopenia. Physical activity level was also significantly associated with sarcopenia (p = 0.013). Participants who were minimally active had higher odds of sarcopenia (adjusted OR = 4.393, 95% CI: 1.583-12.193, p = 0.004) compared with HEPA active participants. Sarcopenia was identified in nearly one-third of participants among community-dwelling older adults in Seberang Perai Utara, Penang. Compared with HEPA active participants, minimally active participants were associated with higher odds of sarcopenia. Whereas higher BMI was associated with lower odds of the condition. These findings highlight key cross-sectional correlates of sarcopenia in community, emphasizing the importance of monitoring body weight, muscle health, and physical activity engagement among community-dwelling older adults.

cards.title: Study on the dynamic fracture behavior and energy consumption characteristics of granite with a pre-cut mode-I crack under impact loading.
cards.abstract: To investigate the dynamic fracture behavior and energy consumption characteristics of granite containing pre-cut mode-I cracks of different sizes under impact loading, split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) tests are conducted on Brazilian disc specimens with four height-to-diameter (H/D) ratios. The results show that the deformation and failure process of pre-cracked granite can be divided into three stages: linear elastic deformation, plastic yielding, and post-peak failure. Both peak stress and fracture toughness exhibit an exponential increase with average strain rate, with the strongest strain-rate sensitivity observed for H/D = 0.1. Increasing the H/D ratio enhances peak stress and fracture toughness, whereas higher strain rates weaken this size effect. The cracking process is dominated by mode-I failure. Impact pressure enlarges the crushing zones and increases the degree of fragmentation, but damage extent decreases with increasing H/D ratio, leading to improved specimen integrity. The reflected, transmitted, and absorbed energies all increase with incident energy, and the absorbed energy exhibits significant strain-rate and size effects. The specific energy absorption (SEA) and mass-specific crushing energy consumption (Md) both increase exponentially with dynamic peak stress and fracture toughness.Specimens with H/D = 0.5 show the highest energy absorption capacity and require the most energy for fragmentation. The damage variable and dissipated energy evolution curves follow a "slow growth - rapid growth - approximately linear growth" pattern. Numerical simulations for H/D = 0.1 and 0.5 reproduce the observed size-dependent fracture patterns and energy partitioning, confirming that lateral confinement controls the size effect under diametral impact loading.

cards.title: NSAID use, osteoporosis, and trabecular bone score in community-dwelling older adults: the bushehr elderly health (BEH) ​program.
cards.abstract: The relationship between nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) use and skeletal health remains uncertain. We examined reported NSAID use in relation to overall and site-specific osteoporosis and trabecular bone score (TBS) in community-dwelling older adults. This population-based cross-sectional analysis included 2,353 adults aged ≥ 60 years from the Bushehr Elderly Health Program, Iran. Osteoporosis was defined by a dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry T-score ≤ - 2.5 at the lumbar spine, femoral neck, or total hip. Sex-stratified logistic regression estimated prevalence odds ratios adjusted for age, body mass index, rheumatoid arthritis, and osteoarthritis. Sex interactions were tested for osteoporosis outcomes. Exploratory TBS analyses used ordinal and multinomial logistic regression; ordinal models adjusted for age, smoking, physical activity, body mass index, and diabetes. NSAID use was reported by 369 participants (15.7%), and overall osteoporosis prevalence was 41.4%. Among women, NSAID use was associated with higher odds of overall osteoporosis (adjusted OR, 1.50; 95% CI, 1.10-2.05), femoral-neck osteoporosis (1.53; 1.13-2.07), and total-hip osteoporosis (1.53; 1.01-2.30). The lumbar-spine estimate was close to the null (1.07; 0.78-1.47). Associations in men were statistically inconclusive, and interaction tests did not establish differences by sex. Among women, adjusted ordinal logistic regression also identified an association between NSAID use and worse TBS categories (OR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.00-1.85; p = 0.047). Category-specific multinomial comparisons were inconclusive. Reported NSAID use was associated with higher prevalence odds of osteoporosis and poorer TBS status in older women after covariate adjustment. These findings support investigating how NSAID type, dose, and cumulative exposure relate to bone density and trabecular bone status in aging populations. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02127-8.

cards.title: Carbonyl reductase 1: A redox-regulating carbonyl detoxification enzyme in health and disease.
cards.abstract: Carbonyl reductase 1 (CBR1) is a cytosolic monomeric enzyme belonging to the short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase superfamily and is ubiquitously expressed in human tissues. It catalyzes the NADPH-dependent reduction of a wide range of carbonyl compounds and plays a major role not only in phase I metabolism of xenobiotics, including drugs, but also in the metabolism of endogenous substrates such as prostaglandin E2, S-nitrosoglutathione, ketosteroids, and lipid peroxidation-derived aldehydes. Notably, glutathione binds near the active site of CBR1 and enhances its reductase activity toward non-glutathionylated substrates. Accumulating evidence indicates that CBR1 is involved in cancer, functioning either as a tumor suppressor or a tumor promoter depending on the cancer type. This dual role suggests that CBR1 functions as a context-dependent regulator of cellular redox adaptation. CBR1 is also implicated in several noncancerous diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, diabetes, ischemia/reperfusion injury, osteoporosis, ulcerative colitis, and COPD. In this review, we summarize current knowledge on the structure, enzymatic functions, gene regulation, modulators, and polymorphisms of CBR1, and discuss its diverse roles in cancers and noncancerous disorders.

cards.title: Development of biodegradable nanoparticles surface-modified with oligopeptides for bone-targeted bisphosphonate delivery.
cards.abstract: This study designed and developed a carrier for the delivery of bisphosphonates to the bone surrounding the site of inflammatory lesions to treat peripheral osteoporosis. We attempted to create biodegradable nanoparticle carriers that exhibit high affinity for hydroxyapatite (HAP) and evade recognition by macrophage-like cells. Nanoparticles prepared using poly(d,l-lactide) (PLA) with a carboxyl end group exhibited moderate binding affinity to HAP, but showed significant association with macrophage-like cells. Nanoparticles prepared from a blend of a polyethylene glycol (PEG)-PLA block copolymer and PLA homopolymer were modified with acidic oligopeptides, which served as the bone-targeting moiety. Nanoparticles with PLA chain ends modified with octa-glutamic acid exhibited low binding affinity to HAP. In contrast, nanoparticles with PEG chain ends modified with octa-glutamic acid exhibited strong binding affinity to HAP and low association with macrophage-like cells. Nanoparticles encapsulating risedronate (RIS), a bisphosphonate drug, were incubated at 37 °C, and the release behavior of RIS from the nanoparticles exhibited a biphasic pattern consisting of an initial rapid release followed by a subsequent slow release at a neutral pH, while the release was accelerated under acidic conditions. Furthermore, upon cellular internalization, RIS-loaded nanoparticles demonstrated potent cytotoxicity toward osteoclasts and induced apoptosis.
