cards.title: Kidney dysfunction under cardiometabolic stress promotes calorie-intake-independent wasting and frailty-like muscle phenotypes.
cards.abstract: Although age-related sarcopenia and frailty are linked to impaired metabolic flexibility and disrupted energy homeostasis, whether this framework explains chronic kidney disease (CKD)-related wasting remains unclear. We show that superimposed nephron loss redirects cardiometabolic stress from obesity and glucose intolerance toward calorie-intake-independent wasting with sarcopenic and physical frailty features. This switch was accompanied by impaired skeletal muscle glucose-utilization programs, a blunted glycemic response to gluconeogenic substrates, and altered hepatic-renal gluconeogenic programs. Integrated omics revealed suppressed glucose programs, impaired fatty acid utilization-related compensation, and amino acid catabolic signatures in skeletal muscle. Similar features occurred with aging plus nephron loss and in older human CKD kidneys with reduced renal PCK1 expression. Cornstarch-based nutritional modulation improved exercise capacity, muscle mass, and serum albumin, highlighting slow-release carbohydrate modulation as a potential therapeutic entry point. These findings support a model in which kidney dysfunction promotes wasting by limiting systemic metabolic reserve and skeletal muscle metabolic flexibility.

cards.title: A modular synthetic hydrogel with cell-scale micropores modulates osteocyte-like morphogenesis and osteogenic differentiation in vitro.
cards.abstract: One crucial step during early osteogenesis is the embedding of osteoblasts within a collagen-rich extracellular matrix (osteoid), where they subsequently differentiate into a functional network of osteocytes. However, reconstructing 3D osteocyte networks in vitro remains a major challenge. We recently developed a synthetic microporous hydrogel to support the in vitro culture of 3D bone cell networks. Although matrix biodegradability facilitates cell-material interactions, the influence of micropores on bone tissue morphogenesis and differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the effect of cell-scale micropores on bone cell morphogenesis and osteogenic differentiation in vitro. By exploiting polymerization-induced phase separation (PIPS) between 4-arm polyethylene glycol vinyl sulfones and dextran in the presence of hyaluronan, we generated matrix metalloproteinase-sensitive hydrogels with cell-scale micropores. Increasing the dextran concentration enlarged the average pore size from 4 μm to 8 μm, accompanied by a slight decrease in mechanical stiffness. Following encapsulation within these hydrogels, primary human osteoblasts remained highly viable. Hydrogels with larger pores supported extensive 3D cell network formation, whereas hydrogels with smaller pores exhibited enhanced osteogenic differentiation following 21 days of osteogenic culture. Together, these findings highlight that bone cells are sensitive to microporous physical cues and even minor changes over pore sizes can make an impact on osteocyte-like morphogenesis and differentiation in vitro.

cards.title: Relationship of Multidimensional Frailty With Social Participation and Emotional Well-Being in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
cards.abstract: Multidimensional frailty may limit participation and psychological well-being among community-dwelling older adults, yet evidence comparing multiple frailty domains remains limited. This study examined associations of physical, cognitive, social, and oral frailty with social participation and emotional well-being among community-dwelling older adults in the United States. This cross-sectional secondary analysis included 4,878 Medicare beneficiaries aged 65 years and older from the 2024 National Health and Aging Trends Study. Frailty domains were assessed using performance-based and self-reported measures. Social participation and emotional well-being were measured using summed scores. Survey-weighted multivariable linear regression models adjusted for age group, sex, education, comorbidities, and residential area. Physical, cognitive, and social frailty were associated with lower social participation, whereas physical, social, and oral frailty were associated with poorer emotional well-being. Social frailty showed the largest negative association with both outcomes.

cards.title: Automatic Multiparametric Quantitative Ultrasound Framework for Segmentation and Characterization of Layered Soft Tissues.
cards.abstract: To diagnose diseases associated with changes in body composition, such as sarcopenia or muscle wasting due to cancer, it is necessary to accurately evaluate muscle and fat layers. However, conventional B-mode ultrasound has limitations due to its high dependence on the ultrasound examiner and subjective interpretation. In this study, we propose a multiparametric quantitative ultrasound (QUS) framework that automatically detects tissue boundaries and segments laminar tissues by combining attenuation images estimated using the Regularized Spectral Log Difference (RSLD) method with midband fit, spectral intercepts, Nakagami images and echogenicity mapping. Boundaries were identified through 2-D connectivity component analysis on the integrated QUS map, which allowed for the detection of discontinuous or stepped boundaries without assuming lateral continuity, followed by refinement using a Chan-Vese active contour model. This framework was evaluated using a homogeneous reference phantom, a customized lateral heterogeneous staircase phantom, and an ex vivo swine shoulder specimen. The results of the staircase phantom experiment showed that the segmented block thickness matched actual physical measurements within 2.3%-5.0% across all four regions, despite the stepped boundary geometry. In ex vivo experiments, the estimated fat and muscle thicknesses also matched actual measurements within 4.8% and 1.3%, respectively, and fat and muscle regions showed distinct QUS parameter values. These preliminary results support the feasibility of automatically characterizing tissue characteristics by combining multiple QUS parameters into a single integrated segmentation framework, and lay the groundwork for further validation studies using diverse samples for future body composition assessment.
